title: Ravens agree to trade DL C.J. Okoye to the Giants
summary: Giants head coach John Harbaugh is bringing another Raven with him to his new team.
full_text: Giants head coach John Harbaugh is bringing another Raven with him to his new team. NFL Media reports that the Giants have agreed to send a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Ravens for defensive lineman C.J. Okoye. Okoye entered the league as part of the International Player Pathway Program and spent the 2023 and 2024 seasons on the Chargers' practice squad. He moved on to the Ravens last year and played in 15 games during Harbaugh's final season in Baltimore. Okoye had 15 tackles and a pass breakup in those appearances. Trading Okoye takes care of one roster move the Ravens need to make to get to the 53-player limit by Sunday's deadline while the Giants will now have one more cut to make.
author: Josh Alper

title: As NFL intends to go global, new supersonic engine is "weeks away" from testing
summary: The Concorde concept is making a comeback, which would make it easier for the NFL to continue its effort at global conquest.
full_text: The Concorde concept is making a comeback, which would make it easier for the NFL to continue its effort at global conquest. The successor to the mothballed supersonic jet is reportedly " weeks away " from engine testing. Boom Supersonic's Overture would cut the travel time from New York to London to 3.5 hours. Currently, the trip requires roughly eight hours. The NFL is monitoring the potential return of flight at velocities faster than the speed of sound. It would make it easier to take teams across oceans for international games. The Overture may only be the beginning. Another project, known as Invictus, could result in a plane that flies at 3,800 miles per hour — and that could cut the time for a London-to-Sydney trip to three hours. If that ever becomes a mainstream option, the NFL could put teams anywhere it chooses. And the Commissioner has said teams will inevitably be located in other countries. Obviously, international franchises would present other logistical issues. Tax rates, exchange rates, governmental differences, cultural differences are just some of them. The bigger problem could be the reluctance of players to live in other countries. Non-American teams also would complicate the process of churning rosters through in-season tryouts and signings and other moves that would have a player on an American roster one day, and on an international roster the next.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets will evaluate kicking options after Jason Sanders missed two kicks
summary: The Jets appeared to end their kicking competition this week when they released Cade York, but Jason Sanders's performance on Friday night may have opened things back up.
full_text: The Jets appeared to end their kicking competition this week when they released Cade York, but Jason Sanders's performance on Friday night may have opened things back up. Sanders missed an extra point after a touchdown in the first quarter and he missed a field goal in the fourth quarter of the game. That led to a question for head coach Aaron Glenn about whether the Jets are going to look elsewhere for help at the position before they face the Titans in Week 1. "Am I worried about it? I didn’t like the fact that we missed these field goals, but the thing is we’re not going to panic and we’re going to make sure that we make the right decision to make sure we either fix those issues or we get the right person in here," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "But Jason has been good for us. He’s been good in practice. I’m going to evaluate that and see exactly what direction we’ll go." Sanders spent seven seasons as the Dolphins' kicker before missing all of last year with a hip injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Marvin Mims bruised his foot, Broncos think he'll be fine
summary: The last thing any team wants to see is a significant contributor get hurt in the final week of the preseason, so it wasn't a great development for the Broncos when wide receiver Marvin Mims went to the medical tent early in Thursday's game.
full_text: The last thing any team wants to see is a significant contributor get hurt in the final week of the preseason, so it wasn't a great development for the Broncos when wide receiver Marvin Mims went to the medical tent early in Thursday's game. Mims limped off after an incomplete pass in his direction and had his right foot checked out. After the game, head coach Sean Payton said it was a minor issue. "With Mims, he's going to be fine . It's a bruise," Payton said. "We were really more just cautious with him. There were a few guys that we were going to get some snaps with that may have been —certainly front-line guys for us and he was one of those players." Mims missed time this summer with another lower-body injury and did not play in the first two preseason games, which explains why the Broncos gave him some snaps on a night when other key players were out of uniform. The injury wasn't ideal, but it doesn't sound like it should impact his availability for the Monday night opener against the Chiefs.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jason Licht "very optimistic" about Baker Mayfield staying beyond 2026
summary: Baker Mayfield said he felt disrespected and undervalued by the contract offers that came from the Buccaneers this offseason, so the quarterback is now set to play out the final year of his current deal.
full_text: ' Baker Mayfield said he felt disrespected and undervalued by the contract offers that came from the Buccaneers this offseason, so the quarterback is now set to play out the final year of his current deal. Mayfield also said that he wasn't interested in continuing to negotiate when he got to training camp this summer, which sets up a lot of possible ways for things to go between now and the start of the 2027 season. During an interview on WFLA during Friday night's preseason game, General Manager Jason Licht said he thinks that the end result of whatever happens in the coming months will be Mayfield in a Bucs uniform. "I'm very optimistic about it," Licht said, via Jenna Laine of ESPN.com. "He wants to play. He wants to prove to us that he is the franchise quarterback that we said that he was. So, we'll just have to see how it plays out. I'll never close the door on anything in the short term, but right now, he's focused on football." The Bucs have the franchise tag at their disposal, so there's little chance of Mayfield simply walking away off of a stellar season. Anything short of that opens up more possibilities that would make it a bit harder to share certainty about what the future will bring in Tampa.
author: Josh Alper

title: Big Ten will have four "availability reports" per week
summary: As sports betting continues to proliferate, college football is taking more steps aimed at minimizing inside information.
full_text: ' As sports betting continues to proliferate, college football is taking more steps aimed at minimizing inside information. Via the Associated Press, the Big Ten announced on Friday that it will expand its requirement to submit player availability reports from one per week to four . The rule, which applies only to in-conference games, mandates the submission of a report on each of the three days before a game, with a final report provided on game day. The midweek reports require teams to identify players as probable, questionable, doubtful, out, or out for the first half. On game day, the categories will be game-time decision, out, or out for the first half. The existence, and misuse, of inside information regarding player injuries continues to be one of the biggest potential sources of betting scandals. With more information provided to the public, less information will be private — and less information will be available to provide the basis for wagering by those who have access to it. All conferences should have similar rules. All programs should strive to ensure that the inside information is kept to a minimum. For most coaches, however, the sacrifice of a strategic edge arising from misinformation outweighs the risk that someone will share the inside information (possibly for a fee) with someone who will try to turn it into a tidy profit.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bill Belichick's second season in college football starts today
summary: Two NFL seasons have transpired without should-be Hall of Fame head coach Bill Belichick, who had spent half of a century in pro football.
full_text: Two NFL seasons have transpired without should-be Hall of Fame head coach Bill Belichick, who had spent half of a century in pro football. Today at noon ET, he embarks on his second season at the college level, with North Carolina. Like last year, the season commenced with a game against TCU. (It started well, before imploding.) Unlike last year, the game will be played not in Chapel Hill but in Dublin, Ireland. UNC won't have defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, who remains on medical leave. And the Tar Heels haven't had the services of G.M. Michael Lombardi, who was placed on paid administrative leave last month while the school conducts an internal investigation of him. The bigger question is the quality of the roster that Belichick and Lombardi have compiled for the coming season. They opted to go heavy on high-school recruits for 2026, with less of an emphasis on the transfer portal. The performance of these young players will ultimately influence Belichick's fate. Only the first three years of his five-year, $50 million contract are guaranteed; if he's fired after 2026, the school would owe him one season of pay. Last year, Belichick went 4-8 with a team that simply wasn't good enough — regardless of his legendary ability to devise and implement game plans tailored to outscoring any given opponent. If the players aren't good enough this year, it's hard to imagine Belichick returning for a third season. Which likely would bring his coaching career to an end. Unless one of the NFL's franchises decides to roll the dice on him. With Belichick getting only one interview in three NFL hiring cycles (and not a sniff in January, when 10 jobs were open), it's hard to imagine Belichick finding a landing spot in the pro game. Especially if he'll be looking for a place where the deck would be pre-stacked in his favor. But it's not impossible. Crazier things have happened. Like, for instance, the Hall of Fame voters inexplicably denying him a bronze bust in his first year of eligibility.
author: Mike Florio

title: The annual frenzy of NFL transactions happens this weekend
summary: Rosters must cut from 90 to 53 by Sunday at 4:00 p.m. ET.
full_text: The Turk will be very busy this weekend. The traditional name for the in-house harbinger of doom, each team's Turk will be telling players on the bubble that the coach wants to see them. "And bring your playbook," he usually adds. It's one of the basic realities of a sport that has 90 players on the roster until the limit plunges, in one fell swoop, to 53. And it will happen through an avalanche of moves that will trim the rosters, build practice squads of up to 16 players, and then spark a flurry of additional cuts and signings at the bottom of the roster. The process is the most basic reminder of the reality that the supply of willing NFL players far outweighs the demand. And that, once the preseason ends, the demand for players to play in the games that don't count instantly evaporates. Players who are released with four or more years of service instantly become free agents. Players who aren't "vested veterans" migrate to the waivers system. Any team can claim a player on waivers, with no limit on the number taken. The players are awarded by priority based on the 2026 draft order, with the Raiders having dibs on all of them. This means that players who make the 53-man roster as of Sunday at 4:00 p.m. ET may not be around for long. For every player claimed on waivers, another player needs to be removed from the roster. The roster cuts at one point were made on the Saturday of Labor Day weekend, only five days before the first game. When the season moved to 17 games, the process was accelerated by a week or so, giving the players who make the team a break before Week 1 preparations begin in earnest. The deadline had been Tuesday. This year, the decision to move the first game to the Wednesday after Labor Day (with two teams heading to Australia for a game the next day) prompted a shift to Sunday. All in all, it's a harsh process. The teams largely have become desensitized to it, because it's a fundamental step in building a team. And the players who don't have starting jobs set in stone understand that there's a risk they'll be leaving their current teams, possibly temporarily. Possibly for good. The practice squad helps to soften the blow. And those 16 spots for 32 teams create up to 512 more jobs. The churning of the roster and the practice squad will continue, throughout the regular season and into the playoffs. The availability of short-term injured reserve will create opportunities. Players who aren't attached to a team will get tryouts. For those who don't make it to a 53-man roster, the dream isn't dead. It's in limbo. And many of them will choose to stay in shape and wait for the phone to ring.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys linebacker and special teamer Marist Liufau suffers broken forearm
summary: Cowboys outside linebacker and special teams contributor Marist Liufau exited Friday night's preseason finale early, returned with his arm in a cast and sling, and is now expected to get surgery and miss time.
full_text: Cowboys outside linebacker and special teams contributor Marist Liufau exited Friday night's preseason finale early, returned with his arm in a cast and sling, and is now expected to get surgery and miss time. Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Liufau will miss " weeks ," while owner Jerry Jones said Liufau could be back "quickly," according to ESPN. "Losing Marist as a football player is tough," Schottenheimer said. "Unfortunately, it's part of the business. You guys all know him and the way he'll attack his rehab, and so we'll get surgery done as soon as we can and next man up. But yeah, he was a critical, critical part of not just two or three special teams, really all four. He's a 'four-core' guy that you just rely on and he plays the game with violence and we have some other guys in that locker room that do that as well." It's unclear whether the Cowboys will keep Liufau on the 53-man roster after Sunday's final cutdowns, or put him on injured reserve to start the season. Liufau was a 2024 third-round draft pick who has played all 17 games in both of his first two seasons with the Cowboys. Last year he was on the field for 18 percent of the Cowboys' defensive plays and 75 percent of the Cowboys' special teams plays.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tyler Loop is suddenly on shaky ground in Baltimore
summary: Last year, with the Ravens planning to move on from former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker (who has completely fallen off the map after his Personal Conduct Policy suspension), they invested a sixth-round pick in his replacement, Tyler Loop.
full_text: '' Last year, with the Ravens planning to move on from former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker (who has completely fallen off the map after his Personal Conduct Policy suspension), they invested a sixth-round pick in his replacement, Tyler Loop. Now, Loop could be the one getting replaced. Via Jamison Hensley of ESPN, Loop missed a pair of field goals during the preseason finale against the Commanders. It prompted boos from the home crowd and a lukewarm assessment of Loop by new coach Jesse Minter. "You want to see makes in games," Minter told reporters after the 41-2 win. "And so, it's something we'll continue to look at. We'll continue to look at what the best situation is there . He has had a good camp overall, but again, it comes down to making the kicks and the pressure situations in the game. So, that's something I think that we'll always be looking at to make sure that we're doing what's best for the team." Loop didn't have in-house competition during training camp. Minter hasn't ruled out adding an alternative as Week 1 approaches. "I think there's a million scenarios there to try to make sure that we have the best situation headed into Indy," Minter said. Via Hensley, Loop has made field goals from 20, 24, 42, 49, and 51 yards. He has missed from 49, 51, and 58 yards. As a rookie, Loop made 30 of 34 field goals, and 44 of 46 extra points. His misfires included a 44-yard field goal on the last play of the last game of the regular season, causing the Ravens to lose to the Steelers, to miss the playoffs, and to grease the skids for the firing of 18-year coach John Harbaugh.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean Payton explains social-media defense of Bo Nix against analyst
summary: Broncos coach Sean Payton used Twitter this week to defend quarterback Bo Nix against a community-noted take from former NFL player and current Fox analyst Geoff Schwartz.
full_text: Broncos coach Sean Payton used Twitter this week to defend quarterback Bo Nix against a community-noted take from former NFL player and current Fox analyst Geoff Schwartz. After Friday night's preseason finale, Payton was asked about his decision to say to Schwartz, who inaccurately claimed Nix doesn't "push the ball down the field all that often," this: " Always easy to tell who works at it and who doesn’t ." “That was crazy wasn’t it?" Payton told reporters. "I can’t help myself though. When I see something like that, I’m sorry, it’s just, I have a pause and then it’s like, ‘What are you watching?’ Just watch the tape. Here’s the thing though. I think — and this is for any player — sometimes when you’re on the East Coast, you don’t see, whatever, but when you get to see. . . . I remember the first time I ever saw a Percy Harvin or Adrian Peterson, it was completely different than — so to see someone live and to actually watch them is. . . . "Getting back to your question relative to — they’re just — you guys grind at it, but now you have so many variations. You’ve got the basement podcast with the beer logo and I just couldn’t help myself with that one. It was silly. Everything was the opposite of what he was saying and the worst part was he played at Oregon. I don’t even know the player, so." Schwartz did indeed play college football at Oregon. As did Nix. Payton's point is that the common bond should make Schwartz far less likely to be clueless about Nix's game. The bigger message is that Payton is willing to defend his guy. Which speaks to the quality of a joined-at-the-hip relationship that enters its third season with the Broncos firmly in the Super Bowl window.
author: Mike Florio

title: New Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla bristles at reaction to his Steelers fandom
summary: Khosla complains that "reporters will make every molehill into a mountain."
full_text: Every new NFL owner is largely an unwritten book, with the pages to be filled in one news item at a time. For new Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla, chapter one relates to his admission that he was and remains a Steelers fan . Khosla has bristled at the criticism of the relevant comments from his first press conference after the sale of the team was approved. "Reporters will make every molehill into a mountain just to get column inches to write or video minutes," Khosla said on Twitter. "What’s wrong with admitting my 1976-78 period in Pittsburgh (CMU) got me excited about the NFL? I still watch their games doesn’t mean I won't unconditionally ALWAYS as owner, want the [Seahawks] to win and have every edge up, EVERY TIME over every other team!!!! Zero questions!!! At the other end is a set of teams I always want to lose every advantage. But happy to have the sports writer getting more column inches and fill their pages. You are welcome. Apologies in advance for my very transparent style." Khosla's message appears over a reposting of a tweet from Barstool Sports with this observation: "What not to do during your opening press conference as the new Seahawks owner? Reveal you've been a Steelers fan your whole life and still watch all of their games." The reaction to Khosla's comments was widespread. He chose to share the "little-known fact" while demonstrating his longstanding passion for football. Of course he's now fully aligned with the Seahawks. The point isn't that he was a Steelers fan. It's that he decided, without prompting, to tell the world that he was and still is a Steelers fan, and that he still watches all of their games. “ So, actually, I was originally, and still am, a big Steelers fan also — a little-known fact — but I still watch all the Steelers games, too." That's what he said. No one put words in his mouth. No one was grilling him over the legitimacy of his commitment to the Seahawks, and no one is. The reaction came from the basic reality that it probably wasn't the best thing to wear on his sleeve in the first press conference as the owner of the Seahawks. And it wasn't just, you know, the rest of the world that came to that conclusion. Watch the video. Khosla's son, Neal, had just enough of a crack in his poker face to reveal that he was thinking something like, "Dad. Don't." The strong reaction to the criticism now becomes the second chapter in the Book of Khosla. And the chapters will come one after another — especially since Khosla seems to be very active on social media. At least he didn't close with, "Thank you for your attention to this matter!"
author: Mike Florio

title: Kevin O'Connell doesn't rule out keeping four quarterbacks on 53-man roster
summary: J.J. McCarthy isn't guaranteed the backup job, or a roster spot.
full_text: With all teams cutting to 53 players on Sunday afternoon, with a current maximum of 90, most if not all franchises will be making tough decisions. The Vikings will likely be making tough decisions at quarterback, where the team has four quarterbacks. After Friday night's preseason finale, coach Kevin O'Connell opened the door to the possibility of keeping all of them on the 53-man roster. "I don’t think it is out of the question that we try to keep all of those guys," O'Connell told reporters after the game (via a transcript generated by Minnesota's opponent, the Broncos), "but at the same time, we got to do what’s best for our team. So we’ll work through that and that will definitely be part of the conversation because there was a reason why we wanted to have a deep quarterback room, and all four of those guys had their moments throughout the last month and six weeks or so, and that’ll definitely be a part of the evaluation as we go throughout each position — making sure that our 53[=man roster] and the practice squad are exactly what we want them to look like.” Earlier in the session, O'Connell was specifically asked where 2025 starter J.J. McCarthy stands. “We're going to obviously evaluate our entire depth chart now," O'Connell said. "First and foremost, we got to cut down our football team. It's just going to be a tough couple of days and figure out our practice squad and potential additions to the roster at different positions. But we're going to work through that as a staff and see where he's at from a health standpoint, first and foremost. We don't have any long term concerns, still consider him day-to-day and see what that looks like." That's hardly a firm guarantee McCarthy will be on the roster. When asked point blank about the player's status, O'Connell didn't say he's the backup to Kyler Murray. Then, O'Connell mentioned roster cuts and the practice squad. The response opens the door to a possibility we hadn't considered: The Vikings cut McCarthy, he goes to waivers, he clears waivers (given his fully-guaranteed contract through 2027), and they offer him a spot on the practice squad. Of course, he may not take it. But if he's going to be third on the depth chart, he's not going to play. And if an opportunity emerges with another team that would get him closer to the field, he could take it. Would it be a major blow to the ego of a top-10 pick to be on the practice squad? Sure. But how much worse is that than not being the starter — and possibly being No. 3 behind Carson Wentz? Regardless, the Vikings have a decision to make. Murray is QB1. Wentz may indeed have won the backup job. What will happen with McCarthy and Max Brosmer? We'll find out by Sunday at 4:00 p.m. ET.
author: Mike Florio

title: Matt LaFleur: I fully anticipate Josh Jacobs being a member of our team
summary: Jacobs is facing charges of battery and criminal damage to property, and LaFleur said he doesn't know if Jacobs will be on the field Week One.
full_text: Packers running back Josh Jacobs is charged with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property, but head coach Matt LaFleur expects Jacobs to remain with the team. "I fully anticipate him being a member of our team," LaFleur said of Jacobs after Friday night's preseason finale. Asked about the court process with Jacobs facing charges, LaFleur said the Packers will respect that process but believe Jacobs will be part of their team. "I think you've got to let everything play out, but I anticipate him being a member of our football team," LaFleur said. Because the woman who accused Jacobs of battery was his girlfriend, the NFL may invoke its typical approach to domestic violence cases, which could include putting Jacobs on paid leave while the legal process plays out, and then suspending him six games if there is a finding against him. That could mean Jacobs missing a significant period of time, and LaFleur said he doesn't know whether Jacobs will be on the field Week One. "I can't really comment on that, because I don't know," LaFleur said.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jordan Love served as Packers' play caller for second half of preseason finale
summary: Packers third-string quarterback Kyle McCord had an excellent game in the preseason finale, throwing for four touchdown passes and leading a fourth-quarter comeback as the Packers beat the Cardinals 42-38.
full_text: Packers third-string quarterback Kyle McCord had an excellent game in the preseason finale, throwing for four touchdown passes and leading a fourth-quarter comeback as the Packers beat the Cardinals 42-38. And it was Packers first-string quarterback Jordan Love's voice in McCord's helmet during that comeback. Love was given the play calling duties by Packers head coach Matt LaFleur, who delegated the duties to offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich for the first half and surprised Love by making it his job in the second half. "Steno called the first half, did an outstanding job, and then we had J-Love call the second half," LaFleur said. "That was pretty cool, to hear his demeanor on the headset and how calm, cool and collected he was throughout the entire game, especially during those critical moments. That's what we see on the field, too." It was the first time Love had called plays, and LaFleur didn't tell him he would have the job until they were on the field before the game. "I just went up to him. It's not like he had time to prep. I was just like, 'Hey, you want to call the second half?'" LaFleur said. "He said, 'Sure. Yeah, I'll do it.' And he did it and he did an outstanding job." McCord also did an outstanding job, and might have given the Packers a tough decision for the 53-player roster. Love is the No. 1 quarterback and Tyrod Taylor is No. 2, but the Packers might have to consider keeping three quarterbacks rather than risking another team claiming McCord before Green Bay can put him on the practice squad. Love helped McCord look good.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Odell Beckham says it would mean everything to make the Giants' roster
summary: Giants head coach John Harbaugh did not say whether Beckham will make the team after the preseason finale.
full_text: '' Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. caught three passes for 53 yards in Friday night's preseason finale, and he said afterward that he hoped he had done enough to earn a roster spot. "It would mean everything," Beckham said of making the roster. "It would be my dream. This is where I started. There's no place I want to give my whole heart to, more than any place in the world, than this place right here." Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the game that Beckham had done well in training camp and the preseason, but he wouldn't say that Beckham will be on the 53-player roster after Sunday's final cutdowns. "I don't want to say exactly who's making it right now," Harbaugh. "Yes, I think he has done enough to make an NFL roster, for sure." Harbaugh was careful to say Beckham has done enough to make "an NFL roster," but not necessarily that he has made the Giants' roster. Beckham, who played for the Giants from 2014 to 2018, said he wished he had never left and would love to finish his career there. "It would be a great day," Beckham said of making the team.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tua Tagovailoa on being booed by Dolphins fans: "It is what it is"
summary: Tua says of Miami, "I love the city."
full_text: ' Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa returned to Miami on Friday night, for a preseason game. The crowd of Dolphins fans gave him an earful of boos. Did he hear it? "Well, of course I did," Tagovailoa told reporters after the game. "But, you know, needless to say, like, being able to come back here, like, I've had six years here, and those are probably some of the best six years of my life, being able to, you know, play for Miami, being able to be in front of the crowd. "You know, I mean, [I] had a Pro Bowl here, like, had a good amount of accolades. So, regardless of the reaction, like, I mean, I love the city. We have a home out here. Like, we still have our house and whatnot. But, I mean, it is what it is. You know, I can't change any of what they did and whatnot, but, you know, it was really cool to see a lot of the guys after the game, and then, you know, talk to some of the guys during the game. So it was a cool homecoming, if you will." Tua won't return to Miami during the regular season. The more immediate question is whether he'll be the quarterback when the regular season begins in 16 days with a trip to Pittsburgh — the site of his final start as the Miami quarterback.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kevin Stefanksi: Tua Tagovailoa "did a nice job" in preseason finale
summary: The Falcons still haven't named a starter for their Week 1 game at Pittsburgh, even though Michael Penix Jr. only recently received clearance to participate in team drills after his latest ACL tear.
full_text: ' The Falcons still haven't named a starter for their Week 1 game at Pittsburgh, even though Michael Penix Jr. only recently received clearance to participate in team drills after his latest ACL tear. On Friday night, Tua Tagovailoa got the start in the preseason finale at Miami. Although the assembled Dolphins fans booed him, his current head coach offered a more favorable assessment. "I thought Tua did a nice job operating," Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters after the game. "Obviously, [he] moved the football there for a couple drives, plenty to clean up. You know, unavoidable center-quarterback exchange, which we have to clean that up. And we will. But I thought, by and large, operated." The center-quarterback exchange to which Stefanski referred resulted in a fumble, which the Dolphins recovered. For the night, Tua completed seven of eight passes for 95 yards. In three first-quarter drives, he led the Falcons to a touchdown. "Tua's a pro," Stefanski said. "I thought he handled the game really well. You know, there's a lot of emotion that comes when you come back into a place that you've been before, and he compartmentalized it, and, you know, other than being on an opposite sideline, I thought he really did a nice job of handling all of it." Whether that's enough to make him the starter to start the season remains to be seen. If he's getting the assignment, he hasn't been given it yet.
author: Mike Florio

title: Polymarket withdraws wager on Patrick Mahomes playing in Week 1
summary: At a time when the scrutiny of prediction markets seems to be increasing, Polymarket has withdrawn a wager based on Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes playing in his team's Week 1 game against the Broncos.
full_text: '' At a time when the scrutiny of prediction markets seems to be increasing, Polymarket has withdrawn a wager based on Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes playing in his team's Week 1 game against the Broncos. Via David Purdum of ESPN, Polymarket self-certified the wager on Tuesday. The company withdrew it the next day . A Polymarket source told Purdum on Friday that the Commodity Futures Trading Commission asked Polymarket and other prediction market operators to remove such wagers. Polymarket did. Kalshi, as of Friday, continued to offer the wager. The NFL has objected to prediction markets based on injuries. The league told ESPN that it regards the Mahomes wager to be injury-related. NFL executive V.P. Jeff Miller also told ESPN that he hopes the CFTC will prohibit such wagers, and that the CFTC eventually will create a process pursuant to which the NFL will be asked whether such wagers are viable before they are posted. That's all the league can really do, given that it has no formal relationship with Kalshi or Polymarket. The issue of inside information hovers over wagers of this nature. Certain people will know whether Mahomes is actually planning to play. Those people can either make wagers, or they can share the information with others who will. And that continues to be one of the biggest threats to the overall integrity of all wagers placed on football, through sportsbooks or prediction markets. Certain people have access to information that the public doesn't, and that information easily can be misused.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets rookie RB Chip Trayanum transported to hospital with neck injury
summary: Jets rookie running back Chip Trayanum was injured on the final play of the first half in Friday night's preseason game against the Giants.
full_text: Jets rookie running back Chip Trayanum was injured on the final play of the first half in Friday night's preseason game against the Giants. Giants linebacker Trace Ford reached Trayanum just as quarterback Cade Klubnik handed the ball to Trayanum on the final play of the first half. Ford trucked Trayanum, who remained on the ground as medical personnel worked on him for several minutes. Many of the Jets remained on the field, taking a knee and watching with concern. Rich Cimini of ESPN reports that Trayanum appeared to be wearing a neck brace as he was strapped into the cart. Trayanum had 12 carries for 38 yards and a touchdown and caught two passes for 25 yards in the first half. The Jets report that Trayanum is headed to the hospital, but is awake, alert and has movement in his extremities. They have ruled out sixth-round rookie guard Anez Cooper (shoulder).
author: Charean Williams

title: Jets pass rusher Joseph Ossai leaves with foot injury
summary: Jets pass rusher Joseph Ossai was seeing his first preseason action Friday night.
full_text: Jets pass rusher Joseph Ossai was seeing his first preseason action Friday night. It didn't last long. Ossai injured his left foot after 11 snaps, two tackles and one pressure. The Jets list him as questionable to return. Ossai began camp on the active/physically unable to perform list. He signed with the Jets on March 12. A third-round pick of the Bengals in 2021, he has totaled 116 tackles, 44 quarterback hits and 14.5 sacks. In 2025 with the Bengals, Ossai played a career-high 616 defensive snaps and logged 71 special teams snaps.
author: Charean Williams

title: Former NFL QB Bob Lee dies at 81
summary: Former NFL quarterback Bob Lee died Aug. 17 in San Francisco, the University of Pacific announced in a news release.
full_text: Former NFL quarterback Bob Lee died Aug. 17 in San Francisco, the University of Pacific announced in a news release. Lee was 81. The Vikings selected Lee in the 17th round of the 1968 draft, and he spent most of his career in Minnesota over two stints. He played for the Falcons from 1973-74 and with the Rams from 1979-80. He won an NFL championship as a rookie with the Vikings in 1969. Lee was primarily a backup in the NFL but started 30 games, including 10 with the Falcons in 1973. He finished with a 19-11 record as a starter and appeared in 77 games. Lee threw for 5,034 yards, with 30 touchdowns and 40 interceptions. After retirement, Lee served as director of athletics at Pacific from 1991-96. He is credited with his efforts to build and expand several of Pacific's athletic facilities. Lee lettered two seasons at Pacific from 1966-67, playing both quarterback and kicker, and was named the Team MVP as a senior. He also played two seasons at Arizona State before transferring to Pacific. He is survived by his wife, Janice, his children Matt, Jenna and Zac, and six grandchildren.
author: Charean Williams

title: Dolphins fans boo Tua Tagovailoa
summary: The Dolphins don't have a big crowd tonight at Hard Rock Stadium, but they made a big noise nonetheless.
full_text: '' The Dolphins don't have a big crowd tonight at Hard Rock Stadium, but they made a big noise nonetheless. Dolphins fans let Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa have it, according to multiple reports, booing him loudly as he came onto the field as the starter Friday night. Tagovailoa spent his first six seasons in Miami after the Dolphins selected him fifth overall in 2020. He went to one Pro Bowl and played in one playoff game, ending his tenure there with 18,166 passing yards, 120 touchdowns and 59 interceptions. The Dolphins released him March 9, and he signed with the Falcons in free agency. Tagovailoa completed 3 of 4 passes for 54 yards, including a 37-yarder to Kyle Pitts on the Falcons' first drive. Atlanta scored a touchdown on Brian Robinson's 3-yard run.
author: Charean Williams

title: J.J. McCarthy won't play for Vikings in preseason finale, due to ankle injury
summary: To the extent the Vikings still have a competition for the backup quarterback spot behind Kyler Murray, J.J.
full_text: To the extent the Vikings still have a competition for the backup quarterback spot behind Kyler Murray, J.J. McCarthy won't get a chance to make a preseason closing argument. Via Kevin Seifert of ESPN, McCarthy won’t play on Friday night at Denver, due to an ankle injury suffered last Saturday against the Ravens. McCarthy participated in scaled-down practices on Monday and Tuesday. He didn't practice on Wednesday. Per Seifert, it's not considered to be a long-term injury. The situation comes two days before all rosters must be reduced to 53. Unless the Vikings plan to keep four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster, they may have to choose between McCarthy or Max Brosmer — especially if Carson Wentz cements the spot behind Murray. Brosmer could potentially clear waivers and join the practice squad. But he could, if waived, be claimed by another team. McCarthy also could be a candidate for short-term IR, which would keep him off the 53-man roster while he heals. Then there's the possibility that the Vikings will simply decide it's time to end the McCarthy experiment, either by trading him or releasing him. No one truly knows what's happening behind the scenes; if the Vikings believe the best interests of the team are served by not having McCarthy on the roster, they could become motivated to admit the mistake and move on. The fact that the Vikings have already moved on from the G.M. who drafted McCarthy makes it easier to be objective about whether it makes sense to keep him on the team. His two preseason performances did little to show that the deficiencies from last year (durability, accuracy, touch) have been resolved.
author: Mike Florio

title: Steelers waive 11 players
summary: The Steelers finished their preseason on Thursday, so they have begun the process of trimming their roster to the mandatory 53-player limit before Sunday's 6 p.m.
full_text: The Steelers finished their preseason on Thursday, so they have begun the process of trimming their roster to the mandatory 53-player limit before Sunday's 6 p.m. ET deadline. The Steelers announced the release of 11 players: TE Jaheim Bell, OL Greg Crippen, DB Jaylon Guilbeau, DB Jack Henderson, DB Brandon Hill, WR Jakobie Keeney-James, DB Tamon Lynum, DB Daryl Porter, WR Cornell Powell, RB Alex Tecza and WR Isaiah Winstead. They still have a number of decisions to make, including whether to keep four quarterbacks on their active roster. Will Howard was being evaluated for a concussion after Thursday night's game, and the results of that testing are not known yet. That could open the door to a stint on injured reserve to open the season, which would give the Steelers at least four games to evaluate whether they want to roll with four quarterbacks for the long term.
author: Charean Williams

title: Klint Kubiak open to naming Aidan O'Connell QB2, Fernando Mendoza QB3
summary: Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza might start his rookie season as a third-stringer.
full_text: '' Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza might start his rookie season as a third-stringer. Coach Klint Kubiak has not said who his starting quarterback is, but it's widely expected to be Kirk Cousins. Kubiak was asked today whether, if Cousins is the starter, Mendoza or Aidan O'Connell will be the backup. And Kubiak said that decision has not yet been made. "We've got three guys that are ready to play. It's going to be some hard decisions on who's 1, who's 2. That's not a decision we have to make today, but those are discussions that are ongoing," Kubiak said. It's not often that the first overall pick in the draft starts his career on the third team, but Kubiak seems to be in no rush to get Mendoza on the field. It appears likely that Cousins is going to start the season with Mendoza on the sideline, and Mendoza may not get on the field early in the season even if Cousins goes down.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Federal appeals court rules that states can regulate betting markets
summary: The legal odyssey regarding prediction markets vs. gambling continues.
full_text: The legal odyssey regarding prediction markets vs. gambling continues. On Friday, Kalshi stumbled onto an island full of giants wearing black robes. Via the Associated Press, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit ruled on Friday that federal commodities-trading law does not preempt Nevada’s gambling law as to the regulation of placing wagers on sports. The 3-0 ruling becomes the biggest loss to date by the prediction-market industry, and it could set the stage for the inevitable decision from the U.S. Supreme Court resolving the issue one way or the other. Especially since the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit has ruled that New Jersey cannot regulate Kalshi. A split among the various circuits often becomes a key factor in the Supreme Court's decision to take up a given issue. As noted by the AP, roughly 20 states currently are involved in litigation over the question of whether prediction markets can offer sports-related contracts independent of their gambling laws.
author: Mike Florio

title: SEC loses again in court, on effort to bar schools from signing former NFL players
summary: "[The NCAA] created this cluster, and now they've got to lay in that bed," one of the player's lawyers said.
full_text: '' The SEC now stands for "Sucks when Entering Court." The conference continues to lose rulings regarding the effort to block its member schools from adding players who were on NFL rosters. Most recently, a Louisiana judge ruled that the SEC can't issue punishments to programs that use players who had signed NFL contracts. On Wednesday, a Dallas judge issued a similar ruling . Via Dan Murphy of ESPN, the new temporary restraining order blocks the SEC from penalizing schools for welcoming back players with NFL offseason or preseason experience. The judge also signed an order requiring the SEC and NCAA to show cause as to why the rule doesn't put them in contempt of the prior ruling allowing players to return from the NFL and play. "If Sankey shows up, I'd like to hear his argument," attorney Tony Clayton said, per Murphy. "What gives him the right to anoint himself God and take these constitutional rights from these kids?" Clayton also blamed the NCAA for making the current mess. "[The NCAA] created this cluster, and now they've got to lay in that bed," Clayton said. "If this were going to happen every year, they might be on to something. But this is a one-time deal that they opened up." He's right. The situation flows from the NCAA's new five-year rule — and from an effort by players to have it applied retroactively to them. Even the loss counts as a partial win. The notion of NFL players playing college football is not popular, and the SEC, other conferences, and the NCAA obviously hope to harness that into momentum for getting the Protect College Sports Act passed.
author: Mike Florio

title: Man who posed as 49ers player is arrested for fraud
summary: The week began with news of the arrest of the 49ers' owner posing as a man named "Joe."
full_text: The week began with news of the arrest of the 49ers' owner posing as a man named "Joe." It's ending with news of the arrest of a man posing as a 49er. Via Nick Wagoner of ESPN, federal authorities have arrested two men in connection with a fraudulent scheme that entailed one of them repeatedly posing as a 49ers player. The men allegedly defrauded 26 women out of roughly $1.3 million. Daejon Love, 35, and Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, have been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud in Idaho. It allegedly started in 2022, with Love meeting multiple women on dating apps. He repeatedly told them he was a member of the 49ers or a wealthy real-estate investor. He used the names Jon Love, Avril Lyto Love and Jordan Love. Chan posed as Love's financial advisor. From the U.S. attorney's office in Boise: "Love convinced many of the victims they were in sincere romantic relationships with Love, that he was a sophisticated investor, and that Chan was his investment adviser who helped Love grow a fortune worth tens of millions of dollars. Love had romantic relationships with many of the victims and told them he wanted to build wealth and a future together. Love advertised nonexistent investment vehicles and claimed these investments would generate massive returns for both him and his victims." Some of the victims loaned Love significant amounts of money. Some took out personal loans to pay Love. When the women ran out of money or started asking too many questions, Love blocked communications with them. The FBI believes there are "many more victims" than the 26 who have been identified.
author: Mike Florio

title: Browns start slashing roster, cut 15 players from active roster
summary: The Browns have started the process of setting their initial 53-man roster.
full_text: The Browns have started the process of setting their initial 53-man roster. They announced 15 cuts from their training camp roster and one cut from injured reserve on Friday afternoon. All 32 teams need to get down to 53 players by Sunday afternoon's deadline. Four of the players were released as vested veterans. Cornerbacks Tre Avery and Tyler Hall joined offensive tackle Tyre Phillips in getting dropped from the active roster while tight end Jack Stoll was released from injured reserve. They also waived tight end Drew Biber, offensive tackle Jeremiah Byers, punter Nik Constantinou, safety Christopher Edmonds, cornerback Nate Evans, defensive tackle Coziah Izzard, defensive tackle Patrick Jenkins, cornerback Jeremiah McClendon, offensive tacke Izavion Miller, defensive end Jamil Muhammad, wide receiver Ben Patterson, and tight end Jermaine Terry. Cleveland has many more moves to make to hit the roster limit and there will likely be some immediate churning as other players shake free around the league in the coming days.
author: Josh Alper

title: Seahawks new owner Vinod Khosla defends still being a fan of this AFC team
summary: The two teams play each other in 2027
full_text:
Vinod Khosla's introductory press conference as the Seattle Seahawks ' new owner included him admitting that he is a fan of another NFL team.
"I happened to come to this country in '76 when the Steelers were winning the Super Bowl ," Khosla said . "So actually, I was originally and still am a big Steelers fan. Also, a little-known fact, but I still watch all the Steelers games too."
As you can imagine, those comments led to some criticism. How can an NFL owner openly cheer for another team? And if they do, why would they openly admit that? It's something that you typically don't hear from a sports owner, especially during their introductory press conference.
Making Khosla's comments even more odd/interesting is the fact that the Seahawks lost to the Steelers in a Super Bowl that included several controversial penalties that came at Seattle's expense. Seahawks fans are still salty about how their team lost their first-ever Super Bowl.
Khosla clearly heard some of the criticism, and he decided to address it on Friday via X.
"Reporters will make every molehill into a mountain just to get column inches to write or video minutes. What's wrong with admitting my 1976-78 period in Pittsburgh (CMU) got me excited  about the NFL? I still watch their games doesn't  mean I won't unconditionally ALWAYS as owner, want the Seahawks to win and have every edge up, EVERY TIME over every other team!!!! Zero questions!!! At the other end is a set of teams I always want to lose every advantage. But happy to have the sportswriter getting more column inches  and fill their pages. You are welcome. Apologies in advance for my very transparent style."
Khosla's initial adoption of the Steelers as his NFL team makes sense and is one of the reasons why Pittsburgh has one of the biggest fan bases in sports.
While it started with the 1958 NFL Championship Game (the first NFL game that went to overtime), the transitiion from baseball to football as America's most popular sport took place in the 1970s, when the Steelers fielded arguably the most talented team pro football has ever seen. Boasting a roster that featured 10 future Hall of Famers, the Steelers won four Super Bowls over a six-year span.
In 1976 -- the year Khosla alluded to -- the Steelers defeated the Cowboys in what was at the time the most exciting and most watched Super Bowl ever. Pittsburgh's 21-17 win over Dallas was its second of four Super Bowl wins during the decade.
Many people who were first discovering pro football at that time -- and didn't have a rooting interest to that point -- adopted the either the Cowboys or Steelers as their team, Khosla included.
The winning score of Super Bowl X, this date in 1976 With just over three minutes remaining, #Steelers QB Terry Bradshaw stands his ground — getting absolutely starched by the #Cowboys ' Larry Cole in the process — to fire a 64-yard TD dime to game MVP Lynn Swann for a 21-10 lead pic.twitter.com/xPONFlYLpS
Rest assured that Khosla will be asked about his Steelers fandom again in 2027, as Seattle is slated to face Pittsburgh that season.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Raiders' Klint Kubiak still won't name Week 1 QB starter, here's why all signs point to Kirk Cousins
summary: Kubiak has said it's Cousins' job to lose, but won't officially name a QB1
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are making us wait a bit longer to find out who the starting quarterback will be, as the competition between veteran Kirk Cousins and rookie first overall pick Fernando Mendoza comes to a close. Head coach Kirk Kubiak has been adamant about waiting to name his QB1, though many signs have pointed to Cousins as their guy. With just over two weeks until the team's opener against the Miami Dolphins , the mystery remains, but the hints are there.
Following the team's final preseason game, Kubiak said his No. 1 overall pick could benefit from a few more preseason games, but unfortunately for Mendoza, that's not something he has. The NFL now only holds three preseason games per team, meaning the players, especially the rookies, have less time to prove themselves and get those valuable in-game reps.
"[Mendoza] needs another three preseason games, all those rookies do. Now that the season's starting the practice reps get smaller and that's just life," Kubiak said after the Raiders' 18-12 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday. "Us as coaches we gotta get them ready to play, keep developing them."
The HC noted that this time in the preseason is beneficial not only for the rookie to learn from his own reps but also for him to learn from Cousins. Kubiak called the time "very valuable" for Mendoza.
"I'd love to play [Mendoza] the whole game but there's other guys we want to get looked at and I thought overall this preseason that we got him plenty of time," Kubiak said.
Both played in Thursday's game, with Cousins taking the first two drives and Mendoza taking over until the beginning of the fourth quarter, when he was swapped for Aidan O'Connell .
The 38-year-old went 8 of 11 with 51 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions, while Mendoza went 7 of 14 with 57 yards, no touchdowns, an interception and two sacks, producing a low passer rating. It was not as strong as his debut, where Mendoza went 10 of 16 with 97 yards, one touchdown and one sack against the Arizona Cardinals .
Cousins began training camp as the starting quarterback and has been listed first on the depth chart throughout the practices. He's led the first-team offense through training camp and has seemed to have the edge in the competition since the beginning. When Cousins has struggled, Mendoza hasn't been able to outplay him when his chances come. Despite some great moments in camp, Mendoza had some lowlights as well, including a pick-six during joint practice with the Texans.
At the start of preseason, Kubiak said Cousins was in charge of his own fate , noting, "Kirk's been getting the reps with the ones. I think he's had a solid training camp, and it's his job to lose."
He referred to Cousins as the starter on Day 1, on July 28, but hasn't mentioned it again since then.
"When we go out to practice tomorrow, Kirk Cousins is the starting quarterback," Kubiak said at the time. "He's the guy, and he's going to get a ton of reps. He deserves them because he's played really good football. But I want Fernando and I want Aidan (O'Connell) to push him."
Looking at his preseason numbers compared to Mendoza, Cousins hasn't struggled enough to hand the rookie the job, and the No. 1 pick hasn't excelled enough to make an obvious leap ahead.
Here's a look at how Cousins and Mendoza have compared in their three preseason games:
The Raiders begin the season at home on Sept. 13 and will head just up the road to Los Angeles in Week 2 to take on the Chargers .
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Start, Bench, Cut: If Steelers don't roster 4 QBs, who's the odd man out?
summary: A hypothetical look at Pittsburgh's QB quandary
full_text:
If you take Mike McCarthy at his word, it appears the Steelers ' initial 53-man roster will indeed include each of the team's four quarterbacks.
McCarthy again alluded to that likelihood following Pittsburgh's preseason finale on Thursday, a 28-27 loss in Buffalo that saw second-year quarterback Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar take the entirety of the snaps. Howard, who started the game and played the entire first half, went 9 of 15 for 69 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. Allar, who played the entire second half, went 9 of 18 for 88 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions.
"I feel good about the quarterback room," McCarthy said . "I've been saying it for quite some time, and they've showed it on the field. We've got two veterans that we can win with, and we've got two young guys that we're really excited about their future."
While it appears that keeping all four quarterbacks is the plan, nothing is set in stone until Pittsburgh is required to finalize its initial 53-man roster. If the Steelers decide to change course between now and Sunday night, here's a hypothetical rundown of which quarterback they should start, bench, and cut/trade.
This was a pretty easy choice, but is it the right one? It depends on how you view the Steelers' prospects for the 2026 season. Most oddsmakers have set their Over/Under at 8.5 wins, which once again puts Pittsburgh on the cusp of making the playoffs.
It's the classic glass half full/half empty metaphor. The Steelers have gone 10-7 with a wild card playoff loss each of the last three years. One logic is that Rodgers' return gives a relatively talented roster another run at ending the franchise's nine-year drought without a playoff win. The other is that Pittsburgh should prioritize finding its next franchise quarterback even if that means jeopardizing the franchise's record of 22 consecutive non-losing seasons.
The Steelers are clear believers in trying to contend for a title every year, which is why Rodgers is back for a second and final season with the black and gold. Rodgers, even at the advanced age of 42, probably gives the Steelers the best chance at winning a playoff game and perhaps more than that.
There are clear limits to being a 42-year-old quarterback. Rodgers can't move like he used to, and he clearly isn't a fan of subjecting himself to big hits, which can lead to hurried throws and questionable decisions .
Rodgers' deficiencies, however, pale in comparison to what he still brings to the table. He's armed with an elite football IQ, a legendary throwing touch and enough mobility to still get the job done. Rodgers also hasn't lost his fierce competitive drive.
Rodgers put up solid numbers last year despite having a subpar receiving corps. He should be even better this year after the Steelers added several playmakers this offseason in Michael Pittman , Rico Dowdle and rookie Germie Bernard , among others.
Pittsburgh's offensive line will largely determine the success of Rodgers and ultimately the rest of the team in 2026. While the unit is promising on paper, the Steelers' line didn't have the best summer from a performance standpoint. Pittsburgh's line needs to be good enough to not only protect Rodgers, but to also orchestrate a running game that can take some of the pressure off of him.
Again, this comes down to what you prioritize. If you prioritize having a proven veteran backup in the bullen, Rudolph is the easy pick. If you'd rather go all in on the young quarterbacks, Allar and Howard are the move.
As previously established, the Steelers plan on contending this (and every) season, which is why Rudolph will more likely than not be Pittsburgh's No. 2 quarterback. Beyond that, Rudolph's performance this summer also merits a spot on the 53-man roster. Rudolph's name was the first one McCarthy mentioned when he was recently asked which players have made the biggest impression on him.
" Mason Rudolph , just I can't I can't tell you how pleased I am with him," McCarthy said. "The experience that he's gained, I think, is incredibly valuable to us."
Regarding Allar, Pittsburgh's fourth-round pick has been largely impressive this summer. He parlayed his strong start to training camp with a sensational NFL debut during Pittsburgh's preseason opener. Any chance of Allar being the No. 2 quarterback, however, ended when he was unable to duplicate that performance during Pittsburgh's last two preseason games.
Allar wasn't great in those games, but neither was Howard, who started both contests. The consensus entering the preseason was that Allar was probably ahead of Howard on the hypothetical depth chart, and that continues to be the case.
Most Steelers fans feel that Allar is the team's future at the quarterback position. While that remains to be seen, Allar will likely get his chance to earn that opportunity after spending his rookie season as the team's No. 3 quarterback. That includes getting a chance to watch one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time up close during his farewell season.
If there is a scenario where the Steelers cut ties with a quarterback, Howard would likely be the odd man out.
Like most young quarterbacks, Howard is talented but raw in terms of competing at the highest level. He has a strong arm, is a tireless worker and a natural leader. There is room for improvement in terms of his play speed and his decision-making.
Howard's preseason was a mixed bag of results. While he was much more accurate than Allar, he also threw more touchdowns than interceptions, was sacked more often and had a lower passer rating.
In Pittsburgh's perfect world, it could stash Howard on the practice squad. The reality, however, is that Howard would likely get cliamed by another team before the Steelers could do that. That's why the Steelers would likely try to trade Howard before they would ever release him.
The Steelers would only trade or release Howard if they are certain that he isn't in their future plans at quarterback, which doesn't appaer to be the case. And because Howard likley wouldn't fetch more than a sixth- or seventh-round pick, the odds the Steelers actually trading him are slim to none.
This brings us back to McCarthy's quotes about the likiless of him keeping four quarterbacks. McCarthy is not only thinking about 2026, but 2027 and beyond that. By keeping all four, McCarthy will put himself in position to maximize this season's potential and starting the post-Rodgers era next season with two young quarterbacks under contract.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Predicting NFL All-Pros at every defensive position: Young Browns, Seahawks stars among those to watch in 2026
summary: Jared Verse, Byron Murphy II lead a crop of rising defensive stars poised to make the leap to first-team honors this season
full_text:
Aside from Player of the Year and other individual honors, the All-Pro list is the highest form of recognition NFL players receive annually. There were 12 first-time All-Pros on the defensive side of the ball last year, including all four linebacker selections. Who are some of the candidates to earn All-Pro status for the first time this season? CBS Sports provides one name, and some others to consider, at each position.
Verse had the sixth-most pressures (80) last season. He relies supremely on his bull rush, but could take his game to another level if he is able to craft more hand-fighting moves to counter. Los Angeles had multiple players capable of pushing the pocket and Verse went under the radar because so much of the pass-rush production was attributed to the collective. In a new setting, can he start to change that narrative?
Over the past five years, nine of the 14 edge rushers selected to the first- or second-team All-Pro teams were taken in the first round. Verse was the 19th overall selection in the 2024 NFL Draft .
Abdul Carter of the Giants is one to monitor as being capable of ascending to this tier. Jacksonville's Josh Hines-Allen finished with the second-most pressures (95) and the sixth-highest pressure rate (18.2%) last season, but is 29 years old and voters have obviously been hesitant to place that label on him. Jaelan Phillips ( Panthers ) and Tuli Tuipulotu ( Chargers ) are a few others to add to the conversation.
Murphy has been willing to do the dirty work in Seattle's defense to free up an arsenal of edge rushers. He still amassed his own personal achievements, however. The Seattle lineman ranked No. 19 in pressures (50) among players with 200+-pass-rush snaps in 2025, according to TruMedia. He registered seven sacks, which were eighth-most among interior defenders.
Derrick Brown (Panthers) and Jordan Davis ( Eagles ) were a few other considerations, but nose tackles traditionally are not represented unless it is Dexter Lawrence , who averaged six sacks when he was on the list in 2022-2023. New England's Milton Williams was the primary contender to Murphy.
Seven of the 11 defensive tackles named first- or second-team All-Pro over the past five years were former first-round picks. Murphy was the No. 16 overall selection in the 2024 NFL Draft.
Linebacker is perhaps the greatest example of box score scouting not necessarily translating to on-field performance. Through the years, there have been several high-volume tacklers who were getting driven out of the box and making plays in the second and third level of the defense. Where the play is being made is important. Schwesinger had 11 tackles for a loss last season, which was fourth-best among off-ball linebackers; behind the Vikings ' Eric Wilson (17), Dolphins ' Jordyn Brooks (13) and Raiders ' Devin White (11). Wilson plays in an aggressive scheme, Brooks has already been named an All-Pro and White is joining a new team. Schwesinger has great range and is comfortable making plays in space.
Linebacker is one of two positions -- safety being the other -- where the number of non-first picks to be named All-Pro is larger than the alternative. Schwesinger was a second-round pick named Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2025.
Cornerback is easily the most difficult position to project, because results are volatile year-over-year and the usual suspects have already attained that status.
Horn is somehow only 26 years old despite being on the cusp of his sixth NFL season. He was limited to 22 games over the first three years of his career, but has missed just three games over the past two seasons. Carolina rewarded him with a contract extension in March of 25 before he picked off five passes. An improved defensive front, with edge rusher Jaelan Phillips, should give Horn even more chances to create turnovers in 2026.
Cleveland's Denzel Ward has not been named an All-Pro, but it is a little late in his career to expect that to change. Joey Porter Jr . may have been a consideration had he not missed a lot of time during training camp. Baltimore's Nate Wiggins is a profile worthy of the topic, but availability has been an issue. Jacksonville's Travis Hunter and Cincinnati's DJ Turner were a few sleepers.
There are several young, up-and-coming players who will be a part of the conversation in the next few years, but Emmanwori played an impactful role on a Super Bowl -winning defense. The South Carolina product essentially missed four games recovering from an injury, so the hope is that he is able to play a full season with a boosted resume. The chaos created by Mike Macdonald's front should create opportunities for Emmanwori and others on the back end.
At 6-foot-3-inches, Emmanwori is able to use his length to muddy pass windows and cover a lot of ground.
Ten of 13 All-Pro safeties over the past five years were top 100 overall draft picks. A torn Achilles in 2025 cost Detroit's Brian Branch a position on the list.
author: Josh Edwards

summary: Find best bets and props for the biggest games in sports on Friday from the SportsLine Projection Model and top CBS Sports experts

title: Christian Gonzalez landing spots: Cowboys, Giants among trade candidates as Patriots CB seeks record contract
summary: Gonzalez and the Patriots are reportedly not close to striking a long-term deal
full_text:
Christian Gonzalez easily stands among the most talented cornerbacks in the NFL . As he graduates from his rookie contract to his first megadeal, he ought to be compensated as such. The New England Patriots have been outward in their willingness to pay a premium to keep Gonzalez around for the long term, but according to ESPN , the sides are not close to an agreement.
Patriots owner Robert Kraft said at the start of training camp that the team offered Gonzalez a contract that would make him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. That, however, was before Seattle Seahawks star Devon Witherspoon reset the market with a four-year, $132 million extension. That deal raised the bar for Gonzalez and appears to have raised it too high for the Patriots.
"I don't think that at any one point here that they have been close to a deal," ESPN's Adam Schefter said on "The Pat McAfee Show." "Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez have the same agent, so in a way, he can kind of dictate how this is going to go and see into the future in a better way than each of the two teams can. Witherspoon was going to get done first, and it got done at an average of $33 million a year. The Patriots have not been in that category. Witherspoon has established the benchmark, and the Patriots haven't gone there. They weren't there before, and they don't appear to be going there right now."
To be clear, there is no immediate deadline for this deal to get across the finish line. The Patriots picked up Gonzalez's fifth-year option for 2027, and he has not threatened to hold in during training camp or sit out of regular-season games.
In a now deleted tweet reacting to the Adam Schefter news saying the Patriots and Gonzo aren’t close to a deal, Christian Gonzalez trainer says the Patriots should just trade him. He is saying what the Patriots have been behind the scenes. There is a lot more to this story. pic.twitter.com/uXcIKVD4me
Anytime a team struggles to find an acceptable number for a star player, though, the negotiations come with the risk of blowing up . The Micah Parsons saga last summer proved how teams can ultimately lose the best players on their rosters if they are unwilling to pay a premium.
"I have conversations with Christian, and I understand that this is probably something that's difficult," Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said, via Patriots wire . "I've never been in that position to this extent. Try to treat it with class, but he and I communicate, and our players are always free to feel how they feel. They just have to stay patient and just hope that we can work to some kind of agreement."
The Patriots could do what the Dallas Cowboys did in 2025 and trade their defensive asset, but for a team squarely in its contention window (and with a reigning MVP runner-up quarterback on his rookie contract, no less), parting with a player of Gonzalez's caliber over a contract dispute would be an extreme move. That does not mean it will not happen, though, so here are a few potential landing spots should Gonzalez be moved out of New England.
Jerry Jones has been hinting for a while that he'd be interested in making another big move, even if in the past 12 months he's already made plenty: trading away Micah Parsons, trading for Quinnen Williams and moving up to draft Caleb Downs . When the Cowboys opened training camp, he said he'd be "very interested" to "give up the future to substitute where we are today."
Dallas has made a concerted effort to improve its secondary, not just with Downs, but with free agents Jalen Thompson and Cobie Durant. But after a woeful 2025, a player like Gonzalez would take this secondary to an entirely different level -- not only a No. 1 cornerback, but a superstar one. Gonzalez is in the upper tier at a position the Cowboys look middling at best. He's a big name. Maybe Jones pulls off the reverse Parsons, acquiring a disgruntled star in his prime and paying him, rather than trading one away.
As recently as this summer, the Lions had to have felt great about the state of their cornerback group. Terrion Arnold's arrest, release from the roster and plans to sign with the Seahawks flipped the unit on its head. All of a sudden, D.J. Reed is thrust into the No. 1 job, and the depth behind him is questionable. That is not to mention the injury woes that continue to plague the rest of the defensive backfield.
Bringing in Gonzalez to not only fill Arnold's shoes but also potentially provide an upgrade over his production would be a home-run move for a team that needs to make strides defensively in order to get back to the playoffs. Signing him to a long-term deal would limit the Lions' flexibility at other positions, but they can afford it so long as it does not go into effect until next year.
Commanders fans have looked at Gonzalez and wondered "what if?" ever since the 2023 NFL Draft . Washington took Emmanuel Forbes 16th overall, one pick before Gonzalez went to New England. Forbes didn't even last two seasons before being cut.
Washington went on a spending spree this offseason on defense, but is still set up to have a relatively open checkbook in the future, even with a potential Jayden Daniels extension. Adam Peters has pulled off big trades for Marshon Lattimore (which didn't work out) and Laremy Tunsil (who played excellently last year but tore his triceps in training camp this year). Might he have another big move up his sleeve?
For the "buyer beware" idea, Gonzalez is much younger than either Lattimore or Tunsil was when they were acquired; he's an ascending superstar, having just turned 24. The Commanders have gotten younger, faster and more athletic all offseason, and this would continue that trend. Trey Amos has missed almost all of training camp, and the rest of the group has been inconsistent. It's a win-now year for Dan Quinn and, if it's a bad year, Peters would be under a microscope, too. Washington never should have let Gonzalez slip past them. This regime could right the old one's wrong.
A young and inexpensive core gives the Giants all the flexibility they need to not only acquire Gonzalez now but also make him the highest-paid cornerback in league history. To place a cornerback entering his prime on the same defense as recent first-round picks Arvell Reese and Abdul Carter would set that unit up to flourish as a talent-rich operation for years to come.
The Giants can easily move on from Greg Newsome II after signing him to a one-year, $8 million deal, which would clear a lane for Gonzalez to form a tandem with Paulson Adebo , who remains under contract for the next three seasons.
The young pieces are starting to fall into place with the aforementioned defenders plus Jaxson Dart , Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo . Any established stars New York can pair them with would be welcome additions that could help fast-track the team's rise to contention.
Gonzalez isn't the only cornerback at a frustrating impasse with his team. In Pittsburgh, Joey Porter Jr . and the Steelers are at odds. Porter is technically still on the PUP list, but really, it's a hold in regarding his contract. As such, the Steelers might be able to offer New England something other teams could not: a good young player at the same position Gonzalez plays.
This, of course, would be contingent on the Patriots presenting a financial solution to Porter and the Steelers doing the same for Gonzalez. Maybe dealing with Gonzalez within the AFC is a non-starter for New England anyway. But the Steelers are giving it one more go with Aaron Rodgers , and there's a very good defense opposite him. It could go from very good to elite with Gonzalez.

title: One team's healthy scratch is another's treasure: Making sense of why Patriots traded Kayshon Boutte to Texans
summary: Boutte led all Patriots wide receivers in touchdowns last year, but didn't fit into New England's plans this season
full_text:
The New England Patriots traded wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a future seventh-round draft pick this week. The move made sense, as Boutte had been the subject of trade rumors this offseason given the upgrades New England made at the position, while the Texans just saw second-year pass-catcher Jayden Higgins go down with a torn ACL.
What didn't make sense about this deal, however, was the compensation. CBS Sports' Bryan DeArdo said the Texans easily won this trade , grading it as an "A" for Houston and much worse for the Patriots.
Boutte is a solid player. He caught 33 passes for 551 yards and a career-high six touchdowns in 2025, and his 16.7 yards per reception ranked fourth in the NFL . Boutte even caught three passes for 75 yards and a touchdown in the divisional-round victory against the Texans on the way to Super Bowl LX.
Despite Boutte's 2025 campaign, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters following New England's final preseason game against the Browns that Boutte was on track to be a healthy scratch on game days.
"That was the one place where we do have some depth," Vrabel said, via MassLive . "I think for all parties involved, that was probably the best thing. Without injuries Kayshon probably would have been inactive, unfortunately. That's just kind of the way it was with him not playing special teams. I tried to thank Kayshon as many times as I could. I texted him again today.
"His maturity, his growth, his ability to put into words last year and share his own personal struggle , but also the growth that he made from that. That's positively going to affect a lot of people. I know that wasn't easy for him to do and I tell him all the time how much I respect him for being able to do that."
No one thought Boutte would lead the Patriots in receiving this year, but it's pretty interesting to hear that the player who ranked second on the team among wide receivers in yards last season would have likely been a  healthy scratch multiple times this year.
Looking at the Patriots' official depth chart, it's obvious that Boutte would have been listed behind trade-acquisition A.J. Brown and free-agency addition Romeo Doubs. "Pop Douglas" received the same amount of targets in the passing game as Boutte in three more games played last year, but New England has him listed as a starter.
Perhaps the main takeaway with the Boutte trade is that Kyle Williams is going to play a legitimate role in the offense this year.
The former third-round pick caught just 10 passes for 209 yards and three touchdowns as a rookie, but he's been a preseason standout for New England. In the first exhibition game, Williams caught two passes for 37 yards and a touchdown. In the second, he caught two passes for 74 yards and another score. On Thursday in Cleveland, Williams completed the hat trick with two receptions for 55 yards and his third touchdown.
Williams has shown the ability to be a deep-ball threat and is due for more looks in his second NFL season.
. @tommydevito007 to @k_mmoneyyyy DIME 🎯 📺: Prime Video pic.twitter.com/wtuNHzpYIa
One team's healthy inactive is another team's treasure. On paper, the Texans had one of the best wide receiving corps in the NFL with Nico Collins , Jayden Higgins, Xavier Hutchinson , Tank Dell , Justin Watson and Jaylin Noel .
However, Higgins tore his ACL while Dell is not as far along in his recovery from a serious leg injury as previously thought. Longtime reporter John McClain said this week that Dell is " nowhere ready to play ."
With Houston down two of its top-five guys, general manager Nick Caserio went out and acquired an ascending talent for pennies. It remains to be seen if Boutte's long-term home is in Houston, as he's set to enter the final year of his rookie deal, but he will have the opportunity to contribute immediately for C.J. Stroud .
