title: The Ja'Kobi Lane hype is real: Ravens rookie could quickly become Lamar Jackson's WR2
summary: The mid-round rookie has already earned a starting role in three-receiver sets, and uncertainty surrounding Rashod Bateman could create an even bigger opportunity
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Ja'Kobi Lane has been one of the biggest stars of training camp league-wide and the biggest star of Baltimore Ravens camp. That continued Wednesday during Baltimore's joint practice with the Washington Commanders.
The 6-foot-4, 200-pound rookie out of USC looks the part. He can win 50-50 balls, make spectacular catches outside his frame and provide the type of size-skill combination Baltimore has long sought for Lamar Jackson . Just as importantly, Lane isn't only making plays against backups. He is earning extensive work with the first-team offense.
Still, I left Wednesday's practice with one question: How seriously should we take Lane's rapid rise?
So I asked CBS Sports NFL reporter Matt Zenitz, who said the Ravens' enthusiasm surrounding Lane is very real. Within the first week of training camp, a Baltimore source told Zenitz that Lane was already a starter in 11 personnel and the team's No. 3 receiver alongside Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman .
"They're obviously very enthusiastic about what they've seen from him so far, and he's clearly had a great offseason," Zenitz said.
There was one important caveat from a team source: "It is camp. We'll see what he does when the season starts."
That is a fair warning. Every August produces a breakout star or two whose regular-season role never matches the training camp hype. Lane hasn't taken an NFL snap that counts, and Bateman remains ahead of him in Baltimore's pecking order.
That was evident Wednesday, too. With Flowers sidelined, Bateman had a big day. He beat Commanders cornerback Amik Robertson twice during one-on-one drills and added several catches in team periods. Bateman hasn't lived up to his first-round billing through five NFL seasons, but he remains a talented player who could benefit from Baltimore's new offense -- and perhaps from the added competition created by drafting Lane (No. 80 overall) and Elijah Sarratt (No. 115 overall).
"I would definitely say I could benefit from the situation that I'm in," Bateman said last week.
So no, Lane is not Baltimore's No. 2 receiver right now. But there is a plausible scenario in which the Ravens need him to become one.
Bateman was arrested in June in Georgia and faces charges of family violence battery , reckless conduct and first-degree criminal damage to property stemming from an alleged incident involving the mother of his child. According to court records obtained by ESPN, police alleged Bateman damaged a vehicle carrying the woman and their 3-month-old daughter and that the woman sustained injuries during the incident.
Bateman's attorney, Jordan Siev, said the family situation had been "taken completely out of context" and that the facts would emerge through the court process. The case remains pending.
The Ravens said they have been in direct communication with Bateman, notified the NFL and are cooperating with the league. Coach Jesse Minter declined to comment beyond the team's statement.
In addition to the court proceedings, Bateman could face discipline under the NFL's personal conduct policy. The league's baseline discipline for a first offense involving assault, battery, domestic violence or sexual assault is a six-game suspension, although the circumstances and eventual findings of each case can affect the outcome.
That uncertainty matters when evaluating Lane's potential role -- both for the Ravens and for fantasy managers.
Baltimore has spent much of Jackson's career searching for consistent outside receiving help. Flowers has emerged as a legitimate top option, but the depth behind him remains largely unproven. Flowers was the only Ravens wide receiver last season to record more than 22 receptions or 330 receiving yards.
Lane, a third-round pick, is currently positioned as the third receiver in an offense that will still flow through Jackson, Flowers and a deep group of tight ends and running backs. That may make it difficult for him to command a significant target share immediately.
But the Ravens clearly believe he can play. He is already working with the starters, already making difficult catches and already giving Baltimore an element it has often lacked on the outside. If Bateman misses time -- whether because of injury, league discipline or another reason -- Lane may not have the luxury of easing into the NFL as a complementary rookie.

title: Rare change: Why the NFL's 2026 cut deadline is being held on a Sunday for the first time in 22 years
summary: The league shifted the 53-man roster deadline to Sunday for the first time since 2004 to accommodate the 49ers and Rams traveling to Australia for their Week 1 matchup
full_text:
It is going to be a busy weekend in the NFL. Not only is it the final weekend of preseason play, but all 32 teams are going to have to make their final cuts, and they're going to have to make those moves by Sunday at 6 p.m. ET when the cut deadline hits.
By the time that rolls around, a total of 1,184 players will have been released. During the preseason, NFL teams are allowed to carry 90 players on their roster, but every team must reduce that number to 53 by the deadline.
The NFL's 32 teams usually get a small breather between their final preseason game and the cut deadline, but that won't be happening this year. Back in May, the league announced that the cut deadline would he happening on Sunday, Aug. 30, which is mostly notable because cut day almost never happens on a Sunday.
As a matter of fact, this will mark the first time in 22 years that the NFL cut deadline has been held on a Sunday. Over the past four years (2021-25), the deadline was set for the first Tuesday after the final preseason weekend. From 2005 through 2020, cut day was always held on the Saturday before Labor Day, except in 2012, when it was held on the Friday before Labor Day.
The last time it was held on a Sunday came all the way back in 2004.
When the NFL makes a big change, there's always a reason for it, and we have no exception here. It was pretty clear that a change was likely after the owners voted to amend a by-law at the NFL's annual spring meeting in March. The policy change flew under the radar, but it's certainly worth noting now.
The new by-law permits "the League office to adjust the procedures and related dates and deadlines for the final roster reduction to accommodate an international game scheduled in the first week of the regular season."
In layman's terms, this means that if there's an international game in Week 1, the league office is allowed to change the date for final cuts, and that's exactly what's happening this year.
With the 49ers and Rams playing in Australia in Week 1, there was no way the NFL could stick to its normal schedule, with cut day falling on the first Tuesday after the final preseason weekend, which would have been Sept. 1 this year. If that had been the deadline, waiver claims would have been due on Sept. 2 and that would have created an issue because the 49ers are flying to Melbourne on Sept. 2 . It wouldn't have been fair to ask them to fill out their practice squad, make waiver claims and potentially sign free agents while they're on a 14-hour flight to Australia, so the NFL decided to move the cut deadline to Aug. 30.
Going forward, it won't be surprising if the NFL moves cut day back to the Tuesday deadline, but if there is an international game in Week 1, the league has given itself some leeway to change the date for final cuts if that's what needs to be done.
Although the NFL is moving the deadline for final cuts to accommodate teams traveling to Australia, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan still isn't thrilled that his team will essentially miss out on several rest days due to their travel schedule.
"Everyone gets that bye week after your fourth week [of preseason]," Shanahan said back in May . "The whole NFL gets three bonus practices and four mandatory days off. We're traveling on that third day to Australia, so you kind of miss that week to recover and to have those days off and those bonus days. So, it ends up being about a week different than usual."
The 49ers are dealing with more injuries than almost any other team, so they could certainly have used the extra rest days, but now, they won't be getting them. If the 49ers sign anyone to their active roster after Sept. 2, that player will have to get to Australia, which adds another interesting twist to cut day. As for the Rams, they're planning to fly Down Under just one day before the game, so they won't be in such a rush next week when it comes to potentially signing any free agents.
author: John Breech

title: Ranking every NFL team's WR room: Cowboys and Bengals battle for top spot; Chiefs not helping Patrick Mahomes
summary: Good luck to opposing defenses trying to stop Dallas and Cincinnati this season
full_text:
Even in an NFL where the run game has been resurgent in recent seasons, the passing game is still king. After all, the reason we've seen teams lean more into the run of late is because defenses have prioritized taking away explosive passes. They are more content to let offenses try to beat them with the body blows of a series of runs, betting they can't do it without making mistakes before they reach the end zone.
Because the NFL is still a passing league, wide receivers have never been more important. We've seen evidence of that in recent offseasons, as the financial market for wideouts has exploded and now tops $40 million per year.
Of course, you can't just get away with having one good wide receiver. You need to build a receiver room that can threaten defenses in a variety of ways -- at least, if you want to have a really good offense.
And with that in mind, we set out to rank the league's receiver rooms from worst to best:
This one is fairly obvious. After moving on from Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , the Dolphins have the most barren wide receiver room in the league. There are hopes for rookies Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell , the latter of whom is coming off a major injury, but there's nothing we can count on here.
The Raiders are lucky the Dolphins exist. The top options in this room are Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor , along with potentially Jack Bech and rookie Malik Benson . It's not an inspiring group.
This might be too low for the Browns, but with such an unproven room, it was hard to push them any higher. KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston could make this ranking look silly if they get off to fast starts to their respective careers.
With Rashee Rice still looking hobbled after rehabbing his knee injury in jail and Xavier Worthy again banged up in camp, the Chiefs might be counting on training-camp star Cyrus Allen to be a real factor, rather than a mere curiosity. That's a dangerous game to play.
Tennessee had arguably the worst receiver room in the NFL last season and upgraded with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson , but the depth is still questionable. Thirty-two-year-old Calvin Ridley is looking like the No. 3, while Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike are up next. There doesn't appear to be a true game-changing talent among the group.
If Alec Pierce were definitively healthy rather than merely working his way back from offseason ankle surgery -- and therefore in question for Week 1 and perhaps beyond -- the Colts would probably rank higher. He's a good player, as is Josh Downs . But the depth beyond them, even with Keenan Allen in the fold, is still questionable.
The Bills brought in DJ Moore to be their No. 1 wideout this year. He took a step back last season in Chicago and is now trying to recapture the form he had a few years ago. Khalil Shakir is a slot slot/gadget option. But the room beyond those players ( Josh Palmer , Keon Coleman , Skyler Bell ) is uninspiring.
If Jordyn Tyson were healthy, the Saints would definitely rank higher, especially given how good Tyson looked during training camp. As is, though, you have to knock New Orleans because outside of Chris Olave , there is nobody on the depth chart that really scares you -- even if DeVaughn Vele had a solid stretch to end last season.
Malik Nabers is working his way back from a serious knee injury. He seems on his way to full health, but we obviously can't know for sure until we see him on the field. Beyond him, the depth chart looks like it's clearing out for rookie Malachi Fields , because Darius Slayton and Darnell Mooney are role players and Calvin Austin III just tore up his knee.
Garrett Wilson is awesome. Adonai Mitchell is somewhat tantalizing. Omar Cooper Jr . is apparently working his way up the depth chart after seeming like he may have been behind return specialist Isaiah Williams early in the preseason. If Mitchell taps into his talent and Cooper hits the ground running, the Jets could be better than expected.
Terry McLaurin is a baller and Stefon Diggs is reliable, but the depth chart after those two is filled with question marks like Treylon Burks , Van Jefferson and rookie slot man Antonio Williams .
Tetairoa McMillan showed his immense potential as a rookie despite questionable quarterback play. Jalen Coker is solid, too, and earned himself a contract extension after working his way up the depth chart as a former undrafted free agent. This is another group with questionable depth beyond the top two, though, especially after Chris Brazzell II's injury.
If the Falcons had anybody we could remotely rely on behind the fantastic Drake London , they'd rank higher than this. Perhaps rookie Zachariah Branch blossoms early and becomes that guy. But Olamide Zaccheaus and Jahan Dotson aren't our idea of reliable options.
Nico Collins is an elite No. 1 receiver. The Texans took a blow with Jayden Higgins ' season-ending torn ACL, but rebounded nicely by trading for Kayshon Boutte . We don't know Tank Dell's health status (reports don't sound great, to be honest) and Jaylin Noel has been in and out of camp with injuries, so it's hard to get excited about the down-the-depth-chart options.
Zay Flowers is an underrated player, even after his big payday. Rashod Bateman has always excelled on a per-route basis, even if the volume hasn't always been there. The Ravens probably need camp star Ja'Kobi Lane to turn into a real factor in order to rise higher than this because Devontez Walker hasn't been one yet and there doesn't seem to be much buzz around Elijah Sarratt .
Michael Wilson essentially turned into Randy Moss down the stretch of last season, though some of the volume he sucked up obviously came as a result of Marvin Harrison Jr . being out with an injury. Still, he flashed high-level talent, and we're betting that Harrison can bounce back from his down second season because the long view of his talent is still strong and the offense should better suit his skill set.
The Bears have a pair of exciting receivers in Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze . Burden had unbelievably good per-route efficiency last year but didn't play a full-time role. Odunze started hot but cooled after a foot injury. If they can put it together at the same time, look out. Kalif Raymond is a solid role player behind them, and Jahdae Walker flashed a bit when called upon last year.
If Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel can stay upright for the entire season, there's a lot of intrigue with this group, especially given the buzz around rookie De'Zhaun Stribling throughout training camp. Even guys like Demarcus Robinson and Christian Kirk are solid players further down the depth chart.
The Steelers seem boring on the surface, but DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. are good players, man! Pittsburgh doesn't have a proven option behind them, though, and will count on Germie Bernard and/or Roman Wilson to be the No. 3 receiver.
Emeka Egbuka was shot out of a cannon to start last season, but cooled down after Baker Mayfield got banged up. Still, the future looks bright. Chris Godwin is finally healthy again. Jalen McMillan is back in the mix, too. Ted Hurst is an interesting prospect. And Tez Johnson can be a nice role player as a deep threat. This is an intriguing group.
The Chargers have a strong top trio with Ladd McConkey , Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris . Those three guys bring a ton of speed to the table. Rookie Brenen Thompson brings even more of it. KeAndre Lambert-Smith is an interesting deep threat, too.
The Eagles could arguably be even higher than this. DeVonta Smith is fantastic. Makai Lemon was a first-round pick. Dontayvion Wicks has always excelled at earning targets. (Less so at actually catching passes, though.) If Lemon hadn't missed so much of camp and looked likely to hit the ground running immediately, we might have bumped Philly into the top 10.
The Packers had one of the deepest rooms in the league last year, but cleared things out a bit so that the top three could get on the field more…
author: Jared Dubin

title: Infectious energy? More like 'infectious disease' as Cam Skattebo ruffles feathers at Giants practice
summary: Skattebo's play style is not always well-received, especially during training camp
full_text:
Cam Skattebo is about as physical a running back as there is in the NFL . His hard-nosed play style made him a standout performer before his season-ending ankle injury as a rookie. He is also among the more flamboyant ballcarriers in the league. His backflip celebrations sometimes garner as much attention as the plays that warrant them.
All of that is well and good on Sundays when Skattebo is doing it against a different team. But in the context of the New York Giants ' training camp, his brash football personality has tended to rub teammates the wrong way.
Skattebo was reportedly at the center of a fight this week that stemmed from a couple of close calls with vulnerable defensive players. On one rep, when the defense was not allowed to hit, he made a catch and slid close to a couple of defensive backs' legs, according to the New York Daily News . Jevon Holland and Gregory Newsome took exception to the potentially dangerous play, and the situation between Newsome and Skattebo escalated.
Days earlier, Skattebo ran over linebacker Zaire Barnes in a period where, again, defensive players were not permitted to make hits.
At the suggestion that Skattebo is wearing on his defensive teammates' nerves, one of his fellow offensive players pushed back. Offensive lineman Jermaine Eluemunor squashed the idea that Skattebo is the source of any rotten team chemistry.
🧢 Stop trying to create a BS Narrative https://t.co/CkLFunX6jg
At the same time, though, the Giants want Skattebo to keep himself in check. Coach John Harbaugh earlier this offseason asked him to limit his backflips during camp so as to reduce the potential for reinjury. And after his slide at Wednesday's practice, Harbaugh made it clear he wants to set boundaries between the whistles, too.
"Skatt's great," Harbaugh said . "He does bring a lot of energy. But he did get a 15-yard penalty at the end of practice. Did you notice that? That's not infectious. Well, it is infectious, actually. Infectious in a bad way. Like an infectious disease type of thing. You don't want that. You want it to be directed in a positive way."
During his rookie season in 2025, Skattebo's "infectious" personality made him a favorite among teammates and Giants fans. However, that ended when he suffered a gruesome dislocation of his right ankle on Oct. 26, 2025.
Giants fans are aching to see Skattebo headbutt defenders, run right through them and pull off backflips when he crosses the goal line. That is what made him a must-watch ballcarrier in a rookie campaign that featured 617 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns across just eight games. Defenses cannot stand him, which is terrific when he plays against another team and less so when he lines up across from his own teammates for weeks on end. Fortunately for the Giants and their fans, the season is just over two weeks away. They begin the 2026 season on Sunday Night Football on Sept. 13 against the NFC East rival Dallas Cowboys, which means Skattebo will have the opportunity to run over defenders in another uniform instead of his own.
Skattebo is listed atop the depth chart at running back, but Harris has drawn praise since his arrival via free agency.
Harris, who by all accounts has looked good in practice, has the running style that suits the Greg Roman system, and he could cut into Skattebo's carries, especially if he keeps up his practice antics.
"Najee offers something different," Assistant general manager Brandon Brown told reporters on Wednesday. "When you have a back that played at 235 before his injury that doesn't need things blocked up cleanly for him to push the pile, and then he has a familiarity with G-Ro from L.A., those are things that you can't just gloss over. When you have an opportunity to add talent, we're never going to shy away from that."
On the addition of Harris, Brown added: "No one was butthurt." "It was very much adding competition, and that's the thing that's been very cool about the meritocracy. It's not personal. It's just the business of making this team as good as it can be."
The Giants have plenty of competition for carries and touches this season, with four capable running backs (Skattebo, Harris, Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary), and a coach like Harbaugh won't put up with the drama.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Man posing as 49ers player arrested after defrauding women of $1.3 million
summary: The fake football player convinced many of the victims that they were in a romantic relationship with him before asking them for money for investment opportunities
full_text:
The United States Attorney's Office in the District of Oregon announced this week that two men were arrested and charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. One of the men posed as a player for the San Francisco 49ers and ran a scheme that defrauded at least 26 women of more than $1.3 million. The FBI believes there are "many more" victims.
Daejon Labrayae Love, 35, and Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, were arrested on Aug. 24 in Idaho. Love pretended to be the star athlete, while Chan posed as his financial adviser. The two created fictitious investments for a plot that dated back to 2022 and defrauded women in four states: California, Oregon, Washington and Idaho. Investigators say Love met most of his victims on dating apps and used several names, including Jon Love, Daejon Love, Avril Lyto Love and Jordan Love, to continue his scheme.
Prosecutors also shared an Instagram profile that appears to belong to Love, which had " NFL Wide Receiver @49ers #undrafted" in the bio.
Most of the pictures on this profile included a man wearing 49ers gear. There are images with exotic cars and videos of him working out on a beach in a 49ers helmet.
"The scheme relied on Love's creation of fictitious personas and display of a lavish lifestyle which Love presented to victims both in person and on social media websites," the U.S. Attorney's Office said in a statement . "Love convinced many of the victims they were in sincere romantic relationships with Love, that he was a sophisticated investor, and that Chan was his investment adviser who helped Love grow a fortune worth tens of millions of dollars."
Chan and Love would create investment opportunities and convince victims over three-way FaceTime calls to send them money, showing falsified investment gains. If the victims did not have money to invest, Love would sometimes urge them to take out loans. If the victims ran out of money to invest or asked too many questions, Love would block them so they had no way of communicating with him.
Love traveled to New Mexico, California, Oregon, Nevada, Utah and Idaho in the months of July and August, and was arrested along with Chan at the Boise Airport. The FBI discovered Love was in Idaho to meet new victims.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Predicting first-time NFL All-Pros at every offensive position: Caleb Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs among young stars
summary: Let's break down the players primed to make the leap and earn their first All-Pro recognition this season
full_text:
There were 11 NFL offensive players whose stellar performance earned them inclusion on the Associated Press' All-Pro teams for the first time last season. That's nearly half of the prior year's first and second teams that were turned over.
With that in mind, CBS Sports explores which offensive players may be next to blossom and reach All-Pro status:
Joe Burrow and Justin Herbert have yet to make an All-Pro appearance, so those are options for this category, but also not in the spirit of the exercise. The intended purpose is to project a player who has yet to reach his peak.
Caleb Williams ' first season under head coach Ben Johnson was fruitful, but the encore should be even better if his offensive line protection holds up. Williams has a better understanding of the offense and has had more time to develop relationships with primary pass catchers Rome Odunze , Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland .
The key for the USC product will be finding consistency while maintaining the ability to make downfield plays late in the down of which others are incapable.
Six of the nine quarterbacks who were named All-Pros over the past five years were first-round picks. Williams was the No. 1 overall selection in the 2024 NFL Draft .
Jahmyr Gibbs is the running back most likely to be named an All-Pro who has not already been so. Although the team signed Isiah Pacheco in free agency, the trade of veteran David Montgomery feels like Gibbs taking ownership of the role in the Motor City.
The franchise is hoping the arrival of new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing can re-instill some of the magic that departed with Johnson. Gibbs has accounted for 1,800-plus all-purpose yards in each of the past two years.
A candle is still lit for Ashton Jeanty, and while the trio of Quinshon Judkins , Breece Hall and De'Von Achane have battled injuries, they are more than capable of ascending to this level. As you're reading this, Arizona's Jeremiyah Love is dealing with a high ankle sprain, but he has three-down capabilities, and Arizona is clearly content giving him the bulk of the carries.
Feature backs may be returning to the NFL. There have been at least a dozen 1,000-yard rushers in each of the past four seasons. There had been only two such seasons dating back to 2015. Of the nine running backs named All-Pros over the past five years, eight were taken in the first or second round; Kyren Williams ( Rams ), a fifth-round pick, was the exception.
The only 6-foot-4 All-Pro receiver over the past five years was Tampa Bay's Mike Evans . Drake London would buck that trend.
The former USC Trojan is entering his first season with Kevin Stefanski as head coach. Aside from tight end Kyle Pitts and London, Atlanta's pass catchers are Jahan Dotson , Olamide Zaccheaus and third-round pick Zachariah Branch .
If London puts together a full season -- as opposed to the five games he missed last season -- then he may finish closer to the 158 targets he accumulated in 2024; in that season, he finished fourth in receiving yards.
Thirteen of 17 All-Pro receivers have been taken in the top 100. When exploring the four who were not ( Stefon Diggs , Puka Nacua , Tyreek Hill and Amon-Ra St. Brown ), two likely would have been taken earlier if not for off-field concerns (Hill) and injuries (Nacua).
The Texans ' Nico Collins and the Giants ' Malik Nabers are a few others who fit the mold of a first-time All-Pro.
There is one less mouth to feed in Chicago's offense with DJ Moore traded to Buffalo, but wide receivers Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze may eat away at a portion of those newfound targets.
Colston Loveland tallied 58 receptions for 713 yards and six touchdowns last season. Will new opportunities lead to the requisite statistics for him to ascend to All-Pro status?
Green Bay's Tucker Kraft , Cleveland's Harold Fannin Jr . and Indianapolis' Tyler Warren are also worth consideration for the list. San Francisco's George Kittle is the only All-Pro tight end over the past five years to be drafted outside of the top 100.
Joe Alt drew Offensive Rookie of the Year consideration after the 2024 season but was limited to six games as a sophomore due to injury. If he can put together a full season, then he has the athletic and physical potential to earn postseason accolades. A healthy Rashawn Slater would also go a long way towards bringing stability to the unit.
Alt had fewer penalties, pressures and sacks allowed per game last season before getting injured. His 1.1% beaten rate, according to TruMedia, was fourth-best among linemen with at least 150 pass blocking snaps.
Offensive tackle remains a premium position in the NFL. Of the 10 to be named an All-Pros over the past five years, nine were drafted in the first round and six were taken with top-10 picks. The exception was Jordan Mailata for a variety of reasons. Prior to being taken in the seventh round of the 2018 NFL Draft, Mailata had only played rugby.
Alt, meanwhile, was the No. 5 overall selection in the 2024 NFL Draft.
Peter Skoronski has gotten better in each of his three NFL seasons despite not having much talent or consistency on either side of him. In 2025, TruMedia credited him with two sacks allowed. Tennessee rewarded him with a lucrative contract extension this offseason.
Chiefs offensive guard Trey Smith would be another candidate, and it would not come as a surprise if Ravens rookie Olaivavega Ioane were on the radar next season.
Over the past five years, Houston's Wyatt Teller is the only All-Pro offensive guard to be taken outside of the top 10, and he'll graduate from that list following the 2026 season unless he makes the All-Pro team again.
If Las Vegas' offense shows significant improvement this season, Tyler Linderbaum will be viewed as one of the catalysts for change. He is a light, mobile center who may jumpstart Jeanty's return to prominence in 2025.
Steelers center Zach Frazier is an ascending player who will gradually earn more league-wide notoriety.
Only four undrafted free agents have been named All-Pros over the past five years, and Miami's Aaron Brewer is the only one on the offensive side of the ball. Of the five centers to be named All-Pros during that timeframe, three were taken in the fifth round or later. This is the biggest example of a position where teams may be able to identify value later in the draft.
author: Josh Edwards

title: College football Week 0 picks; NFL roster cutdown day looming; MLB call-up candidates
summary: Plus the latest buzz from NFL preseason games and training camps
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
It's time for the annual harsh reminder that football is a business. Teams have until 6 p.m. ET on Sunday to trim their rosters down to 53 men, which means a whole host of players will receive bad news in the next couple of days. A large handful of big-name veterans are on the chopping block , so don't be surprised if these guys end up as free agents by the end of the weekend:
There is some give and take at the roster deadline. While every team has to part ways with some players, this is also an opportunity to make last-minute additions. Our Josh Edwards identified one position of need for all 32 teams . It's hard to imagine the Rams needing any more help than they already found this offseason, but Edwards says they would benefit from bolstering their linebacker group.
In other roster news, the Seahawks handed out another huge extension when they signed Leonard Williams to a three-year, $90 million deal. Don't hold your breath on an extension for Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez , though — and keep an eye on these potential landing spots if he hits the trade block. And speaking of the Rams, we graded their trade for Tutu Atwell .
Football isn't the only sport with a roster deadline coming up in the next couple of days. When the clock strikes midnight and the calendar flips from August to September, postseason eligibility locks and rosters expand by two spots. Anyone not in a specific organization at 11:59 p.m. ET on Aug. 31 cannot play for that team in the postseason. Clubs are allowed, however, to carry two additional players on their active roster for the rest of the year.
This means two things: first, players available on waivers will become hot commodities as teams look for last-minute help ahead of the playoff push. Arguably no one carries as much upside as Eugenio Suárez , whom the Reds reportedly placed on Waivers earlier this week. Here are a few others who could become available:
The second factor at play is the arrival of top prospects. When rosters expand, teams will in many cases be inclined to call up the biggest names from their farm system . Shall we get ready to see Franklin Arias in a Red Sox uniform? Our Mike Axisa says the 20-year-old could make his debut soon.

title: Taylen Green has our attention after NFL preseason debut: Rookie makes Browns' QB room even more complicated
summary: Now the waiting game begins to see if Green will make Cleveland's roster
full_text:
Much of the focus in the Browns ' training camp and preseason was on the Deshaun Watson vs. Shedeur Sanders quarterback battle, which Watson officially won on Monday .
On Thursday, though, another quarterback with a noteworthy background finally took the stage. Sixth-round rookie Taylen Green made his preseason debut in the second half of the Browns' preseason finale against the Patriots , taking over after second-year quarterback Dillon Gabriel gave way.
(Gabriel, for what it's worth, lit it up in the first half, going 12-for-15 for 186 yards and three touchdowns. That's a good sign for both Cleveland, which selected him in the third round last year, and for Gabriel, who hadn't exactly impressed this preseason.)
Pinned deep in his own territory on his first drive, Green nearly scrambled for a first down on third-and-9 but came up a yard short.
Then came the fun. Again in the shadow of his own end zone and behind the sticks, Green nearly pulled a Dan Orlovsky and ran out the back of his end zone, but instead turned a broken play into this ...
Rookie, Taylen Green, showing off his speed 🏃 NEvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Vf6XHfIMw6
He was accurate on a pair of short passes before showing off his legs again, first scrambling for 9 yards on third and 5 and later 5 more yards on third and 4. He also converted a quarterback sneak before Davon Booth capped the drive with a 12-yard rushing touchdown.
On his third drive, he added 12 more rushing yards on two carries, but the drive petered out when Green misfired badly on third and 9. The Browns' defense got a late interception to set up Green for a chance at his first NFL touchdown, but Cleveland's offense had to settle for a field goal to put a bow on a 37-13 win.
Overall, Green finished 5-for-7 for 27 yards throwing and had a game-high 66 rushing yards on just eight carries.
Green is an absurd athlete, and not just in an "athletic for a quarterback" way. At the NFL combine back in February, the Arkansas product posted ...
The vertical jump and the broad jump were both best ever for a quarterback at the combine, and his 40-yard dash was the second-fastest for the position, only behind Michael Vick. All of that athleticism is packed into a 6-foot-6, 230-pound frame that is on par (or better than) the prototype quarterback numbers.
For some non-quarterback context, how about ... DK Metcalf ?
Quite the comp for @RazorbackFB QB Taylen Green 👀 @dkm14 2026 NFL Combine on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/BUtxInUeDJ
Green threw for 2,714 yards, 19 touchdowns and 11 interceptions (on an SEC-best 13.7 yards per completion) last year while also picking up 777 yards rushing and eight scores on the ground. But his falling to the sixth round wasn't exactly an accident. For all the fun highlights and outrageous testing numbers, he completed only 60% of his career passes. He is the definition of a raw prospect, and there's a long way to go in terms of accuracy and processing in an NFL offense.
In essence, he is the perfect preseason player at this stage of his career: a ton of fun and physical promise on display in a game full of backups.
There have been outstanding athletes at the quarterback position who haven't panned out. Anthony Richardson Sr. is the most recent notable example; he's currently battling to be the Colts ' backup after being the No. 4 overall pick in 2023.
Green doesn't come with those gigantic expectations, though. As a sixth-round pick, he's likely looking at a spot as a third or fourth-stringer or on the practice squad. Still, with roster cutdown day on Sunday, the Browns have an interesting decision to make. Will they keep three quarterbacks -- generally the most any team keeps -- or a basically unheard-of four?
The Browns, it should be noted, have had basically unheard-of quarterback misfortune. They started three different quarterbacks last year, four the year before, and five the year before that. Watson has started just 19 of 68 possible games since arriving in Cleveland and has had season-ending injuries in 2023 and 2024. With that perspective, keeping four doesn't sound so unreasonable.
Coach Todd Monken said Green "played pretty well in the limited reps he had against the Bills " in joint practice last week, per The Athletic's Zac Jackson , but also acknowledged there have been so few reps to go around to either Green or Gabriel, given the quarterback competition.
Cutting Gabriel would be a hard pill to swallow. He wasn't a pick of the current coaching staff like Green was, but the same front office, headed by GM Andrew Berry, is still in place. And while Gabriel hasn't had the smoothest training camp and preseason, he certainly played well Thursday. Green, on the other hand, is such a rare athlete that the Browns might not be able to sneak him onto the practice squad should the Browns cut him; other teams might be circling.
Cleveland made a big decision about their starting quarterback to start the week. They'll make a big decision about their backup quarterback(s) to end it.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL waiver wire explained: How it affects the Arizona Cardinals in 2026
summary: The Arizona Cardinals wrapped up their preseason tonight in Green Bay and now they prepare for the regular season. Part of the preparation is getting the roster down to 53, and as that is happening, also working the waiver wire to add players they think can help them in 2026 and maybe even beyond. How […]
full_text: Arizona Cardinals linebacker BJ Ojulari (9) signs autographs parking lot of Lambeau Field before a joint practice with the Green Bay Packers on Aug. 26, 2026, in Green Bay, Wis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Arizona Cardinals wrapped up their preseason tonight in Green Bay and now they prepare for the regular season. Part of the preparation is getting the roster down to 53, and as that is happening, also working the waiver wire to add players they think can help them in 2026 and maybe even beyond. How does the NFL Waiver Wire Work? A nice explainer from our friends at Buffalo Rumblings: Players with less than four accrued seasons who are waived are subject to the waiver wire, where any team that claims them picks up their current contract. Any player claimed off the waiver wire must added to the claiming team’s active 53-man roster. If they pass through waivers unclaimed, they become free agents and are free to sign with any team’s practice squad they choose, which includes their prior team. The waiver order is set by the original 2026 NFL Draft order for the first three weeks of the season, one that does not include trades, which means the Arizona Cardinals are third in the waiver wire priority. title: The biggest positional questions that need to be answered versus the Packers
summary: The Arizona Cardinals end their exhibition schedule against the Green Bay Packers tonight. None of the starting players will suit up for the contest. Head coach Mike LaFleur has already stated that his starting offense and defense will not play, along with RB Jeremiyah Love and punter Blake Gillikin. What both the Packers and the […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Tre Tucker #1 of the Las Vegas Raiders picks up a first down on a pass play as BJ Ojulari #9 of the Arizona Cardinals defends in the first quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Cardinals defeated the Raiders 27-14. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals end their exhibition schedule against the Green Bay Packers tonight. None of the starting players will suit up for the contest. Head coach Mike LaFleur has already stated that his starting offense and defense will not play, along with RB Jeremiyah Love and punter Blake Gillikin. What both the Packers and the Cardinals want to accomplish is to see which players to keep and which to send on their way to seek employment elsewhere. The final cutdown is this Sunday, August 30, at 4:00 p.m. (Eastern). RELATED: UPDATE FROM PACKERS-CARDINALS JOINT PRACTICE There are plenty of storylines that need to be solved. Will this final preseason game address those concerns, or will there be little resolution? Here are four questions that need answers this weekend: Who will play right guard? During training camp, rookie Chase Bisontis and Isaiah Adams were in a heated battle for the starting role. Then Bisontis suffered a knee injury against the Las Vegas Raiders and had surgery. Next, he was placed on season-ending IR. This left Adams (6’-4”, 315 pounds) as the default starter at right guard. However, he recently started having knee issues on his own during the joint practice sessions with the Packers. He did not travel to Green Bay and missed the Monday practice. Now what? His replacement on the depth chart is listed as Oli Udoh, but for the Green Bay game, it appears backup center Jon Gaines (6’-4”, 320 pounds) will either replace Adams or split time with Udoh. Gaines has had a very good training camp. He has looked really good when the second-team offense plays against the opponent’s second-string. Which is not really an apples-to-apples comparison, but it does show he has consistency. Udoh (6’-6”, 320 pounds) is fighting for a roster spot and played extensively against the Dallas Cowboys last weekend. He could become the starting right guard or become quality depth. He is entering his eighth NFL season with 74 games played and 22 starts, so the experience is there. It appears the job is Adams’ unless he cannot go due to an injury. But you can’t look past what Gaines has done so far this preseason and training camp. What will the coaching staff do with LB/DE B.J. Ojulari? The Cardinals did not choose Ojulari in Round 2 a few short years ago just to release him. But where is his production? This is his third year since being drafted in 2023, and he has a grand total of zero starts. He sat out all of 204 with a torn ACL, then began last year on the PUP list. He finally suited up in Week 11. So far, his NFL career consists of 49 total tackles, 5 sacks, 9 QB hits, and 11 pressures, among other stats. This is a guy who was named First Team All-SEC in his final college season. At LSU, he was a beast at rushing the passer with 16.5 sacks, 129 total tackles, and 25 tackles for loss. In his rookie year, he didn’t tear up the league or be named to the NFL All-Rookie Team, but he showed a lot of promise. He was good against the run and had a huge array of pass-rushing moves. Mostly, Ojulari (6’-2”, 248 pounds) was impressive with his change of direction and quickness. He needed some tutelage in losing bigger offensive linemen and consistency in the use of his hands. But again, he showed promise that better days were ahead of him and that he was coachable. Mike LaFleur on B.J. Ojulari's performance Thursday night: "I thought he did some good stuff in the game. He's a fast rusher off that edge right there. And I just think it's just for him just continue to get time on task value received. Continuing to practice. Obviously there's a… — Josh Weinfuss (@joshweinfuss) August 9, 2026 This year’s training camp, he has shown flashes. But are flashes enough to keep him? Other hybrid players such as Jordan Burch, Eku Leota, and Owen Pappoe are outplaying him. So far in the preseason, Ojulari’s numbers are: Panthers: 3 tackles Raiders: 1 tackle, 1 QB hit Cowboys: 3 tackles Yeah, as if at this point the head coach is going to say he's another bust — Dr. Shrimp Puerto Rico (@JkrempskiJerry) August 10, 2026 This Cardinals coaching staff does not care for one second where a player was drafted. They want the best 11 guys on the field at all times. These coaches did not draft Ojulari, so they have no skin in his game. What will the coaching staff do with DE Darius Robinson? Another guy drafted high and yet has not fulfilled his destiny. In this year’s training camp, Robinson (6’-5”, 290 pounds) has been a roller coaster. He will dominate one day and then disappear in the preseason games. Maybe he has learned how to outplay his Cardinals’ offensive counterparts, but can’t do anything against the talent in the league. Yes? No? Maybe? He has excellent size and agility. 12 sacks and 78 tackles in his final two years at Missouri, where he was a pass-rushing demon in a difficult conference. 21.5 tackles for loss tell you about his run-stopping ability. And right now, Robinson is listed as a starter on the defensive line. In most media projections of the final 53-man roster for Arizona, every single one has Robinson listed. So far in preseason, he has one tackle, and that’s it. Coming to the Cardinals, Robinson’s role was to wreak havoc in the opponent’s offensive backfield. But so far, he has just two sacks in two seasons, along with 5 tackles for loss, 3 QB hits, and 6 pressures. He has struggled to consistently rack up sacks or explosive pass-rush plays. Maybe DC Nick Rallis should keep him at one position instead of moving him to various spots along the defensive line like he was a “Swiss Army knife.” Keep him at one position, and let him live or die there. One word? Underperforming. He was taken with the 27 th pick in the first round, for goodness ‘ sake. He is not fulfilling the idea of him coming in and becoming that complement to Josh Sweat. What kind of depth do the Cardinals have at cornerback? Arizona has a really good defensive backfield. They better, because the NFC West Division is full of exceptional receivers and quarterbacks who can place the ball. However, name a player in the Cardinals’ cornerback room who has never been hurt? Exactly. So, the depth machine has got to be there and become a plug-and-play. Will Johnson could become one of those league-wide known corners – if he can remain on the field. Garrett Williams has solidified this group with his veteran presence – if he can remain on the field. Denzel Burke took over last year because of an injury and proved that he belonged in a starting role. Behind them has been a quagmire of talent. Max Melton has shown flashes but has had issues adjusting to the speed at the NFL level. He has had several injuries to his heel and knee. Sean Murphy-Bunting has provided entertainment in that he is a roller coaster himself. He is coming off a horrific knee injury from last year involving a torn ACL plus MCL damage that required surgery. The year before that, it was a neck issue plus a dislocated elbow. The Cardinals’ fanbase was surprised when the front office restructured his deal to a more incentive-laden contract and lowered his salary instead of releasing him. Kei’Trel Clark had found a groove after being drafted in Round 6 last year before ending up on IR with a back injury. He is fighting for the sixth and final roster spot in this room. He sustained a hip injury in the preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys but was playing well in training camp and had five total tackles in the preseason. As an audition for this Falcons roster, it told many tales, some of them tragic […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Tua Tagovailoa #1 of the Atlanta Falcons throws against the Miami Dolphins during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images As a football game, it was pretty artless, with some nice stretches from the defense and a handful of big plays on offense and special teams adding a little excitement to a contest that was otherwise plodding, penalty-ridden, and low-scoring. As an audition for this Falcons roster, it told many tales, some of them tragic and some of them terrific. That was the third preseason game in a nutshell, with the Falcons dispatching the hapless Dolphins 17-12. Atlanta’s starters went out there against Miami’s backups and struck first, with Brian Robinson capping off a Tua Tagovailoa-led drive with a score. Tua would then fumble an iffy snap from Corey Levin to derail a drive, marring an otherwise effective but unexciting night featuring a lot of short passes, and then the backups were in. Cooper Rush mostly stuck to short passes himself, with a nice quick toss to Jack Velling for a touchdown, but uncorked a beautiful in-stride ball to Tyler Goodson that set up a field goal before the half. The 17 points were all the Falcons would score, as the second half featured an extremely bland gameplan for Jack Strand—though he was still fairly sharp, minus an interception that went off Nate Carter’s hands and into the air for Miami—and some poor defense that set up a pair of Dolphins field goal drives. There are no big takeaways for the starters, except for the fact that it was nice to see them largely dominate Miami’s reserves and the stern warning Tua must receive over the number of fumbled snaps he’s had this summer. The reserves are a different story, given that players like Goodson, Velling, Harold Perkins Jr., Chris Williams, and Rush did well enough to make a big push for roster spots, while others scuffled mightily. If the coaching staff was wavering on who to keep around at positions like cornerback and running back, tonight probably provided them with the data points they needed to make a decision. And blessedly, preseason is now over. Roster cuts are tough because good players and good people ultimately will get the axe, but knowing the shape of the roster lets us properly evaluate what the team will be capable of. Knowing the practice squad helps us get a better sense of who the Falcons want to develop and what break-in-case-of-emergency options exist for them. All of that is welcome, especially for a first year front office and staff, even if I’ll undoubtedly be sad to see many Falcons who spent the spring and summer here headed elsewhere. While we wait for news of cuts and additions both before and after the Sunday cutdown deadline, let’s dive in to the full recap. The next time we gather to talk about a game, it will be one that counts in the NFC South standings. The Good The Falcons almost seemed like they were keeping Jack Strand corked in this one, so the heavy lifting fell to Cooper Rush. While Rush was also seemingly held in check by a vanilla game plan early on and missed a couple of short throws, he led the offense to two scoring drives and had two of the best throws of the night for any quarterback on a sharp slant to Jack Velling for a touchdown and a beautiful ball to Tyler Goodson for the long gain before the half that set up a field goal. I don’t know Atlanta’s plans at quarterback, but at this point, Rush hasn’t done anything to play himself out of a QB3 role. It’s just a question of whether the Falcons view Strand’s upside as significant enough to part ways with Rush or try to sneak him on to the practice squad. For what it’s worth, I think they very well might. Tyler Goodson rocks. Once again he looked terrific in this one, with the highlight play coming in the second quarter on a pretty ball from Cooper Rush that hit him in stride downfield, with Goodson hitting an insane spin move to pick up more yards and then smartly spiking it to set up a field goal try right before the half. He’s the third running back and has been good enough that he might get a little regular season work even with the Robinsons healthy. Vinny Anthony and Chris Blair are my picks for WR5/6, if the Falcons keep that many guys. Blair continues to run effective routes and look very sure-handed, while Anthony has been dynamic as a receiver and damn good as a returner, with the patience and vision to turn good blocking into a late kick return that went past midfield. Both guys deserve spots, but if there’s only one up for grabs, Anthony’s return value might give him the edge. If Tua is the quarterback, it looks likely Jahan Dotson will get plenty of run. He was a favored security blanket during Tua’s short starting stint in this one, and looked good and decisive in that role. Kyle Pitts looked really good in this one. He got loose on a screen for a big pickup early on and easily led the team in receiving yardage, showcasing those long strides that let him simply outrun defenders and the sure hands that give him an opportunity in the first place. In an offense built to showcase tight ends and looking healthy and sure of himself, Pitts could be headed for a monster season. Nick Muse is a solid blocking tight end and player overall, and I think the Falcons will try to keep him around in some capacity. But it was Jack Velling who did a lot of damage in this one as a receiver, and a really solid summer has given the rookie undrafted free agent a genuine shot to stick around as the fourth tight end. The only question is whether the Falcons will keep four on the 53 man roster—unlikely, in my opinion—or sneak him on to the practice squad. I loved Harold Perkins Jr. pursuing Cam Miller to the ends of the earth on a third down in the second quarter. This is the third preseason game and the stakes seem low, but Perkins treated every Miller juke as a personal affront and eventually got him, sacking him and forcing a fumble that fell out of bounds. That relentlessness is going to stand out for this coaching staff, and Perkins did open as a starter in this one. Chris Williams has been heating up as the summer has gone along. He’s shown some legitimate pass rushing ability, getting after Cam Miller repeatedly in this one, and then blocking a field goal try early on in the game. He’s making this roster and should be a fun player in a go get ‘em front. Cameron Thomas has been another good addition, making the most of his early down snaps and picking up a pretty effortless sack tonight. If he can get home consistently and deliver that solid work against the run, the Falcons have another very useful piece. Quietly, the Falcons run defense has looked pretty good this summer, with a few tough stretches against the Broncos looking like the only knock against this front. I don’t know if that will translate to the regular season just yet, but it’s an encouraging sign. Josh Woods should make the roster. I know Channing Tindall has ties to special teams coordinator Craig Aukerman, but Woods is a very capable special teamer and has played his ass off on defense all preseason long. The highlight in this one was a hustle play where he came in to recover a high snap and fumble by quarterback Mark Gronowski, another testament to his instincts and effort. With zero offense intended to Tindall or JD Bertrand, Woods has been doing this long enough and well enough that I’d hope he would make it ahead of either of them. James Pearce Jr. got two sacks working against the deep reserves, but we know he can also do that against the starters. The Falcons are going to miss him through the first half of the season, but the hope is that all goes well during his suspension, he abides by the term of his trial diversion program, and we see him later in the year. The Falcons have some good problems at safety, where Sydney Brown and Natrone Brooks offer positional…

title: Projecting the Falcons final 53-man roster and practice squad
summary: The third and final preseason game is over, and it’s time for our final roster predictions. Cutdowns are a lot earlier this year—Sunday instead of Tuesday—which means there’s little time for consideration. Accordingly, I’ll be trying to get this to you all as early as possible on Saturday. The Dolphins game didn’t provide many new […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Jack Velling #84 of the Atlanta Falcons reacts to his touchdown against the Miami Dolphins during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The third and final preseason game is over, and it’s time for our final roster predictions. Cutdowns are a lot earlier this year—Sunday instead of Tuesday—which means there’s little time for consideration. Accordingly, I’ll be trying to get this to you all as early as possible on Saturday. The Dolphins game didn’t provide many new insights, but how the snaps were divvied out might provide some clues as to where certain players stand. Let’s dive right in to my final thoughts on Atlanta’s 2026 53-man roster. The roster projection is also available in both video and audio format, which you can find embedded below. If you enjoyed the written version, consider giving us a click on these platforms as well. Listen to the audio version of this article using the player below, or find it on your favorite podcast platforms. Italics denote a change from the previous roster projection. OFFENSE – 25 Quarterback – 4 Michael Penix Jr. Tua Tagovailoa Cooper Rush Jack Strand The Tua vs Penix camp battle has been anticlimactic, to say the least. Tua started out camp fine, but has struggled since the start of the preseason. The fact that he hasn’t taken control of the starting job at this point is fairly telling. Meanwhile, Penix just returned to full 11-on-11 work on Monday, and is having a bit of an adjustment period. There’s just enough time for Penix to win the starting job before Week 1, and I think he will ultimately do so. Put simply, the Falcons have a lot more incentive to put Penix on the field, assuming he’s healthy and ready to go. The most interesting battle of the offseason might actually be at the bottom of the depth chart at quarterback. UDFA Jack Strand has consistently impressed through training camp and the preseason, and I simply can’t imagine risking him on the practice squad. Cooper Rush remains a steady veteran option and is not subject to waivers, but at least initially, I think both begin on the roster. Shuffling will be likely in the coming days. Running Back – 3 Bijan Robinson Brian Robinson Tyler Goodson I’m really excited to see what Bijan Robinson can do in this offense. The Falcons offensive line is still working on incorporating more power concepts into the rushing attack, but once they’ve got it down, I think Robinson might be in line for his best season yet. He’ll also be heavily involved as a pass catching option, and I expect to see a lot of stuff schemed up for Robinson. Brian Robinson is a steady veteran who more or less replicates Tyler Allgeier’s role, just at a fraction of the price. I wouldn’t expect Robinson to match Allgeier’s play, but he’ll be fine. The pleasant surprise of the offseason has been the emergence of Tyler Goodson, who looks like a legitimate threat as a runner, pass catcher, and returner. Impressive UDFA Cash Jones could also be in consideration here if Atlanta opts for more RBs. Tight End – 4 Kyle Pitts Charlie Woerner Austin Hooper Nick Muse The Falcons are going to run their fair share of 12 personnel packages this season, which is why I favor the team keeping 4 TEs over 4 RBs or 6 WRs. Kyle Pitts looks to be in line for a featured role, and I expect his target share to be a lot more consistent in Tommy Rees’ offense. Charlie Woerner will be the primary blocking tight end, and he offers a unique skillset there. Austin Hooper will be the secondary receiving tight end, and may end up playing a similar number of snaps to Woerner. A big surprise has been the play of recently-signed Nick Muse and UDFA Jack Velling. Both were excellent as blockers and receivers against the Colts, and are making a serious push for the roster over Joshua Simon. At this point, I give the slight lead to Muse, but it’s close. Wide Receiver – 5 Drake London Jahan Dotson Zachariah Branch Olamide Zaccheaus Chris Blair One of the biggest developments of the summer is Atlanta’s high usage of 11 personnel (3 WR sets), and the quality of their receiving corps in general. 2025’s unit was among the NFL’s worst due to injury, mismanagement, and a lack of coaching. Things turned around quickly thanks to two veteran additions and the addition of electric rookie Zachariah Branch, and as a result, we could see a lot more receivers on the field than originally anticipated. Drake London will continue to dominate targets and remains the top pass catcher on the roster. His size and physicality stand out in a room filled with smaller, speedier options. Jahan Dotson acquitted himself well in training camp and seems to have the WR2 job locked up thanks to his experience, route running prowess, and versatility to play outside or in the slot. The biggest riser is Branch, who dominated throughout training camp and preseason and is likely to take over the WR3 role. Veteran Olamide Zaccheaus is a quality rotational option who provides depth in the slot and at returner. Chris Blair finally seems to have a staff who actually recognizes his talent, and is likely to be a fixture on special teams and as Drake London’s primary backup. Offensive Line – 9 LT Jake Matthews LG Matthew Bergeron C Ryan Neuzil RG Chris Lindstrom RT Jawaan Taylor T Michael Jerrell T/G Ethan Onianwa C/G Corey Levin T Wanya Morris IR: Kyle Hinton The Falcons have four solid starters on the offensive line all returning from 2025, and one big question mark in right tackle Jawaan Taylor. We’ve hardly seen Taylor this summer, but he appears fully healthy now and should be a meaningful upgrade over the depth tackles and 2025 starter Elijah Wilkinson. Taylor’s play will determine both the ceiling and floor of this line, and it’ll be up to Bill Callahan to see if he can squeeze more run blocking prowess out of the veteran. Most of the intrigue in this group is with the depth players, as there’s been a pretty fierce battle for swing tackle. Michael Jerrell has more or less manned the swing tackle spot since the start of training camp, and rebounded with a strong performance against the Colts after a rough outing against the Broncos. He’s not an overly inspiring option, but at least he’s shown some improvement. The shocker might by trade acquisition Wanya Morris falling behind rookie Ethan Onianwa. Onianwa got the bulk of the right tackle reps in both preseason games, with Morris being relegated to the depth unit. The rookie was legitimately impressive against the Colts and is learning quickly—I think he gets the roster nod, in part due to his draft status. There’s a bit of intrigue with the depth guards, as both Kyle Hinton and UDFA Kam Dewberry played pretty well thus far. Hinton is apparently in a large knee brace and didn’t participate in the third preseason game: he might be headed to IR, short-term or otherwise. Dewberry is someone to watch as a developmental practice squad player. Veteran Corey Levin looks like the far superior center option (who also offers guard flexibility), with UDFA James Brockermeyer struggling through the preseason. DEFENSE – 25 Edge Defender – 5 Za’Darius Smith Samson Ebukam Cameron Thomas Azeez Ojulari Bralen Trice SUSPENDED: James Pearce Jr. We officially got word on an eight-game suspension for James Pearce Jr., and the Falcons will struggle to generate pressure off the edge in his absence. As a result of the suspension and Jalon Walker’s season-ending injury, Atlanta brought in veteran Za’Darius Smith to bolster the room. I’m not sure what to expect from Smith entering his age 34 season, but by all accounts he’s impressed the coaching staff early and has brought a lot of veteran swagger to the room. At worst, he’s a good run defender who can also bring some juice on passing downs. I still like Atlanta’s rotational rushers, though they’re going to be relied upon a lot more than expected with the…

title: NFL waiver wire rules and the Falcons waiver order position
summary: The 2026 NFL preseason is over, at least for the Falcons. That means the worst time of the year, final roster cutdowns, is about to begin. The cutdown deadline happens earlier than usual this season, with teams needing to have their final cuts submitted no later than Sunday, August 30 at 6 PM ET. That […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - AUGUST 14: An equipment cart with the Falcons helmets is rolled to the locker room after the Friday evening NFL preseason football game between the Atlanta Falcons and the Denver Broncos on August 14, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 2026 NFL preseason is over, at least for the Falcons. That means the worst time of the year, final roster cutdowns, is about to begin. The cutdown deadline happens earlier than usual this season, with teams needing to have their final cuts submitted no later than Sunday, August 30 at 6 PM ET. That doesn’t leave a lot of time for Atlanta to make some very tough decisions. Speaking of tough, the Falcons face a difficult road to make the playoffs this season. Atlanta has the second-worst odds in the NFC South at +240 , behind the Bucs (+130) and Saints (+210). A lot of people throwing their money away on the Saints, apparently! Final roster cuts aren’t necessarily the end for NFL hopefuls, however. Some players will end up on practice squads, while others will be claimed by other teams through the NFL’s waiver process. We’ll detail those rules, and the Falcons position in the waiver order, below. When is the deadline for waiver claims? NFL teams must submit waiver claims for eligible players by 1 PM ET on Monday, August 31 . That’s a little less than 24 hours after the official cutdown deadline on Sunday. Once claims are submitted, the league will determine who goes where by using the official waiver order—which we’ll detail below. After the waivers have officially processed shortly after 1 PM ET, the rest of the players will officially become free agents and can then be signed to practice squads or other rosters. Which players are eligible for waivers? When determining waiver eligiblity, there are two types of players. Those with less than four “credited” seasons are subject to waivers, and are subject to claims before becoming free agents. Those with four or more credited seasons are considered “vested veterans” and are not subject to waivers. Once released, they immediately become free agents and are eligible to sign with whomever they wish. A “credited” season is different from an “accrued” season. The latter is used to determine if players become Unrestricted Free Agents (UFAs), Restricted Free Agents (RFAs) or Exclusive Rights Free Agents (ERFAs). A credited season is as follows: a player must be on an active, inactive, IR, or PUP roster for three or more regular season games. A player who receives and injury settlement (or grievance) for the equivalent of three or more regular season games is also given a credited season. What’s the current waiver order? Las Vegas Raiders New York Jets Arizona Cardinals Tennessee Titans New York Giants Cleveland Browns Washington Commanders New Orleans Saints Kansas City Chiefs Cincinnati Bengals Miami Dolphins Dallas Cowboys Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Tampa Bay Buccaneers Indianapolis Colts Detroit Lions Minnesota Vikings Carolina Panthers Green Bay Packers Pittsburgh Steelers Los Angeles Chargers Philadelphia Eagles Jacksonville Jaguars Chicago Bears Buffalo Bills San Francisco 49ers Houston Texans Los Angeles Rams Denver Broncos New England Patriots Seattle Seahawks How does the NFL determine the waiver order? For the offseason, preseason, and first three games of the regular season, the NFL uses the draft order from the most recent draft—in this case, the 2026 NFL Draft. Trades in that draft do not affect the waiver order, it’s based on where teams were originally slotted. Things change after the first three games of the season.

title: Falcons – Dolphins preseason instant recap: Plenty to consider
summary: The Atlanta Falcons turned the ball over twice and still went into halftime with a 17-6 lead, which says a lot more about the Dolphins than it does the Falcons. Then things got predictably slow and ugly. Atlanta’s offensive gameplan seemed to be heavily predicated on screens and short passes, and that had the dual […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Jack Velling #84 of the Atlanta Falcons reacts to his touchdown against the Miami Dolphins during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons turned the ball over twice and still went into halftime with a 17-6 lead, which says a lot more about the Dolphins than it does the Falcons. Then things got predictably slow and ugly. Atlanta’s offensive gameplan seemed to be heavily predicated on screens and short passes, and that had the dual effect of not revealing much of what Atlanta plans to get up to on offense this year and making this something of a slog. Tua Tagovailoa’s fumbled snap, Brian Robinson’s fumble, and a comically tipped and bobbled Jack Strand pass that was intercepted made for an ugly night, even if the Falcons were very obviously if narrowly the better team against Miami’s reserves. The defense got plenty of pressure and did a nice job against the run all night, but saw the cornerbacks implode a bit to give Miami a real shot at climbing back into this one. Ultimately, the defensive effort up front and just enough offense combined to give Atlanta a 17-12 win, but that’s the less important result. The more important one is that the Falcons have enough information between these games and training camp to make the roster decisions they must make before Sunday at 6 p.m., especially at spots like running back, inside linebacker, and cornerback where the decisions might have been tougher before Friday night. Here’s the drive-by-drive recap of the game you just watched. 1st Quarter Jalen Reagor took the kickoff to about the 25 yard line, but an illegal formation call on the Dolphins backed them up immediately. A quick pass to Chris Bell picked up about five yards on a comeback route working against A.J. Terrell. A handoff to Carlos Washington Jr. (former Falcon sighting!) lost multiple yards after Samson Ebukam hit him. Cam Miller scrambled for a first down, but a penalty backed the Dolphins up 10 yards. Miller then ran backwards away from pressure and threw it away, with Brandon Dorlus almost getting him. The punt saw a nice return from Zachariah Branch that got the Falcons close to midfield. Tua Tagovailoa took the field as the starting quarterback and hit Jahan Dotson for a first down. Brian Robinson Jr. was swallowed up on the secnod down carry for no gain. A penalty backed the Falcons up to 2nd and 17, and then Tua hit Kyle Pitts over the middle for six yards. On 3rd and 11, Pitts took a screen almost to the 10 yard line for 37 yards. Robinson then took it about seven yards through contact. Robinson then took it again and picked up the first down. On first down, Tua rolled away from pressure but had to throw it away. On second down, though, Robinson pushed his way through to the end zone to make it 7-0 Falcons. Miller hit Jalen Tolbert, who made an impressive 19 yard leaping grab. Cameron Thomas then sacked Miller on first down. Miller then ran up the middle and slid to gain back the lost yardage. Miller then hit Bell over the middle for 18 yards. Washington then picked up three yards. Miller then threw it too low for Reagor, and then Mike Hughes and DeMarcco Hellams combined to knock out a pass to Bell. The field goal attempt was good to make it 7-3 Falcons. The kick went out of bounds, giving the Falcons the ball at the 40. Unfortunately, Tua couldn’t get his hands on the snap and fumbled it, giving the Dolphins the ball around the 35. Miller threw a floater that Bell nearly reeled in on the sideline, with CJ Henderson working in coverage. A quick pass to Tolbert picked up six or so yards but Henderson was there to wrestle him out of bounds. Miller then almost threw a pick as Mike Hughes and DeMarcco Hellams arrived. The field goal was blocked by Chris Williams, who made a hell of a leap. A quick Tua pass to Brian Robinson went for eight yards. Then he hit Pitts over the middle and Pitts high stepped away from a tackle for a first down and much more. A quick sideline ball to Jahan Dotson went for about seven yards, and a penalty on Miami was declined. A false start on Jawaan Taylor backed the Falcons up. A quick pass from Tua to Dotson went for another first. Unfortunately, Robinson fumbled on the next carry and the Dolphins recovered. Miller missed badly on first down. Washington got six yards on second down. Miller then tried to run and did not make it to the first down marker. 2nd Quarter Dylan Drummond returned the punt for a handful of yards. Then a quick pass from Cooper Rush went for five yards, and a handoff to Tyler Goodson went nowhere. The Falcons did not pick up a first down on the next play. Punt. A false start backed the Dolphins up. Miller then tried to roll out and Jammie Robinson got him. Washington then took a toss and got upended after about four yards. Miller held on to the ball too long and Harold Perkins Jr. got him with the sack as the ball squirted out of bounds. Punt. Cooper Rush got away from pressure and hit Jack Velling for a first down. Goodson was stymied on first down. Then Rush hit Nick Muse just short of a first down, and the run was stuffed. A fourth down pass to Chris Blair was good for a first down. Rush then hit Nate Carter for a very small gain. Rush under pressure threw it very low and Blair scooped it for a first down. A quick pass to Goodson picked up five yards. Rush then folled out and hit Vinny Anthony for a first down. Goodson then pushed his way down to the three yard line. Rush then threw it a little behind a tumbling Drummond for an incompletion. On third down, though, Rush hit Jack Velling over the middle for a touchdown to make it 14-3 Falcons. Reagor then got back to almost midfield on the return. Miller then completed a pass over the middle for a first down. A toss to Washington went for about two yards. A quick throw to Tolbert picked up four yards. Miller then had the pass dropped with Henderson hitting him. Riley Patterson juuuuust hit the 45 yard field goal try to make it 14-6 Falcons. Goodson took it across the 30, but a penalty backed up the return. Rush patted it and then hit Drummond for about five yards. Rush then ran away from pressure and just missed Velling to the sideline. Rush under pressure tried to hit Blair and just missed him. Punt, and it was a beauty from Bailey to prevent much of a return. Miller was almost sacked on first down by Christian Harris. Miller was under a ton of pressure on second down and then nearly threw a pick. Another incompletion followed, and then it was punt time. Bradley Pinion’s punt went out of bounds. Cooper Rush then threw a low pass that Anthony tried to reel in but just couldn’t. Rush then got Velling for about eight yards over the middle. Rush then hit Blair again for a first down. Then Rush finally uncorked one after a lot of short passes, hitting Goodson in stride, with Goodson hitting a nice spin move and spiking it to set up the field goal try Nick Folk easily hit. 17-6 Falcons. 3rd Quarter The punt was muffed, but recovered. Jack Strand handed it to Nate Carter for a good pickup, but a penalty on Atlanta backed things up. Strand then hit Keelan Marion for about six yards. Strand followed that up with a very quick pass to Muse for a couple of yards. Strand then tried to get away from pressure and was sacked on third down. Punt. Washington made it nowhere on first down. Under pressure, new quarterback Mark Gronowski rolled away and threw it away. Gronowski then threw a pretty downfield ball and Terrace Marshall simply got leverage on Cobee Bryant to make the big grab. Gronowski then hit Tolbert for another first down, this one against Clark Phillips (who also got called for a pass interference call). Washington then picked up about six yards. Washington then almost picked up the first down and then almost got it again. On fourth down, Washington powered through before Phillips finally got…
