title: Aaron Leming’s Final Chicago Bears 53-Man Roster Projection
summary: In the blink of an eye, the 2026 NFL preseason is over. It’s always amazing to watch the buildup to training camp and how quickly things start to move once all 32 teams report. For the Chicago Bears, it was no different. Despite the lack of storylines surrounding the team this offseason, it has felt […]
full_text: In the blink of an eye, the 2026 NFL preseason is over. It’s always amazing to watch the buildup to training camp and how quickly things start to move once all 32 teams report. For the Chicago Bears, it was no different. Despite the lack of storylines surrounding the team this offseason, it has felt like business as usual for them heading into Year 2 of Ben Johnson. With high expectations in place, is 2026 finally the year the Bears can be considered serious Super Bowl contenders? Only time will tell, but for now, we’ll project the “final” 53-man roster and the 16 practice squad players that can be set starting Monday once waiver claims are processed. Quarterback (3): Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent, and Case Keenum None of this list should surprise anyone. Williams is the starter, Bagent is the primary backup, and Keenum is the QB3, assistant coach, and Caleb Williams hype-man. The Bears clearly valued their quarterback room last season and will move into 2026 with the same configuration. Bagent’s hamstring status could dictate who is active in Week 1, but other than that, there’s no mystery here. Practice Squad: N/A Running Back (3): D’Andre Swift, Kyle Monangai, and Roschon Johnson Assuming Monangai is healthy and ready for Week 1, the Bears’ one-two punch will be the same as a year ago. Only this time, the optimism surrounding them is much greater. The primary focus of camp this year has been figuring out the RB3 role. None of the depth players have been able to stake a claim to it, and while I’d like to project Ahmed as the “winner” of this race, Johnson’s experience on special teams and the respect he has in the building might be enough to win him the job. That said, don’t be surprised if the team looks to upgrade this spot during the waiver wire process. Practice Squad: Salvon Ahmed and Brittain Brown Tight End (3): Colston Loveland, Cole Kmet, and Sam Roush The only real question with this group is whether they stick with the same number they had last year (3) or carry an extra player they worry they might lose to waivers. Regardless, this is one of the league’s better groups, both in talent and depth. For now, I’ll stick with projecting just three, with two on the practice squad ready to be called up (or eventually promoted). That said, don’t be surprised to see Hayden Large make the final roster due to his advanced blocking abilities. Practice Squad: Stephen Carlson and Hayden Large Wide Receiver (6): Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, Kalif Raymond, Jahdae Walker, Zavion Thomas, and Kaden Davis The Top 5 of this group have been set in stone, barring injury, since the team drafted Thomas in the third round back in April. The biggest question remaining is whether they’ll choose to keep an extra receiver. Heading into camp, I wasn’t sold they would, but after seeing the impressive competition, I’m projecting Davis to earn the sixth and final spot. Maurice Alexander is another name to watch for the final spot. Practice Squad: Maurice Alexander and Scotty Miller Offensive Line (9): Braxton Jones, Joe Thuney, Garrett Bradbury, Jonah Jackson, Darnell Wright, Logan Jones, Luke Newman, Theo Benedet, Jordan McFadden, and Ozzy Trapilo The battle at left tackle might not have been as big of a disappointment as last year, but it’s not far behind. By default, Jones wins the battle, but with Trapilo coming off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list much sooner than expected, Jones will be on a short leash heading into October. In my other projections, I had the Bears keep 10 offensive linemen. Still, with Jedrick Wills Jr. and Kiran Amegadjie failing to stick out, Trapilo could stick on the roster into the regular season, even knowing it could be a few weeks before he’s game-ready. Practice Squad: iOL Caden Barnett, OT Jedrick Wills Jr., and C Jaren Kump Defensive End (5): Montez Sweat, Austin Booker, Dayo Odeyingbo, Daniel Hardy, and Jamree Kromah In-Season PUP List: Shemar Turner If all goes well, the Bears could have a logjam of options once everyone returns to full health. That said, we’ve seen how these situations play out, and no team will ever assume that everything will go to plan. Instead, the front office will keep five (including Kromah), keep Turner on PUP, and put Davenport on the practice squad. The Davenport situation has been weird because, despite being signed over a week ago, he has been a non-factor in team drills. Similar to what they did with Tanoah Kpassango last year, they’ll stash Davenport on the practice squad and wait to see if he can become healthy enough to contribute. Practice Squad: Marcus Davenport Defensive Tackle (5): Grady Jarrett, Gervon Dexter Sr., Neville Gallimore, Jordan van den Berg, and James Lynch NFL insider Jordan Schultz has linked Dexter to trade rumors. Still, unless something materializes, I refuse to believe the team would consider releasing him in the final year of his rookie deal. Assuming no trades are made, the team will likely keep four, maybe five, names, which leaves either Lynch or Kentavius Street out of the mix. Street has “started” each preseason game, but Lynch has had the bigger impact, which is why I’m taking him as DT5. Practice Squad: Kentavius Street and Jayden Loving Linebacker (6): Devin Bush, DeMarco Jackson, T.J. Edwards, Ruben Hyppolite, Keshawn Elliott, and Jack Sanborn In most cases, keeping six linebackers doesn’t make a ton of sense, but with Elliott fresh off PUP and availability being an issue most of training camp, it could make sense to keep six bodies until they figure out the depth chart a little more. The bigger question will be who starts alongside Bush once the regular season starts. Practice Squad: Jon Rhattigan Cornerback (5): Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad, Jaylon Jones, and Josh Blackwell PUP: Kyler Gordon Cornerback is a tough spot for the Bears heading into the season. Sound familiar? Health and availability from the top part of their depth chart have been spotty at best, and with the unknown status of Gordon moving forward, how they stack their practice squad will be key to the first month-plus of the season. For now, we’ll roll with five, but don’t be surprised to see an outside addition early next week. Practice Squad: Terell Smith and an outside addition Safety (4): Dillon Thieneman, Xavier Woods, Cam Lewis, and Elijah Hicks Injured Reserve: Coby Bryant (Designated To Return) This is yet another spot on the depth chart where it’ll be interesting to watch things play out. Every team can place two players on Injured Reserve with a designation to return (without them counting against the final roster total before the deadline). While it’s still unclear if Bryant will return this season, it might make more sense to “save” his roster spot by doing this. Thomas has shown enough to grab a practice squad spot. Practice Squad: Skyler Thomas Special Teams (3): K Cairo Santos, P Tory Taylor, and LS Beau Gardner The only mystery in this group was at long snapper, but the Bears erased that early in the process when they cut Luke Elkin shortly before the start of the preseason. Barring the team wanting a veteran snapper (which should not be ruled out), this is the trio they’ll go with in 2026. Practice Squad: N/A
author: Aaron Leming

title: Bears Preseason: Could a big game by Jamree Kromah secure a roster spot?
summary: The Chicago Bears’ offseason has seen several players raise their stock. None more so than sixth-round draft pick Jordan van den Berg, who went from a fun athletic day-three prospect to getting reps with the starters. full_text: Chicago Bears defensive lineman Jamree Kromah (59) stretches during a joint training camp at the Kettering Health Practice Fields, Thursday, Aug. 20, 2026, in downtown Cincinnati. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Chicago Bears’ offseason has seen several players raise their stock. None more so than sixth-round draft pick Jordan van den Berg, who went from a fun athletic day-three prospect to getting reps with the starters. At this point, van den Berg’s roster spot is a lock, but there’s another defensive lineman who made a splash in the last couple of weeks. Jamree Kromah came out of college in 2024 as one of the most athletic defensive tackles in his class ( 9.67 RAS ), but he went undrafted and signed with the Bears. He moved up and down the line at James Madison, but as a pro his future was at defensive end. The 275-pounder had a nice camp and totaled 3 tackles and 2 QB hits in the preseason and was ultimately signed to Chicago’s practice squad. The New England Patriots signed him to their active roster a couple of weeks later, but he was waived and signed back to the Bears’ practice squad, where he remained the rest of 2024. He was back in Chicago the next year, and in the 2025 preseason he had 6 tackles and a QB hit. The Bears once again signed him to the practice squad, where he stayed all season. This year, he came into camp a new man. “One thing I did for sure was I changed my body, changed my nutrition, because I was much heavier last year,” Kromah said in the locker room following the preseason opener against the Browns, where he hit the D-lineman trifecta of a sack, forced fumble, and recovery all on the same play. “So I wanted to make some changes by losing weight. I lost over 20 pounds, but got stronger and then put more lean mass on. So this is the best I have felt … I had to look at the man in the mirror and be true to myself, and come up with a real plan.” In his first two preseason games, the 6’3″, now 268-pounder, has 6 tackles, 3 tackles for loss, 2 sacks, and a forced fumble and fumble recovery. His second game wasn’t as impactful, but he did have a half-sack negated by a holding penalty. In Saturday’s game in Tennessee, he’ll get another chance to shine and make a final push for a roster spot. The Bears may not play their starters, but starting defensive end Austin Booker is sidelined with a groin issue, which could create more opportunities for Kromah. Our friends at FanDuel Sportsbook currently have the Titans as a 2.5 point favorite in the preseason finale. If you think the Bears will win outright, the moneyline is at +122, with the point total over/under at 37.5.

title: Is it fair at this point to question Kyler Gordon?
summary: Over the years as a sports fan, I have certainly questioned a player or two about their desire to get back on the football field. But over the years I’ve learned that’s not a good idea. I will admit, I originally questioned Jay Cutler in the moment during the NFC Championship game when we had […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 18: Kyler Gordon #6 of the Chicago Bears stands on the sidelines during the national anthem prior to an NFL divisional playoff game against the Los Angeles Rams at Soldier Field on January 18, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over the years as a sports fan, I have certainly questioned a player or two about their desire to get back on the football field. But over the years I’ve learned that’s not a good idea. I will admit, I originally questioned Jay Cutler in the moment during the NFC Championship game when we had the Caleb Haine experience. In hindsight, that was stupid. It took me a long time to question Nate Davis. Let’s not forget, the summer Nate Davis arrived in Chicago, his mother died. It’s impossible to know how that’s going to affect someone’s professional life, and to this day, we still really don’t know how that impacted him. Kyler Gordon is entering his fifth season in Chicago. And while he’s never played a full season, before last year, he never missed more than 4 games in a season. Last year, Gordon missed 14. This year, Gordon basically hasn’t been on the field at all. If the Bears were coming out and talking about Gordon’s injury and how his rehab is going and a projected timeline, we would be classifying this as an unfortunate injury, but that’s not what the Bears are saying. Both Ben Johnson and Ryan Poles have been pretty flippant talking about Gordon during the spring and summer and certainly seemed agitated about his lack of progress and lack of participation. They also seem to be missing details about what his status is. The Bears have plenty of injured players. You don’t hear Johnson or Poles talking about any other injured players like that. We just heard Ben Johnson say that “ALMOST every player” that is injured is trying hard to get back on the field. That certainly seems like a shot at Gordon. At this point, with the Bears clearly frustrated, is it time to question Gordon’s motivation to get back on the field? Like I said at the top, questioning an injury with a player is almost always bad business. I think 19 times out of 20 (maybe more), you find out that you didn’t have all the information and the player was more hurt than anyone realized (sometimes coaching staffs included). But let’s go back to Nate Davis. And now, I am not saying Gordon is Davis. But Davis clearly didn’t want to play football. Davis got through his rookie contract, signed a contract that earned him $20 million guaranteed with the Bears, and at that point, decided to do the bare minimum to fulfil his contract so he could collect his money. At this point, we know Davis was released in November of 2024, and he hasn’t even sniffed a tryout with another team. Davis is a good enough player that teams would absolutely bring him in for a tryout if he was interested. He clearly is not. Is that Gordon’s situation? I have a hard time believing that. Gordon has played hard in plenty of football games and has never come across that way. But Gordon was paid in August of 2025, and since then, not only has he barely played, he’s barely practiced. Ryan Poles is frustrated. Ben Johnson is frustrated. Chicago Bears fans are frustrated. Is it fair to question Gordon’s motivations and wonder if he’s lost his drive to play now that he has a contract that guarantees him $31 million? We’ve seen more and more players retire at younger ages once they get the guaranteed money from their second contract. Heck, Drew Dalman only got through one of his two guaranteed years before he decided to hang it up. Has Kyler Gordon quietly quit? I certainly hope not, and I’m not there yet, but I have to admit, the thought is now creeping into my mind. I don’t like that it has, but it’s almost impossible at this point not to start thinking it’s a possibility. For now, we wait. We see if Gordon gets on the field in the regular season, and we see how hard he’s playing and how effective he is. If this dance continues throughout the season, every Bears fan is going to have the same thought. If Gordon gets on the field and plays 12 or 13 games and looks good in the process, we are all going to put this behind us. To me, I’m starting to wonder if this is similar to the Derrick Rose situation with the Bulls. Rose, post injury, was very honest about how he approached injuries and how he wasn’t willing to punish his body if it meant the possibility that his body breaks down in the future when he’s in his 50s and 60s. That frustrated Bulls fans, but when Rose was on the court, he was 100% committed to being on the court. It was how he approached his recovery that was frustrating. Is Gordon the same? Only time will tell, but as for now, I’m just wondering if it’s time to question Kyler Gordon?

title: Chicago Bears Question of the Day: Which Historical Roster Cut Stung the Most?
summary: Chicago Bears fans are some of the most loyal fans you will ever find. We love our players, and that includes backups, undrafted free agents, practice squad players, and even former players (we miss you, DJ!) But one thing I have noticed about emotions is that the highs are matched by the lows. No better […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - AUGUST 26: Trevis Gipson #99 of the Chicago Bears celebrates with Terrell Lewis #52 after forcing a fumble against the Buffalo Bills during the first half of a preseason game at Soldier Field on August 26, 2023 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Chicago Bears fans are some of the most loyal fans you will ever find. We love our players, and that includes backups, undrafted free agents, practice squad players, and even former players (we miss you, DJ!) But one thing I have noticed about emotions is that the highs are matched by the lows. No better reminder of that than roster cuts. Right?! With teams required to make cuts to get down to 53-man rosters this Sunday at 5:00 pm CST, it got me thinking about which players I hope make the cut. Then my mind went to which cut stands out above the rest over the years, which is my question to you all! Since you have been a fan of the Bears, which roster cut was the hardest one to witness? A few camp legends come to mind. Devin Aromashadu, who eventually made the team at WR, as did another camp hero, Dane Sanzenbacher, but others like OLB James Vaughters were not so lucky. Terrell Lewis is another whom I thought earned his roster spot, only to get released at cutdown day, with Trevis Gipson soon to follow. Tanner Gentry, Daniel Braverman, MyCole Pruitt, Armanti Edwards, Tom Zbikowski, Harvey Unga, Josh Beekman, Brandon Rideau, and even our own Ryan Poles were also notable cuts at the end of camp. But the hardest one for me to stomach was Terrell Lewis in 2023. We entered that year with a glaring hole at edge rusher despite signing free-agent Yannick Ngakoue that offseason to a 1-year, $10.5 million deal and eventually trading a future 2nd-round pick for Montez Sweat. But why cut Lewis? He was on fire that pre-season and led the league in sacks and forced fumbles. He would go on to practice for the Eagles but not play another down professionally, so clearly Chicago wasn’t the only one to deem him unworthy of a roster spot, but man – he was looking good for us all camp. What about you? Who comes to mind as far as one of the most difficult roster cuts of all time?

title: Final Chicago Bears 53-man roster prediction
summary: The Bears’ initial 53-man roster will be announced in just a few days, and trying to project this one is rather difficult. Most of the main positions are mostly settled, but there are several players dealing with injuries, so trying to figure out how the Bears plan to maneuver those players so they can get […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 22: The Chicago Bears offense huddles during the preseason game between the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Bears’ initial 53-man roster will be announced in just a few days, and trying to project this one is rather difficult. Most of the main positions are mostly settled, but there are several players dealing with injuries, so trying to figure out how the Bears plan to maneuver those players so they can get everyone to their designated injury list is a bit more challenging. Here’s my best guess as to how the 53-man roster looks on Sunday (* are explained in the comments for each group) Quarterback (3): Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum Why burn words on the most straightforward group at any position on the team? Running Back (4): D’Andre Swift, Kyle Monangai, Salvon Ahmed, Roschon Johnson I think most projections here will be three running backs. I’m going to go with four thanks to Ozzy Trapilo (more on that later). I think Ahmed makes the team as the third running back and Roschon finishes out his contract playing largely on special teams. Wide Receiver (6): Rome Odunze, Luther Burden, Kalif Raymond, Jahdae Walker, Zavion Thomas, Kaden Davis Based on how the Bears have signed multiple veteran wide receivers, I get the idea they want to keep 6 on the roster. I think the top 5 are pretty straightforward, and I think with a strong camp, Kaden Davis makes the roster this year and the Bears see if Davis has finally found a home after being quite the nomad to start his career. Tight End (3): Colston Loveland, Cole Kmet, Sam Roush This one is about as straightforward as the QB room. Offensive Line (9): Braxton Jones, Joe Thuney, Garrett Bradbury, Jonah Jackson, Darnell Wright, Logan Jones, Luke Newman, Jordan McFadden, Theo Benedet Alright, so with this one, you’ll see that Ozzy Trapilo is missing. The Bears are allowed to move two players directly to IR without playing the “put them on the original 53, and then move them to IR the next day and bring back someone you just cut” game. I say they do that with Trapilo. I think based on the struggles of Amegadjie and Wills, it’s just time to let them go and use Benedet as the swing tackle until Trapilo can return. When Trapilo gets back, if the offense is fully healthy, that’s when I would look at Roschon Johnson potentially getting released, but odds are, there will be more injuries to the team because, well, it’s the NFL. Special Teams (3): Cairo Santos, Tory Taylor, Beau Gardner With Luke Elkin gone, this room is already set. Defensive Ends (6/5): Montez Sweat, Austin Booker, Daniel Hardy, Marcus Davenport, Jamree Kromah, Shemar Turner* The defense is certainly trickier than the offense, but let’s take a shot. With this group, I think Turner is moved to the injured list but not with one of those two initial spots, which means he’s going to have to be placed on the 53 and moved the next day. I think the Bears initially keep 6 here with the idea that it’s actually a 5-person room. Sweat and Austin, of course, are here. Hardy is a great special teamer and has been getting rotations with the 1s. Kromah has flashed enough that I think they give him a shot, and I can’t see the Bears bringing in Davenport just to let him go before the season starts. Defensive Tackles (5): Grady Jarrett, Gervon Dexter, Dayo Odeyingbo, Neville Gallimore, Jordan van den Berg For this exercise, we’ve moved Odeyingbo inside. The Bears really seem to want to try him as an interior pass rusher, so we will call him that for this purpose. I don’t know if Dexter is on the block or if the agent is just trying to drum up interest to try and get his client a bigger payday, but I think he’s here still on Sunday. Gallimore, of course, makes it, as does van den Berg. It does mean there is no room for Kentavius Street. Linebackers (5): Devin Bush, TJ Edwards, D’Marco Jackson, Keyshaun Elliott, Ruben Hyppolite I think this room is pretty straightforward. Noah Sewell is in the final year of his contract and hasn’t been on the field, and I just don’t see a spot for Jack Sanborn. Hyppolite could be gone, but I doubt the Bears go another direction after just one season. I think he gets another year to show improvement. The other four aren’t going anywhere. Cornerbacks (5/6): Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad, Josh Blackwell, Jaylon Jones, Dontae Manning* Here we see Kyler Gordon missing because I think he, like Trapilo, gets moved immediately to IR when the initial 53 comes out. I think Manning is initially released but is brought back as the 6th CB once they can move Turner over to the injured list. I think Terell Smith misses making the team this year after countless years struggling to stay healthy. Safeties (4): Dillon Thieneman, Cam Lewis, Xavier Woods, Elijah Hicks*, Skyler Thomas* No Coby Bryant here, and a banged-up Elijah Hicks makes this an interesting group. I think the Bears initially keep Hicks on the 53 and release Thomas, but swap them 24 hours later, with Hicks moving to the injured list and Thomas coming back onto the 53. IR/PUP (4): Kyler Gordon, Ozzy Trapilo, Shemar Turner* , Elijah Hicks* With this group, as I’ve mentioned in previous paragraphs, Gordon and Trapilo immediately move to IR, and Turner and Hicks get transferred to the injured list after initial cuts.

full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Kentrel Bullock #31 of the Cincinnati Bengals runs the ball against Isaiah Bolden #49 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the fourth quarter of a preseason game at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals mean business this year. And it showed in how they carried themselves in preseason games. After defeating the Chicago Bears 27-9, the Bengals went out last night and beat the Philadelphia Eagles 30-13. They finished 3-0 in the preseason. Here’s what we learned from the win over the Eagles (or, in some cases, what it solidified). Josh Johnson will land somewhere He may be 40 years old, but Johnson can still sling it, as evidenced by his last two outings for the Bengals in preseason wins over the Bears and Eagles. Johnson was composed, accurate, and efficient in those two games after a rough start in the preseason opener against the Detroit Lions. Engage 8 in the PRESEASON?? 😂 Josh Johnson handling it like 19-year vet pic.twitter.com/Y3MrkRR0UH — Coach Dan Casey (@CoachDanCasey) August 23, 2026 Though he won’t land on the opening roster, he, at the very least, deserves a spot on the practice squad, though it’s likely another team will snatch him up, especially after a QB goes down. Whew🔥🔥🔥🔥 Jamal Haynes👀 pic.twitter.com/cKNTthusIK — James Rapien (@JamesRapien) August 29, 2026 These are all great signs. And he seems to have done that again in Cincinnati. Nice play here by Bengals rookie cornerback Tacario Davis. He was 1-on-1 with Eagles first round pick Makai Lemon🏈 pic.twitter.com/oVvWvNSoJT — James Rapien (@JamesRapien) August 29, 2026 Those young players will get to team with the veterans the team brought in through free agency, who have all shown flashes of what they can do for the Bengals in practice and the preseason. title: 3 draft-eligible prospects to watch this weekend as college football begins
summary: Week 0 of the college football season begins this Saturday. While there aren’t any marquee matchups this week, 14th-ranked USC will be in action against San Jose State. There will also be a handful of other prospects to pay attention to spread throughout the seven other games of the weekend. Arguably the best game could […]
full_text: Jul 24, 2025; Las Vegas, NV, USA; USC offensive lineman Elijah Paige speaks to the media during the Big Ten NCAA college football media days at Mandalay Bay Resort. Mandatory Credit: Lucas Peltier-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Week 0 of the college football season begins this Saturday. While there aren’t any marquee matchups this week, 14th-ranked USC will be in action against San Jose State. There will also be a handful of other prospects to pay attention to spread throughout the seven other games of the weekend. Arguably the best game could be NC State versus Virginia. Virginia played in the ACC title game, and NC State returns a dynamic quarterback in CJ Bailey. Let’s take a look at a few draft-eligible prospects worth watching this weekend. Elijah Paige The Bengals have questions about the swing tackle position heading into the 2026 season. There are really even some questions about the starting left tackle spot going forward as Orlando Brown Jr. will be turning 31 years old after this season. Elijah Paige is a left tackle prospect for the USC Trojans. The 6’7” 315 pound prospect finished the 2025 season with an 84.0 pass blocking grade. He plays with a wide base, is quick out of his stance off of the snap, and allowed just six total pressures through the seven games he played last season. Lower body injuries plagued him throughout the season though, ultimately shutting him down early. He will need to improve as a run blocker, grading out with a 60.2 last year. He also lunged quite often which led to him missing his intended target when getting out in space as a run blocker. There are traits worth monitoring here, and he is just now entering his redshirt junior season. Elijah Paige (#72) USC ✅ Size at 6’7” and 325 pounds ✅ Recovery athleticism ✅ Quickness off the snap ✅ Allowed just 6 pressures and 0 sacks in 7 games played during 2025 ✅ 84.0 pass blocking grade in 2025 pic.twitter.com/AsOqRE6nbf — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) May 31, 2026 Xavier Chaplin Sticking with offensive tackle prospects, Chaplin fits the mold of the size Cincinnati typically covets in an offensive tackle prospect. A transfer from Auburn, Chaplin will be playing for Florida State in 2026. He was recently listed at 6’6” and 346 pounds. He is a massive player at tackle who moves fairly well for a player with that size. While the size, athleticism, and finishing mentality are all positives, his footwork has been a mess. Hopefully he will be able to clean that up, along with playing with better pad level consistency in 2026. He will also need to clean up the penalties, recording 12 of them during the 2025 season. As of now, this could be a day-three type of prospect that the Bengals could target as a future swing tackle. Chaplin and his Florida State teammates will kick off the season against New Mexico State on Saturday night. Xavier Chaplin (#65) Florida State ✅ Massive frame at 6’7” 338 pounds ✅ Arm length ✅ Over 2,200 career snaps played ✅ Good overall athleticism ✅ Upper-body strength pic.twitter.com/H6cnjpqAHU — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) June 8, 2026 McKale Boley A clean sweep of offensive tackle prospects for whom I will be watching the closest this weekend in college football. Boley is a 6’5”, 329-pound left tackle for Virginia. He is an experienced player, entering the season having already played over 2,300 total snaps. Boley is an athletic offensive tackle, having been clocked at 19 miles per hour on the GPS data tracking system. He comes from NFL bloodlines, with his father Michael playing nine seasons in the NFL at linebacker. I thought Boley struggled at times handling power into his chest, and he had difficulty connecting with his target out in space. This is an experienced day three prospect, and there is a world where the Bengals could double dip at the offensive tackle position during the 2027 NFL Draft. It should be an exciting game as Boley and Virginia take on NC State Saturday at 3:30 pm. McKale Boley (6’5 325) Virginia ✅ Wide base in pass protection ✅ Over 2,300 career snaps played ✅ Father played 9 seasons in the NFL ✅ Just 1 penalty during 2025 season ✅ 70.2 pass block grade in 2025 pic.twitter.com/NnlctiotiD — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 9, 2026

title: The preseason is over for the Bengals: Here’s what you need to know for the waiver process
summary: The preseason and training camp are over for the Cincinnati Bengals. With final roster cuts coming, the Bengals will place several players on waivers and could potentially snag other players from the waiver wire. Teams will have until Sunday, August 30th to trim their final rosters to 53 players. How the NFL waiver wire works […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Erik Ezukanma #49 of the Philadelphia Eagles is tackled by Bralyn Lux #21 of the Cincinnati Bengals in the first quarter of a preseason game at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The preseason and training camp are over for the Cincinnati Bengals . With final roster cuts coming, the Bengals will place several players on waivers and could potentially snag other players from the waiver wire. Teams will have until Sunday, August 30th to trim their final rosters to 53 players. How the NFL waiver wire works Preseason & First 3 Weeks: The priority follows the previous April’s draft order. For example, the Bengals picked 10th in the 2026 NFL Draft, so they currently sit 10th on the waiver wire. After Week 3: Once every team has played four regular-season games, the waiver wire order changes, placing teams in order by record. So the team with the worst record at that point will be at the top of the order, with the best record last. Eligibility: Players with less than four accrued seasons in the NFL are subject to waivers upon release. Players with over four seasons in the league are immediately free agents and can sign with any team. When a team claims a player, they absorb all of the contract that player had with their previous team. Teams will typically have 24 hours to claim a player once they are waived. If the player does not get picked up in the allotted timeframe, they will become an unrestricted free agent. ——————————————————————————— Check out 2026 NFL season odds at FanDuel Sportsbook . ——————————————————————————— The Bengals aren’t historically active on the waiver wire, but with questions at backup offensive tackle, they could have their eye on the transactions around the league. Some think the Bengals should look for a third running back as well. Time will tell what final cuts will look like for the Bengals and how active they could be with waived players. With all eyes on the September 13th opener, the team should be looking to improve the roster however they can.

title: The Bengals have some very good problems to solve before final cuts
summary: For years, one of the biggest questions surrounding the Cincinnati Bengals has been whether the team has enough depth behind its established stars. That question feels a lot different heading into 2026. After finishing the preseason with a perfect 3-0 record, capped by Friday night’s convincing 30-13 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, the Bengals have […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Cincinnati Bengals running back Jamal Haynes (24) walks off the field after the preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images For years, one of the biggest questions surrounding the Cincinnati Bengals has been whether the team has enough depth behind its established stars. That question feels a lot different heading into 2026. After finishing the preseason with a perfect 3-0 record, capped by Friday night’s convincing 30-13 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, the Bengals have something that NFL teams generally don’t complain about: too many players making legitimate cases for roster spots. That’s not to say Cincinnati’s roster is perfect. There are still questions to answer before the 53-man roster is finalized, and some players who have performed well this summer are inevitably going to wind up on the outside looking in. But that’s precisely what makes this year’s preseason so encouraging. As we discussed on the Orange & Black Insider, several of Cincinnati’s most difficult roster decisions aren’t necessarily the result of a lack of talent. They’re the result of the Bengals having more viable options than available spots. And the preseason finale against Philadelphia only reinforced that point. The defensive line might be the biggest “good problem” It’s difficult to find a position group that has changed more dramatically than Cincinnati’s defensive line. The Bengals entered the offseason needing to improve their interior pass rush and overall defensive-front depth. They responded by adding significant veteran talent, including Dexter Lawrence, while continuing to develop younger players such as Kris Jenkins, McKinnley Jackson, and others. Then came the emergence of players such as Landon Robinson. Suddenly, Cincinnati has a defensive line where some talented players could find themselves fighting simply to make the roster. The preseason finale offered another glimpse of that depth. Isaiah Foskey and Antwaun Powell-Ryland combined for a sack on Philadelphia’s opening possession, with Powell-Ryland getting credit for the sack after the play. The Bengals’ defense consistently disrupted the Eagles early, holding Philadelphia without a touchdown until well into the second half. Foskey, in particular, has made a strong case throughout the preseason. That’s the kind of competition Cincinnati desperately needed. A year ago, the questions may have been whether the Bengals had enough pass-rush depth, as well as concerns surrounding the secondary and offensive line. Now the question is: Who doesn’t make the team? That’s a considerably better problem. Dohnte Meyers may have eliminated one of the biggest roster questions Few players have benefited more from the preseason than Dohnte Meyers. He entered training camp as a relatively unknown player who was trying to establish himself after playing in the CFL. However, he leaves the preseason looking like a player the Bengals would be taking an enormous risk by trying to sneak onto the practice squad. Meyers played early on Friday night, but he made it count and exited early as well. The receiver caught three passes for 51 yards on three targets, accounting for 51 of Cincinnati’s 60 yards on its opening drive. His catches went for nine, 17 and 25 yards. Then the Bengals wisely took him out. Meyers finished the preseason with 11 catches for 121 yards, while also contributing 22 rushing yards, 54 kickoff-return yards and 45 punt-return yards during the preseason. At some point, the question stopped being whether Meyers could make the roster. Now it’s more about how Cincinnati plans to use him. And that creates another good problem. The final receiver spots could be extremely difficult Meyers isn’t the only player who has made things complicated. Ke’Shawn Williams caught a touchdown pass from Sean Clifford in the second half Friday night, while Charlie Jones continued to demonstrate his value as a returner and receiver. Jones had a 31-yard punt return and caught two passes for 36 yards against Philadelphia. Williams, meanwhile, caught the 11-yard touchdown from Clifford, providing another significant moment in a preseason filled with competition for the final receiver spots. Then there are Mitchell Tinsley, Charlie Jones, Andre Iosivas, and the other receivers who have been competing for roles behind Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. The Bengals don’t simply have to determine who can catch passes. They have to consider: Who contributes on special teams? Who can play multiple receiver positions? Who blocks? Who can return kicks or punts? Who has the most developmental upside? Who can help immediately if an injury strikes? That’s why this isn’t simply a statistical competition. It’s a roster-construction puzzle. And the Bengals have several pieces that could fit. Josh Johnson and Sean Clifford have made the quarterback decision fascinating Perhaps no player has done more to complicate an otherwise straightforward roster decision than Josh Johnson. The Bengals entered camp with Joe Burrow and Joe Flacco firmly established as the top two quarterbacks. The question was whether Cincinnati would keep a third quarterback on the 53-man roster or attempt to develop one on the practice squad. Johnson has made that decision considerably more difficult. The 40-year-old veteran started the preseason finale and completed 12 of 19 passes for 156 yards, helping Cincinnati put nine points on the board during his first-half appearance. He had also already made a strong impression against Chicago, throwing for 156 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ second preseason game. Then there’s Sean Clifford, who took over in the second half against Philadelphia and led three scoring drives, including a touchdown pass to Williams. He also looked solid against the Bears. The Bengals probably don’t want to devote a 53-man roster spot to both (or maybe even one of them, despite the recent roster rule change on the position). But the fact that this is even a legitimate debate is another sign of the depth Cincinnati has accumulated. The tight end room is another fascinating puzzle The Bengals also have an unusually deep collection of tight ends. Mike Gesicki remains a legitimate receiving threat. Drew Sample provides veteran blocking and versatility. Tanner Hudson has been a productive depth option. Jack Endries flashed during the preseason opener. And, perhaps most importantly, Erick All is attempting to return to the field and establish himself as another weapon. The Bengals don’t necessarily need one player to dominate this position. They can potentially use the different skill sets to create matchup problems. A healthy All could give Cincinnati another athletic option who can line up in different places, while Gesicki’s receiving ability creates another target for Joe Burrow. The question isn’t necessarily whether Cincinnati has enough talent at tight end. It’s how many of them the Bengals can realistically keep. The secondary has quietly created another roster battle The preseason finale also provided another strong showing from rookie cornerback Tacario Davis. Davis broke up a pass on Philadelphia’s opening possession and later intercepted Tanner McKee after the ball bounced off Makai Lemon. He also made a strong tackle against Carson Steele and finished with four tackles and an interception. That’s another position where Cincinnati appears to have developed meaningful depth. Davis isn’t the only young corner competing for playing time, either. The Bengals have veterans and young players battling for the final spots, while special teams contributions could ultimately determine which players survive the final cuts. And again, that’s the theme. It’s not necessarily: “Do the Bengals have enough corners?” It’s: “Which corners deserve to be here?”…

full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Landon Robinson (96) runs onto the field before the preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. With the preseason finale against the Philadelphia Eagles over , the Bengals will soon have to determine which players from their crowded roster have done enough to earn a spot on the 53-man roster — and which ones will be looking for work elsewhere. There is plenty of reason for optimism around Cincinnati entering the 2026 season. Joe Burrow is healthy, the offense has its familiar collection of elite weapons, and the Bengals have made significant investments in rebuilding the defense, most notably with the additions of Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen. That optimism is reflected in the current betting market, too. FanDuel currently lists Cincinnati at +170 to win the AFC North, +900 to win the AFC Championship, and +2000 to win Super Bowl LXI. The Bengals are also -196 to make the playoffs and -165 to win more than 9.5 games. ——————————————————————————— FanDuel Sportsbook’s latest NFL odds ——————————————————————————— Of course, none of those expectations make roster decisions any easier. The Bengals have several position groups with legitimate competition for the final few spots, and some players who appeared relatively safe entering training camp may now face a much less certain future. Below, we’ll keep track of the Bengals’ roster cuts as they happen, along with some of the more notable surprises and decisions. Cincinnati Bengals 2026 Roster Cuts Tracker OFFENSE Quarterback Cut: — Surprise: — Notes: — Running Back Cut: — Surprise: — Notes: — Wide Receiver Cut: — Surprise: — Notes: — Tight End Cut: — Surprise: — Notes: — Offensive Line Cut: — Surprise: — Notes: — DEFENSE Defensive Line Cut: — Surprise: — Notes: — Edge Rusher Cut: — Surprise: — Notes: — Linebacker Cut: — Surprise: — Notes: — Cornerback Cut: — Surprise: — Notes: — Safety Cut: — Surprise: — Notes: — SPECIAL TEAMS Kicker Cut: — Notes: — Punter Cut: — Notes: — Long Snapper Cut: — Notes: — Notable Roster Decisions to Watch While the final cuts will ultimately determine the 53-man roster, there are already several players who have emerged as names worth watching as Cincinnati works through its decisions. Tahj Brooks: The former Texas Tech running back hasn’t necessarily shown enough to make his roster spot feel completely secure. With competition at running back and the Bengals having other options available, Brooks could be one of the more interesting decisions. T.J. Slaton: Cincinnati’s offseason additions along the defensive interior have created a fascinating numbers game. Slaton has plenty of NFL experience and could very well make the roster, but the Bengals have added significant competition to a position group that could force a difficult decision. Mitchell Tinsley: Tinsley’s recent emergence has made the wide receiver competition considerably more interesting. If he continues to show the ability to contribute on offense and special teams, he could force the Bengals to make a tough decision elsewhere. Charlie Jones: Jones has plenty of experience in the Bengals’ offense and has been a valuable return option, but the emergence of Tinsley, Dohnte Meyers, and Ke’Shawn Williams has made the receiver/returner competition one to monitor closely. Jack Endries: Endries is another player who has made the roster conversation more interesting. The tight end competition is crowded, and the Bengals will have to determine how many players they want to carry at the position versus using those roster spots elsewhere. The Final Roster Is Coming Into Focus The next several days should provide the Bengals’ coaching staff with its final opportunity to evaluate players before the regular season begins. While some roster spots have essentially been decided, the bottom of the roster is where things become particularly fascinating. For players on the bubble, one play can make the difference between making the 53-man roster and finding themselves on the practice squad or looking for another opportunity. And for the Bengals, those decisions could prove particularly important. Cincinnati has legitimate aspirations of returning to the postseason — and perhaps making a much deeper run than that. With Burrow openly talking about manifesting a Super Bowl and the betting market giving the Bengals a legitimate chance to win the AFC North, the margin for error is getting smaller. Now comes the difficult part: Deciding which 53 players give Cincinnati its best chance to make that happen. This tracker will be updated as the Bengals make their roster decisions.

title: Jamal Haynes had a near-miraculous TD run as he pushes for a 53-man roster spot

Or could the Bengals surprise everyone and keep four running backs on the 53-man roster? In Friday’s preseason finale vs. the Philadelphia Eagles, college […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Cincinnati Bengals running back Jamal Haynes (24) walks off the field after the preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals’ third running back spot has been one many assumed would go to Tahj Brooks, but after a forgettable training camp and preseason, could someone else take that spot? Or could the Bengals surprise everyone and keep four running backs on the 53-man roster? In Friday’s preseason finale vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , college free-agent running back Jamal Haynes made a play that could make the front office at least consider keeping him on the roster or the practice squad. It truly was a sight to watch, even for a preseason game. Haynes to the house. #CINatPHI on CBS/Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/SpGkzLiQHs — Cincinnati Bengals (@Bengals) August 29, 2026 That run had everything. He danced around when the initial hole wasn’t there. He created his own cutback lane as the defense overpursued to contain him, breaking it outside. Tore through an arm tackle and took a few ankles before letting it rip to win the footrace to the end zone. Haynes has had a decent camp after coming out of Georgia Tech as an undrafted product. At only 5’7, he can certainly get lost behind that huge offensive line. However, a third or fourth running back would be relied on more for special teams as either a returner or coverage player. Maybe he catches on the Bengals’ practice squad, but he certainly will be on at least someone’s practice squad in the NFL after that one.

title: Bengals 53-man roster projection ahead of preseason finale vs. Eagles
summary: The final preseason gameday is here for the Cincinnati Bengals, who will take on the Philadelphia Eagles tonight at Lincoln Financial Field, where many players are getting their final chance to prove they belong on a 53-man roster. With that in mind, here is our latest Cincinnati Bengals 53-man roster projection! Quarterback: Joe Burrow, Joe […]
full_text: The final preseason gameday is here for the Cincinnati Bengals, who will take on the Philadelphia Eagles tonight at Lincoln Financial Field, where many players are getting their final chance to prove they belong on a 53-man roster. With that in mind, here is our latest Cincinnati Bengals 53-man roster projection! Quarterback: Joe Burrow, Joe Flacco (2) Completely straightforward with the two players who will make the Bengals’ initial 53-man roster here. The only question is whether the Bengals will keep both Josh Johnson and Sean Clifford on the 16-player practice squad. If not, which one do they end up keeping there? Running Back: Chase Brown, Samaje Perine, Tahj Brooks (3) The biggest question of this trio is Tahj Brooks. While he hasn’t really stood out running the football through two games, his blocking and receiving skills look to be improved. For now, Brooks makes the initial 53-man roster, but this could be a spot where the Bengals make a waiver claim. Tahj Brooks is penciled in as the third running back on the roster for now. While we would all like to see more explosive runs from him, I do think other areas of his game are coming along. Do you think he sticks on the 53-man roster, or will the Bengals potentially make a waiver… pic.twitter.com/pSXtD8bcaA — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 26, 2026 Wide Receiver: Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Andrei Iosivas, Colbie Young, Dohnte Meyers, Mitch Tinsley (6) The biggest question mark is the last spot at the position. They could decide to keep Charlie Jones as the primary returner. They could opt for Ke’Shawn Williams in that spot, and potentially float Jones out as a trade candidate for a late-round pick swap. Or they could go with Tinsley as I did here. I don’t think he has had a major standout performance like last preseason, but Burrow knows he has made plays for him in the past, and that could ultimately help him claim the final spot. In this scenario, Meyers is the primary returner. Tight End: Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample, Erick All Jr., Tanner Hudson, Jack Endries (5) The Bengals kept five tight ends last year, and I think they will do the same again this year. If it comes down to keeping just four, both Hudson and Endries have made cases for earning that final spot. They could opt for the proven veteran or the young rookie with upside. Ultimately, I think they keep both. Offensive Line: Orlando Brown Jr., Dylan Fairchild, Ted Karras, Dalton Risner, Amarius Mims, Brian Parker II, Connor Lew, Jalen Rivers, Javon Foster (9) The uncertainty at the swing tackle position could force them to keep both Rivers and Foster for now. If that happens, Jacob Bayer is the biggest snub for making the 53-man roster. He has been really impressive during the preseason. He can play both guard and center for the Bengals, and would be a prime candidate to sign back to the practice squad if he goes unclaimed on waivers. Defensive Line: Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, Dexter Lawrence, Myles Murphy, Cashius Howell, BJ Hill, Shemar Stewart, TJ Slaton, Kris Jenkins, Cedric Johnson, Landon Robinson (11) Unless there is a Kris Jenkins trade, the Bengals will go heavy with 11 defensive linemen. Landon Robinson has earned his spot on the roster and should be active on game days. My biggest question is whether they decide to put Shemar Stewart on IR to start the season. If that happens, it would open the door for Isaiah Foskey to make the 53-man roster. Landon Robinson with another standout performance on Saturday night. pic.twitter.com/4bOMXTp9RU — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 23, 2026 Linebacker: Barrett Carter, Demetrius Knight Jr., Swayze Bozeman, Oren Burks (4) Going heavy at tight end and defensive line would mean another position would have to go light. The position could end up being at linebacker. I have Joe Giles-Harris just missing the 53-man roster in this projection. If they keep five linebackers, he is on it. They could also start him on the practice squad and call him up early in the season. He has been an integral member of our special teams units. There are other good practice squad candidates at the position, including Liam Anderson and Jack Dingle. Cornerback: DJ Turner, Dax Hill, Jalen Davis, Tacario Davis, DJ Ivey, Ja’Sir Taylor (6) I could make an argument for Bralyn Lux or Josh Newton to nab the final cornerback spot, but the Bengals feel strongly about Taylor as the backup slot corner behind Jalen Davis. Taylor played solid during preseason game two, and likely solidified his spot on the Bengals’ 53-man roster. Safety: Bryan Cook, Jordan Battle, Kyle Dugger, PJ Jules (4) While Jules has had some struggles with coverage, he is making this 53-man roster for his special-teams ability. He will likely be the leader of that unit this season, and the Bengals had him serve as a captain during the game against the Bears. Russ Yeast will likely start the season on the practice squad behind these four players. PJ Jules has had some struggles in coverage, but what he provides on special teams is why he should be on this roster. pic.twitter.com/kSqFypt3Op — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 23, 2026 Specialists: P Ryan Rehkow, K Evan McPherson, LS William Wagner (3) No decisions to be made here. These spots are locked up for the foreseeable future.

full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 22: Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Landon Robinson (96) walks off the field at the end of the preseason game between the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tonight marks the Cincinnati Bengals’ final preseason game, as they’re set to take on the Eagles in Philly. We already know the starters won’t play, but plenty of young guys and roster-bubble players will be putting their blood, sweat, and tears into this game. Many of the guys who will play in this game for both sides will have serious job uncertainty by Sunday evening (6 PM ET), when teams officially have to cut down to 53 men. Then comes the flurry of calls for practice squads or possibly spots on other teams’ rosters. The most stressful game of musical chairs, where if you are left without a seat, you likely have to focus on staying in football shape, hoping to get a call, or call it quits on your dream. People will diminish this game, but truthfully, it will be the last time so many guys in the NFL suit up and get a shot until next offseason, if at all. Players like wide receiver Dohntae Meyers and defensive tackle Landon Robinson going off and showing they belong on an NFL roster is what this time of year is all about. However, as one story rises, we often see the end of another. Someone like Charlie Jones or Mitchell Tinsley — who was a preseason darling himself last year with some highlights during the regular season— could find themselves on a different roster or sitting on the practice squad. It is a numbers game at the end of the day. You can only keep so many wide receivers, tight ends or defensive tackles. And players know the harsh truth that this is a business at the end of the day. It is just one of those times to remember that the players who aren’t the Joe Burrows or Ja’Marr Chases of the NFL are closer to their dream being over at the drop of a hat than many of us realize. Who was the player you were rooting for the most this offseason, or who do you think is going to be the most surprising cut come Sunday? Bengals News What to Watch For | Bengals at Eagles Preseason Week 3 Some other young O-lineman have made a strong impression on Taylor and the coaching staff through training camp, including fourth-round draft pick Connor Lew, who spent the early portion of camp recovering from a knee injury but started at center against the Bears. According to Taylor, Lew has made up for the valuable time lost while finishing his rehab. Another strong vote of confidence in Lew from the head coach. There is no question this guy will likely be the first man up if something happens at guard. Marvin Lewis says ‘Mike Brown doesn’t give a (expletive) about money’ “His words trigger action,” Lewis said. “No question in my mind, they trigger action, because (Brown) loves quarterbacks and he wants to win in the worst way.” Well worth a listen to the interview. It feels like Lewis has not really talked in depth about his experience with the Bengals. Him talking about Burrow’s word triggering actions is interesting in particular. One Bengals Offseason Acquisition Itching to Start 2026 Season “I’m buzzing with a lot of excitement right now,” Cook said when talking about taking the field for the first time as a member of his hometown team this season. Safe to say most Bengals fans are also buzzing with excitement. Hopefully replacing Geno Stone with Cook offers a better result on the back end of the defense. NFL News NFL Network: Seahawks, DT Leonard Williams agree to three-year, $90M extension Somewhere down the line Dexter Lawrence is going to need paid. Whether the team is willing to go that high for someone entering their 30’s will remain to be seen, but this is a bit of a look into the future as the defensive tackle market isn’t rising as rapidly as some other positions. 2026 NFL fantasy football draft tips: 18 must-know Do’s and Don’ts Some quick advice going into your fantasy drafts. My advice, start an auction league. It is way more fun and takes more skill than simply drafting players typically. There is nothing wrong with regular drafts, but give auction a try. We have seen that it has (unfortunately) taken videos coming out for the public to show a real outcry about this kind of stuff.

title: Browns 53-man roster prediction: Last 4 in, last 4 out
summary: The Cleveland Browns finished their 2026 exhibition schedule on a high note by having their second-and third-string guys demolish the New England Patriots. The contest gave both coaching staffs an idea of who to cut and who to keep. None of the projected starters played, with the exception of the special teams guys. RELATED: BROWNS […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 10: Michael Burton #34 of the Cleveland Browns catches a pass during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 10, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns finished their 2026 exhibition schedule on a high note by having their second-and third-string guys demolish the New England Patriots . The contest gave both coaching staffs an idea of who to cut and who to keep. None of the projected starters played, with the exception of the special teams guys. RELATED: BROWNS CUT TRACKER Now for the difficult part of being an NFL head coach: cutting players. Training camp involves 90 players. On August 30, that roster has to be pared down to 53 guys. It used to be in increments. On the first cut, the roster was down to 75. The cut to 62, and then finally to 53. It made for a lot of drama. But now? That’s a lot of athletes calling their agent to see if some other team put in a waiver claim for them. Who to release, and who to retain? There are rumors that the Browns coaching staff wants to keep all four of their quarterbacks . That is highly unusual because only one plays in every game. After the starter, Deshaun Watson, the remainder in the room are all developmental first-and second-year guys. Yikes. No wily, seasoned veteran to lean on, like when Baker Mayfield had Casey Keenum, or when Deshaun Watson was on suspension, the roster had Jacoby Brissett. By keeping four QBs, this means the roster will release a tight end, a cornerback, or a defensive line player instead. A larger yikes. Every Browns media outlet will give their list of what the final 53 will look like, as DBN did . Today, we are just going to predict who the final four guys the coaching staff will keep, and the four last bubble guys they bumped off. Last four in FB Michael Burton Burton was used in the preseason more as another tight end/H-back than a traditional fullback, although he did line up occasionally in the backfield. He is strictly a blocker, but was thrown to a few times in the Patriots preseason game. Head coach Todd Monken likes having a fullback. The team was expected to draft one but didn’t, so Burton signed. By keeping him, the tight end room can become three players instead of four. WR Luke Floriea This one was tight. Floriea had a great preseason. So did Malachi Corley and Greg Larvadain. Maybe the coaching staff sees Floriea as their very own Wes Welker who will take some slot reps. Hard to tell, but he played well when his number was called, and is a good blocker downfield. S Donovan McMillon McMillon is a missile on special teams on kickoff and punt coverage teams. And he does get defensive snaps as well. He is a willing tackler. His special teams play was commendable, which is enough to earn a roster spot in that role with potential upside defensively. CB Michael Coats, Jr. He was signed with a $100,000 guarantee and showed he can ball out as an undrafted rookie. Runs a 4.41. He has had an ankle injury during the first preseason game, and now a second leg injury has arisen. But he has shown quite a bit in training camp. If he can remain healthy, the coaching staff could believe that Coats can provide good depth plus value on special teams. He may not play right away, but once he heals, he should become an asset. Last four out TE Joe Royer Yeah, the coaching staff had high hopes for Royer. He hasn’t been placed on any list – yet. He could end up on the final roster, and then be added to some sort of list, and then get back one guy they wanted to keep. It has happened before. Nobody but the front office seems to know what personal issues Royer is dealing with. WR Malachi Corley Just a numbers game, and Floriea had three to none. That is three touchdown catches to zero for Corley. If he clears waivers, the Browns will get him back to the practice squad and perhaps bring him up as a returner. The coaching staff really likes this guy. Plus, Greg Larvadain has offered more as a returner. S Daniel Thomas The question concerning the fourth safety was: is it going to be Chris Edmonds or Donovan McMillon? Edmonds is already gone, and there is no competition for Thomas to beat out McMillon. Too many players in the room, which most likely sends him to the practice squad. If the coaching staff retains five safeties, then Thomas would become that choice. DE Sam Kamara The Browns keep going back to Kamara like a security blanket since 2022, in that he can play outside or slide into the middle. He has been on the practice squad six times, released five times, and promoted to the roster on six different stints. This will even out all numbers to six with his release once again. title: Browns QB room: Patriots game enough to secure roster spots?
summary: The Cleveland Browns’ final preseason game against the New England Patriots allowed both Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green to make their case for a spot on the initial 53-man roster. Gabriel brings experience to the table, having played at multiple college programs and appeared in several games during the 2025 season. Green is coming in as […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns’ final preseason game against the New England Patriots allowed both Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green to make their case for a spot on the initial 53-man roster . Gabriel brings experience to the table, having played at multiple college programs and appeared in several games during the 2025 season. Green is coming in as the rookie looking to show that there are enough tools there that could develop into a competent NFL quarterback. Gabriel started in this matchup and put up a solid performance. He completed 12 of his 15 passes for 186 yards with three touchdowns. Green took over at quarterback in the second half and completed five passes for 27 yards. Additionally, he had eight rushes for 66 yards. Both quarterbacks impressed in different ways and made an argument for why they deserve a spot on this roster. Although Gabriel is clearly the more impressive quarterback of the two, it is more likely that the rookie Green will end up getting a roster spot. Gabriel has the higher floor of the two quarterbacks, but Green is younger and possesses the physical tools that could make him an intriguing player for the team to develop. When looking at the third quarterback on the roster, it is better to look at who has higher upside and could develop into something really valuable for the team in the future. full_text: The Cleveland Browns have until Sunday at 6:00 PM ET to make roster cuts and announce their initial 53-man roster. Some of those cuts or rumors about roster moves might leak early, though. The Browns may also announce them in waves — for example, some cuts may be announced Friday, some on Saturday, etc. All players who are released with less than four years of service must go through waivers and are eligible to be claimed by any other team until 1:00 PM ET on Monday . After that, any unclaimed player can be signed and teams will begin to fill out their 16-man practice squads. Veterans with more than four years of service can sign immediately after being released. You can also use the comments section to discuss cuts around the NFL that may be of interest to Cleveland. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 225/1 odds to win the Super Bowl, heading into final roster cuts. Browns Roster Cuts Live Blog Friday (August 28, 2026) 3:36 PM: By my count, the Browns are now down to 73 players, meaning they have 20 moves remaining to get down to 53 players by Sunday at 6:00 pm ET. I’m not sure if there will be any more moves today, but my current guess is that the remaining moves will be announced tomorrow. What you might start hearing, before that official news release, are player’s agents leaking that “so and so has been informed that they have made the 53 man roster,” or some sources indicating that a particular player has been notified that they’ll be cut. Going back to the first batch of cuts below, none of them are a surprise. Avery was a guy on my 53-man roster, but he was meant to be a temporary placeholder due to injury concerns; I did not expect him to be a long-term player on the roster. 3:25 PM: We have our first batch of Browns cuts: 16 moves in total (4 contracts terminated, 12 players waived). The terminated players are TE Jack Stoll (from IR), OT Tyre Phillips , CB Tre Avery , and CB Tyler Hall . The players waived are WR Ben Patterson , TE Jermaine Terry II , TE Drew Biber , OT Jeremiah Byers , OT Izavion Miller , DT Coziah Izzard , DT Patrick Jenkins , DE Jamil Muhammad , CB Jeremiah McClendon , CB Nate Evans , S Christopher Edmonds , and P Nik Constantinou . 1:24 PM: Not a reportable rumor as I don’t have a second source, but enough to at least share here as a keep-your-eyes-out kinda thing. I’ve heard that the Falcons and Chargers at least discussed a Tua trade, which could open up a spot for Dillon Gabriel in Atlanta (just as everyone joked/expected when Kevin Stefanski was hired there). – Jared 10:15 AM: Regarding the timing of the Browns’ roster cuts, Jared Mueller made a good point on one of our site’s internal communications. Head coach Todd Monken is scheduled to talk to the media at 11:00 AM ET on Saturday, with practice to follow at 12:15 PM on Saturday. It seems highly likely that the Browns will have their 53-man roster decided by then. I’ve never heard of a case where the team keeps players around for one more practice in between making their final roster cuts. 10:02 AM: Good morning, everyone! I posted my 53-man roster projection this morning. There were plenty of tough decisions at quarterback, wide receiver, tight end, and cornerback. With these potential roster cuts, news could literally hit any time between now and Sunday evening. Typically, Andrew Berry does not wait through the deadline to make cuts. We’ll keep you posted on any Browns-related news that comes in, as well as other cuts around the league. One thing to keep in mind is that the final preseason games in general takes place today, as only a few games took place Thursday evening. In general, you likely won’t see league-wide news about roster cuts until Saturday. 12:00 AM: The Browns just finished their third and final preseason game, beating the New England Patriots by a score of 37-13 . We already heard about one big roster cut on Thursday morning, as reports indicated that Cleveland was waiving WR Cedric Tillman . Tillman was going to be a cut on my 53-man roster projection anyway, due to the way things have unfolded in camp this year and the impressive nature of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston . title: Browns 53-man roster: Expect creative moves with a few vets, QB room
summary: It is quite impressive how quickly things need to turn from the Cleveland Browns final preseason game to the initial 53-man roster decisions. As we shared in our roster tracker piece, the Browns planned schedule tells us that most of their moves will be made a full 24 hours plus before the NFL’s mandate. As […]
full_text: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Tylan Wallace (16) and Cleveland Browns running back Dylan Sampson (22) run through drills during the first day of training camp, July 29, 2026, at the Cross Country Mortgage Campus in Berea, Ohio. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It is quite impressive how quickly things need to turn from the Cleveland Browns final preseason game to the initial 53-man roster decisions . As we shared in our roster tracker piece , the Browns planned schedule tells us that most of their moves will be made a full 24 hours plus before the NFL’s mandate. As always with the NFL, the details are very important when it comes to the 53-man roster. The waiver process and order can lead teams to make a myriad of decisions differently than they would. As can having veterans on one-year contracts and the flexibility that it can provide the team. Cleveland fans will remember the team doing this with OT Greg Robinson , who was the Browns starting left tackle heading into the 2019 season. Robinson was cut from the initial 53-man roster before being re-signed just a day later. The reason for the Robinson process (to get a player onto IR but not lose them for the season) is no longer a problem, but if GM Andrew Berry and HC Todd Monken want to try to keep all four quarterbacks, releasing a veteran like newly signed DE Derek Barnett , WR Tylan Wallace , and /or FB Michael Burton could be in the cards. The scenario is simple: It is rare that waived players get claimed (no matter the preseason hubbub), but those that do get claimed are generally at high-value positions like QB, OT, CB, DL, and WR. If the Browns hope to keep all four quarterbacks, waiving Dillon Gabriel or Taylen Green at the initial cutdown day could lead to a claim. Doing so a day or two later, when they would re-sign a vet they cut, like Barnett, Wallace, or Burton, would make it less likely that another team would claim them. Then Gabriel or Green could have an easier time getting to Cleveland’s practice squad. Teams don’t like claiming a player only to waive them a day later because a more important player became available. It is seen as bad business with agents and even within the team itself. A move of this sort is not certain and would not be limited to just the quarterback position. As long as the player, their agent, and the Browns are on the same page, veterans will often go along with the process and earn slightly more ($100,000 or so) when they return to the team a day or two later.
