title: Making a case for the Browns to keep WR Luke Floriea
summary: The worst position group for the Cleveland Browns last year was arguably the wide receiver group. GM Andrew Berry took on the assignment to improve this group and get them out of the hole of being ranked #32 last year. In case you are scoring at home, that is dead last.   In the April […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Wide receiver Luke Floriea #81 of the Cleveland Browns scores a touchdown against cornerback Kindle Vildor #28 of the New England Patriots in the first quarter of a preseason game at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The worst position group for the Cleveland Browns last year was arguably the wide receiver group. GM Andrew Berry took on the assignment to improve this group and get them out of the hole of being ranked #32 last year. In case you are scoring at home, that is dead last. In the April draft, Berry selected KC Concepcion of Texas A&M in Round 1, and then with his very next pick he chose Washington’s Denzel Boston. RELATED: 2026 GAVE FANS WHAT THEY WANT Each NFL club usually retains five or six receivers. For the Browns, Jerry Jeudy and the two rookies are a lock. The coaching staff really likes the development of Isaiah Bond. That leaves two spots. Berry signed Tylan Wallace from the Baltimore Ravens , who is a receiver but was inked for his return skills. But still, he would count as one of the six spots. That leaves one. The competition is between Cedric Tillman, Larvadain, Luke Floriea, Malachi Corley, and undrafted rookie Ben Patterson. Tillman was released before “The Turk” shows up on August 30. That means the one roster spot is down to one guy. Floriea was signed to a reserve/futures deal in January. Jamari Thrash and Corley were tendered in March. Wallace came to Cleveland during the free agency period. Undrafted rookies Aaron Anderson and Kole Wilson were inked right after the draft. Anderson and Thrash ended up injured and were waived with an injury designation. Undrafted rookie Ben Patterson was then signed to fill the void. The Ohio kid Back to Floriea, which is pronounced as “Flo-REE-uh.” He is an Ohio player. He grew up in Mentor, Ohio, and attended Mentor High School, where he played basketball and football despite only being 5’-8” tall and weighing 179 pounds. Floriea was an exceptional basketball player, playing 101 contests and averaging 11.5 points a game, 2.7 rebounds, 2.0 steals, and 4.4 assists. 22 times in his final three seasons, he was named the “Player of the Game.” In football, he played receiver and ran a 4.48 in the 40 with a vertical leap of 32”. As a senior, he had 52 receptions for 939 yards and 14 touchdowns. He was named Second Team All-Ohio, First Team All-District, and First Team All-County. He was listed as a three-star recruit. Athletics run in the family, as his sister Paige was a track star. He had plenty of offers, but chose Kent State. His career totals are 48 games played, 100 receptions for 1,321 yards, 12 TDs, a 13.2 yards-per-reception average, and four rushes for 23 yards with a single score. Floriea was also a return man with seven kickoffs for a 17.8 yards-per-return average, plus 21 punt returns with an average of 7.6 yards per return. After his junior and senior seasons, Floriea was named First Team All-MAC and received a Hula Bowl invite. As a senior, he caught 44 receptions for 699 yards with seven touchdowns. He ranked fifth in the conference in yards per catch (15.9). The sixth and final receiver spot on the Browns’ roster is up for grabs. Last year, Floriea was a bubble guy as well, was waived, and then spent the year on Cleveland’s practice squad. Versus the Patriots Going into the final preseason game with the New England Patriots, it was made known that the starters weren’t going to play, and this contest was for the bottom third of the roster to prove that they deserved a roster spot. Like Floriea. Against New England, Floriea was lined up with the second team. The final catch of the first drive impressed. Cleveland had driven down to New England’s seven-yard line with a first-and-goal. Rocket Sanders had gotten most of the yardage to finally get the offense down close. With Dillon Gabriel at quarterback, he found Floriea who had come from the left slot to the right flats, alone at the 9-yard line. He then headed to the right pylon despite three defenders bearing down on him. Staying in-bounds by inches, he fought his way to the pylon for the game’s first touchdown with CB Kindle Vildor and S John Saunders all over him. Luke powering it in for 6! #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/b8BAvwthgP — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 It wasn’t the crossing route, or getting wide open, or his decision to turn upfield, or his speed. It was the fight to get into the end zone for points that was the most impressive. Make that two touchdowns in two weeks. On the next possession, the pass was to WR Greg Larvadain with 7:31 left in the first quarter. Larvadain caught the ball while Floriea then walled off his man, which gave the receiver an extra six yards on the completed pass. It’s plays like this that don’t show up on the stat sheet. Let’s discuss his second touchdown of the game. The Browns drove down to New England’s fourteen-yard line. Dillon in shotgun, with Floriea now as the right slot receiver. He did a right juke, then immediately cut to the inside and headed towards the left center of the end zone. He pretty much shrugged off his man, CB Marcellas Dial, but still had a safety man deep. The pass hit him perfectly at the seven-yard line with two steps now on Dial. His speed got him to the three as S Dell Pettus approached, Floriea gave him a right-turn head bob. This caused Pettus to pause, which gave Floriea a millisecond. Then the two met at the one with a fight to cross the goal line. DG + Luke = TD 🙌 #NEvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/mYVj4n5MnH — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) August 28, 2026 Yes, both scores were against the Patriots’ second-team defense. We get that. However, receivers have the job of catching passes and trying to score. Floriea is doing both. He doesn’t drop balls. He doesn’t throw his arms up when he doesn’t make a contested catch. He accepts incompletions. He runs crisp routes. He sells his fakes. He does his job. This year, it just seems different for Floriea. His routes have more meaning. He is giving extra deception and is selling it more. I’ll be completely honest: What you saw from Luke Floriea tonight is what we see every day in practice. He consistently gets open, makes plays, works hard and is a great teammate. This isn’t a feel-good story anymore. I talked about him last year, and he continues to produce.… https://t.co/yL72FhBOJm — Lance Reisland (Coach Riz) (@LanceReisland) August 28, 2026 Take Floriea’s touchdown-not-touchdown in the second quarter. The throw was bad and died heading towards the ground. Yet Floriea made the effort with both hands and was one inch away from his third touchdown of the game. In fact, the initial call was touchdown, but the replay showed a small skip off the turf. Is it enough? Patterson did some good things in the Patriots game, including the 52-yard gain and leading all receivers. He seems destined for the practice squad. Larvadain has had a roller coaster in training camp as well as in preseason games. That might become two down. Sources: Former #Jets WR Malachi Corley is signing with the #Browns . I’m told Corley had multiple opportunities on the open market, and ultimately chose Cleveland. pic.twitter.com/bHXDWo8MGn — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) August 27, 2025 Corley is a guy who failed to wow anybody in preseason, but the coaching staff loves him. He offered more as a complete player last year, even though that was with another staff. But he has a lot of potential, has genuine juice, and came from a college program that was on full throttle every game on offense. He is a weapon once he catches the ball and is an above-average kickoff returner, adding to his versatility. The last receivers on the depth chart usually have to also play on punt and kick coverage units as well, something Corley has experience with. Preseason Comparison: vs. Chicago Bears Corley: 2 targets, 0 receptions,…

QB: The biggest decision here is to keep three quarterbacks vs. four quarterbacks. Based on what I’ve seen from Dillon Gabriel , I don’t see him cutting it out as a starter. I liked what I saw in the final preseason game, but that was also a very basic defense that he thrived against. We’ve seen him against starting defenses, and things fall apart because teams know what to expect from him. Could he be a decent backup? Maybe. But Shedeur Sanders won that role, and Taylen Green was drafted. I’m forecasting Gabriel being dealt somewhere for a minimal draft pick. RB: The competition at running back is supposed to be Ahmani Marshall vs. Raheim Sanders . I like Sanders, and think he would be the team’s best blocking back too for pass protection, so I picked Sanders. I also threw veteran fullback Michael Burton on the roster, even though he’s missed most of camp. Todd Monken uses fullbacks, and Burton can be leveraged there while Carsen Ryan floats over to tight end. WR: The first four are locked in for sure: Jerry Jeudy , KC Concepcion , Denzel Boston , and Isaiah Bond . After that, determining the remaining two spots is difficult. On one hand, I wanted to pick Gage Larvadain and Luke Floriea , but then I’m thinking, “Is Tylan Wallace going to return punts, and why isn’t Malachi Corley being given more consideration?” I could easily see any combination of the four making it. Initially, I rolled with Larvadain and Wallace. I made the switch after the final preseason game to put Floriea on instead of Larvadain. Unfortunately, Larvadain has shown a bit of a knack of trying to make something out of nothing at times, both at receiver and on punt returns. Floriea has done everything one could ask of a receiver this camp, he gets open, he wins match-ups, and he catches everything. I think either one could clear waivers and get to the practice squad, but I think there’s a slight chance Floriea catches people’s attention, whereas Larvadain more easily gets to the practice squad. TE: The depth here appears thin or inexperienced, and with Jack Stoll on IR, the team lost their potential blocking back. I think they’ll look closely at the waiver wire for a blocker. OL: I don’t think I have anything too surprising here, except whether to keep Zak Zinter or not. I think he and Luke Wypler can slip to the practice squad. DL: Same thing on the defensive trench — I think it seems pretty obvious who will be kept, the question is more so will they keep an extra (tenth) guy. LB: Rinse-and-repeat, there wasn’t a whole lot of debating at linebacker. Although if Carson Schwesinger is to miss any regular season action, they’d need an extra guy temporarily. CB: This is challenging. Michael Coats earned a spot as an undrafted player, but now he’s hurt, and we don’t know how long. I’m hoping it’s just a small ankle injury that maybe warrants short-term IR. New this year, teams can designate two players to go directly to IR without having to “put them on the roster, cut someone else, and then put the player on IR.” Myles Bryant could also make it here over Tre Avery , but I just don’t know his health. And I know very little about Mekhi Blackmon , but Cleveland claimed him on Thursday, so I assume he’s making the initial 53-man roster. S: Considering the top three safeties are basically starters, it might be necessary to have two backups here. For now, I just have one. ST: It’d be a stunner if this differed at all. Note: I have the option to update my 53-man projection if injury-related or other news comes out by Saturday, as far as counting my accuracy goes. I always try to aim for at least 49/53! What Do You Think? Feel free to share your roster projections here, or some changes you would make to mine.

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys 27-24 preseason loss to the Saints
summary: And just like that, the Dallas Cowboys’ preseason is over. They couldn’t pull off the sweep and stay undefeated, but they made it interesting. After falling behind 24-9 after three quarters, the team fought back and tied it before the New Orleans Saints added a field goal late to prevail 27-24. It had the typical […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Sam Howell #16 of the Dallas Cowboys runs into the endzone to score a two point conversion during the fourth quarter of the 2026 NFL preseason game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images And just like that, the Dallas Cowboys’ preseason is over. They couldn’t pull off the sweep and stay undefeated, but they made it interesting. After falling behind 24-9 after three quarters, the team fought back and tied it before the New Orleans Saints added a field goal late to prevail 27-24. It had the typical unexciting third-preseason game aura, but there were things worth noting. Here are 10 thoughts on Friday night’s action. 1. The other side of the Barham Last week, third-round rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham dazzled in his preseason debut. He was smashing, crashing, and all kinds of violent stuff. In this game, we saw a little more of the uncontrolled version of his play style as he attacked a little more recklessly. On a few different occasions, blockers took advantage of his overaggressiveness and just pushed him a smidge off the mark, causing him to run himself out of the play. 2. Milton was a tad off The first two preseason games were breaths of fresh air for those who have watched the third-year quarterback struggle during his time in Dallas. He’s looked immensely better with his poise in the pocket and accuracy, but against the Saints we saw a little of the old Milton. He had multiple passes deflected at the line of scrimmage and missed a wide-open receiver when he airmailed it way over his head. It’s not a big deal, but it would have been nice to see the team’s new backup finish the preseason on a high note. 3. Howell about that! It’s been the Milton show for the first two preseason games, but just as the young quarterback cracked open the door just slightly, veteran quarterback Sam Howell burst through with a final plea to show he belongs on the roster. Howell had his best preseason game, going 12 for 18 for 155 yards and two touchdowns in a very impressive second half. He led two straight touchdown drives in the fourth quarter, and tied the game by running the ball in for a successful two-point conversion. Just like that, the quarterback battle has been spruced up. 4. Brown is human With no Jonathan Mingo suiting up, that essentially seals the deal for him to secure the WR5 spot, but that doesn’t mean undrafted free agent rookie Camden Brown doesn’t still have a chance. He’s been putting up highlight plays in each preseason game, so why would this one be any different? Brown had a nice 27-yard catch on a key third-down play to keep the drive going. He also had an uncharacteristic drop on a perfectly thrown slant route, but his body of work has still been impressive. 5. Another undrafted WR The Cowboys didn’t have many big plays in this one, but it was nice to see undrafted free agent wide receiver Jordan Hudson put together a good game. He led the game in receiving with four catches for 97 yards, including a 26-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. While all eyes have been on Brown, the Cowboys gave Hudson the same amount of money, and don’t forget that Anthony Smith was a seventh-round pick. Between all these young receivers, there’s a good chance at least two make it through waivers if they’re cut. 6. RB2 and RB3 decided It appears that the Cowboys have settled on their first three running backs on the depth chart. Starter Javonte Williams didn’t play at all in the preseason, and both Malik Davis and Jaydon Blue didn’t play on Friday. Instead, the team gave the work to Phil Mafah, who ran hard on 12 carries for 46 yards (3.8 ypc), while Israel Abanikanda ran the ball seven times for 16 yards (2.3 ypc). The team was getting the other guys a shot to strut their stuff, but if they are to remain with the team, it’s most likely going to be on the practice squad. 7. Shelton’s improvement It’s been a rough go for the team’s fourth-round rookie Drew Shelton. He’s struggled with his footwork, his hand usage, basically everything. Defenders have been getting past him with ease. But he’s young and still developing, and took a nice step forward, doing a much better job staying in front of the defender. He set a wider base, used his arms better, and secured blocks for most of the evening. According to PFF, he didn’t allow a single pressure on 19 pass-blocking snaps in the first half. That was a promising showing. 8. The center swap Usually, it’s been Nick Leverett at center (minus the small reps T.J. Bass has played) with Trevor Keegan at left guard. In the second half, Keegan played center while Leverett slid over to guard. Both looked good on initial review, and the team continues to tinker with different arrangements. Keegan playing center adds a new element to the equation, which will only complicate the tough decisions the Cowboys’ coaching staff has to make to find their offensive line group. Second-year lineman Ajani Cornelius sat out with knee soreness, so he remains in the mix. 9. Fighting Sammy Outside linebacker Sam Williams entered this game as a fringe player trying to make the team at a crowded position. In this game, he was in the middle of a lot of the action, but at times he couldn’t finish the play. Several times, he got his mitts on ball carriers, but they escaped and kept running. He did make plays later in the game, including a nice sack when he flew around the edge. The veteran needed a good showing to give himself a better chance to make the squad, but it’s unclear if he did enough to punch his ticket on the roster. 10. Don’t forget about Wheat Veteran practice-squader Tyrus Wheat is routinely forgotten, and he’s again an afterthought considering how deep the team’s edge rushing group is. Despite his longshot odds, he keeps fighting. He shows up regularly on special teams and came away with a nice sack in this game. It seems like he’ll again be cut loose and brought back, but file his name away in the “shocking roster decision” should he surprise everyone and make the team. It’s happened once, it could happen again.

title: Cowboys Marist Liufau breaks forearm in Saints game
summary: The Dallas Cowboys lost to the New Orleans Saints in the final preseason game for 2026. They may have also lost a player to injury for a while. Outside linebacker Marist Liufau had to leave the game early with an injury to his arm. It turns out that it is a broken forearm. Dallas head […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Marist Liufau #35 of the Dallas Cowboys sits on the sideline after being injured during the 2026 NFL preseason game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys lost to the New Orleans Saints in the final preseason game for 2026. They may have also lost a player to injury for a while. Outside linebacker Marist Liufau had to leave the game early with an injury to his arm . It turns out that it is a broken forearm. Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Liufau will miss “ weeks ,” while owner Jerry Jones said Liufau could be back “quickly,” according to ESPN. “Losing Marist as a football player is tough,” Schottenheimer said. “Unfortunately, it’s part of the business. You guys all know him and the way he’ll attack his rehab, and so we’ll get surgery done as soon as we can and next man up. But yeah, he was a critical, critical part of not just two or three special teams, really all four. He’s a ‘four-core’ guy that you just rely on and he plays the game with violence and we have some other guys in that locker room that do that as well.” As Schottenheimer noted, Liufau had been used extensively on special teams while also trying to make an adjustment to playing outside linebacker in Christian Parker’s new 3-4 defense. The experiment at OLB is still to be determined as he was not the most consistent player there. But that special teams ability was the thing expected to keep him on the roster. The Cowboys will now have to make a decision about carrying him, cutting him then trying to bring him back, or designating him as one of the two ‘return from IR’ guys when the final 53 is decided. What do you think the Cowboys will do here?

In other news, Jaishawn Barham hasn’t wasted any time making an impact in Dallas during the offseason, and now he’s set to […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Spencer Rattler #2 of the New Orleans Saints runs with the ball toward the endzone during the second quarter of the 2026 NFL preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys were unable to go undefeated in the preseason, dropping the final game to the New Orleans Saints. Next on the horizon are roster cuts which will be coming this weekend. In other news, Jaishawn Barham hasn’t wasted any time making an impact in Dallas during the offseason, and now he’s set to contribute in a big way as a rookie. Malachi Lawrence is in a loaded defensive end room, but what he brings to the table skill wise will earn him notable playing time. Zach Wilson leads winning drive for Saints, who are unsettled at backup QB along with Cowboys – AP The Cowboys almost pulled off a comeback, but fell short. Zach Wilson led a drive to Daniel Carlson ‘s 53-yard field goal with 1:55 remaining, and the New Orleans Saints beat the Dallas Cowboys 27-24 in a preseason finale Friday night. Sam Howell threw two fourth-quarter touchdown passes and had a tying 2-point conversion run for the Cowboys (2-1), who erased a 15-point deficit but missed out on their first undefeated preseason in 20 years. A man of few words, intense rookie will play big role for Cowboys’ defense – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham has been a standout during training. His role in his first year is set to be a significant one. Beginning at camp with the second-team unit getting snaps off the ball and on the ball as an outside linebacker, Barham built trust with his coaching staff in a hurry to start getting first-team reps almost as soon as the pads came on one week into camp. Also, don’t mistake his quiet nature for confusion. In fact, it’s Barham’s intelligence that not only allows him to be versatile for new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, but also an option as a lead communicator in the defense. “Him playing both [positions] is one of the cheat codes that he has,” Parker said. “It’s not like he’s seeing things he hasn’t seen before. I think he’s a fast processor, and he’s one of those guys that’s eager to learn.” Mailbag: Who is battling for final spots? – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Dallas is wrapping up their training camp as preparations for the 2026 season are set to begin. However, a plethora of players are fighting to make the final 53-man roster. Patrik: This might be one of the most difficult cutdowns in recent memory for Brian Schottenheimer and the Cowboys. Of course, the majority of the roster is something most people can predict well ahead of time. That said, I don’t think it’s as much as most my think. Schottenheimer says pump the brakes on crowning Joe Milton over Sam Howell, so will Dallas carry three QBs? Or can Milton push Howell out in the preseason finale?? Snaps are hard to come by, but ‘Sky is the limit’ for top Cowboys rookie – Reid D Hanson, Cowboys Wire Malachi Lawrence will have to earn his reps in 2026 with the bodies in the defensive end room. However, he’s got the skill set to make an impact. Malachi Lawrence, one of Dallas’ first-round picks from 2026, joins Guyton in this elite fraternity. Like Guyton, he’s a raw first round talent who needs lots of development as he learns the pro game. Like Guyton, Lawrence is a player needing a ton of technical refinement. Like Guyton, he’s going to flash good and bad early in his career. And like Guyton, the sky is the limit for this supremely talented young player. 4 Cowboys who could survive roster cuts thanks to their contracts – Jess Haynie, The Landry Hat Dallas will trim its roster soon for the upcoming season. There may be several players who could end up making the final roster due to financial reasons. Sam Williams – OLB Coincidentally, it’s the Sam on defense who presents a similar conundrum. It was surprising enough that Dallas brougth Williams back at all this offseason, but especially that the bulk of it was guaranteed. Williams’ entire $1.4 million base salary is owed to him regardless of if he makes the roster, and he got a $600k signing bonus along with it. Cowboys are gambling with major OL depth issues – Shane Taylor, Inside The Star The offensive line as a whole has been a topic of discussion this offseason. Could depth concerns end up costing the Cowboys? Outside of Steele being the starting right tackle and continuing to get worked every single day in drills, I don’t think the team has their current backup swing tackle on the roster, and that is another issue. One other thing to note, take a look at the transaction wire, nobody is cutting starting caliber offensive tackles, and for the Cowboys that is a major issue. It is not like they can just wait until they do their round of cuts and dumb whomever they want, and go look at the wire, pick up the phone and get the average guy in the building. It just hasn’t shaken out like that this summer.

title: NFL waiver wire rules and the Cowboys’ position in the waiver order
summary: This Sunday, August 30th, is a big day on the NFL calendar. By 6 PM ET on that day, NFL teams will have to cut down their roster to the initial 53-man roster. The Cowboys have some tough decisions to make as we have discussed extensively over the past few weeks. The Cowboys are trying […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - AUGUST 22: A detail of the NFL logo on The Duke Wilson football ball before a preseason game between the Washington Commanders and Detroit Lions at Ford Field on August 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images This Sunday, August 30th, is a big day on the NFL calendar. By 6 PM ET on that day, NFL teams will have to cut down their roster to the initial 53-man roster. The Cowboys have some tough decisions to make as we have discussed extensively over the past few weeks. The Cowboys are trying to rebound from two straight years of missing the playoffs and have been getting positive reviews on their offseason so far. Even the sports books, like our partner FanDuel, have the Cowboys as probable for playoff action (-124) which ranks sixth in the NFC. After the cuts occur, a flurry of transactions will happen as other teams try to patch holes by picking up players who are cut, or by trading for them before the cut happens. The process can be confusing, so here are the rules around the waiver wire in the NFL. When is the waiver deadline? Teams have until 1 PM ET on August 31st (the day after the cut deadline), to place a waiver claim on a player. The NFL reviews the process, finalizes the moves, and then teams then can begin filling out their practice squads. Which players can go on waivers? Once the cuts happen, players are then placed into two buckets depending on their service time in the NFL. The buckets are vested players and players who have yet to reach that designation. Our sister site, Behind The Steel Curtain, has outlined this process. A vested player is one who has been credited with four or more seasons of NFL experience. To be credited for an NFL season , a player must have been on the active, inactive, IR, or PUP roster for three or more regular-season or postseason games. A player can also be credited for a season if they receive an injury settlement or grievance for the equivalent of three or more regular-season games. Note that a credited season is different from accrued seasons , which determine what type of free agent a player is. Vested players do not go onto waivers and are free to sign with any team at any time, between the day after the Super Bowl and the NFL trade deadline. They are subject to waivers in the period after the deadline through the Super Bowl. Non-vested players, or players with three or fewer credited seasons, are subject to waivers. If these players go unclaimed, they are free to negotiate with teams as free agents. How does the NFL determine waiver wire priority? Once players are determined to be subject to waivers, teams must then be allotted players they claim. But it goes through a waiver order to determine which team’s claim wins on each player. This waiver wire order is used for now and through the first three weeks of the season. That order is the same as the 2026 draft order before any trades were made. There is also one other key item – after a team is allotted a claimed player, they do not go to the back of the line and wait their turn again. Instead, the team with the top priority who makes a claim gets that player. If the Raiders, who are at the top of the waiver order claim five players, they will get those five players. There is no rotating to the back of the line after making a claim. What’s the current waiver order? title: 5 potential roster cuts Cowboys should consider trading for
summary: With the preseason on the books, the Dallas Cowboys and the rest of the league will now turn their focus to getting under the league mandated 53-man roster limit. We could see me a multitude of trades made around the league with all of this roster movement and the Cowboys could be both buyers and […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 02: Blake Fisher #57 of the Houston Texans looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at NRG Stadium on November 2, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the preseason on the books, the Dallas Cowboys and the rest of the league will now turn their focus to getting under the league mandated 53-man roster limit. We could see me a multitude of trades made around the league with all of this roster movement and the Cowboys could be both buyers and sellers. Here are a handful of players they should attempt to acquire via trade. OT Blake Fisher, Houston Texans From top to bottom, Dallas’ OT position is arguably their biggest roster concern. It’s unlikely they trade for a plug-and-play starter, but attempting to upgrade the swing tackle position makes a ton of sense after Nate Thomas’ regression/struggles and at the nonexistent options behind him on the depth chart. Fisher, a 2024 second-round pick, has two years remaining on his rookie deal and 15 starts under his belt in two seasons with the Texans. He’s currently competing for the swing OT job, but has been outplayed by his competition. He’s a young, affordable option who could upgrade Dallas’ swing OT position. C Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, Buffalo Bills Other than T.J. Bass, the Cowboys current backup guard/center options are less than ideal. And, considering Bass hasn’t had much experience snapping the ball, it might be wise for the Cowboys to attempt to upgrade things behind Cooper Beebe after letting Brock Hoffman walk in free agency. Van Pran-Granger, a 2024 fifth-round pick, looks to have lost the backup center job to Lloyd Cushenberry in Buffalo, potentially making him available via trade. He’s another young, affordable option who would fit in nicely in Klayton Adams’ zone/gap blocking scheme. DT DeWayne Carter, Buffalo Bills Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, and Otito Ogbonnia an impressive DT Trio for the Cowboys, but behind them the depth is questionable at best. Because of that, it wouldn’t be at all surprising in Dallas attempts to upgrade this position via trade to acquire a savvy vet or a young player with the upside. Carter, a 2024 third-round pick, is a victim of unfortunate circumstances. After missing his entire rookie year with a season-ending injury he now finds himself on the outside looking in at Jim Leonhard’s defensive scheme. The Cowboys may prefer a more seasoned vet to upgrade things, but Carter’s youth/upside makes him an intriguing trade target. LB Junior Colston, Los Angeles Chargers If DeMarvion Overshown can stay healthy, he along with Dee Winters and Jaishawn Barham are all upgrades from what the Cowboys deployed at the position a season ago. But, that doesn’t mean Dallas won’t attempt to upgrade the LB position further from either a starting four depth standpoint, acquiring another starting caliber option. Colston, a 2024 third-round pick, is currently buried on the Chargers LB depth chart, making him a potential trade target for the Cowboys. The 23-year-old is another young, affordable player who could come in and provide a solid floor with a potential high ceiling RB Kaleb Johnson, Pittsburgh Steelers As long as Javonte Williams stays healthy for the entire season, the Cowboys are pretty good shape at RB. But, if Williams were to miss any amount of time you don’t really have anyone else ready to step into the RB1 role, although Malik Davis could fill-in adequately a few games on a short-term basis if needed. Johnson, a 2024 third-round pick, is someone the Cowboys showed an interest in pre-draft not long ago. He’s been in the doghouse in Pittsburgh pretty much from the get-go and isn’t faring any better under Mike McCarthy. He could push Davis for the backup job.

title: Final 53-man roster prediction after Cowboys’ preseason finale
summary: With preseason finally over, the Dallas Cowboys and the rest of the league have to now get down to the nitty-gritty of roster manipulation to get under the league mandated 53-man limit. New additions via the waiver wire or trade will surely shake some things up, but as things stand right now below is a […]
full_text: With preseason finally over, the Dallas Cowboys and the rest of the league have to now get down to the nitty-gritty of roster manipulation to get under the league mandated 53-man limit. New additions via the waiver wire or trade will surely shake some things up, but as things stand right now below is a final 53-man roster prediction for the Cowboys. Quarterback (2) Dak Prescott, Joe Milton Prescott is the unquestioned QB1 and a MVP candidate this year, and Milton will once again be his primary backup after outperforming Sam Howell. Ideally Howell is traded, if not, hopefully clears waivers and re-signs to the practice squad. Running back (4) Javonte Williams, Malik Davis, Jaydon Blue, Hunter Luepke Williams and Davis are the Cowboys top two backs and Luepke will reprise his role as a Swiss Army knife FB. Blue provides an explosive element and could have a specific package just for him. Phil Mafah and Israel Ibanikanda hopefully revert to the practice squad. Wide receiver (6) CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, KaVontae Turpin, Jonathan Mingo, Camden Brown After the top four, a tough decision will have to be made. The Cowboys are high on both Mingo and Brown, the former due to his blocking/special teams ability and the latter due to his upside. Both stick with Anthony Smith and Jordan Hudson hopefully re-signed to the PS. Tight end (4) Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford, Luke Schoonmaker, Michael Trigg Both Ferguson and Spann-Ford are the unquestioned top TEs for the Cowboys, and as such, are roster locks. We believe Schoonmaker and Trigg will round at the group. No. 86 for insurance and Trigg due to his upside and the fact he likely won’t make it through waivers. Offensive line (9) Tyler Guyton, Tyler Smith, Cooper Beebe, Tyler Booker, Terence Steele, TJ Bass, Nate Thomas, Nick Leverett,, Drew Shelton Dallas’ starting five OL is set with Thomas backing them up as the swing OT and Bass as the backup iOL. Leverett has proven to be a solid backup C/G, but could be replaced by an outside addition. Shelton makes the cut for now purely based on his draft status, but hopefully can be stashed on IR to make way for a more proven vet swing OT. Defensive tackle (5) Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, Otito Ogbonnia, Jonathan Bullard, LT Overton The top three are easy predict, but after that less so. Overton and Bullard make the cut for now, but the latter could revert to short-term IR to be recalled later. Keep an eye out for an experienced vet DT to add to the mix and look for Tommy Dunn and DJ Withers back on the PS. Outside linebacker/Edge (5) Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku, Malachi Lawrence, Von Miller, James Houston The top four are locked in with Houston rounding out the group. Marist Liufau or Sam Williams could force the Cowboys to go six and deep here, but neither has looked particularly impressive. A waiver wire addition or trade wouldn’t be shocking here. Inside linebacker (5) DeMarvion Overshown, Dee Winters, Jaishawn Barham, Shemar James, Justin Barron Overshown, Winters, and Barham will rotate as the starters with James and Barron backing them up. No. 55’s pass rushing ability also helps going a little short at OLB. Adding a veteran such as Bobby Wagner to solidify things could still be very much in play. Cornerback (5) DaRon Bland, Cobie Durant, Shavon Revel, Devin Moore, Reddy Stewart Dallas’ top three CBs are locked in, but the depth behind them is still in question. Moore, much like Drew Shelton, makes the cut due to his draft status and we believe Stewart rounds out the group with Ameer Speed barely missing out. Hopefully Speed slips through to the PS. Safety (5) Caleb Downs , Malik Hooker, Jalen Thompson, P.J. Locke, Markquese Bell The Cowboys love for Bell forces them to go five deep here with the top four already locked in. They would love to find a way to hold on to Julius Wood, also keep an eye on Alijah Clark to return to the PS. He was on the first team kick return unit in practice. Special teams (3) Brandon Aubrey, Bryan Anger, Trent Sieg Nothing new here. There’s no questioning these three are roster locks.

title: Cowboys 24, Saints 27: Dallas closes preseason with loss, but optimism for what’s next
summary: It has come and gone. We made it. The preseason is over for the Dallas Cowboys, and at long last they finally lost an exhibition game as they fell to the New Orleans Saints on Friday night by a final score of 27 to 24. For all of this calendar year our discussions around this […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys tight end Mitch Van Vooren (80) makes a catch for a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints during the fourth quarter at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It has come and gone. We made it. The preseason is over for the Dallas Cowboys, and at long last they finally lost an exhibition game as they fell to the New Orleans Saints on Friday night by a final score of 27 to 24. For all of this calendar year our discussions around this team have centered around how “differently” things have been. The approach to roster construction, the avoidance of off-the-field drama, and now it has all served as a common denominator all the way to the regular season. That’s what this moment signifies. There are still things to tend to before we fully get there. The Cowboys have to finalize their 53-man roster (in an initial sense at least, they’ll obviously tend to it) by Sunday afternoon. But next up… real football. Below you will find a recap of how things went against New Orleans. So long, preseason. First Quarter The Saints won the toss and elected to receive which put the Cowboys on defense first. Spencer Rattler got things moving a little bit and before you could blink the Saints were in field goal range. Thankfully the Cowboys defense buckled and held them there, but Daniel Carlson did boot one in from 38 yards out for the game’s first points. SCORE: COWBOYS 0, SAINTS 3 Joe Milton got the start at quarterback on the night which seemed to underscore that he is QB2 for this team. Phil Mafah did a lot of the work on that first possession, but the Cowboys also had to settle for a field goal. Brandon Aubrey was good from 49 yards out. SCORE: COWBOYS 3, SAINTS 3 The Saints began moving the ball once again, it felt like 2024 (if you know you know), and this time were able to cash all the way in. Touchdown, visitors. Saints 6th-round pick Barion Brown finds the end zone Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/s3lAfyzFq0 — NFL (@NFL) August 29, 2026 The quarter ended with the Cowboys somewhat threatening, partly thanks to this beauty from Joe Milton to Camden Brown. . @CamdenBrown7 continues to make plays 😤 📺: #NOvsDAL on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/LW1eOzcvjQ — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 29, 2026 Very nice. Second Quarter The Cowboys wound up scoring on the possession, but they couldn’t quite match the Saints. Brandon Aubrey lined up from 51 and you know the drill. SCORE: COWBOYS 6, SAINTS 10 On the game’s fifth possession… we finally got a punt. It looked like New Orleans was going to benefit from a roughing the passer penalty that Spencer Rattler seemed to draw, but replay assist showed that the Cowboys were fine. What a world we are living in these days. Unfortunately while the Cowboys were able to get within striking distance, they finally blinked themselves. Brandon Aubrey gave a 57-yard field goal is best effort and couldn’t quite convert. Soon enough the Saints were back in the endzone, this time courtesy of Spencer Rattler on the ground. TOUCHDOWN RATTLER! #Saints | 📺: FOX-8 pic.twitter.com/9fkseoQ4O8 — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) August 29, 2026 SCORE: COWBOYS 6, SAINTS 17 Milton and co. took over with about two minutes left which was very interesting in terms of seeing what he could do. Joe was solid and he helped the team set up another Brandon Aubrey attempt. This one was from 58 and was as good as could be. SCORE: COWBOYS 9, SAINTS 17 That was that and both teams went to their locker rooms for halftime. Third Quarter Sam Howell was in at quarterback for the second half and things weren’t exactly spectacular to start as the Cowboys punted. New Orleans picked up where they left off and scored another touchdown. This time it was Zamir White from 11 yards out. Zamir White runs into the endzone with ease 🤝 #Saints | 📺: FOX-8 pic.twitter.com/S0X4wHyTEs — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) August 29, 2026 SCORE: COWBOYS 9, SAINTS 24 It was another punt for the Cowboys. A penalty did wipe away a fresh set of downs, but by this point in the game the offense wasn’t exactly doing a ton of work. New Orleans wound up punting. The vibe was clearly shifting towards the end of the preseason in an overall sense. Fourth Quarter As the fourth quarter started the Cowboys did it with a bang. Sam Howell found Jordan Hudson for a huge touchdown to turn the mood right around. . @Sam7Howell to @d1Jordan3 for a TD ❗️ 📺: #NOvsDAL on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/Wn7kAeQ0ae — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 29, 2026 SCORE: COWBOYS 16, SAINTS 24 The Saints punted it back to the Cowboys which provided life in the game with Dallas down by one score. With that opportunity the Cowboys seriously cashed in. Like… seriously cashed in. Sam Howell found Mitch Van Vooren for the touchdown, and then he took care of things himself for the game-tying two-point conversion. MITCH VAN VOOREN TOUCHDOWN 📺: #NOvsDAL on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/10ABfgrCja — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 29, 2026 . @Sam7Howell TIES THE GAME ‼️ 📺: #NOvsDAL on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/LFMLhdWaas — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 29, 2026 SCORE: COWBOYS 24, SAINTS 24 The Saints went down and kicked a field goal and left 1:55 to work with. Kellen Moore clearly did so because New Orleans is working through kickers. You can’t blame him. SCORE: COWBOYS 24, SAINTS 27 This set the Cowboys up with a fun opportunity. Sam Howell and co. had a chance down by 3 to go the length of the field to score a touchdown to end the preseason undefeated. Unfortunately it wasn’t in the cards and the Cowboys lost a preseason game for the first time this year.

title: Broncos WR/KR Marvin Mims Jr. is going to be fine and is dealing with a bruised foot
summary: Broncos All-Pro kick returner and big-play specialist Marvin Mims Jr. received his first preseason action of the summer last night. Unfortunately, his night would not last long after he suffered an apparent lower-body injury in the opening series. He was down in pain for a bit before jogging off the field. However, he did have […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - AUGUST 21: Marvin Mims Jr. (19) of the Denver Broncos leads teammates onto the field before the game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Friday, August 21, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Broncos All-Pro kick returner and big-play specialist Marvin Mims Jr. received his first preseason action of the summer last night. Unfortunately, his night would not last long after he suffered an apparent lower-body injury in the opening series. He was down in pain for a bit before jogging off the field. However, he did have a limp and was seen visibly angry on the sideline before heading to the locker room with a trainer. His night was done, and his preseason was limited to just a handful of plays. This raised concerns about the Broncos’ playmaking receiver/returner, but after the game, Head Coach Sean Payton gave a positive update on Mims’ health. He told reporters that “Mims is going to be fine” and that he is simply dealing with a bruise. Payton: “Mims is going to be fine. It’s a bruise.” — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) August 29, 2026 Mims, who started out camp hot and was making plays early on, suffered what was called a “soft tissue injury,” and it sidelined him for the majority of training camp and, outside of a few snaps last night, the vast majority of the preseason. Now, he is dealing with a bruised foot, but thankfully, according to Payton, it seems like a minor injury. The good news for Mims and the Broncos is that they do not play their next game until September 14th, when they head to Arrowhead on Monday Night to take on the returning Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. This gives Mims plenty of time to heal up and be ready for the Broncos’ big opening-night matchup vs. their divisional rivals on the road. This is a big year for Marvin Mims. He is entering the final year of his rookie deal and will be a free agent at the end of the year. A productive contract year could make him one of the more sought-after players on the free-agent market and could lead to him receiving a big contract. It remains to be seen if the Broncos will attempt to re-sign their All-Pro returner, but we will see how things work out for Mims as the season progresses. At the end of that day, Mims only suffered a minor injury and should be good to go for Week 1 of the season, when the Broncos will begin their quest to the Super Bowl.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Future Broncos: 3 prospects to watch in Week 1 of 2026 NCAA Football season
summary: For the first two installments of Future Broncos, we took a look at the team’s slate of draft picks and potential needs to address in the 2027 NFL Draft. This week, we will take a look at three prospects fans across Broncos Country should tune into for the official first week of college football that […]
full_text: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 18: Jamari Johnson #9 of the Oregon Ducks points after the game against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at SHI Stadium on October 18, 2025 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first two installments of Future Broncos , we took a look at the team’s slate of draft picks and potential needs to address in the 2027 NFL Draft. This week, we will take a look at three prospects fans across Broncos Country should tune into for the official first week of college football that runs today through next Saturday. Cayden Green — Offensive Tackle — Mizzou Garett Bolles and Mike McGlinchey will return again to be the tackle duo for the Denver Broncos this season. Bolles is coming off a great season and continues to play at a high level. While McGlinchey has arguably been the steadiest right tackle the franchise has had in ages. Speaking of time, it’s been forever since Denver has invested an early selection at offensive tackle. In fact, next April’s draft will mark a decade since Bolles was selected out of Utah with the Broncos’ first round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Maybe the Broncos finally opt to go that route this spring. One player to watch this week and throughout the season will be Mizzou Tigers left tackle Cayden Green who projects as a first-round pick. Green’s collegiate career started back in 2023 with the Oklahoma Sooners, but he transferred the following season to go back to his home state and play for Mizzou. In 2024, he was an 11-game starter for them at left guard. For their 2025 season, Green held down the left tackle spot for 11 games. He missed two games with a foot injury last year but played well over the course of the season. He surrendered just two sacks and helped pave the way for the Tigers’ dominant rushing attack. At 6’5” and 324 pounds, Green certainly meets the physical traits teams covet at the position. He is hoping follow in the footsteps of former teammate Armand Membou who was picked 7th overall by the New York Jets in the 2025 NFL Draft. If he can put together a great senior season, I wouldn’t be surprised to see him become a Top 20 selection. Green and the Tigers will host Arkansas-Pine Bluff at Memorial Stadium on Thursday, September 3rd. Jamari Johnson — Tight End — Oregon One position group the Broncos may opt to address early in next year’s draft is tight end. The Broncos added Justin Joly and Dallen Bentley on Day 3 of the 2027 NFL Draft. I like their potential, but Evan Engram is in the final year of his contact, while Adam Trautman will end up being 30 by the start of next season. The Broncos are loaded at wide receiver. However, finding a dynamic talent at tight end who has the chops and ability to play inline would be extremely beneficial for their offense. That’s why Oregon redshirt junior Jamari Johnson is someone I’ll be watching closely throughout the collegiate season. Johnson spent his first two years at Louisville but transferred to Eugene last year in hopes to get more playing time. He played second fiddle to Kenyon Sadiq in the Duck’s offense—who was a first-round pick this past April by the New York Jets. Nevertheless, he still had a productive season with 32 catches [on 40 targets] for 510 yards and 3 touchdowns. Johnson’s traits (6’5” and 257 pounds) and playmaking ability have him scheduled to be a first-round selection next April. He can beat you in a lot of ways, but the fact he logged over 300 run blocking snaps last season goes to show he is someone who projects confidently as an inline ‘Y’ tight end at the next level. You can catch Johnson and the Ducks in action when they host Boise State on Saturday September 5th. Chris Cole — Linebacker — Georgia Last year’s Future Broncos segments had a significant focus on inside linebackers. Sadly, the Broncos bypassed selecting any of the top-tier players. Instead, they opted for continuity bringing back Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad to be their starting duo for the 2026 season. C’est la vie. I was a big fan of Georgia standout CJ Allen for Denver throughout the draft process who wound up being picked in the second round by the Indianapolis Colts. However, his teammate Chris Cole also flashed during games when given the opportunity. He has a chance to catapult up draft boards as a full-time starter this season. Cole was a reserve player as a true freshman and appeared in all fourteen games for the Bulldogs back in ’24. As a sophomore in ‘25, he started just one game but proved to be a versatile player in Chris Schumman’s defense. The former five-star recruit posted 38 tackles, 7 tackles for loss, 4.5 sacks and totaled 18 quarterback pressures on the season. At 6’3″ and 235 pounds with an estimated 4.5 40-yard dash, Cole’s athleticism and range flash on tape. He profiles as one of the better coverage backers in this year’s class and would be a good fit in Vance Joseph’s defense due to his tremendous blitzing skills. This year’s draft class has some great talent at the position, so I’ll try and remain hopeful the Broncos can find a long-term upgrade at the position. You can catch Cole and the Bulldogs when they go up against Tennessee State on Saturday, September 5th.

title: Cuts season opens as Broncos preseason ends
summary: On Sunday, before 4:00pm MT, the Denver Broncos and all NFL clubs will have to cut their rosters from 90-players down to 53. …there are a number [of players for which] it’s the most important thing, period. I don’t watch a lot of TV, but my wife likes watching that Voice where the singers sing. […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Sam Ehlinger #4 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after throwing a touchdown pass to Cody Schrader #25 during the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos won the game 34-6. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday, before 4:00pm MT, the Denver Broncos and all NFL clubs will have to cut their rosters from 90-players down to 53. "Hey, make us spin the chair" 🗣️ Sean Payton on his message to the players on the bubble and why the last preseason game is important 💪 pic.twitter.com/zOlfrvrUjm — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) August 29, 2026 …there are a number [of players for which] it’s the most important thing, period. I don’t watch a lot of TV, but my wife likes watching that Voice where the singers sing. So today it was like, ‘Hey, make us spin the chair.’ Make us spin it.” While it’s awfully bodacious of Sean Payton to align himself in the same constellation as Voice contributors like Lionel Ritchie, CeeLo Green, the Jonas Brothers, his point is not lost. They are looking for that Terrell Davis-like preseason performance that forces the Broncos hand into keeping a particular player (one wonders what example they used prior to that 1995 Tokyo Bowl game, but I digress). Mile High Report fans picked Jonah Coleman as their most impressive performer in this poll after the game against the Falcons in week 1. In week 2, Scotty Payne identified Que Robinson as having had a ‘great night’ in this article summing up the Broncos not-so-great performance against Green Bay. Against the Vikings, there was no doubt that the stand-up performer of the night was running back Cody Schrader. You can’t help but feel for all these players who are waking up on Saturday morning wondering if they did enough to be enough for the Denver Broncos this year. Jonah Coleman and Que Robinson each made Christopher Hart’s 53-man projection , but eyes will certainly be upon Schrader, not for his 42-yards on 13-carries, but for his 90-yards and 1 touchdown on 6 pass receptions. Scotty Payne believes Schrader may have done enough to possibly sneak onto the Broncos practice squad, so it’s entirely possible there could be a little spin yet in Payton’s chair. It’s finally that part of the NFL calendar when dreams are realized or dashed, sometimes both in the same week. Players have given their blood, sweat, and tears toward making this Denver Broncos squad and Broncos Country is mere hours away from knowing their 2026 squad. It’s a time of excitement and sadness, but you can rest assured Mile High Report will be here to help you navigate, celebrate, and mourn the outcome of these coming hours. Buckle up, Broncos Country, the 2026 season is about to begin.

title: 5 Broncos’ players who made a good case for a roster spot in final preseason game
summary: The final preseason game was anything but boring as the Denver Broncos rolled over the Minnesota Vikings in a 34-6 blowout win. There were a lot of great individual performances last night and head coach Sean Payton is going to have a real problem filling out the back end of the initial 53-man roster and […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - AUGUST 28: Justin Joly (80) of the Denver Broncos jogs off the field during the third quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Friday, August 28, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The final preseason game was anything but boring as the Denver Broncos rolled over the Minnesota Vikings in a 34-6 blowout win . There were a lot of great individual performances last night and head coach Sean Payton is going to have a real problem filling out the back end of the initial 53-man roster and deciding who he might be able to sneak onto the 16-man practice squad. Out of all those performances, here are four players we think made a really good case for an active roster spot after that final preseason game. Cody Schrader Cody Schrader absolutely killed it and showed just a ton of talent at the running back position. He can run, he can catch, and he can block out of the backfield. He had over 100 yards from scrimmage, including a touchdown in the back of the end zone on a broken play. I honestly think he might cost Jaleel McLaughlin his spot on the roster with this performance. – Sadaraine CODY MFN SCHRADER TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/GoL2zNOfD9 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 Red Murdock Red Murdock actually had a fairly quiet night on the tackle side of things with just four total tackles, but he had a critical forced fumble living up to his turnover creating reputation. I feel like both he and Taurean York are playmakers, but its also hard to see two rookies getting two active roster spots. I feel like one of them will get it and the other gets stowed away on the practice squad, but we might be seeing the future unfold at inside linebacker with these two. – Tim Lynch Red Murdock ending the preseason with a FORCED FUMBLE — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 29, 2026 Sam Ehlinger Sam Ehlinger had a really good showing against the Vikings. Carrying a 3rd QB might not be what Sean Payton wants to do, but Ehlinger showed that he can hold down a spot on a roster. 15/20 for 233 yards and 3 TDs. I don’t care who it was against. His performance was worthy of note. He might not find himself on the final roster, but you can bet that the Broncos want to keep him around, while other teams might be interested in giving him a shot at a true backup spot. – Adam Malnati Ehlinger finds the speedy Jaleel McLaughlin for a TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/FZfKuuExHH — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 Justin Joly Justin Joly didn’t stand out much in the first two preseason games, but his 88-yard touchdown pass from Sam Ehlinger in the fourth quarter versus the Minnesota Vikings was incredible. This solidified his spot as one of the depth tight ends on the roster. Moreover, it was emblematic of the big-time plays he made throughout college. Hopefully this is just the first of many touchdowns he scores in his career with the Broncos. – Chris Hart Justin Joly with an 88 yard TOUCHDOWN! WIDE ASS OPEN pic.twitter.com/xuSJDqPASe — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 Kolbe Katsis This kid just kept making plays in the return game. He added a second 40+ yard kick return last night with a 48-yard kick return, but more importantly, he adjusted field position in each of his two punt returns also with 2 returns for 31 yards. If it wasn’t for the presence of Marvin Mims Jr., I think he would make the final 53-man roster. However, Denver might have found the heir of Mims if he isn’t extended by free agency next March. We’ll have to see if they can hide Katsis away on the practice squad. – Tim Lynch Kolbe Katsis shows off his speed on the return. title: Did RB Cody Schrader show enough to make the Broncos roster?
summary: After the game, Head Coach Sean Payton referenced the popular singing competition show The Voice when talking about the preseason finale. When asked about his message to players on the roster bubble and why the last preseason game matters, he told reporters, “Hey, make us spin the chair.” One player who came out of nowhere […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - AUGUST 28: Cody Schrader (25) of the Denver Broncos gains positive yards against the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Friday, August 28, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images After the game, Head Coach Sean Payton referenced the popular singing competition show The Voice when talking about the preseason finale. When asked about his message to players on the roster bubble and why the last preseason game matters, he told reporters, “Hey, make us spin the chair.” "Hey, make us spin the chair" 🗣️ Sean Payton on his message to the players on the bubble and why the last preseason game is important 💪 pic.twitter.com/zOlfrvrUjm — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) August 29, 2026 One player who came out of nowhere and may have done that tonight is sixth-string running back Cody Schrader. He has played behind Dobbins, Harvey, Coleman, Badie, and McLaughlin all preseason and mostly was getting late-game work. He is likely viewed as a sure-fire cut candidate and likely a long shot for a practice squad spot. However, after tonight, he may have made the Broncos spin that chair. Schrader finished the night with 132 total yards from scrimmage (90 yards receiving and 42 yards rushing) and simply looked like the best player on the field. He showcased tough running and good vision, and made multiple plays in the passing game, including getting open on a broken play and catching a touchdown from quarterback Sam Ehlinger. Realistically, this performance may not have changed much for Schrader. We have seen players have big games in the finale and not make the team or the practice squad. Former tight end Albert Okwuegbunam is a great example of this. He had a great game in the finale, and we were having this same conversation, but he was still cut hours later and did not make the practice squad. Could things be different for Schrader? He was claimed off waivers late last season, later waived again, and then signed to the Broncos’ practice squad. He later signed a futures contract with the team in the offseason and has served as a back-of-the-roster running back depth all offseason. As I said, heading into this game, not many people had him on their radar, but he may have quickly built a fan base after tonight’s performance. I think the Broncos will keep three running backs on their 53-man roster, and Tyler Badie will be on the practice squad. However, if they want to keep two backs on the practice squad, Schrader made a strong case for that spot tonight.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Winners and Losers from the Denver Broncos’ 34-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings
summary: The preseason is finally done! Next up, Kansas City. After a disappointing showing last week, the Broncos ended the preseason with a dominating 34-6 victory over the Vikings. It was a typical third preseason game that saw the vast majority of the starters sit out the game and the backups get some playing time in […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Cody Schrader #25 of the Denver Broncos catches a pass for a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos won the game 34-6. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The preseason is finally done! Next up, Kansas City. After a disappointing showing last week, the Broncos ended the preseason with a dominating 34-6 victory over the Vikings. It was a typical third preseason game that saw the vast majority of the starters sit out the game and the backups get some playing time in ahead of cut day. As for the winners and losers, this game is a tough one to navigate. Most roster decisions are likely already decided, and players in a good spot either do not play or don’t play much at all. We all witnessed tight end Albert O. have a big game in the preseason finale, only to be cut a few days later and not make the practice squad. With that said, here are my winners and losers from the Denver Broncos’ 34-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings WINNER – RB Cody Schrader Schrader isn’t making the 53-man roster, and honestly, wasn’t on many people’s radar for a spot on the practice squad, but that all likely changes after tonight. The reserve running back had the game of his career tonight, where he totaled 132 total yards from scrimmage (42 yards rushing and 90 receiving yards) and 1 touchdown. This was the Cody Schrader game. CODY MFN SCHRADER TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/GoL2zNOfD9 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 He looked elusive, had good vision, ran hard, and made plays in the passing game. The highlight of his night was getting open on a broken play and catching a wide-open touchdown from quarterback Sam Ehlinger. Coming into the night, he was a borderline practice squad player, and it’s unclear if this performance changes that, but he certainly made the decision tougher for the Broncos coaches. As Sean Payton said at halftime and after the game, this game is like The Voice. “Make us spin the chair”. Cody Schrader may have done that tonight. WINNER – WR Pat Bryant and RB Jonah Coleman I’ll keep this short and sweet, but neither player played tonight, which is great news for both players. A clear sign that Bryant locked down the WR3 job and that rookie running back Jonah Coleman will have a role in this offense. WINNER – QB Sam Ehlinger Veteran Jarrett Stidham started the game and looked decent. He improved on his disappointing performance vs. the Packers, but only played a handful of drives before handing things off to Sam Ehlinger for the rest of the game. Well, it didn’t start off great for the Broncos’ third-string quarterback. He threw an ugly interception on his first pass of the game. Not what you want to see from a player fighting for a spot on this roster. However, Ehlinger didn’t let that mistake keep him down, and he had a pretty good game overall. He finished the game going 15 of 20 for 233 yards and 3 touchdowns. Sam Ehlinger with a dime to Dane Key pic.twitter.com/enmuJ0ZsSd — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 When asked after the game if they will keep three quarterbacks, Payton told reporters, “We’ll see.” Ultimately, I believe they should keep two on the 53 and do what they did last season with Ehlinger as the third quarterback who will bounce on and off the practice squad. As for the backup competition, I don’t think he did enough, and Stidham played ahead of him throughout the preseason. I believe it’s more about whether or not they will keep 2 or 3 quarterbacks, and Ehlinger made a strong case tonight. LOSER – RB Jaleel McLaughlin This isn’t a performance-related loser. It’s the fact that the Broncos sat three running backs, and Tyler Badie, who was active ahead of him for most of the season last year, got the start ahead of McLaughlin and left the game while Jaleel played into the 4th quarter. The writing just seems to be on the wall for the former undrafted free agent. I don’t think he makes the 53-man roster and honestly, it seems like Badie has a better shot at the practice squad spot right now. Then you have Cody Schrader having an insane game, and it gets tough for McLaughlin. He did have a nice catch-and-run touchdown tonight and showed off his speed. I just think he’ll be playing elsewhere this season. WINNER – TE Justin Joly Disclaimer: I could have caught and run this in for a touchdown(maybe), but still. Rookie tight end Justin Joly was about as wide open as you can get and hauled in a Sam Ehlinger pass and ran it in for a walk-in 88-yard touchdown. Justin Joly with an 88 yard TOUCHDOWN! WIDE ASS OPEN pic.twitter.com/xuSJDqPASe — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 It has been a tough summer for the Broncos ‘ 5th-round pick, but he finished the preseason on a high note with this. Again, it was about as easy as you can get, but hey, at least he didn’t drop it. LOSER – Jonathon Cooper While every Broncos starter on offense and defense did not dress for this game, edge rusher Jonathon Cooper did, which isn’t a great sign about his availability moving forward. There is a lot of talk that he will land on the Commissioner’s Exempt list as his legal process moves forward. This will remove him from the 53-man roster and place him on paid leave while his legal matter moves forward. The fact that he played tonight suggests the Broncos do not plan to have him available moving forward. Other Winners and Losers WINNER – S JL Skinner: He got the start and appears to have locked up a spot on the 53-man roster WINNER – LB Karene Reid: It sounds like he will be the Broncos LB3 and has locked up a roster spot WINNER – LB Red Murdock: He unsurprisingly forced a fumble, but does he make the 53-man roster? WINNER – FB Adam Prentice: The preseason MVP scored another touchdown WINNER – TE Nate Adkins: Made some plays in the opening few drives and seems like a player who locked up a roster spot WINNER – WR/KR Kolbe Katsis: Had some good returns and showed off his speed and playmaking ability – Does he make the practice squad? LOSER – WR/KR Cameron Ross: Muffed a punt – Does he make the practice squad? WINNER – Broncos fans: The preseason is FINALLY over, and we’re on to Kansas City

title: Instant reaction: Broncos crush Vikings in preseason finale
summary: The Denver Broncos rested most all their key starters this evening. That gave the Broncos’ coaches plenty of tape to evaluate the backup players vying for a spot on the final 53-man roster. When the game clock struck zero, the Broncos came away with a dominating 34-6 victory in their preseason finale versus the Minnesota […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Jarrett Stidham #8 of the Denver Broncos celebrates a touchdown run by Adam Prentice #46 during the first quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos rested most all their key starters this evening. That gave the Broncos’ coaches plenty of tape to evaluate the backup players vying for a spot on the final 53-man roster. When the game clock struck zero, the Broncos came away with a dominating 34-6 victory in their preseason finale versus the Minnesota Vikings. Here are some instant reactions from tonight’s game. Broncos’ offense bounces back versus Vikings; Cody Schrader has an incredible performance. Last week in their 20-point defeat to the Green Bay Packers, the Broncos struggled in the offensive trenches and couldn’t tote the rock on the ground. In turn, their offense fluttered and they only put 13 points up on the board. Earlier in the week, Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb stated he wanted to see more consistency from the group. Tonight, they didn’t disappoint and executed tremendously. Denver’s starting offensive line was Matt Peart, Kage Casey, Luke Wattenberg, Calvin Throckmorton, and Alex Palczewski. Those five were able to manhandle the competition in the trenches. Wattenberg was eventually replaced by Throckmorton at center, with Palczewski going to right guard, and UDFA rookie Tyler Miller manning down reps at right tackle. With them paving the way, the Broncos’ running game did much better. Tyler Badie had a few good runs. Meanwhile, Cody Schrader impressed in the first half and averaged nearly eight yards per carry. Schrader continued to perform well in his reps in the second half. Quite honestly, he was the player of the game for Denver. He finished with 132 all-purpose yards. Will that be enough for him to make the final 53-man roster? I don’t think so. Denver likely keeps just three running backs. Nevertheless, his performance tonight assured him a spot on the 16-man practice squad. He showed a lot of burst and wiggle in the open field. The only back who struggled in his limited carries early on was Jaleel McLaughlin. However, McLaughlin made up for it with a 20-yard touchdown reception late in the first half. Even so, I’m not sure that will be enough for him to earn a spot when the roster is finalized in less than 48 hours. He saw a lot of playing time even in the second half which usually isn’t a good sign in a preseason finale. The Broncos finished the game with 400 yards of total offense and 34 points scored. As Head Coach John Fox once said, “Not too shabby.” Cody Schrader making the defense miss! MINvsDEN on @NFLNetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YCq09q1cLv — NFL (@NFL) August 29, 2026 Welcome to the NFL, Justin Joly! Justin Joly has had a relatively quiet training camp and preseason. He hadn’t been targeted much in the first two games and only had a couple of receptions. During his collegiate years, he was one of college football’s most productive players. At North Carolina State, he was a vertical threat and bigtime playmaker. With that in mind, he was one of the players I hoped would shine tonight versus the Vikings. It took a while for it to happen, but he hauled in an 88-yard touchdown reception from Sam Ehlinger late in the fourth quarter. Sure, the Vikings had busted coverage, but Joly came down with the ball and took it to the house. Head Coach Sean Payton talks all the time about how a single play or moment can give a player confidence. Maybe this moment will serve as a motivator and momentum builder as he continues to carve out his role with the team and path in the National Football League. Congrats on the big play, Joly! 8️⃣8️⃣ yards to the 🏡! 📺: 9NEWS pic.twitter.com/R1xQTw5Xbe — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 29, 2026 Two players I felt that stood out for Denver on defense. One of the big variables before the final roster cutdowns is what will shake out with EDGE rusher Jonathon Cooper. The Broncos haven’t been informed of a decision yet, but he very well could be suspended for at least six games due to his off-the-field issues earlier this summer. Even if that doesn’t happen, 9News insider Mike Klis mentioned Cooper could be placed on the NFL commissioner’s exempt list as the legal process continues to play out. That means guys like Jonah Elliss, Dondrea Tillman, and Que Robinson will have to step up. I expect Elliss to be the first in line to start. However, I thought Robinson looked quite good in extended playing time. Against the Vikings, he put a lot of pressure on Max Brosmer in the first half. A fourth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, Robinson has tantalizing traits and upside as a starter. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph has spoken highly of him this offseason and he should see quite a bit of playing time early on this season if Cooper is not on the roster to begin the season. Another player I thought impressed again was inside linebacker Karene Reid. In every preseason game to date, Reid has shown a knack for making plays on the ball. Truth be told, he was someone I thought would be a cut. Now? He appears to probably be the best bet for the third backer in the Broncos’ rotation. I still feel Denver may opt to carry five inside linebackers, but will Red Murdock and Jordan Turner be the other two? We’ll know by Monday evening. Que Robinson with a disruptive set of plays in the red zone here down the stretch of the first half. A good reaction to the flat on second down and then a third-down pressure. — Parker Gabriel (@ParkerJGabriel) August 29, 2026 Miscellaneous thoughts and observations: I don’t envision Kolbe Katsis making the final roster, but he solidified his spot on the 16-man practice squad. Katsis had terrific 48-yard return in the first half. He was a tremendous returner in college and could eventually be a future asset for the franchise down the road for his special team’s ability. However, Marvin Mims Jr. did suffer a foot injury early in the game. The severity is unknown, but if it’s significant enough, Katsis may sneak onto the final roster if Mims has to go on short-term IR. Tight end Nate Adkins looked good tonight as well. He lined up in a variety of positions and threw some key blocks and had a nice 26-yard catch and run early in the game. I think he will end up making the final roster this year as well. Adam Prentice also got a few looks in the run game including another touchdown score. I think both players will have a big role in propelling Denver’s rushing attack in 2026 and be important in short yardage and goal line situations. In the third quarter of the broadcast, Klis noted that he didn’t expect the Broncos to make any outside additions via the waiver wire during the roster cutdown process. From what he has heard, Denver’s coaching staff feels good about the players who are developing in the system. That would be a mild surprise to me, but we will just have to see what shakes out over the next couple of days. Kudos to Sam Ehlinger for bouncing back after an interception to start the game. I don’t feel the Broncos will carry three quarterbacks on the final roster, but he really stepped up and was dialing up great throws down the field in the second half. Ehlinger finished the game going 15-of-20 for 233 yards, 3 touchdowns, and 1 interception.
