title: 2026 preseason: Denver Broncos vs. Minnesota Vikings final score
summary: The final preseason game is often a snooze fest, but this one between the Denver Broncos and Minnesota Vikings was anything but. Denver had themselves plenty of big plays and long, sustained drives. All things you hope to see from the team even if starters are on the bench. It also helps that the Broncos […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Cody Schrader #25 of the Denver Broncos runs with the football during the first quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The final preseason game is often a snooze fest, but this one between the Denver Broncos and Minnesota Vikings was anything but. Denver had themselves plenty of big plays and long, sustained drives. All things you hope to see from the team even if starters are on the bench. It also helps that the Broncos dominated from start to finish. Despite the fun game, I am so ready for Week 1. How about you? Broncos vs. Vikings final score Team 1st 2nd 3rd 4th Final Minnesota Vikings 0 6 0 0 6 Denver Broncos 10 10 0 14 34 First Quarter With most of the starters on the bench for this one, it was Jarrett Stidham who got the start and the Broncos took the field first on offense. The offense was clicking on all cylinders early sparked by a 26 yard catch and run by tight end Nate Adkins to get the team into field goal range. Things went south from there after a near interception and a Jaleel McLaughlin stuffed run up the middle. Stiddy would throw an incomplete pass on the next play to Marvin Mims Jr. to kill the drive. Wil Lutz would put Denver on the board first with a 43-yard field goal. Facing Carson Wentz, the Broncos defense was unfazed and forced a very quick three-and-out to get the ball right back into Stidham’s hands. Denver’s second drive began just outside of their own 10 yard line. It looked like they might get back in the down and distance mark, but a nifty run by Tyler Badie gained a first down. He had three carries for nearly 20 yards to start that drive making a strong case for his roster hopes. Tyler Badie making people miss pic.twitter.com/vdhyFUluTW — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 Then Cody Schrader came in to catch a ball out in the flat and turned up field for a 20 yard gain near midfield. Cody Schrader making his case for a roster spot 💪 pic.twitter.com/nTHRv0wzrl — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 Stidham went back to the Schrader well two plays later for another 12-yard gain. He’d get a carry on the next play for another 10+ yard run and a first down into field goal range. After a nine yard scramble by Stiddy and a stuffed run by McLaughlin, the Broncos faced a third and short. A catch by Adkins picked up the first down to setup a first and goal. A short pass to Michael Bandy and then an Adam Prentice plunge would put the Broncos up by two scores late in the first quarter. The 12-play, 88 yard drive had a bit of everything. The first quarter would come to an end with the Vikings coming up three yards short of the first down marker at midfield to bring up fourth down. Broncos 10, Vikings 0. Second Quarter Stidham’s day was done after the first quarter. He finished 6/9 for 78 yards and two scoring drives. Sam Ehlinger would take command of the Broncos offense from the start of the second quarter on. That drive would be disastrous. After two short runs, Ehlinger sailed a pass on third and seven that would be easily intercepted by the Vikings. Sam Ehlinger throws an ugly INT pic.twitter.com/pDxV8Oqu58 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 The Vikings, with that good field position, were able to capitalize on the turnover — sort of. They would need a great effort on a third and long to get into the fringe field goal range. The 46-yard field goal cut the lead back to seven points. Kolbe Katsis ripped off his second 40+ yard return with a 48-yard kickoff return to setup the Broncos up with great field position to start the next drive. Kolbe Katsis shows off his speed on the return. Can he make the 53 man roster? pic.twitter.com/kwXJTvlrhD — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 On the first play of the next drive, Cody Schrader would rip off a big gain for a first down. That would settle Ehlinger a bit for this drive as two plays later he would find Cameron Ross open over the middle for another nice gain and then found Schrader open for a first down into the red zone. An attempted sweep would get blown up to put the Broncos into a second and 16 from their own 18 yard line. A holding penalty pushed them even further backwards. That would kill all momentum and ultimately bring Wil Lutz out for another field goal attempt to put Denver back up by 10. Minnesota would charge back before the end of the half, but the Broncos defense would have an impressive goal line stand to keep the damage minimized to a field goal. The Broncos went into hurry-up mode and three massive pass plays by Ehlinger got Denver right into field goal range with half a minute left in the half. Pass plays to Michael Bandy and Justin Joly got to midfield, then a 20 yard dart to Dane Key set the Broncos up nicely on that drive. Sam Ehlinger with a dime to Dane Key pic.twitter.com/enmuJ0ZsSd — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 Two plays later, Ehlinger would find Jaleel McLaughlin on a crossing route for as 20-yard touchdown pass to put Denver up big heading into halftime. Ehlinger finds the speedy Jaleel McLaughlin for a TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/FZfKuuExHH — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 Broncos 20, Vikings 6. Third Quarter Kolbe Katsis had a decent 17-yard punt return after making something out of nothing. He is making the most of his chances with the football and that should be noted. The Vikings stole the show early in the third quarter with a quality drive spurred by a pretty insane first down catch by Dontae Fleming. Dontae Fleming with an insane first down catch 🔥 MINvsDEN on @NFLNetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sl05mVgm4K — NFL (@NFL) August 29, 2026 That drive would result in a punt, though, as Denver’s defense would clamp down after two chunk plays to keep Minnesota outside of field goal range. Schrader took over the Broncos’ next drive early with big runs and big receptions. A 22-yard gain took the Broncos offense across midfield on that drive. Cody Schrader, have a night! pic.twitter.com/LxDR9GM35n — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 McLaughlin then added another nine yard run where Prentice would pick up the first down into field goal range. Back-to-back negative runs pushed them back and it looked like they would be stopped on third down, but a five-yard defensive penalty gave them an automatic first down. The quarter would end with the Broncos flirting with the red zone. Broncos 20, Vikings 6. Fourth Quarter The drive would stall inside the red zone on a third and two inside run to McLaughlin that was stuffed. They decided to go for it with Ehlinger getting pressured and throwing it up into the end zone to a wide open Schrader for a 14-yard touchdown pass. CODY MFN SCHRADER TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/GoL2zNOfD9 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 The play looked absolutely broken, but they pulled a rabbit out of that hat. The Broncos defense would add a fourth-down goal line stand and two plays later Ehlinger would find a wide-open Justin Joly at midfield for an incredible 88-yard touchdown to keep the blowout rolling. Justin Joly with an 88 yard TOUCHDOWN! WIDE ASS OPEN pic.twitter.com/xuSJDqPASe — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 29, 2026 Ehlinger would finish the game 15/20 for 233 yards, 3 touchdowns and one interception. The ache and need to see these teams run out the clock began to hit after that big play. The would somewhat comply and get us to the final eventually. Broncos 34, Vikings 6.

title: Broncos vs. Vikings: 3 storylines to watch for in Week 3 of NFL preseason
summary: Tue Denver Broncos host the Minnesota tonight for their preseason finale. Coming off an embarrassing blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers last week, the Broncos have a lot of issues to work out. Here are several storylines to watch this evening in Denver’s last gridiron battle before the regular season kicks off in a […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 21: Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on in the second half of a preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field At Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Tyler Schank/Clarkson Creative/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tue Denver Broncos host the Minnesota tonight for their preseason finale. Coming off an embarrassing blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers last week, the Broncos have a lot of issues to work out. Here are several storylines to watch this evening in Denver’s last gridiron battle before the regular season kicks off in a few weeks against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football . Can the Broncos play disciplined and dial back the penalties? The Broncos have experienced an impressive turnaround with Head Coach Sean Payton leading the way. Despite incurring a historic amount of dead cap by moving on from Russell Wilson several seasons ago, Denver has assembled one of the best rosters in the NFL. Moreover, General Manager George Paton has done a tremendous job inking the team’s best players to long-term contracts that have aged well as the market continues to explode at premium positions. Coming off their first AFC title in a decade and 14-win season, the Broncos are in the best spot they have been in ages. However, they have one of the toughest schedules for the upcoming 2026 season. They face a gauntlet in the first half of the season—going head-to-head against a lot of playoff teams and potential Super Bowl contenders. It’ll be tough to win those games, especially if they continue their poor trend of drawing flags. Last season, the Broncos were the fourth-most flagged team in football. A lot of offensive drives were stalled due to them, and many drives for the opposition were extended due to consistent defensive holding, pass interference, or roughing the passer penalties. So far this preseason they have had 18 called against them. That’s a nine per game average which is absolutely alarming. This is a well-coached team, but the miscues and penalty issues that have plagued them for the past several seasons needs to be addressed. Payton was visibly upset with their lack of discipline after their loss to the Packers and mentioned it has to be rectified. That’s one of the major things I’m looking forward to seeing. Will the Broncos’ rushing attack bounce back? One of the reasons why the Broncos were able to trounce the Atlanta Falcons in the preseason opener was because of their ground game. They rushed for over 160 yards. By doing so, they set the pace of the game and controlled the clock. Against the Packers last week, they had less than half of that and barely averaged three yards per carry. That isn’t going to cut the mustard when it matters most. The Vikings have a well-coached defense led by Brian Flores who has a penchant for being aggressive and blitzing. Sometimes, that can backfire on them, and they were in the bottom half of the NFL last season with respect to run defense. I want to see Denver take advantage of that and have a strong rushing performance this evening. Having a solid ground attack will make a huge difference for the Broncos this season. Fans across Broncos Country saw what happened in the second half of the season without J.K. Dobbins. I’m hoping to see Denver deploy a formidable rushing attack against Minnesota and would like Dobbins, alongside RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman, to show what kind of trio they can be in the regular season. What players make the strongest case to make the final 53-man roster? Continuity was a major theme for the Broncos this offseason. Outside of trading for Jaylen Waddle and their 2026 NFL Draft class, Denver didn’t opt to bring in a lot of outside players to their roster. It’s a team loaded with quality starters and solid backups at most positions. Truth be told, there aren’t a lot of positions up for grabs. The preseason finale against the Vikings will be the last chance for fringe roster players to make a case to earn a spot on the roster. The spots I’m looking at the most are who impresses the most at safety. With Taylor Rapp in the fold alongside Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga, those three will be locks for the final roster. The last two spots, if Denver opts to keep five safeties like last season, will come down to Devon Key, Tycen Anderson, J.L. Skinner, and Miles Scott. Key, given his prowess as an All-Pro special team’s player seems likely. Whichever player flashes the most in their defensive reps, in my opinion, will be the one to make the squad. Outside of safety, the battle for two depth spots behind Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad looms large. Karene Reid has played well in both preseason games and seems like a good bet to make the squad. The last spot will come down to Red Murdock, Taurean York, and Jordan Turner. My gut tells me Murdock has the inside track for this one given the praise he has received from Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph throughout training camp. Last but not least, I’ll be keeping a close eye on the offensive trenches. The Broncos have been banged up at center and most all the reserve lineman struggled immensely last week against the Packers. While I’m confident in the team’s starters to play at a high level, finding the right combination of depth players behind them will be crucial. There have been far too many offensive line penalties and blown blocks the past two weeks. What about you, Broncos Country? What things are you keeping a close eye on in the preseason finale against the Vikings? Sound off in the comments section and let me know what you think.

title: 16 Detroit Lions fighting for rosters spots in preseason finale
summary: Earlier this week, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell noted that because of the team’s quick turnaround from their preseason game (Saturday, 1 p.m. ET) and the roster cuts deadline (Sunday, 6 p.m. ET), the team will have to have many of their roster decisions already made by the time they take the field against the […]
full_text: Aug 2, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions wide receiver Tom Kennedy (85) catches a pass during Detroit Lions training camp at Meijer Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Earlier this week, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell noted that because of the team’s quick turnaround from their preseason game (Saturday, 1 p.m. ET) and the roster cuts deadline (Sunday, 6 p.m. ET), the team will have to have many of their roster decisions already made by the time they take the field against the Indianapolis Colts. “You have got to have a pretty good idea where you’re at before you go into that game, knowing there’s a few spots left,” Campbell said. And there are a few spots left, and at least a dozen players vying for those final spots. Here are 16 players I believe are still battling for a spot on the Lions’ 2026 53-man roster, and that doesn’t even include the 20+ players who will be fighting for a place on the 16-man practice squad. QB Josh Dobbs, QB Luke Altmyer The Lions’ backup quarterback job has been wide open since Teddy Bridgewater retired in the middle of training camp. Campbell has already offered his final thoughts on the backup job going into the preseason finale, and this is a battle that really feels like it could go either way. While Altmyer has impressed given his status as an undrafted rookie, it would not be surprising to see Detroit go with the experienced veteran. WR Tay Martin, WR Tom Kennedy, WR Dominic Lovett The Lions are likely set with their top four receivers (Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa, Greg Dortch), but there is a strong competition for a fifth (and potentially sixth) spot in a receiver room Campbell has praised. Martin is likely the top candidate given how much he has been repping with the first and second teams, as well as the top special teams units. But don’t count out the veteran Tom Kennedy, who can play multiple offensive roles and has recently expanded his value by being a top returner on the team. Lovett has the biggest mountain to climb, as he fell out of the returner competition and has been inconsistent on offense. I’m not completely counting out other players, either, like Lucky Jackson or Tarik Black. TE Jackson Meeks I don’t think there’s much question that Meeks is TE4 on the team, but he still needs to justify Detroit keeping that spot over a WR6 or LB6/7 or CB7 or DL10. Meeks is still very much learning the tight end position, but his athleticism, strength, and moxie could make him a decent special teams player—and that’s where he’ll have to win a roster spot. G Mason Miller The Lions’ offensive line situation is a little messy with injuries right now. Here’s how I view the room right now: Locks: Penei Sewell, Blake Miller, Christian Mahogany, Juice Scruggs, Tate Ratledge, Larry Borom Probably safe: Miles Frazier, Ben Bartch Injured: Michael Niese, Cade Mays, Seth McLaughlin(?) Probably out: Colby Sorsdal, Melvin Priestly, Gus Hartwig, Devin Cochran With eight players likely in, but Detroit in desperate need of a healthy backup center, Mason Miller could suddenly see his value skyrocket. He took second-team center reps on the final day of training camp, despite very little experience there. Now, it’s possible McLaughlin’s injury is not considered serious (we currently have no update), and he could be the easy ninth OL on the roster, but if Miller balls out on Saturday, it’s possible he makes a run for the 53-man roster that no one saw coming. DT Chris Smith, DT Mekhi Wingo, DT Ben Stille All camp, Campbell has raved about the depth along the defensive line, and there’s a very good chance Detroit has to let go some player who will eventually find playing time elsewhere. What’s particularly difficult about this group is that they all give you something a little different. Chris Smith is a strong, disciplined nose tackle who “does everything right.” Mekhi Wingo is a pass rushing three-tech who has made a late push at training camp. Ben Stille can play anywhere from the nose to the big end position, and has made a play at nearly every practice over the last two weeks. Smith and Stiller, in my opinion, are fighting for the last roster spot on the team, and both have made strong cases. LB Troy Reeder, LB Joe Bachie, LB Erick Hunter, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga With the unfortunate injury to Damone Clark and the very real possibility that rookie Jimmy Rolder starts the season on IR, there is at least one—possibly two—roster spots available to these four linebackers. Either Campbell or special teams coordinator Dave Fipp have given all four of these players individual praise on their work both on defense and special teams. Linebacker is such an important position on special teams and Reeder, Bachie, and Ogbongbemiga all have extensive history helping out in that regard. But Hunter brings the most intrigue as a rookie with a ton of athletic potential and flashy plays in training camp. CB Ennis Rakestraw, CB Roger McCreary Detroit could easily fit both players on the 53-man roster, and that may be exactly what they end up doing. But Rakestraw and McCreary have both danced around the roster bubble this training camp. McCreary may have pulled himself out with two strong preseason performances, but he is still not repping particularly high. Rakestraw likely needs the big finish more, but the Lions may also be more willing to be patient with the 24-year-old corner.

full_text: Nov 24, 2024; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; The Detroit Lions take on the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Marc Lebryk-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con It’s last call for the 2026 NFL preseason. The Detroit Lions and Indianapolis Colts face off in the penultimate game of the exhibition season. Thus far, 28 teams have concluded their preseason slate and are preparing for roster cuts, which are due by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, Aug. 30. The Lions, however, still have one important piece of the evaluation puzzle left. Saturday’s game against the Colts could absolutely win or lose jobs for certain players, so you know they’ll be giving it their all. Here’s how you can watch Lions vs. Colts in preseason Week 3. When is the Lions vs. Colts? The game is on Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026, and kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET. Where is the game being played? The preseason finale is in Indianapolis, Indiana, at Lucas Oil Stadium. Who is playing in the game? While Dan Campbell has not specifically said it, it’s unlikely the Lions will be playing any starters in this game. Instead, the Lions head coach said he wanted Saturday’s game to be an opportunity for players battling for jobs to showcase their talent. “We want to give a lot of exposure to some of these guys to give them the best opportunity to put their best stuff on tape, whether it’s here or for another team, because they’ve earned that,” Campbell said. “And so, they’re going to get a lot of reps, a lot of snaps, and it’ll be good exposure for them.” How can I watch Lions vs. Colts live? The Lions will be televised live locally on all of the Detroit Lions TV Network affiliates. In the metro Detroit area, that’s Fox 2 Detroit. For other affiliates, check the Lions’ map here . It’s also being played nationally on NFL Network. Is it being replayed nationally? Yes, but it won’t be worth it. NFL Network is replaying the game on THURSDAY, Sept. 3 at 1 a.m. ET. Can I stream the game? Yes! If you are not a local Lions fan, you can watch the game on NFL+ with a subscription. Local fans can watch the game on DetroitLions.com or via the official Lions app for free! Who are the TV announcers for Lions vs. Colts? The Lions’ local TV broadcast consists of Jason Benetti, T.J. Lang, and Patti Cesarini. Radio options for Lions vs. Colts game? Same as always. Get your fix of Dan Miller and Lomas Brown over on 97.1 The Ticket or whatever Lions Radio Network affiliate is available in your area . Or, if you want all of that information condensed: Lions vs. Colts game information: When: Saturday, August 29, 2026 — 1 p.m. ET Where: Lucas Oil Stadium — Indianapolis, IN Local TV: FOX 2 Detroit ( or other local Lions affiliates ) National TV: NFL Network Online streaming: NFL+ (national), Lions team app (local) Announcers: Jason Benetti, T.J. title: Lions fans believe Luke Altmyer is favorite for QB2 job headed into preseason finale
summary: Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook, and asked Detroit Lions fans: Which Lions QB is the favorite for the backup job heading into the preseason finale? The battle for QB2 on the Lions’ 2026 roster could come down to the final moments of the […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - AUGUST 22: Luke Altmyer #2 of the Detroit Lions looks to pass the ball during the fourth quarter of a preseason game against the Washington Commanders at Ford Field on August 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , and asked Detroit Lions fans: Which Lions QB is the favorite for the backup job heading into the preseason finale? The battle for QB2 on the Lions’ 2026 roster could come down to the final moments of the offseason, making it one of the highlights of the preseason finale . Once Teddy Bridgewater elected to retire, undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer stepped into the QB2 role and has been competing with veteran Josh Dobbs over the past three weeks. Historically, the Lions have heavily favored a veteran in the QB2 role, but coach Dan Campbell insists that the team is keeping all options open in this battle. “I mean, you would like that because those guys have played; there are real reps,” Campbell said of leaning on a veteran QB2 in the past. “They’ve been under real fire in real football games, and that is important. But that’s not the end-all, be-all, either. If you think there’s somebody to work with here and that he’s shown enough progress and he’s only going to get better, then we don’t close our eyes to that either.” So, will the Lions stick with their historical preference and run with Dobbs? Or, has Altmyer shown enough upside to convince Campbell he’s ready? According to the majority of Lions fans, Altmyer’s progress and upside are warranted and make him the favorite for the job entering the preseason finale. If Altmyer is indeed the favorite for the QB2 job, he’ll need to meet Campbell’s expectations in the preseason finale: “Consistency. Just play good, smart football,” Campbell said of what Altmyer needs to show against the Colts. “We don’t need some wild throws, whatever. Be able to run the offense, be efficient, make smart decisions, even if that means that you’re punting the ball. That’ll be the most important thing. We don’t want the wild plays, and then there’s an ill-advised throw across the middle for an interception—those won’t get it done. So just be smart, take what’s there, run the offense and that’ll go a long way.” Let’s take a closer look at the comment section of our original article and The Feed post to see fans’ explanations for their selection (lightly edited for clarity). NOTE: There were a lot of comments supporting Dobbs, but the comments below only reflect those of the winner of the poll. Cmonman14 (via the FEED) : “I hope it’s Altmyer, he will have to clear waivers to end up on practice squad, and another team might pluck him. I’m impressed with him so far, and imo he has a much higher ceiling than Dobbs.” TomRem .: “… I would much rather see Altmeyer backup Goff, even though Dobbs might be better in Goff’s ear to tell him what he sees from the sideline.” LifetimecubsandLionsfan : “I say, Altmeyer. I realize he’s young and inexperienced, but he has a ton of heart and toughness. And grit. He worked his ass off in Champaign and got progressively better while not giving up who he is as a QB. I know that Dobbs is a more proven commodity, and I do understand the argument for him, but I just like Altmeyer in the backup role learning from Goff for the future.” While this comment isn’t Pro-Altmyer, it’s certainly a solid argument against Dobbs: FeelTheBern2020 : “Dobbs was signed August 9th. No team signed him all summer, and it’s not like he’s proving everyone wrong with his preseason play. Barring an exceptional performance this weekend, I’d be shocked if another team even goes after him for their practice squad, let alone 53.” As a reminder, this survey was sponsored by the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook , who currently have the Lions listed as +1700 to win this year’s Super Bowl, +850 to win the NFC Championship, and +155 to win the NFC North as the current favorites. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Detroit Lions fans and fans across the country. If you want to receive these surveys by email weekly, you can sign up here .

title: Best Lions content of the week: Goff, St. Brown discuss their telepathy
summary: The connection between a quarterback and wide receiver is one of the more storied partnerships in all of sports, and for good reason. full_text: The connection between a quarterback and wide receiver is one of the more storied partnerships in all of sports, and for good reason. So many details go into the artistry that occurs between the two positions on gameday. And if you are looking for proof, just ask one of the best duos in NFL—Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown. “When you watch Goff and St. Brown on the field, you can see they’re finishing each other’s sentences — if every sentence was punctuated with a first down,” wrote Henry McKenna of Fox Sports in his recent feature on the pair. “It’s not normal. They can make changes mid-play without even having to look at each other. It goes beyond coaching.” If you have been watching the Lions for the last several years, then chances are you know exactly what McKenna is talking about. “I think we’ve been playing for so long together that he understands my body language when I’m running routes,” St. Brown told McKenna. “That he can anticipate throws before I’m even out of the break. He kind of knows, ‘Oh, that’s how it looks when he’s about to break down.’ So he already knows. He can anticipate the throw.” The article dives into what makes the relationship between the two pros so special, including frequent visits to St. Brown’s favorite sushi restaurant near their Los Angeles area offseason homes. You can read the entire article from McKenna right here . And now onto the rest of the best Lions content from this week. If you didn’t already see, Chris Long and The Greenlight Podcast were in Allen Park recently, and they got some excellent interviews in with St. Brown, Goff, and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. full_text: Just like that, Detroit Lions training camp is officially complete. After about four weeks of practices, the last hurdles standing between the team and the regular season are the final preseason season game against the Indianapolis Colts on Saturday, and cut-down day on Sunday where coach Dan Campbell and general manager Brad Holmes will be faced with some difficult decisions in regards to who is going to make the final roster. And while we can expect the majority of the Lions’ starters to be in street clothes for the preseason finale in Indiana, there are still several hotly-contested competitions taking place, starting at the quarterback position. Can rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer do enough to unseat the battle-tested veteran Josh Dobbs? Staying on the offensive side of the ball, there are still things to sort out concerning the running back and wide receiver positions, too. Defensively, there are potentially even more tough decisions to make. Along the defensive line, there is a bit of a logjam at defensive tackle between the likes of Skyler Gill-Howard, Chris Smith, and Mekhi Wingo. Moving into the secondary and there may be even more questions than the defensive line. That brings us to today’s question of the day: What will you be watching for in the Lions’ final preseason game against the Colts? My answer: As usual, my eyes will be fixed on the trenches. On the offensive line, who gets the most work at center? Will Juice Scruggs see any reps, or will he also be in street clothes? If he isn’t dressed, will Seth McLaughlin see the majority of the opportunities? On the other side of the ball, will the last preseason game help the coaching staff figure out which direction they want to go in as far as the active roster is concerned? What about you? title: Detroit Lions backup quarterback race highlights preseason finale
summary: The Detroit Lions enter their final preseason game with likely most of their roster spots decided, but one that may still be up in the air is the backup quarterback job. Entering training camp, there likely wasn’t going to be much drama at the position. However, Teddy Bridgewater’s abrupt retirement midway through camp forced the […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16), and center Cade Mays (64), left, practice next to offensive lineman Juice Scruggs (70), and quarterback Luke Altmyer (2) during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions enter their final preseason game with likely most of their roster spots decided, but one that may still be up in the air is the backup quarterback job. Entering training camp, there likely wasn’t going to be much drama at the position. However, Teddy Bridgewater’s abrupt retirement midway through camp forced the Lions to pivot. While undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer has been with the team all offseason, suddenly thrusting a 23-year-old into the backup position wasn’t something the Lions were willing to do unopposed. So they quickly added nine-year veteran Josh Dobbs to the room. But thus far in camp, Altmyer has continued to get the bulk of the backup reps. And what seemed like a far-fetched approach—letting Altmyer be the backup to veteran Jared Goff—now seems closer to reality than ever. On Thursday, Lions coach Dan Campbell asked what he needs to see from Altmyer to have the confidence that he can handle such a critical role. “Consistency. Just play good smart football,” Campbell said. “We don’t need some wild throws, whatever. Be able to run the offense, be efficient, make smart decisions, even if that means that you’re punting the ball. That’ll be the most important thing. We don’t want the wild plays and then there’s an ill-advised throw across the middle for an intercept—those won’t get it done. So just be smart, take what’s there, run the offense and that’ll go a long way.” It hardly seems like a coincidence that Campbell would bring up the example of an ill-advised pass over the middle that was intercepted. That could be fresh in his mind because Altmyer’s competition, Josh Dobbs, did exactly that in the team’s second preseason game last week . But under Dan Campbell, the Lions have seemingly preferred to have a veteran set of eyes behind Goff. Be it Bridgewater, David Blough, or Kyle Allen, the Lions almost always wanted a seasoned player among the quarterback reserves, with the lone exception being 2024 (Hendon Hooker, Jake Fromm). Campbell admitted they prefer to have experienced players at quarterback, but that won’t trump overall talent when it comes to cut-down day. “I mean, you would like that because those guys have played, there are real reps. They’ve been under real fire in real football games and that is important. But that’s not the end all be all, either,” Campbell said. “If you think there’s somebody to work with here and that he’s shown enough progress and he’s only going to get better, then we don’t close our eyes to that either.” Further complicating the Lions’ decision is the amount of roster gymnastics they could try to perform to keep both players around. Because Dobbs is a veteran, the Lions could opt to cut him, not subject him to waivers, and bring him back later either on the practice squad or 53-man roster. But at the same time, how likely is it that Altmyer would get claimed on waivers if Detroit opted to cut him? Last year, there were only 27 total waiver claims after initial NFL roster cuts , and just one of them (Tommy Devito) was a quarterback. So the Lions could keep Dobbs on the roster, and bring back Altmyer assuming he clears waivers. Regardless, the Lions won’t make that decision until after Saturday’s preseason finale against the Indianapolis Colts. It’s unclear how the Lions will share the load between Altmyer and Dobbs on gameday, but their performance could be the tipping point for a difficult decision.

title: Dan Campbell delivers an awesome message to high school football players
summary: Thursday night, high school football teams around the state kicked off their 2026 season. For some kids, it’s the last “opening week” of football they’ll ever play at an organized level. Several hours before football kicked off in the state of Michigan, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell delivered an awesome message to the high school […]
full_text: Aug 3, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell addresses the media prior to Detroit Lions training camp. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Thursday night, high school football teams around the state kicked off their 2026 season. For some kids, it’s the last “opening week” of football they’ll ever play at an organized level. Several hours before football kicked off in the state of Michigan, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell delivered an awesome message to the high school kids out there ready to strap their helmets on. “Make the most of it,” Campbell said. “Because you’re not guaranteed to be able to get another chance to play and be with those guys that you grew up with and enjoy the game at that level and the wins and the sacrifice and the hard work and the blood and the sweat and the tears, It’s a special time, enjoy it.” Campbell is obviously one of the lucky ones to make a career out of football, both as a player and a coach. But despite playing for 10 seasons, participating in a Super Bowl, coaching for nearly another two decades, and being a part of endless classic NFL games, he still remembers both the sting and the wonder of his last game in high school—a loss, as he’s quick to point out. “We lost, and it wasn’t good. Yeah, we weren’t going to the playoffs, I remember that,” Campbell said. “But I remember being with that group of guys that I knew and I grew up with and I was with for a long time. And it is, you don’t forget those, you just don’t. You just don’t forget and it is a special time. And you’re going to look back and wish, ‘Man, I wish I could do that one more time. I wish I could go back and play that game one more time or play with those guys one more time.’” While Campbell pleaded to high school seniors appreciate the moment and give it all you’ve got so you don’t have any regrets, he also had a message for the underclassmen. “If you’re a young guy, man, I’m a freshman, I’m a sophomore, you owe it to the seniors because this may be the last time that—you get one more shot, they don’t,” Campbell said. “So, give them everything you have got and make it a special year for them because next year is your year and you’re going to want those young guys to help you. So, man, enjoy it. It doesn’t last and you’ll remember it the rest of your life.” It’s one thing to read Campbell’s words. It’s another to experience them. So do yourself a favor and watch his answer to the question below, and share it with any high school football player you know. "Make the most of it" – Coach Campbell on high school football season starting pic.twitter.com/7pZYz1VYXf — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 27, 2026

title: Packers wide receivers make their cases in final preseason game
summary: Earlier in the preseason I suggested the Packers open up their wide receiver competition. I don’t know if the Packers’ brass got the message, but the receivers on the lower end of the roster certainly lived up to their end of the bargain. The third preseason game was a 60 minute wide receiver showcase, with […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - AUGUST 28: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Kisean Johnson (86) scores the game winning touchdown during a preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and the Arizona Cardinals on August 28, 2026 at Lambeau Field, in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Earlier in the preseason I suggested the Packers open up their wide receiver competition . I don’t know if the Packers’ brass got the message, but the receivers on the lower end of the roster certainly lived up to their end of the bargain. The third preseason game was a 60 minute wide receiver showcase, with several contenders putting up their best statistical performances of the exhibition slate. J. Michael Sturdivant has been perhaps the strongest contender and put together the best statistical performance of any Packers receiver this preseason so far. He caught six passes for 112 yards and a touchdown, the score coming on a beautifully designed play that sprung him down the left sideline for six. Sturdivant finishes the preseason with nine catches for 142 yards and a touchdown. Just as importantly, he played 19 snaps on special teams during the Packers’ three preseason games, including six and three, respectively, on the Packers’ crucial punt and kickoff coverage units. I don’t know if it’s enough to make the 53 man roster, but that’s about all you could ask for from an undrafted player trying to make a case for himself. Isaiah Neyor has been the next strongest roster contender, and his stats have been more steady than spectacular. He had ten total catches across three preseason games, finishing with exactly 100 yards. He failed to find the end zone, but that doesn’t mean much in preseason competition, when opportunities can be inconsistent and quarterback play can be spotty. Neyor actually played a bit more on special teams than Sturdivant, logging 21 snaps in three games, but 10 of those snaps came on kickoff return, which is a lower priority than the coverage units. Will Sheppard was the next most productive receiver. Due to being a bit smaller (but not much) than both Sturdivant and Neyor, I think most roster watchers have penciled him in behind his bigger-bodied counterparts, but he showed up against the Cardinals in a big way. He caught three passes for 26 yards and a score, but his real highlight was an 81-yard punt return for his second touchdown of the evening. If big plays carry weight in roster competitions, no wide receiver made a bigger one than that. Sheppard finished the preseason with 10 catches for 81 yards and two touchdowns. Finally, Kisean Johnson saved his best for last. Signed by the Packers on August 9, Johnson has come along slowly and his opportunities have been more limited than the rest of the lower-end receivers, but he made up some ground (statistically, at least) on Friday night. Johnson caught four passes for 52 yards and two touchdowns, including the game-winner to cap off the Packers’ two-minute drive to end the game. Those catches represented his full statistical output in this year’s preseason, but it was an eye-catching performance, to be sure. As impressive as each of these players may have been, the harsh reality is they’re competing for maybe one roster spot. Christian Watson, Jayden Reed, and Matthew Golden have roster spots locked up, as does Savion Williams (despite injuries and generally unimpressive play). Beyond those four, Bo Melton and Skyy Moore seem like good bets as special teams contributors. For any of the four receivers we talked about in this piece to have a shot, the Packers would have to keep seven wide receivers on their initial 53-man roster. That’s not unheard of, but it shows how tenuous the life of a player on the roster bubble can be: no matter how well you perform, the ruthless accounting of NFL roster building still might mean you end up out of a job.

title: Packers Roster Cut Tracker 2026
summary: Sunday, August 30th is a big day for the NFL this year. In 2026, the league has set the deadline for teams to cut their rosters down from 90 players to 53 for Sunday at 6:00 PM Eastern Time (5:00 Central), an odd time compared to recent deadlines. Recent years have seen the league require […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - AUGUST 02: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFluer and General Manager Brian Gutekunst look on during the annual Green Bay Packers Family night practice at Lambeau Field on August 2nd, 2025 in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Sunday, August 30th is a big day for the NFL this year. In 2026, the league has set the deadline for teams to cut their rosters down from 90 players to 53 for Sunday at 6:00 PM Eastern Time (5:00 Central), an odd time compared to recent deadlines. Recent years have seen the league require cuts come in on the Tuesday following the final week of preseason games, giving front offices a few extra days. This year, however, the league’s decision to hold a game in Australia in week one led it to push the cutdown date a bit earlier. Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst revealed that in a press conference earlier this week, noting that while not a fan of the shift, there’s not really anything he or the other 31 GMs around the league can do about it. That means that the Packers will have a little less than 48 hours from the completion of their final preseason game (around 10 PM Central on Friday night) to the cut-down deadline. Here at Acme Packing Company, we will be following along with all of the Packers’ moves to get from 90 to 53, which will include releases, players going on the reserve/PUP list, and more. The Reserve/Physically Unable to Perform list is one mechanism for teams to keep players on their roster in a reserve role if they failed a physical exam before training camp, went on the active/PUP list to start camp, and stayed there all summer long. Players who go on reserve/PUP to start the regular season do not count against the 53-man limit, but they may not be activated until after their team’s fourth regular season game, though they can start practicing after two games have passed. The Packers have four players still on the active/PUP who are eligible for the reserve/PUP to start the season: Luke Musgrave, Matt Orzech, Micah Parsons, and Jordon Riley. Parsons has generally been targeting the Packers’ week 6 game against his old team, the Dallas Cowboys, for his return. Perhaps surprisingly, he is not seen as one of the favorites to win the NFL’s Comeback Player of the Year award; FanDuel sportsbook has his odds at just +3500 , good for 10th in the NFL. That slots in behind teammate Tucker Kraft (7th, +2700), while a host of quarterbacks like Patrick Mahomes, Kyler Murray, and Jayden Daniels lead the way. Stay tuned here for news on the Packers’ roster as it is revealed. Players to be waived None so far Reports of bubble players who have made the initial 53-man roster None so far

title: Green Bay Packers Roster: A final 2026 53-man prediction
summary: Alright, here’s my final stab at the Green Bay Packers’ 53-man roster before Sunday’s cutdowns. As a reminder, this prediction is mostly based on the work I’ve done on the Packers’ depth chart, and there weren’t huge changes to the pecking order in Green Bay’s preseason finale — where 37 players sat against the Arizona […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Kyle McCord #18 and Dalton Cooper #78 of the Green Bay Packers celebrate after a touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals in the fourth quarter during a preseason game at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Alright, here’s my final stab at the Green Bay Packers’ 53-man roster before Sunday’s cutdowns. As a reminder, this prediction is mostly based on the work I’ve done on the Packers’ depth chart , and there weren’t huge changes to the pecking order in Green Bay’s preseason finale — where 37 players sat against the Arizona Cardinals . My guess is that it’s going to be pretty chalky when you look around at 53-man projections this year, barring a suspension, last-minute trade or something injury-related that was unforeseen. For the most part, there aren’t many debates on the roster. Quarterback Jordan Love Tyrod Taylor This one is pretty easy, since both Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor sat on Friday night, while Kyle McCord played every snap of offense. I’m assuming that McCord will be re-signed to the practice squad, and if there’s anyone who displaces Taylor, it will come from an outside addition. The Packers never really seemed to have any interest in letting McCord battle for the #2 job this summer. Running Back Josh Jacobs MarShawn Lloyd Chris Brooks This is another pretty easy one, unless Josh Jacobs gets suspended by the NFL. As of now, head coach Matt LaFleur has stated that he “fully anticipate(s)” Jacobs to be on the team this year, despite his recent charges of battery and criminal damage to property . If Jacobs is suspended by the league before the cutdown deadline, he will be on the reserve/suspended list and not take up a space on Green Bay’s 53-man roster. If Jacobs is suspended, Pierre Strong Jr. — who, unlike MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks, had to suit up in the preseason finale — would be the next man up. Considering the Packers’ circumstances, I wouldn’t be surprised if Strong and undrafted rookie Jaden Nixon both make the initial practice squad. Receiver Christian Watson Matthew Golden Jayden Reed Savion Williams Bo Melton Skyy Moore J. Michael Sturdivant The Packers’ starters at receiver are Christian Watson (Z), Matthew Golden (X) and Jayden Reed (slot), with Savion Williams (Z), Bo Melton (X) and Skyy Moore (slot) being their direct backups. Five of those six receivers sat out all of the preseason finale, with Melton playing three snaps of offense (presumably so he could match up against his brother, Max, who plays for the Cardinals). J. Michael Sturdivant was already ahead of Isaiah Neyor, in terms of what the team asked the two to do on special teams, but Week 3 of the preseason also featured Sturdivant going for 112 yards in the air — putting him over Neyor in both aspects of the position. According to Sports Illustrated ’s Bill Huber , Sturdivant’s yardage was the most of any Packers receiver in a preseason game since 2011. The undrafted rookie streak will continue for another year! Tight End Tucker Kraft Jonnu Smith Josh Whyle With the addition of Jonnu Smith and the resting of Josh Whyle on Friday, it seems pretty clear that this is the direction that the Packers are going in. Green Bay will keep Luke Musgrave (neck) on the PUP list until he’s ready to return. Offensive Line Zach Bako-Bewele (RT) Sean Rhyan (C) Jordan Morgan (LT) Aaron Banks (LG) Jacob Monk (C/C) Jager Burton (G/C) Anthony Belton (T/G) Donovan Jennings (G/C) John Williams (T) I’m dropping an offensive lineman here, since I only had two tight ends making the team in our last prediction . The guy not making the cut is tackle Darian Kinnard, who was working with the third-string offensive line in the preseason finale after he was the team’s sixth offensive lineman in the second half of the 2025 season. Yes, it truly does feel like Kinnard has been passed up by the likes of Jacob Monk, Donovan Jennings and John Williams (as well as rookie fifth-round pick Jager Burton). No returning player has sunk on the depth chart this summer as much as Kinnard. Defensive Line Devonte Wyatt Karl Brooks Javon Hargrave Warren Brinson Chris McClellan Jonathan Ford Jonathan Ford had a visit to the blue tent on Friday for a knee injury, but he was able to jog off the field, so I’m assuming that he’s not significantly injured. Ford has been starting as the team’s true 3-4 nose tackle, which the Packers should play about one-third of the time this year. Anthony Campbell is another option here, too, but Ford having such a defined role for the team makes me think they move in that direction, and it’s going to be very hard for the team to keep seven interior defensive linemen from a numbers perspective. Jordon Riley will also start the year on the PUP list. Edge Defender Lukas Van Ness Barryn Sorrell Brenton Cox Jr. Collin Oliver Dani Dennis-Sutton Until the final preseason game, when Dani Dennis-Sutton made his NFL debut, this was a pretty clear 1-2-3-4 pecking order. I bet that Dennis-Sutton probably slides in over Collin Oliver (and potentially Brenton Cox Jr.) eventually in 2026, but I’m not sure how quickly that will happen — considering Dennis-Sutton missed two preseason games as a rookie. Micah Parsons will be on the PUP list. Whenever Parsons comes back, the team will have a logjam at the position, which will probably result in the team moving on from one of Cox or Oliver, unless injuries free up roster spots. Off-Ball Linebacker Zaire Franklin Edgerrin Cooper Isaiah McDuffie Ty’Ron Hopper Nick Niemann This is just the 2025 linebacker unit with Zaire Franklin playing the Mike position instead of Quay Walker. You can go ahead and lock this one in. Cornerback Keisean Nixon Carrington Valentine Brandon Cisse Benjamin St-Juste Domani Jackson Domani Jackson made my 53-man roster projection, but he’s functionally the last spot on the roster to me. The four other cornerbacks ahead of him were all held out of action in the preseason finale, unlike Jackson. Jackson had a tough go of it in the preseason after missing the opener as he recovered from an offseason surgery to his core. This is a lazy pick, but he’s a rookie draft pick who just got healthy. I’m not sure if the team is just going to risk him passing through waivers after investing time, effort and one of their very few draft picks in 2026 into Jackson. In the past, general manager Brian Gutekunst has held onto draft picks that we didn’t expect. I could see the team holding onto Jackson to essentially redshirt him this year, as only 48 of 53 players (plus two practice squad call-ups per week) are allowed to suit up on gamedays. Safety Xavier McKinney Evan Williams Javon Bullard Kitan Oladapo Kamal Hadden Kamal Hadden taking over as the next man up at the slot position behind Javon Bullard really solidified him on the roster to me. In the past, Hadden has had a problem staying on the game-day roster because he’s a defensive back who didn’t perform too well on special teams, but now that the team is a little thinner at the slot position, it makes all of the sense in the world for Hadden to be a full-time game-day active. An interesting quirk to the whole Kitan Oladapo-Kamal Hadden situation is that Oladapo is the next safety up, but Hadden is playing the “ three safety ” role ahead of Oladapo, as the third safety is really just the slot defender in the Packers’ Penny packages. Again, this doesn’t really matter in Week 1, as long as Javon Bullard recovers from his foot bone bruise. Weird example, but something to keep in mind: If Bullard went down, I wouldn’t expect Oladapo to come off the bench to play the slot. That would be Hadden. But if Xavier McKinney or Evan Williams got hurt, I would expect Oladapo to come off the bench to play safety, allowing Bullard, who would play safety in base 3-4 looks, the freedom to kick into the slot. title: Packers Preseason Game 3: Some statistical nuggets vs. the Cardinals
summary: “Did you all see that awesome preseason game,” is not something I am in the habit of saying, yet here we are. It was an instant (preseason) classic: a 42-38 barn-burner that saw the Green Bay Packers score twice in the final 3-and-a-half minutes to take home a win. We’re going to try something this […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Kedon Slovis #12 of the Arizona Cardinals is pressured by Dani Dennis-Sutton #51 of the Green Bay Packers during a preseason game at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images “Did you all see that awesome preseason game,” is not something I am in the habit of saying, yet here we are. It was an instant (preseason) classic: a 42-38 barn-burner that saw the Green Bay Packers score twice in the final 3-and-a-half minutes to take home a win. We’re going to try something this week with the hope of doing it during the regular season as well. SumerSports – a site I’ve been a fan of since they started – recently released SumerPass . Part of SumerPass is live game-tracking, with some really cool stats available immediately. So we’re going to comb through some of the data and post some tidbits here. This will likely change as we move throughout the season, but, for now, we’re just going to try it on and see how it fits. Offense We’ll start with the big picture. Packers ran this game out of two personnel groupings: 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) was used on 76.4% of their snaps while 12 personnel (1 RB, 2 TE, 2 WR) was used on 23.6% of their snaps. They leaned heavily into the pass this game, passing on 69.1% of their snaps. That would mark a 12.93% increase over the rest of the league. And, lest you think the 4th quarter comeback was propping up those numbers, they passed on 69.6% of their 1st half plays. That means that their 68.8% 2nd half pass rate was actually lower. Which is a bit surprising, given who was calling plays in the 2nd half. Matt LaFleur says Jordan Love called the plays in the second half. — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) August 29, 2026 Either way, they were letting Kyle McCord air it out, and he performed well. For the game, he went 22/35 for 226 yards and an EPA per play of +0.05. He had an average time to throw of 2.39 seconds (0.3 less than the average time) and a 10.4 ADOT (Average Depth of Target). That ADOT was 2.6 yards above the NFL average. He was really cooking out of 11 personnel with a +0.11 EPA per Play. It was a much lower sample size, but his EPA Per Play out of 12 personnel was worse by a decent amount (-0.2). He did some nice work against Cover 1 (4/5 for 38 yards, +0.78 EPA per Play) and struggled against Cover 4 (8/14, 39 yards, 1 sack, -0.52 EPA per Play). His pressure-to-sack rate of 27.27% was 9.87% worse than the NFL average. J. Michael Sturdivant did a great job with his opportunities. His Target Share of 20.6% was 0.8% higher than the NFL average. He caught 6 of his 7 targets for 112 yards, good for +1.63 EPA per Reception. His ADOT of 14.14 yards was 3.3 yards higher than the NFL average, but he showed a much better route tree than we had been seeing from him. He wasn’t just productive on deep routes. He had 1 target on a Go route (the 29 yarder up the right side that I’m sure we’ll cover in a film room article) and 2 targets on post routes, but his other 4 targets were close to the line (2 targets on hitches, 2 targets on quick out routes). He primarily operated as an outside receiver, with 5 targets when aligned outside and 2 targets from the slot. Sturdivant did well against both Man (+1.25) and Zone (+1.71) coverages. Their run game was primarily zone-based, with 11.8% being Inside Zone, 58.8% Outside Zone, 23.5% Man and 5.9% that are simply listed as “Other”. They’ve never truly gone away from their zone running roots, but there are a lot of signs pointing to going back to that at a higher rate this year, so this is something we’ll be monitoring as we get into the season. Defense On defense, the Packers operated primarily out of Nickel (84.8%), with the rest coming out of Base (15.2%). No Dime or anything like that. Nickel and Base. On the whole, they ran much more Zone (68.8%) than Man (25%). I’m curious to see how these stats play out across the year, because Man and Zone are such simplistic buckets. In the Match Quarters system we’re going to be seeing from Gannon this year, we’ll see a lot of Match coverages. Meaning, it’s a malleable system that will present differently depending on how the routes are distributed. Or, more simply, it’s a zone coverage that can often look like man. If we’re talking simply in Man/Zone buckets, these types of calls muddy the water. Might be something we scrap as we move forward with this. We’ll see. For the game, the Packers had a pressure rate of 37.5%, 0.28% below the NFL average. Their Blitz Rate of 14.58% was 12.02% below the NFL average. Vanilla defense, man. The splash player on defense was Nyjalik Kelly, coming in with 8 impact plays: 5 solo tackles, 1 assisted tackle and 3 tackles for loss. I’m really looking forward to watching him. I saw some nice improvement in his game between Week 1 and Week 2, so I’m curious to see if he kept on that upward trajectory this week. Anthony Campbell keeps showing up and making plays. The normal caveats of preseason and all that, but he notched a 17.9% pressure rate in this game, 9.78% higher than the NFL average. He’s been making noise throughout training camp and practices and he’s been making noise in every preseason game. He still is largely just a rotational guy at this point, but he’s huge (6’7”, 300 lbs), shows some real quickness in his feet and heaviness in his hands. I’ve enjoyed watching him. Lastly, let’s talk about Dani Dennis-Sutton. It was our first chance to watch him on the field, and he didn’t disappoint. He posted 2 solo tackles and 1 tackle for loss. He was also a menace as a pass rusher, posting a 17.4% pressure rate. He also posted a 23.1% pressure rate on stunts (9.39% higher than the NFL average). That’s something I’ll be looking for both in the preseason film and during the regular season. Is that a weird preseason blip, or is that a superpower of his? Given his size, strength and linear speed, it could be that he’s near unstoppable on stunts. Special Teams No stats needed. Trey Smack is a gamer. This was a fun little trip into the data. Feels a bit scattered, but that’s probably just because that’s who I am as a person. We’ll lock it in for the regular season. I’m looking forward to seeing where this takes us every week. It’s already given me a couple areas to focus one once the film is made available, so I’m taking that as a win. Albums listened to: Dinosaur Jr. – There Near ; Eykah Badu & The Alchemist – Before the World Blows

title: Matt LaFleur: Packers ‘fully anticipate’ RB Josh Jacobs to remain on roster
summary: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur was asked about starting running back Josh Jacobs’ standing with the club, following Thursday’s news that Jacobs was officially being charged with battery and criminal damage to property, after the Packers’ win on Friday against the Arizona Cardinals. He didn’t leave any grey area in his response: “I […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JUNE 09: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers participates in drills during the Green Bay Packers mandatory minicamp at Don Hutson Center on June 09, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur was asked about starting running back Josh Jacobs’ standing with the club, following Thursday’s news that Jacobs was officially being charged with battery and criminal damage to property , after the Packers’ win on Friday against the Arizona Cardinals. He didn’t leave any grey area in his response: “I fully anticipate him being a member of our team.” Green Bay is standing by Jacobs, at least for now. In Brown County’s report on the Jacobs charges, they state that a video was captured via a security system at Jacobs’ residence. According to the report, Jacobs threw an unnamed woman, described in the report as his girlfriend, on the ground, leaving “observed redness” on the woman’s face and neck. She also was left with a bump on her head, per the report. Brown County stated that the video, among other things, includes “the altercation” that took place in the garage, confirming the unnamed woman’s claims to police, as well as Jacobs taking the unnamed woman’s phone once she was on the floor of the garage. Jacobs was not given a “domestic violence enhancer” on his charges, in part because of the state’s specific requirements for the label “domestic violence.” To receive a domestic violence label on a charge in Wisconsin, a victim must have either previously or currently been married to, living with or have a child with the perpetrator. The presumption here is that the victim did not live with Jacobs, therefor Jacobs cannot receive the domestic violence enhancer, despite the victim being described as his girlfriend in the police report. It is expected that Jacobs will receive probation and enter a batterers intervention program, if found guilty, based on the precedent of previous cases with similar details in the state of Wisconsin. Generally, the NFL punishes domestic violence cases with a five- to six-game suspension, but the question now is whether the Packers believe a suspension would be applied to the 2026 season or the 2027 season, if Jacobs is found guilty in-season. As it stands today, Jacobs was already likely to be released by Green Bay going into the 2027 season, as his cap hit jumps to $16.6 million in 2027, while his dead cap is reduced to just $3.1 million — meaning that the Packers would save $13.5 million in cap space by moving on from Jacobs next year. This is all to say: Even before the charges, it was already likely that Jacobs’ final season in Green Bay was going to be 2026. The other factor looming around the incident, now that Green Bay’s brass have made their stance clear, is what the team’s reaction would be to the video from Jacobs’ residence going public. In the past, general manager Brian Gutekunst has stated that he would not add players to the team if they put hands on women, but would the team still hold that line if a video shows Jacobs doing just that? As of the time of this article, the video that was referred to in Brown County’s report has not surfaced in the media, and LaFleur has not been asked about whether he or the team has seen the video. The Packers will have no media availability until Tuesday, when reporters will be able to get their first opportunity to ask LaFleur and Gutekunst questions following Sunday’s roster cutdowns, as rosters will shrink from 91 players to a 53-man practice squad and (on Monday) a 17-man practice squad. When asked about whether or not Jacobs was going to be able to play in Week 1, LaFleur stated, “I can’t really comment on that, because I don’t know.”
author: Justis Mosqueda

title: Packers-Cardinals Preseason Final Score, Recap: Kyle McCord wills Green Bay to victory
summary: The Green Bay Packers won a thriller, if there can ever be one in August, in their preseason finale against the Arizona Cardinals. Mike LaFleur, trying to best his older brother, called two timeouts in the final five seconds of the game, trying to set up a Hail Mary after receiver KiSean Johnson’s second fourth-quarter […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Kyle McCord #18 of the Green Bay Packers warms up before a preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers won a thriller, if there can ever be one in August, in their preseason finale against the Arizona Cardinals. Mike LaFleur, trying to best his older brother, called two timeouts in the final five seconds of the game, trying to set up a Hail Mary after receiver KiSean Johnson’s second fourth-quarter touchdown for the Packers. The Cardinals’ Hail Mary attempt fell short, though, and was batted away by a crowd of green and gold as Arizona fell 42-38 with zeroes on the clock. The Packers did not play their best players on Friday Night, as 37 were held out. 32 of those players were among the 46 we listed as Packers “roster locks” earlier this week, with the remaining five comprising four players on Green Bay’s physically unable to perform list and tight end Thomas Yassmin, the Packers’ international exemption player who is currently dealing with an injury. On top of that, others who were “active” were held out as reserve/emergency players, like backup quarterback Tyrod Taylor — who didn’t play a single snap in the game. Instead, it was Kyle McCord, Green Bay’s QB3, who played under center for the offense today. The most interesting part of the game, from a players participating standpoint, was probably that the second-team offensive line was able to go for the game and mid-round picks Chris McClellan and Dani Dennis-Sutton (who was inactive for the first two preseason games) suited up on the line of scrimmage. The second-team offensive line was made up of John Williams, Donovan Jennings, Jager Burton, Travis Glover (who hasn’t been getting work with the second-team up to this point) and Anthony Belton (from left to right). Glover was later kicked out to replace Belton, and Darian Kinnard, who was the team’s sixth offensive lineman in the second half of the Packers’ 2026 season, came off the bench to play right guard. Kinnard has had maybe the biggest drop on the depth chart of any returning player on Green Bay’s roster. Defensively, the standout was easily Dennis-Sutton, who recorded one sack in his NFL debut, several pressures and a couple near-sacks, too. He looked like an NFL rookie playing against a group of practice squaders, so he’s checking the box there. McCord continued a solid summer for the rising quarterback, completing 22 of 35 for 226 yards and four touchdowns versus the Cardinals. In total, his preseason has amounted to 70 passes for 37 completions, 446 yards (6.3 yards per attempt) and four touchdowns. Meanwhile, Taylor was 8 of 16 for 38 yards (2.4 yards per attempt) this preseason, but it appears that Taylor will be Green Bay’s backup — barring an outside addition — as he was shielded from contact tonight. Receiver J. Michael Sturdivant, who is the most likely undrafted free agent to make the Packers’ 2026 initial 53-man roster on Sunday as a seventh receiver and special teams contributor, led the team with six receptions for 112 yards, despite Johnson hauling in one more touchdown. Meanwhile, Isaiah Neyor, who is pushing Sturdivant for a roster spot, dropped a wide-open deep ball from McCord. Will Sheppard, who has been ninth in the receiver pecking order this preseason, returned a punt for an 81-yard touchdown against the Cardinals, too. Rookie kicker Trey Smack continues his perfect stretch of play, as he hit two more field goals and four extra points versus Arizona. Unfortunately, the reserve defense was lunch, as they gave up 326 yards in the air (including sack yardage) and 166 yards on the ground. Obviously, an 80-point game isn’t going to have much defense played in it, but the Packers could have been much better in that department tonight. Notably, rookie cornerback Domani Jackson, who had an alright NFL debut last week after missing the preseason opener, played pretty poorly opposite Jaylin Simpson, who himself hasn’t looked good as either an outside cornerback or a slot defender this preseason. Maybe Green Bay should just keep four true cornerbacks, if you consider Kamal Hadden a “safety” now that he’s playing in the nickel spot and” third-safety” packages on the team. The Packers end the preseason 2-1, with more good than bad put on tape. If we’re going to crown anyone a preseason MVP this summer, it’s probably McCord, who will likely be offered a practice squad job in Green Bay this upcoming season, assuming he clears waivers on Monday. Initially, McCord battled with undrafted rookie Kyron Drones for third-team offense snaps until Drones took three sacks in four dropbacks in the preseason opener and was quickly waived — giving McCord the clear runway as the QB3.

The Packers are 1-1 in […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - AUGUST 21: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur walks out with his brother New York Jets Offensive Coordinator Mike LaFleur during a game between the Green Bay Packers and the New York Jets at Lambeau Field on August 21, 2021 in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The joint practices are over — now it’s time for an actual game. Well, a preseason game, at least. That’s what awaits the Green Bay Packers and Arizona Cardinals tonight at Lambeau Field as the LaFleur brothers’ teams meet in their final games before the start of the regular season. The Packers are 1-1 in the preseason so far, having started out with a 28-9 defeat in Pittsburgh before bouncing back to a 33-13 drubbing of the Denver Broncos. Arizona will be playing their fourth preseason game, however, having participated in the NFL’s Hall of Fame Game earlier this summer. That game ended in a 33-30 loss on a last-minute touchdown run by Panthers rookie quarterback Haynes King. The Cardinals then split their next two games, beating the Las Vegas Raiders 27-14 and losing 34-13 to the Dallas Cowboys last Saturday. As always, the final result is not the point of a preseason game, but rather what individual performances can help certain players’ cases for roster spots. The Packers do not appear to have many uncertain places left on their 53-man roster, which will be decided on Sunday, but a couple of last spots could still be decided tonight.
