title: Rams’ Good, Bad and Ugly: CJ Daniels has earned a roster spot
summary: Ty Simpson again stole headlines in the Los Angeles Rams’ 20-18 win over the Chargers on Thursday night, yet fellow rookie CJ Daniels has earned a chance in the spotlight. Following a second straight promising game, Daniels has seemingly done enough to earn a roster spot, as he’s been one of the Rams’ most consistent […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 1: CJ Daniels #6 of the Los Angeles Rams runs after the catch during training camp at Loyola Marymount University on August 1, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ty Simpson again stole headlines in the Los Angeles Rams’ 20-18 win over the Chargers on Thursday night, yet fellow rookie CJ Daniels has earned a chance in the spotlight. Following a second straight promising game, Daniels has seemingly done enough to earn a roster spot, as he’s been one of the Rams’ most consistent wideouts this preseason. We’ll get into that more shortly, but let’s dive into the good, the bad and the ugly against the Chargers in the preseason finale on Thursday night. The Good Ty Simpson has secured the backup position … maybe Did Simpson secure the backup position? There’s a chance, but Sean McVay is going to take his sweet ass time making a decision. Sean McVay didn’t commit to a No. 2 QB tonight between Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson. He said he likes what he’s seen out of both and will make the decision after giving it more thought. — Nate Atkins (@NateAtkins_) August 28, 2026 The quarterback battle in Los Angeles shouldn’t be a battle at all given what we’ve seen this preseason. Simpson has simply outplayed Stetson Bennett and should be rewarded with the backup role. Why should the Rams put up with mediocrity behind Matthew Stafford? They haven’t put up with average with the rest of the roster. There’s more on that in a bit. The rookie has truly been sensational this preseason. He didn’t make a single mistake in his three appearances, which is crucial to note. Additionally, he demonstrated high efficiency and poise like someone who has played in this offense for years. View this post on Instagram Simpson’s performance in the Chargers game proves he was the team’s option all along, because through three preseason appearances, he already looked more NFL-ready than Bennett has after FOUR SEASONS. For crying out loud McVay, this shouldn’t be a difficult choice to make. Ride the hot hand and see where it takes you. Defense did just enough This was perhaps the defense’s worst showing of the preseason, yet they did what they could to finish on a high note. Yes, Justin Herbert tore them up early on, and the Chargers’ running game racked up over 200 yards. Outside of Herbert, they remained strong against the pass. DJ Uiagalelei and Trey Lance were held to a combined 11-of-20 for 141 yards and no touchdowns. Lance had zero completions, so a terrible showing is pretty on brand for him. Both QBs were also sacked four times. The Chargers were also held to a combined 3-of-10 on third- and fourth-down, and 0-for-1 in the red zone. This preseason, the Rams finished by giving up 30 points in three games, which is really good. They also only allowed two touchdowns in that span, both coming against the Chargers. It wasn’t the prettiest effort, yet the unit didn’t break and did enough to keep LA in a position to win every game. I can’t say it enough, but if this is how the backups play, imagine how much fun the defense will be once the regular season kicks off. Best preseason showing in the McVay era Who says preseason efforts don’t matter? Well, I mean, they don’t, yet an undefeated showing is nothing to sneeze at, as many of the team’s backups got valuable reps. It goes without saying that this was the best preseason showing in the McVay era, and it’s not remotely close. The Rams went 2-2 in each of their first three preseason slates with McVay at the helm. They’ve finished close to unbeaten in each of the last two seasons following an 0-3 finish in 2023, which hilariously included a 41-0 loss to the Broncos in Denver. For a team that regularly doesn’t play its starters during the exhibition series — with McVay usually even handing off his play calling duties — it was refreshing to see effort. Part of what helped was Simpson’s play, which has undoubtedly made this preseason more enjoyable to watch than others. During the 2021 campaign when LA most recently won the Super Bowl, they also finished 0-3. In all likelihood, that doesn’t mean a darn thing heading into the 2026 season. Either way, it’s still interesting. The Bad The CJ Daniels waiting game Daniels should make the roster. There I said it. After a quiet start to preseason, Daniels ended the exhibition matches with back-to-back quality games against the Saints and Chargers. In those two games, he had 13 catches for 110 yards on 19 targets. While he didn’t reach the end zone, it shouldn’t matter, as he’s been one of the team’s most consistent receivers the past two weeks. The only issue is, his efforts might be in vain, which would be deeply unfortunate. LA trading back for Tutu Atwell before the game certainly complicates things. It shouldn’t, though, because when has this team ever used Atwell correctly, or at all? Daniels deserves a roster spot due to him being a quality young option who can rack up decent production and be a reliable target. If Atwell’s return is going to cut into another receiver’s reps, why should that be allowed? Since we know enough about Bennett to know he’s not the guy, shouldn’t the front office have already known Atwell is in a similar spot? We’ve been waiting for Tutu to break out for how many years now? Give his reps to someone more deserving, like Daniels, to see if they can take off and make the most of the opportunities Atwell never could. The waiting game is maddening while cutdowns happen, and keep your fingers crossed for Daniels. LA might regret it if they let him go to another team and it pans out. Coaching staff’s management of QBs in a pointless battle If there’s one gripe I’ve had about preseason — besides the common complaint that it’s pointless — it’s that the Rams completely mismanaged the quarterback situation. A week ago, we were wondering where Simpson was. This week, we were asking the same about Bennett. Not that I was clamouring to see him attempt to cosplay as an NFL QB, but still. With Bennett not playing Thursday, does that mean he unofficially locked up the backup job? Were the Rams preserving his health in case they intend to trade him before the season? Has McVay seen enough from him, which again, could be a good or a bad thing? What does it all mean?! In last week’s Good, Bad and Ugly , I complained that Simpson didn’t play enough against the Saints. Every rep he receives is valuable, and it made zero sense not to have him on the field for longer. We’re already well aware that Bennett isn’t in the team’s long-term (and possibly) short-term future. The coaching staff playing Simpson longer this week doesn’t make up for his lack of reps against New Orleans. It stole more opportunities to get valuable NFL experience that could significantly benefit him down the road should he earn the backup role. Regardless of whatever happens, my head still hurts, and I’m off to pop a couple aspirin. The Ugly None for the second straight week. The Rams’ backups looked great and ended preseason on a high note. Now, we’re on to the regular season. Bring it on!
author: Evan Craig

title: PFF grades: Who made the most of final preseason arguments?
summary: Dean Connors and Ty Simpson led the Los Angeles Rams to a victory in the team’s preseason finale against the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday night. The Rams will kickoff their regular season journey in just two weeks. Before we turn the corner, let’s assess who performed well and who didn’t in the final exhibition […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - August 27:Rams Dean Connors (33) dives for a touchdown during third quarter action at SoFi Stadium on Thursday, August 27, 2026. The Rams defeated the Charges in the final preseason game 20-18. (Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Dean Connors and Ty Simpson led the Los Angeles Rams to a victory in the team’s preseason finale against the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday night. The Rams will kickoff their regular season journey in just two weeks. Before we turn the corner, let’s assess who performed well and who didn’t in the final exhibition game. These are the grades and data from Pro Football Focus (PFF): Top five grades on offense 1 – Dean Connors, RB: 77.4 Connors rushed 18 times for 69 yards and added three receptions for 24 yards and a score through the air. The rookie UDFA was LA’s highest-graded receiver on Thursday night. He posted his third receiving touchdown of the preseason. More impressive is the fact that 60 of his rushing yards came after contact (88%). Connors forced five missed tackles and rushed for eight first downs. Will the rookie make the roster? Who knows? He at least made a very compelling case to all the teams across teh NFL. Matthew Caldwell threads the needle to Dean Connors for the TD! 🧵 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYWYi pic.twitter.com/gegcC33UG6 — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 28, 2026 2 – AJ Arcuri, LT: 66.1 Struggling in pass blocking (47.6) with two pressures allowed and a penalty, Arcuri’s best work came in the run game with a grade of 80.7. He played all 74 snaps, which could be a troubling sign ahead of roster cutdowns. The Rams should remain mindful of Alaric Jackson’s possible suspension, though Arcuri playing the full game may be a sign that the team isn’t that worried. 3 – Ty Simpson, QB: 65.7 Worth noting—Simpson’s grade after the first half was in the 75 range. Reserve quarterback Matthew Caldwell was injured and Simpson had to step in for an emergency situation. He did very little more than handing the ball off each time in order to prevent injury. This may have lowered his overall PFF grade from the first half mark. The most promising outcome from Thursday night was that Simpson posted his first big-time throw of the preseason on a scrambling touchdown to Brennan Presley. The rookie’s average depth of target rose to 5.9 after being sub-5 through two games. Prior to the remaining preseason games, Simpson has attempted the most passes. He’s completed an impressive 78.3% of his throws. After adjusting for drops and throwaways, his adjusted completion rate climbs to 82.8%. He isn’t being asked to throw the ball very far downfield; however, he’s executing the plays in front of him very well. It’s an encouraging sign. Ty Simpson delivers a TD strike to Brennan Presley 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5Dc65aRqbk — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 4 – CJ Daniels, WR: 65.6 Daniels added another five receptions on six targets for 42 yards on Thursday night. This brings his preseason total to 15 catches on 24 targets for 128 yards. Before this weekend’s games, Daniels leads all rookie receivers in targets by a 10(!). 5 – Mark Redman, TE: 62.5 Rookie Max Klare played over half the game with 41 snaps out of the total 74. He received a few targets early. The attention then turned to Redman, who caught all three of his targets for 16 yards. His best work came as a blocker where he earned marks of 72.9 in pass protection (two snaps) and 66.6 in run blocking (11 snaps). His run blocking grade ranked third on the team behind Arcuri and Tyler Scott. Other notes on offense After standing out in a very positive way through two games , rookie UDFA Austin Blake did not perform well against the other LA team. Blaske has played four of five spots on the offensive line. His best performance has come at left tackle. After moving to RG against the Chargers, he posted a grade of 46.0. Top five grades on defense There seem to be fewer roster spots up for grabs on the defensive side of the ball. I’m going to keep it shorter for this group because none of them project well in terms of the final 53-man roster. 1 – Darryl Peterson, EDGE: 93.2 Peterson posted an elite pass rushing grade of 93.8 with three pressures on 23 rushes. He earned two sacks and helped closeout the game while the Chargers were driving for the would-be game-winning score. 2 – Jaxson Moi, DT: 73.3 Moi fared well from a grading perspective despite missing one of two tackle attempts. His best contribution came as a pass rusher where he tallied four pressures. 3 – Alex Johnson, DB: 69.7 Johnson played 17 snaps with 10 coming in coverage. He was not targeted, which is a sign he was tight with his assigned receivers. 4 – Eli Neal, LB: 68.0 Neal made three tackles plus an assist without a miss. He was on the field for 21 plays with 14 coming in coverage. 5 – Steven Gilmore, CB: 66.0 The Rams signed Gilmore this week and he was their best corner on Thursday night through 10 reps. He was not targeted in coverage. Other notes on defense Wesley Bailey started the game but played only two snaps after the defense recovered a fumble by Justin Herbert. Standout safety Nick Andersen also started and played just eight snaps. Are the Rams telling us they’d like to keep both players around, whether on the 53-man roster or practice squad?
author: JB Scott

title: Rams’ snap counts in preseason finale indicates decisions for Wesley Bailey, Nick Andersen
summary: The playing time for edge rusher Wesley Bailey and safety Nick Andersen in Saturday’s preseason win over the Chargers could indicate that the two undrafted free agents will make Sean McVay’s final 53-man roster. Bailey was pulled from the game after only two snaps, while Andersen only played in eight snaps. Historically, the less that […]
full_text: Inglewood, - August 22: Linebacker Wesley Bailey (47) of the Los Angeles Rams reacts after a New Orleans Saints fumble in the second half of a NFL preseason football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Saturday, August 22, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The playing time for edge rusher Wesley Bailey and safety Nick Andersen in Saturday’s preseason win over the Chargers could indicate that the two undrafted free agents will make Sean McVay’s final 53-man roster. Bailey was pulled from the game after only two snaps, while Andersen only played in eight snaps. Historically, the less that McVay wants to see of you in the preseason, the better. This should leave McVay with very few unknown bubble decisions, although several of the names in consideration for not making the roster could surprise fans, such as Stetson Bennett and C.J. Daniels. WR CJ Daniels 5 receptions with 42 yards vs the LA Chargers🙌🏽 #ProCane #GoCanes 🟧_🟩🙌🏽 pic.twitter.com/WNGlL928hj — BLEED ORANGE AND GREEN (@Brabra_Savage24) August 28, 2026 A week ago, we highlighted the players who either had not played in the preseason at all or who had been held out of the second game after playing in the first. By all accounts, every single one of those decisions by McVay does indicate that the player is making the roster, with the exception of cornerback Zech McPhearson, who was released due to injury. But while there was pushback on why some players sat out, like Ronnie Rivers, a running back who the majority of fans wanted to see cut in favor of Jarquez Hunter, McVay reiterated how important Rivers is to him because of “trust” . Then Hunter was traded to the Dolphins for Tutu Atwell , clearing the way for Rivers and opening the door for Atwell to make the roster out of left field. A field once thought to be occupied by Daniels. Rams notable snap counts vs. Chargers Per PFF, here are some key snap decisions by McVay on defense: LB Nikhai Green-Hill, 49 snaps EDGE Tomon Fox, 45 snaps CB AZ Hamilton, 42 snaps EDGE Darryl Peterson, 42 snaps CB Cam Lampkin, 36 snaps DT Bill Norton, 30 snaps DT Payton Zdroik, 27 snaps DT Larrell Murchison, 26 snaps DT Tim Keenan, 24 snaps S Nick Andersen, 8 snaps EDGE Wesley Bailey, 2 snaps That’s not the complete list. It just indicates that McVay didn’t want to see a lot of Anderson or Bailey, but he did want to give those snaps to players like Peterson, Fox, and Tanner Ingle and Alex Cook. As of last week, there were 21 defensive players held out of the preseason game against the Saints, not including McPhearson. If we add in Andersen and Bailey, that makes 23 . There aren’t many more players on a defensive roster than that. Maybe 2. Here were some key snap decisions on offense: OT AJ Arcuri, 74 snaps OL Austin Blaske, 74 snaps OL Bryce Henderson, 74 snaps G Wyatt Bowles, 74 snaps WR Brennan Presley, 53 snaps QB Ty Simpson, 48 snaps TE Max Klare, 41 snaps RB Dean Connors, 38 snaps WR CJ Daniels, 34 snaps Last time we did this, 19 players were held out on offense, with Xavier Smith joining the group in preseason week 2. So if you take 19 and you add in obvious “made it” candidates Simpson and Klare, that adds up to 21. If the team keeps Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith (they are similar, but not the same, as Atwell is not a known punt returner), that makes 22. Do the math: 23 on defense 22 on offense 3 on special teams That’s already 48 players, leaving only five available spots. This is a list of 48 that does not include: Bennett Daniels Connors Blaske Arcuri Keenan Lampkin Keagen Trost Unless Trost is placed on IR, he will also be on the 53-man roster. That would only leave four spots. If the Rams keep Daniels, in addition to the ones already mentioned, that would be seven wide receivers. Not only would it be seven receivers, it would be seven receivers on a team that has five tight ends. And if the team keeps Bennett and Connors, it’s an offense with three quarterbacks, four running backs, seven receivers, and five tight ends. A little unusual. However, if A.J Jackson and Puka Nacua are suspended , then McVay has to keep two additional offensive players on the roster anyway. It’s a bit strange that the NFL hasn’t announced anything on that this close to the season. Barring that though, it’s hard to see how the Rams can keep every player who outsiders think they should keep or will keep. Certainly C.J. Daniels is 100% on the bubble and not a lock to make the team. He may be the one most “hopeful”, if you can call it that, that Nacua is suspended. Bennett is taking a roster spot from someone else, if Ty Simpson is named as the backup. Blaske would be an 11th offensive lineman, which is a luxury teams can usually only afford if they don’t have high numbers at every other offensive position. So what’s it going to be? The Rams had good news for Bailey and Andersen with how little they played on Thursday. They can only give out so much more good news in the next couple of days.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Andrew Whitworth still expects Aaron Donald to return
summary: Everyone wants to know whether Aaron Donald will be coming back to the Los Angeles Rams or not, and Andrew Whitworth feels that it’s only a matter of time. Whitworth explained to Ryan Fitzpatrick on their podcast that Donald has been putting on a football helmet and doing drills, and as far as Whitworth is […]
full_text: THOUSAND OAKS, CA - FEBRUARY 09: Offensive tackle Andrew Whitworth #77 of the Los Angeles Rams talks with defensive tackle Aaron Donald #99 during practice in preparation for Super Bowl LVI at Los Angeles Rams Training Facility on February 9, 2022 in Thousand Oaks, California. The Rams will play against the Cincinnati Bengals in Super Bowl LVI on February 13. (Photo by Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images) | Getty Images Everyone wants to know whether Aaron Donald will be coming back to the Los Angeles Rams or not, and Andrew Whitworth feels that it’s only a matter of time. Whitworth explained to Ryan Fitzpatrick on their podcast that Donald has been putting on a football helmet and doing drills, and as far as Whitworth is concerned, Donald wouldn’t be putting on a helmet if he wasn’t serious about playing. Whitworth is seemingly speculating, but his logic makes sense. Why put on a helmet if you don’t want to play football? There is also the possibility that Donald is wearing the helmet because it looks cool in workout videos, point being, until Donald makes an official decision, we don’t know what his plans are. All signs point to Donald on some level is thinking our at least has thought about a genuine NFL comeback. All signs point to the Rams being so open to it that they are letting Donald work this all out on his own time. All signs point to we don’t have an official answer yet, and Donald could come back, he could not. But as far as Whitworth is concerned, Donald’s mind is made up and as long as the Rams are in contention, he’ll be back at some point. Andrew Whitworth still confident Aaron Donald is coming back (ramswire) “He’s barely said anything about his plans and hasn’t addressed it publicly, but signs have pointed to him returning to the Rams – including Sean McVay’s clear excitement when asked about that possibility. Andrew Whitworth has said before that he thinks Donald will play this season and during Prime’s broadcast of Browns -Patriots on Thursday night, Whitworth maintained his confidence in that belief. “Oh, I think he’s playing,” Whitworth said. “I think you gotta figure out all the little parts that go into it. … Listen, if you put a helmet on and hit a sled, you’re playing football. I don’t care what you say, you’re going to figure it out.” Rams’ Sean McVay not worried about possible Puka Nacua suspension despite Tutu Atwell trade (clutchpoints) “Sean McVay said the Tutu Atwell decision is not related to any potential suspension that could come to Puka Nacua. He said they wanted Tutu for depth. He also said it won’t bump any WRs they wanted to keep off the roster either. They have plans to be flexible with the 53,” Atkins wrote on X, formerly Twitter. With everything said and done, ifs and buts around a potential suspension have always been in discussion. Even ESPN’s Adam Schefter mentioned that Nacua could miss Week 1 of NFL action. “Cases that I believe are now being reviewed include that of the Rams wide receiver, Puka Nacua, who could potentially face discipline for some of the off-season headlines that accompanied him and some of those incidents last year with another woman, what did and didn’t occur. We’ll leave that to the NFL to figure out what did and didn’t happen, but it’s possible that when the Niners and Rams play in Australia, it’s within the realm of options that Puka doesn’t play in that game,” Schefter reported earlier in August.“ Tutu Atwell can still provide a spark if the Rams use him in specific ways (ramblinfan) “Rams fans know Atwell, and Atwell knows LA’s offense. That may be why the Rams pursued Atwell as the return piece in trading Hunter. But their current rookies already face the lack-of-use syndrome that plagued Atwell’s career in Los Angeles. His return will only complicate the matter. But LA just upgraded its roster, if for no other reason than to bolster its experience. And if the Rams are to survive any league-mandated suspension for Puka Nacua, Atwell will at least give them another target in the room.“ Hot Mic Picked Up NFL Referee’s Uncensored Comment Explaining How He Really Felt About Being At The Rams-Chargers Preseason Game [VIDEO] (sports.yahoo) “While preparing for an upcoming play, the open microphone suddenly broadcast a weary voice saying, “Jesus, let’s get this over with.” Apparently, the grueling nature of the exhibition schedule had finally exhausted the refereeing crew’s patience.” Rams might need Donald ‘sooner rather than later’ (nbcsports) “Michael Holley and Mike Florio dive into Aaron Donald’s potential return from retirement and discuss the factors at play for the future Hall of Famer to come back.” 47 players who are locks to make the Rams’ 53-man roster (ramswire) “Given the talent from top to bottom, it’s going to be a really challenging roster to make – especially for younger, unproven players. Even all of their rookie draft picks aren’t completely safe from being cut. With the preseason now finished and final cuts mere days away, we’re looking at which players are virtually guaranteed to make the team. Sean McVay and the coaching staff make it easier to discern locks from bubble players based on who plays (and how much) in the preseason, but playing time isn’t always a perfect reflection of a player’s standing on the roster.“ Takeaways from Rams-Chargers Preseason Week 3 matchup | ‘GMFB’ (nfl.com) “GMFB” share their takeaways from the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers Preseason Week 3 matchup.“ Stetson Bennett’s absence in Rams preseason finale bodes well for his future with LA (dawnofthedog) “The LA Rams played their final preseason game of the year on Thursday against the Chargers. Stetson Bennett started their first two games of the preseason, but on Thursday he didn’t step foot on the field once. Instead the Rams chose to ride with rookie quarterback Ty Simpson in his place. On the surface this may seem like a bad sign for Bennett, but in reality it might be the greatest sign yet that he is winning, or has already won, the backup quarterback job for the Rams.“ Chargers vs. Rams Highlights | Preseason Week 3 (chargers.com) “Watch the top plays and highlights from the Chargers’ Preseason Week 3 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams during the 2026 NFL season.” McVay undecided on QB2 after third preseason game (nbcsports) “After getting through the third and final dress rehearsal before the Rams kick off Week 1 in Australia, McVay said he won’t be “pigeon-holding” himself into any decision just yet. Rookie Ty Simpson and fourth-year vet Stetson Bennett have both performed well for the Rams this preseason, with Bennett sitting out Thursday’s game against the Chargers. The decision to sit Bennett on Thursday, coupled with the 62 snaps he saw in the preseason to Simpson’s 111, could be a signal as to which way McVay is leaning at this point, although he is on record saying we shouldn’t read too much into that. Regardless, the good news for McVay and Rams fans is that Matthew Stafford is healthy and will hopefully be under center for all 17 of the Rams’ games this season as he looks to defend his crown as the reigning league MVP.“ Comment of the Day: “Ty is playing under so much pressure from the media after the storyline of the Rams “wasting” a pick on him. His mental toughness is amazing and it doesn’t appear to phase him in the least (so far).“ -Unknown Football Fan Feedpost of the Day:

title: Raiders News: Klint Kubiak won’t commit to naming the starting QB
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders just finished their last football game of the preseason with an 18-12 loss. It is now time for the Raiders to cut their roster to the final 53 and get ready for the Miami Dolphins. The biggest part of the 53 is picking the starting quarterback. The Raiders have Kirk Cousins […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders passes against the San Francisco 49ers during the second quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders just finished their last football game of the preseason with an 18-12 loss. It is now time for the Raiders to cut their roster to the final 53 and get ready for the Miami Dolphins. The biggest part of the 53 is picking the starting quarterback. The Raiders have Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza vying for a shot at being the starter. After three preseason games, it appears that Kirk Cousins is comfortably in the lead. However, Klint Kubiak has not yet committed to a starter. When asked on Friday, he said he wanted more time to make a decision. “I still don’t think we need to name anybody,” the first-year coach said. “We have a lot to talk about at a lot of positions, so we want to watch the film and talk about everything as a staff.” Kubiak seems to take from his dad, who didn’t like to give too much information until the right time. While it is pretty obvious to fans who the starter is, the Raiders will keep us waiting for the actual decision. title: Improved Raiders defense, Mike Washington Jr. shine in preseason finale
summary: A preseason finale is often the time where roster hopefuls dominate the snap counts and a team’s personnel crew get insight on who to keep and who to cut when NFL teams go from 90-man rosters to the 53-man version for the regular season. For rookie head coach Klint Kubiak, though, the exhibition slate against […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Las Vegas Raiders sets up a play at the line of scrimmage in the first quarter of a preseason against the San Francisco 49ers game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images A preseason finale is often the time where roster hopefuls dominate the snap counts and a team’s personnel crew get insight on who to keep and who to cut when NFL teams go from 90-man rosters to the 53-man version for the regular season. For rookie head coach Klint Kubiak, though, the exhibition slate against the San Francisco 49ers was an opportune time to view his roster as a whole. The first-team offensive line played more than one offensive series, as did assumed starting quarterback Kirk Cousins. On the opposite side of the ball, the lone missing starter was edge rusher Maxx Crosby, but Rob Leonard’s defense played with a sense of urgency and performed much better than what’s been displayed in the two prior preseason tilts. Eventually, second- and third-string units joined the fray, but Kubiak getting more work with the first-team units is ample for a neophyte head coach. He along with his coaching staff and general manager John Spytek and his player personnel staff will have their work cut out for them over the weekend as NFL teams must meet the Sunday, 3 p.m. (Pacific Standard Time) deadline to drastically reduce the roster from 90 to 53. There’s a particular rookie from the Raiders’ 2026 NFL Draft class that’s emphatically made it known they not only will make the roster but also be a regular contributor on offense: Running back Mike Washington Jr. The 6-foot-2 and 228-pound fourth-round pick (122nd overall) from Arkansas showcased the power, speed, and vision throughout the preseason slate as he had eight carries for 49 yards (6.1 yards per carry average) against the 49ers. . @Raiders @49ers @MykeWash03 might become the SOD! Take it to the bank #raidernation #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/OjgCDEcO0T — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) August 28, 2026 Like former Raiders quarterback and current broadcast analyst Rich Gannon astutely pointed out during the preseason finale, Washington will need to showcase the ability to be a trusted pass protector on obvious passing downs and prove he’s an ample route runner and pass catcher out of the backfield (more on this in an upcoming piece later this weekend). Combining blocking and receiving will make Washington a versatile option to operate in Kubiak’s offense, especially with starting tailback Ashton Jeanty potentially missing games due to an ankle injury to start the regular season. In total, Washington got 23 totes for 168 yards (7.3 yards per carry average) in preseason action and it’ll be intriguing to see the rookie’s production on his touches in the regular season. In fact, Kubiak indicated Friday that Washington will see the field a lot this season even when Jeanty is fully healthy. It will be interesting to see what kind of carry split the two young tailback share this season. While the offense failed to get into the end zone, seeing Kubiak’s offense being ran efficiently by Cousins portends to good things when games count in the win-loss record. Still, Kubiak’s beckoning for a wide receiver to step up and make it known they can be a trusted and productive pass catcher remains very much up in the air. There were standout moments from individuals throughout preseason and it appears Tre Tucker is slated to be WR1, but the hierarchy is still in flux. Free agent addition Jalen Nailor made highlight one-handed catch five-yard catch to dazzle but then had a bullet from No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza clang off both his hands for an interception. Gannon nailed it on the broadcast. The Raiders need a wide receiver to consistently beat man coverage and get separation. That hasn’t happened quite enough. And when it has happened, the throws aren’t snared in. Tatum Bethune gets the INT for the @49ers ! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hQQDfkKOb9 — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 Let’s hit the Quick Slants as we prepare for regular season action coming September 13 with a home opener against the Miami Dolphins Week 1: —Veteran Matt Gay took all the kickoffs and field goal attempts in the preseason finale going 4-for-5 with his miss being a wide left attempt from 54 yards out. His counterpart (and former Raider) Eddie Pineiro was a perfect 6-for-6 for the 49ers. The Raiders’ kicking competition wasn’t really one, was it? Undrafted rookie free agent Kansei Matsuzawa didn’t even get a single attempt. Welp, crow takes like chicken. —Las Vegas does have the top spot in waiver claims and it’ll be interesting to see how Spytek operates come the flurry of roster moves all 32 teams will make to meet the Sunday deadline of getting down to 53. But it doesn’t end there. Come meeting the mandated 53-man roster comes waiver claims and then building out the 16-man practice squad. Matsuzawa could be an exemption 17th member of that squad based on the NFL’s International Player Pathway program. —All four of the Raiders quarterbacks — Cousins, Mendoza, Aidan O’Connell, and undrafted free agent Jacob Clark — each notched a throw against the 49ers. Clark two passes were the first in the preseason slate and it’s likely Las Vegas carries maybe only three or even two quarterbacks on the 53-man roster. —Dylan Laube is playing with more confidence on offense, which is a great sign for Las Vegas. The 2024 sixth-round pick rarely saw any offensive snaps the past two season — largely due to his penchant of showcasing butter fingers — has earned carries and receptions including a nifty 12-yard catch-and-run where he slithered between two 49ers defenders for a first down. —Veteran Patrick Johnson and undrafted free agent Cian Slone present difficult decisions for the Raiders come cut down day. Johnson showed bite as a pass rusher with two sacks in preseason play to go along with run stopping ability and special teams work. Ditto for Slone who showed relentlessness off the edge, too. Two dudes with a lot on the line tonight: Patrick Johnson and Cian Slone. #Raiders pic.twitter.com/pDRfymJqb3 — Levi Edwards (@theleviedwards) August 27, 2026 —How serious the injury third-round pick Keyron Crawford sustained against the 49ers may dictate both Johnson’s and Slone’s roster chances. Crawford, the 67th overall pick, had a sack in the preseason finale but was injured as he rushed the passer, was brought to the medical tent, and then carted off the field. —Punter AJ Cole III has been his normally booming self as he sent a trio of boots into orbit for 170 yards (56.7 yards per boot average) with a long of 63 yards. He had one touchback and one punt downed inside the 20-yard line and one of the league’s elite punters is on his A-game already.

title: Fernando Mendoza finishes preseason with 2nd interception in Las Vegas Raiders-San Francisco 49ers matchup
summary: Nothing says preseason football quite like a game with 10 field goals and no touchdowns, as the Las Vegas Raiders fell to the San Francisco 49ers 18-12. That drops the Raiders to 1-2 over the last three weeks, officially wraps up training camp, and sets up the final winners and losers before the regular season. […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders passes against the San Francisco 49ers during the second quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nothing says preseason football quite like a game with 10 field goals and no touchdowns, as the Las Vegas Raiders fell to the San Francisco 49ers 18-12 . That drops the Raiders to 1-2 over the last three weeks, officially wraps up training camp, and sets up the final winners and losers before the regular season. LOSER: Fernando Mendoza I cut Mendoza some slack last week, but it’s hard to ignore back-to-back games with interceptions. This time, he got greedy and tried to fit a ball into a very tight window while targeting the 5-foot-11 Jalen Nailor. To be fair, Mendoza managed to get the ball over the linebacker, and a bigger/taller receiver might have been able to come down with it. But it was the wrong throw/decision for the pass-catcher he was throwing to. Also, the Raiders’ offense operates more smoothly with Kirk Cousins behind center right now. Of course, that’s to be expected since he’s the veteran and has played in Klint Kubiak’s system before. However, that’s another strong sign that the rookie won’t be the team’s Week 1 starter, and it feels like any hopes of that ended on Thursday night. WINNER: Mike Washington Jr. Washington has been deserving of some recognition in the winners column but hasn’t gotten it yet. That had nothing to do with his play, though, and everything to do with the fact that he’s held down the second running back job essentially since he was drafted. But that changes because not only did the Arkansas product have another strong outing with eight carries for 49 yards (6.1 ypc) , he also eased some concerns if Ashton Jeanty has to miss some time. The rookie provided some hope that he’s capable of taking on a bigger role if needed and that he can be more than just a home-run hitter out of the backfield. LOSER: Aidan O’Connell In a way, this preseason has summarized O’Connell’s tenure in Las Vegas. He’s been up and down, with a shaky outing in the first contest against the Cardinals, then was much better to lead a game-winning drive last week, and had another tough performance on Thursday night. If the Silver and Black were hoping to shop the fourth-year pro ahead of cutdown day, going three-for-nine with 32 passing yards didn’t exactly help matters. WINNER: JJ Pegeus The Raiders have been looking for defensive tackles to step up all preseason, and not many had answered the call in the first two games. However, Pegues made a statement against San Francisco, standing out against the run with four tackles, the majority of which were near the line of scrimmage. He also made a few plays that won’t show up on the stat sheet by plugging up gaps to make runs bounce, and he had a great rep as a pass rusher, pushing the pocket with a bull rush and getting his hands up to record a batted pass. If the 2025 sixth-round pick was on the bubble heading into the game, he certainly made a strong case to stay on the roster. LOSER: Atonio Mafi I thought Mafi had a chance to make the team with what he was bringing as a run blocker. But he’s been a problem in pass protection, and that continued in the third preseason game by giving up another sack. The franchise needs to protect its investment in Mendoza, and it’s becoming clear that the fourth-year lineman isn’t up for the job. WINNER: Brandon Cleveland Along the same lines as Pegues, Cleveland had a much-needed outing to boost his odds of making the team. The seventh-round pick tied for the team lead with five total tackles and led the club outright with a pair of TFLs. He also had an impressive win as a pass-rusher to get a quarterback hit and was in the 49ers’ backfield on several occasions throughout the night. That should give the coaching staff something to think about ahead of cutdown day. LOSER: Wide Receivers To cut the quarterbacks mentioned above some slack, it seemed like the Raiders’ wide receivers struggled to get open. The passing game was filled with a lot of check downs, and there wasn’t a receiver who really stood out against San Francisco. Tre Tucker led the team with 25 receiving yards and no one else even eclipsed 20 yards, while the group had a handful of drops on the evening. Kubiak called out the position group after last week’s game and can’t be much happier with what he saw on Thursday night. Even after cutdown day, the receivers at the bottom of the roster shouldn’t feel comfortable because it seems like the Silver and Black will be taking a long look at the position on the waiver wire. WINNER: Cameron McGrone It will be interesting to see how many linebackers the coaching staff wants to keep, and if there’s an open spot, McGrone made a strong case to fill it. He was flying around all night, showing off some impressive instincts to tie Cleveland and Greedy Vance for the team lead in total tackles (five). At the least, that could have earned the 26-year-old one of the six veteran practice squad spots.

title: NFL waiver wire rules explained: How Dolphins stand in making roster moves
summary: The Miami Dolphins lost to the Atlanta Falcons earlier tonight, ending an ugly preseason schedule in which the team failed to win a game. In fact, other than the opening drive of their first game when the starting offense was on the field, Miami did not score a touchdown this summer. Is that a sign […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 29: A closeup view of the Miami Dolphins logo on a sweatshirt prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 29, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost to the Atlanta Falcons earlier tonight, ending an ugly preseason schedule in which the team failed to win a game. In fact, other than the opening drive of their first game when the starting offense was on the field, Miami did not score a touchdown this summer. Is that a sign of things to come? Miami is not expected to be a good team this year. They have the second-longest odds of any team in the league to be named Super Bowl champions. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the Dolphins are +50000 to claim the Lombardi Trophy , only ahead of the +100000 Arizona Cardinals. The Dolphins are the youngest team in the league as they reset their roster from the Mike McDaniel era to new head coach Jeff Hafley’s vision of the club. They are probably going to spend plenty of time this year churning the bottom of the roster and trying to find hidden gems that will shine in the future. Waiver claims are likely to be a favorite roster move for the Dolphins this season. When a team releases a player, he may be subject to waivers. If so, any team can put in a claim to acquire the player and assume his contract. With the 6 p.m. Eastern deadline on Sunday, August 30, for roster cuts to be made looming, waiver claims are about to take center stage. But, what are the full rules of the waiver process and what is the waiver order? What are waivers? Waivers are a labor process under which a team may release a player from their roster. The player’s contract becomes “claimable” by any team in the league and, if the team is granted the waiver claim, the player moves to the new team under their current contract. It is almost like a trade with no compensation sent to the old team. How are waiver claims made? Once a player is waived, the rest of the teams around the league have 24 hours to exercise a claim. This is not a full free-for-all, though. Player waivers are processed at the same time each day (usually 4 p.m. Eastern), and claims are processed at the same time the next day. Teams can submit a waiver claim at any time during the 24-hour period; the league collects all claims and processes them in the order explained below. For this year’s roster cuts, they are due by 6 p.m. Eastern on Sunday. The league will process waiver claims at 1 p.m. Eastern on Monday. Are any players exempt from the waivers process? What is released vs. waived? Players who have accrued four seasons of service time do not have to go through the waivers process. Those players are classified as “released” rather than “waived” and they become free agents immediately rather than having to wait to see if a team claims them. A player receives credit for an accrued season if they are on a team’s active roster for six games in a season. Players on injured reserve or the physically unable to perform list still receive credit for their service time. What happens when a team is awarded a waiver claim? Teams are limited to their 53-man roster size. If they receive a waiver claim and are already at 53 players, they must waive or release another player. How does the waiver wire impact practice squad players? Teams cannot start building their practice squads until after the waiver wire processes on Monday. Once players clear waivers without being claimed, they are free to sign with any team in the league, including the team that waived them. This could be on the 53-man roster, or on the 16-man practice squad. A player on a team’s roster cannot be signed directly to the practice squad. The team will have to waive him, allow the next process deadline to pass, then, if he was not claimed, he can be signed to the practice squad. What is the waiver order and what happens if multiple teams make a claim? Waiver claims are processed in the inverse order of league standings. For the first three weeks of the season, the NFL uses the previous year’s standings – which basically makes the waiver order match the draft order, without any trades factored into it. If multiple teams put in a waiver claim on a player, the higher listed team receives the waiver claim. For example, if a player is waived and both the Las Vegas Raiders and the Miami Dolphins claim him, the Raiders will receive the player and his contract because the Raiders are first in the waiver order while Miami is 11th. For the waivers that will start being processed on Monday after the cuts have been made, the order is: Las Vegas Raiders New York Jets Arizona Cardinals Tennessee Titans New York Giants Cleveland Browns Washington Commanders New Orleans Saints Kansas City Chiefs Cincinnati Bengals Miami Dolphins Dallas Cowboys Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Tampa Bay Buccaneers Indianapolis Colts Detroit Lions Minnesota Vikings Carolina Panthers Green Bay Packers Pittsburgh Steelers Los Angeles Chargers Philadelphia Eagles Jacksonville Jaguars Chicago Bears Buffalo Bills San Francisco 49ers Houston Texans Los Angeles Rams Denver Broncos New England Patriots Seattle Seahawks Miami is in a decent position to be able to put in waiver claims, but there are still some needy teams in front of them that could block any move the Dolphins try to make. Who could be subject to waivers from the Dolphins? The Dolphins have to make some tough decisions over the next couple of days, dropping 38 players from their current roster. If these players are cut, they will be subject to waivers rather than being immediate free agents. I removed players who are virtual roster locks and should not find themselves waived. title: Falcons vs. Dolphins final score, immediate reactions
summary: The Miami Dolphins closed out their preseason schedule on Friday night, losing to the Atlanta Falcons in South Florida’s Hard Rock Stadium. The Dolphins played well for much of the game, at least well enough to not be blown out like they were in their first two preseason games. Miami did not play their starters […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Cam Miller #15 of the Miami Dolphins slides after a run against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins closed out their preseason schedule on Friday night, losing to the Atlanta Falcons in South Florida’s Hard Rock Stadium. The Dolphins played well for much of the game, at least well enough to not be blown out like they were in their first two preseason games. Miami did not play their starters in the game, giving the roster bubble, depth, and developmental players a bigger opportunity to make their final pitch for a roster spot. Unfortunately for the Dolphins, they now finish the preseason without a win in three tries. Next on the NFL calendar are roster cuts, which are due by 6 p.m. Eastern on Sunday. Waiver claims and practice squad signings will happen early next week, then the team will start their preparations for the regular season. Miami opens the season on September 13 at the Las Vegas Raiders. Final Score Falcons 17 – 12 Dolphins Dolphins second-team defense stands up to Falcons starters Miami elected to sit all of their starters for this game, using the final preseason game as a chance to get an extended look at the depth players one last time before cutdown day on Sunday. The Falcons played their starters, using the game to tune up the first team and prepare for the regular season. A philosophical coaching difference put a tough task in front of Miami’s second-team defense – but they stepped up to the test. After Miami punted to end the opening drive of the game, the Falcons were able to drive down the field and score on a three-yard run from Brian Robinson, Jr., but the Miami defense stiffened after that. After Miami kicked a field goal, Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, making his return to South Florida after six seasons with the Dolphins, fumbled the first snap of Atlanta’s second drive, with Miami linebacker Willie Gay, Jr., recovering. Miami was unable to score on the resulting possession, having a long field goal attempt blocked, but the defense again made something happen. On a 1st and 10 from the Miami 18-yard line, linebacker Tyrel Dodson hit Robinson on the ball and forced a fumble, with linebacker Jackson Woodard falling on the loose ball. The first quarter ended during Miami’s possession and the Falcons pulled their first team on the next possession. Atlanta’s starters were only able to score a touchdown on three drives against Miami’s second-team defense, with the Dolphins getting two takeaways during the period. Tagovailoa finished the game 7-for-8 for 95 yards, 59 of them to tight end Kyle Pitts who had a 37 yard gain on the opening drive, and Robinson picked up 15 yards on five carries, including the touchdown push, so it was not perfect. But, overall, Miami’s second defense was able to stand up against the Falcons’ first-team offense. Special teams could be key to making or missing the roster Making an impact on special teams is an easy way to stand out among the crowd of players hoping to make it to the 53-man roster. Cornerback Ethan Bonner, who is likely already locked onto the roster, was flying downfield on the first punt from the team – he overran the tackle, but he was moving out there. Cameron Goode was in on the tackle on that punt, and he likely needs to get noticed on special teams to claim a roster spot. Wide receiver Jalen Reagor had one catch for 17 yards for his offensive production, but his return work on kicks and punts is what makes him likely to stick around this year. He had one punt return for 10 yards and he returned three kicks for 96 yards, giving him a 32-yard average; his long return was 46 yards. On the other end of the spectrum, punter Bradley Pinion continues to make me nervous for the season. Miami is going to need its punter to be consistent and a field-position-changing weapon, and Pinion has not been that this summer. He has some good kicks, but he shanks them just as often. After the Preseason Week 1 game against the Washington Commanders, I wrote, “ Punter Bradley Pinion is a concern , with some of his kicks tonight seeming off. He may work off the rust and be ready by the regular season, but his performance tonight didn’t instill confidence.” Nothing tonight changed any of those concerns. I would not be surprised if the Dolphins start shopping for a punter – and given the adventure that was field goal attempts tonight, breaking up the long snapper to punter/holder to the kicker battery is not going to be a major issue. Chris Bell makes impact Rookie wide receiver Chris Bell, who was on the non-football injury list for much of the summer as he recovered from an ACL tear he sustained in his final year at Louisville, made his debut with the Dolphins on Friday night. He was targeted often early in the game, catching two passes for 22 yards. The coaches rightfully got him out of the game fairly quickly, giving him just enough time to take some hits and play at the NFL speed, but then got him to the sideline and protected him for the regular season. It was a solid debut for the receiver. Miami is proving to be allergic to the endzone The Dolphins scored a touchdown on the opening drive of their first preseason game, the only drive the Miami starters played this summer. Miami did not score again in that game. Last week, they kicked a second-quarter field goal, their only points in the game. This week, they had a field goal in each quarter. The Dolphins cannot find the end zone. Hopefully, their allergy to touchdowns is only a depth issue and not something the starters have developed as well. Quarterback Mark Gronowski at least created a discussion The Miami Dolphins will likely head into the regular season with Malik Willis as the starting quarterback and Quinn Ewers as the backup. Cam Miller started the game, then gave way to Mark Gronowski for the second half. Both players are likely to be waived in the roster cuts that are coming, but Miami could consider bringing one back to the practice squad – and Gronowski made an argument that he could stick around as a developmental option. The undrafted rookie finished 4-for-8 for 97 yards, giving him a 94.3 passer rating. That is fine, but it was his ability to run for chunk yardage that could make him an interesting project. He rushed four times for 28 yards and looked fast. He may not stick around, especially since the Dolphins already cut him once this summer only to bring him back when Ewers was injured, but there might be enough there to warrant a practice squad spot.

title: Falcons vs. Dolphins: Miami players to watch in Preseason Week 3
summary: The Miami Dolphins host the Atlanta Falcons on Friday night, closing out the 2026 Preseason schedule. The game may include a cameo appearance by the starters, but the stars of the night will be the roster bubble players. Will anyone crush it on the field tonight and force the coaches to keep them on the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 20: Fatorma Mulbah #95 of the Miami Dolphins warms up during joint practice with the New York Giants at Baptist Health Training Complex on August 20, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins host the Atlanta Falcons on Friday night, closing out the 2026 Preseason schedule. The game may include a cameo appearance by the starters, but the stars of the night will be the roster bubble players. Will anyone crush it on the field tonight and force the coaches to keep them on the 53-man regular-season roster? Several players on the roster bubble are worth watching throughout the game. Could they make an impact on offense or defense? Are they in a key special-teams role that hints at their making the roster? We take a look at some of the players to watch tonight. Defensive tackle Fatorma Mulbah Mulbah went undrafted out of West Virginia in 2025 and signed with the New York Jets. He did not make the roster out of the preseason and spent time on the practice squad during the year. He signed with the Dolphins at the start of August, and he has made an impact quickly. Mulbah has been a force in the middle of the line, especially against the run. He is not perfect and he has growth that still needs to happen, but with a strong performance against the Falcons, he could force Miami to keep him on the roster rather than risking having him claimed off waivers by another team. Fullback D.J. Herman I have gone back and forth on projecting Herman to make the roster, with him on the wrong side of the cut line in today’s 53-man roster projection . He has been solid as a lead blocker, in pass protection, and as an outlet option in the passing game. A linebacker in college, Herman has made the adjustment to being a fullback and he is doing it well enough to force the Dolphins to at least consider using a roster spot to keep him. Tight end Ben Sims, who is listed as the first team fullback on the depth chart, has missed time and Herman has taken advantage of the opportunity. A strong performance on Friday, especially if he makes a special teams play, could land him on the right side of the cut line. Defensive end Cameron Goode The numbers seem to be against Goode making the roster this year, but the 2022 seventh-round pick could change that tonight. Primarily a special teams player, if he can make an impact during the game, he might force his way onto the roster. He has been fine during training camp, but fine might not be good enough to justify a roster position. Stepping up tonight might be a requirement for Goode to stay with the team another year. Safety Major Burns / Lonnie Johnson / Louis Moore I am absolutely cheating here by putting all three players in one spot on my five players to watch, but it is because there really is not any separation between them at this point. One of the three of them will make the roster as the fourth safety on the depth chart – which one could be determined tonight. Johnson has dealt with an injury this summer, Burns has flashed but may not be as consistent, and Moore is a rookie trying to go from undrafted to the roster. Offensive lineman Charlie Heck The Dolphins likely signed Heck as a free agent to serve as the swing tackle and primary game-day backup for both Patrick Paul at left tackle and Austin Jackson at right tackle. He has been inconsistent all summer and he has done everything except claim that role. I do not have him making the roster right now, but a strong performance tonight could change that. Heck could find help in the roster math if guard Josh Priebe sees playing time at center and plays well, that could lead Miami to releasing center Andrew Meyer and open a roster spot for Heck. It might be a backdoor way to make the roster, but it would still land him on the roster.

title: Dolphins to sit starters in preseason finale against Falcons
summary: The Miami Dolphins don’t kick off their regular season until Sunday, September 13th against the Las Vegas Raiders on the road. Unfortunately, for fans of the franchise, your next opportunity to see Miami’s starters in action will be in that contest, as Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network has confirmed that the Dolphins plan to rest […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins throws prior to a pre season game against the New York Giants at Hard Rock Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins don’t kick off their regular season until Sunday, September 13th against the Las Vegas Raiders on the road. Unfortunately, for fans of the franchise, your next opportunity to see Miami’s starters in action will be in that contest, as Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network has confirmed that the Dolphins plan to rest Malik Willis, De’Von Achane and many other starters against the Atlanta Falcons in tonight’s preseason finale. Dolphins plan to sit Malik Willis, De’Von Achane & many starters tonight vs ATL, per sources. Cam Miller to start at QB. Quinn Ewers won’t play due to injury (has to protect himself). Miami is dealing with a lot of injuries/depth Qs so focus on 53-man battles today: — Cameron Wolfe (@CameronWolfe) August 28, 2026 Willis and Miami’s starting offense only played one drive in the preseason — and on that drive, De’Von Achane scored a short rushing touchdown against the Washington Commanders. They sat most of their veteran starters the following week against the New York Giants. According to Wolfe, the plan remains the same tonight. In addition to Willis sitting, another quarterback will not be seen on the playing surface at Hard Rock Stadium on Friday night — backup quarterback Quinn Ewers. Ewers is dealing with a pesky groin injury, and as such, will be unavailable in Miami’s final preseason contest. According to Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, Ewers could possibly be on the hot seat in regards to a roster spot, so him not being able to put anything else on tape may end up hurting the second-year player in the long run when it comes to a roster spot with the Dolphins. Cam Miller will get the start at quarterback for Miami — and he’ll be matched up against former Dolphins starting quarterback, Tua Tagovailoa, who will be trying to impress against the team who drafted him #5 overall in the 2020 NFL Draft. We will continue to keep you updated on all things Miami Dolphins as the organization gears up for the start of the 2026 NFL season.

title: The Phinsider Mailbag: Dolphins back up quarterback, preseason results, and Joe Philbin hanging over team
summary: The Phinsider Mailbag is back to answer your questions ahead of the Miami Dolphins’ Preseason Week 3 game against the Atlanta Falcons. Tonight’s game is the last chance for roster bubble players to show the coaches they deserve a spot on the 53-man roster. It is also the last tune up the Dolphins get before […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 20: Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley smiles as he speaks to the media during a New York Giants and Miami Dolphins joint practice at the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on August 20 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Phinsider Mailbag is back to answer your questions ahead of the Miami Dolphins’ Preseason Week 3 game against the Atlanta Falcons. Tonight’s game is the last chance for roster bubble players to show the coaches they deserve a spot on the 53-man roster. It is also the last tune up the Dolphins get before they head into the regular season and start playing games that actually matter. This week, we asked for your questions and you responded. You asked questions about Miami’s backup quarterback, the importance of preseason results, and the ghost of Joe Philbin hanging over the team. It is time to get into the answers. As we did last week, Marek Brave and I had a round table like discussion to bring you our thoughts to your questions. MB: I’m on record as saying that I don’t believe Miami’s QB2 is currently on the team’s roster. Quinn Ewers has been abysmal outside of Mike McDaniel’s offense — and he wasn’t all that good in that offense either. Cam Miller has gotten slightly better as the preseason has progressed, but he’s got a long way to go. Jon-Eric Sullivan needs to be scouring the waiver wire after cut-down day this Sunday. KN: I think I am in the “show-me” crowd. Ewers is the backup until the team makes a move. Do I think they will make a move? I am probably 50/50 on that. If this team were in “win-now” mode, I would absolutely be screaming that they have to address the position as soon as possible, but since this team is looking toward the future, rather than a Super Bowl run this year, I do not know if Ewers being the backup actually matters. If the Dolphins are relying on Ewers for any stretch this year, they probably are in the market for a new quarterback in 2027 and an earlier draft choice might be a better option. I want this team to win now, and I am never going to be someone who advocates for a “tank” season, but I also think the Dolphins have to be smart about how they use their already limited salary cap space, and I am not sure a move at quarterback is the one I would make. MB: I don’t give any importance to them at all. KN: Absolutely agree. MB: We’ve seen Miami’s starting offense for a single drive this preseason, and they scored a touchdown. Does that mean the Dolphins will be an offensive juggernaut this season? Umm… no. But, I think Malik Willis will be an impressive player, the team will show heart and fight each week, we’ll find out we have the right head coach and GM moving forward, we’ll be happy with our rookie class and we’ll earn the right to have some hope heading into the 2027 season. If you’re expecting much more than that from this team this season, you are probably setting your expectations too high. KN: I do not think head coach Jeff Hafley has put any time into preparing for the specific games Miami has played this summer. He is more concerned with the players on the roster and their individual and group performance. Even when the Dolphins are getting trounced, the individual player responsibilities and performances are what Hafley is trying to see. Do I want to feel better about the team because they won this weekend? Of course. But I do not think Hafley and the rest of the coaching staff are looking at the scoreboard at all. And, like the question said, everything that happened in these three games will be forgotten as soon as Week 1 starts. KN: We as fans live and die by the week when it comes to the Dolphins. This year for the Dolphins, the weekly results do not matter. They need to grow. Are they looking like a better team in Week 18 than the one that took the field in Week 1? That is the true measure. This team is pieced together with rookies, new free agents, and younger players seeing extended playing time for the first time; they will need time to get everyone on the same page. I expect rookie mistakes – even out of the veterans – early in the season because they are still growing together. I want to see those cleaned up throughout the year and a more competitive product on the field late in the year. MB: Jeff Hafley has said himself that wins and losses won’t be the measure of success for Miami this season, so it shouldn’t be for Malik Willis either. Hafley wants to see leadership from the QB position. I think Willis has already shown a high level of leadership through the way he speaks with the media, in addition to the way he has taken accountability for getting the offense on the right page during practices and team meetings. Also, I’m a believer in all three rookie wide receivers, so to say there’s a lack of receiving talent without letting those guys attempt to prove themselves in meaningful games is a bit premature for me. KN: I skipped over that part, but you are right. There is a ton of potential talent on the roster for Miami this year. You do not select 13 players in a single draft and not come away with potential talent. We as fans have to be content with letting them have the time to develop and blossom. We all want immediate results and we are ready to call a player a bust the first time we see him get beaten on the field. This year has to be about patience. The wide receivers have the potential to be stars. Maybe we should let them turn the potential talent into talent. MB: I think he’s more of a practice squad candidate for my money. He’s an intriguing player and someone you want to keep around for sure, but I don’t know if he’s ready to be a primary backup just yet. Maybe he makes the team initially to keep him off of the waiver wire through the first round of claims, but I’m not so sure he’s on the main roster once the regular season kicks off. KN: I am probably a bit higher on Mulbah than you are. I think he does have a shot at making the roster. He is right on the bubble for me – though in today’s 53-man roster projection , I have him on the wrong side of the cut line. I agree he is a practice squad option, especially since I think he is battling Matthew Butler for one roster spot. But, if he plays well tonight, I could see Miami looking for a way to keep him on the roster. MB: Whoa, whoa, whoa… Calm down. In my opinion, Hafley and Philbin couldn’t be any more different. Don’t judge the new head coach on a mostly meaningless preseason game. The Dolphins lack depth. That’s because the Dolphins lack money. Their highest paid player will be playing AGAINST them in tonight’s preseason finale. Let’s give the new guy a bit of a grace period before we start comparing him to Mr. Queasy himself — this is a rebuild after all. KN: I am so glad you answered this question first. The only comparison between the two is Green Bay. I have not seen or heard of Hafley walking around at practice picking up trash. Just based on personality alone, I think Hafley seems more like a head coach than Philbin ever did. I also go back to, I do not think Hafley had any interest in trying to scheme to win that game. I think the coaches knew what they wanted to see from the players on the field, and they called the game to get that film, not to win the game. The play calling, player packages, and formations will be different when the games matter. But, like you said, this is a rebuild. The coaches and front office know they are here to clean up a roster and a salary cap that had gotten out of control. There will be growing pains this year, and there will be times when the Dolphins simply cannot matchup to the opponent, but that is the nature of a rebuild.

title: Tua Tagovailoa set to return to Miami as Falcons visit Dolphins
summary: The third week of the NFL Preseason schedule typically does not include major storylines as everyone focuses on the depth players who are trying to make the roster more than the players who, in two weeks, will be starting and major contributors in the regular season. Roster cuts are coming due, with each team needing […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - AUGUST 14: Atlanta quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (1) reacts during the NFL pre-season game between the Denver Broncos and the Atlanta Falcons on August 14th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The third week of the NFL Preseason schedule typically does not include major storylines as everyone focuses on the depth players who are trying to make the roster more than the players who, in two weeks, will be starting and major contributors in the regular season. Roster cuts are coming due, with each team needing to drop 37 players in the hours between its preseason game and 6 p.m. Eastern time on Sunday. Typically is the keyword in that opening sentence. When it comes to the Miami Dolphins’ final preseason game, another storyline is set to play out. The Dolphins host the Atlanta Falcons on Friday night, and a familiar face will hit the field at Hard Rock Stadium, but he will wear white, red, and black instead of aqua and orange. Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, Miami’s 2020 first-round pick, was released this offseason and now returns as the Falcons’ signal caller. Tagovailoa is expected to start in Friday’s game for Atlanta. He will be the first “franchise” quarterback for the Dolphins to return to South Florida with another team – Bob Griese and Dan Marino never left Miami and Ryan Tannehill never faced the Dolphins in Miami after he moved to the Tennessee Titans. Tagovailoa highs and lows in Miami In six seasons with the Dolphins, Tagovailoa threw for 18,166 yards with 120 touchdowns and 59 interceptions. He led the league with 4,624 passing yards in 2023 and earned a Pro Bowl selection that year. He was the league’s completion percentage leader in 2024 and the passer rating leader in 2022. He is the team’s all-time leader in passer rating and completion percentage and ranks fourth in franchise history in passing yards and touchdown passes. Injuries, particularly concussions, played a major role in the decline of Tagovailoa’s play, ultimately leading to his release. He succeeded when he could anticipate routes and use his accuracy to thread passes through tight defenses. Over the last two years with Miami, the timing seemed off, his arm lost strength, and his confidence seemed shot – both in himself and in his offensive line. Salary cap impact of Tagovailoa’s release It was time for a new start for Tagovailoa and for the Dolphins – even as his release costs Miami $55.4 million in cap space this season and another $43.8 million next year. Are the Falcons getting the quarterback who can lead the league in major passing statistics or are they getting the quarterback who was eventually benched last year for a seventh-round rookie? To get an idea of what the Falcons have in Tagovailoa, I spoke with Jeanna Kelley from The Falcoholic, SB Nation’s Falcons team site. She provided a great breakdown of Tagovailoa’s time in Atlanta. Tua’s roller coaster summer Kelley: Tua’s performance has definitely been up-and-down this summer, but there are several caveats. One, Atlanta’s right tackle Kaleb McGary retired unexpectedly this offseason, and Jawaan Taylor was brought in as the probable replacement, but he was working through some injury issues early on that delayed his ability to really integrate with that unit. You know what it’s like when an offensive line hasn’t quite developed the chemistry they need to be effective, and in addition to adjusting to a new scheme and developing his timing and chemistry with his new receivers, that hasn’t made Tua’s life easier. Door open for Tagovailoa to start If Tua’s able to play well, I think it would be bonkers to make a change when Penix is ready to play. Kelley: I do not think Michael Penix will be able to start Week 1. I believe he is healthy, but given how recently he was medically cleared and that he’s just had three days of practice, I feel like the season is creeping up too quicky for Penix to be ready, so I think Tua will be the starter. And if Tua’s able to play well, I think it would be bonkers to make a change when Penix is ready to play. Tua’s work ethic on display Kelley: Tua’s biggest strengths, in my opinion, are his maturity, intelligence (general intellect and football IQ), and work ethic. If it is at all possible for Tua to put himself in a position to succeed — if that is actually something that is within Tua’s control — I believe with his mindset and work ethic, he will get it done. If it’s out of Tua’s control, though — for example, if he (and I truly, truly hope he does not) gets another concussion, then all bets are off. Fans frustrated but Tagovailoa the best option Tua has not been perfect, but I still firmly believe he’s the Falcons’ best option Week 1 unless Michael Penix’s status changes dramatically Kelley: Falcons fans are generally over the Tua experiment and would rather see either Penix regardless of whether he’s fully physically ready, or Jack Strand, the UDFA dynamo who’s shown out against guys buried deep on the depth chart, but needs quite a bit of development coming out of Minnesota-Moorhead. No, Tua has not been perfect, but I still firmly believe he’s the Falcons’ best option Week 1 unless Michael Penix’s status changes dramatically much faster than I expect. And Tua is such a good guy; I can’t help but hope it works out for him — if not in Atlanta long-term, given what they invested into Penix, then I hope he’s able to show enough this season to get another shot at a starting gig elsewhere.
