title: NY Giants 53-man roster projection: Final prediction of initial roster
summary: The preseason is over. The New York Giants and the NFL’s other 31 teams have to set their initial 53-man rosters by 6 p.m. on Sunday. Here is my final projection of what roster will look like. OFFENSE Quarterback (2) IN: Jaxson Dart, Jameis WinstonOut: Brandon Allen, Jake Haener The question here is which of […]
full_text: The preseason is over. The New York Giants and the NFL’s other 31 teams have to set their initial 53-man rosters by 6 p.m. on Sunday. Here is my final projection of what roster will look like. OFFENSE Quarterback (2) IN: Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston Out: Brandon Allen, Jake Haener The question here is which of Allen and the recently-signed Haener the Giants choose to keep on their practice squad. I believe Allen gets the nod. He has gotten more reps than Haener, and I have to believe that means something. Haener played well Friday night, but that might have been too little, too late. Practice squad: Allen Running back (4) IN: Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy, Devin Singletary, Najee Harris Out: Eric Gray, Damon Bankston Unless somebody makes GM Joe Schoen and head coach John Harbaugh an offer they can’t refuse, I believe Tracy will be on the roster. He showed his explosiveness Friday with 37 yards on just four carries. Practice squad: Gray Fullback (1) IN: Patrick Ricard Out: Grant Finley The only real question here is whether or not the Giants will keep the 6-foot-4, 281-pound Finley, an undrafted free agent, on the practice squad in hopes of developing him into Ricard 2.0. Practice squad: Finley Tight end (3) IN: Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson, Chris Manhertz Out: Tanner Conner, Thomas Fidone, Josiah Deguara It was interesting that the Giants used an open 90-man roster spot to add Deguara this week. I don’t believe that will impact the final roster. Practice squad: Fidone Wide receiver (7) IN: Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, Darnell Mooney, Malachi Fields, Braxton Berrios , Odell Beckham Jr. , Dalen Cambre Out: Xavier Gipson, Isaiah Hodgins, Jalin Hyatt IR: Calvin Austin The unfortunate knee injury suffered by Calvin Austin opens a spot for Odell Beckham Jr. I am keeping Cambre as a special teamer, though I might be wrong about that one. We haven’t seen Hyatt on the field for weeks now, and this is probably the end of the line for him. Practice squad: Hodgins Offensive line (9) IN: Andrew Thomas, Jon Runyan, John Michael Schmitz, Francis Mauigoa, Jermaine Eluemunor, Marcus Mbow, Aaron Stinnie, J.C. Davis, Lucas Patrick Out: Bryan Hudson, Evan Neal, Ryan Schernecke, Jake Kubas, Jarrod Gray (International Exemption), Brendan Jaimes It is still hard to believe that the Giants, unable to field competent offensive lines more often than not over the past 15 years, have traded TWO surplus offensive linemen for draft capital over the past couple of weeks. The big decision here is Hudson vs. Patrick as the backup center and emergency guard. I have had Patrick in this spot all along, and I am sticking with that. Hudson made a late push, but Patrick got the call ahead of Hudson on Friday night and I think that is an indication of where the staff sees the competition. Kubas is interesting. If Harbaugh wants an extra offensive lineman, he could get a spot. Still, on game days teams usually dress only eight offensive lineman, so I will drop Kubas to the practice squad. I have to give credit where it’s due. Neal was outstanding against the Jets. He was a wrecking ball as a run blocker, and it makes you wonder how things might have turned out for him had the Giants movd him to guard sooner. I still don’t see a spot on the roster for him. You can try making a case for cutting Stinnie, but I don’t think the Giants want to do that. Practice squad: Hudson, Kubas, Schernecke, Gray (International Exemption) DEFENSE Defensive line (6) IN: D.J. Reader, Darius Alexander, Shelby Harris, Chauncey Golston, Leki Fotu, Bobby Jamison-Travis Out: Josh Tupou, Zacch Pickens, Anquin Barnes Jr., Marlon Davidson, Ben Barten I have waffled on the idea that Jamison-Travis, a sixth-round pick, would make the roster. In the end, I will keep him on the 53 and stash Tupou, a veteran nose tackle, on the practice squad. I won’t be surprised if the Giants add a veteran dropped by someone else, most likely replacing Fotu. His sack dance is fun, but I won’t be shocked if Jamison-Travis lands on the practice squad. I am keeping him in this projection, but I don’t feel great about it. Practice squad: Tupou Off-ball linebacker (5) IN: Arvell Reese, Tremaine Edmunds, Micah McFadden, Jack Kelly , Zaire Barnes Out : Darius Muasau, Chandler Martin, Anfernee Orji I am keeping Barnes for his ability as a special teamer. To be honest, he has also been superior to Muasau as a defender this summer. Practice squad: Muasau Edge defender (3) IN: Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux Out : Caleb Murphy, Khalid Kareem, Trace Ford Golston has earned a role on the defensive line, but is also the fourth edge defender. I am comfortable keeping three “pure” edge defenders because of his presence. Practice squad: Murphy, Ford Cornerback (6) IN: Paulson Adebo, Greg Newsome II, Colton Hood, Dru Phillips, Deonte Banks, Art Green Out: Korie Black, Nic Jones, Ugo Amadi The real question here, as it has been for a while, is which players will start Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. Increasingly, it has looked like Banks and Newsome, with Adebo and his $24.199 million cap hit as the third wheel. That would be 8.1% of the Giants’ cap space coming off the bench. If he isn’t going to start, might the Giants be able to deal Adebo. One other note: I have always had Green making the roster because of special teams, but Black has played well toward the end of the summer. Has he played well enough to steal a job?Maybe. Practice squad: Black Safety (4) IN: Jevon Holland, Tyler Nubin, Ar’Darius Washington, Jason Pinnock Out : Elijah Campbell, Beau Brade, Raheem Layne, J.T. Woods I think Harbaugh, with his special teams background, will try to find room for an experienced core special teamer like Campbell. I just don’t know where that room comes from. Practice squad: Campbell SPECIAL TEAMS (3) IN: Jordan Stout (punter) , Dominic Zvada (placekicker) , Ben Mann (long-snapper) Out: Ben Sauls (placekicker) Harbaugh has already made this call . Practice squad: Sauls

title: Dominic Zvada will be the NY Giants’ placekicker
summary: Very few fans called “kicker” as one of the most compelling roster battles of the New York Giants training camp, but that’s where we find ourselves. And after the Giants’ 23-6 victory over the New York Jets, we have the answer as to who will be the Giants kicker for 2026 season: Undrafted free agent […]
full_text: New York Giants kicker Dominic Zvada | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Very few fans called “kicker” as one of the most compelling roster battles of the New York Giants training camp, but that’s where we find ourselves. And after the Giants’ 23-6 victory over the New York Jets, we have the answer as to who will be the Giants kicker for 2026 season: Undrafted free agent Dominic Zvada , as confirmed by head coach John Harbaugh after the game . The Giants took the unorthodox step of releasing veteran kicker Jason Sanders way back on June 2nd, leaving the kicking competition up to Zvada and three-game veteran Ben Sauls. Both kickers had impressive performances in training camp. However, Zvada, the UDFA out of Michigan, was clearly better. Zvada not only showed off the leg strength that could make him the kind of weapon the Giants have lacked in recent years, but he was both accurate and consistent. He rarely missed a kick in practice and was rock solid when he got the opportunity in preseason games. That isn’t to detract from Sauls, who did a fantastic job settling the Giants’ special teams down in 2025 and was solid himself this summer. NFL teams are loathe to rely on inexperienced special teams players, but both Zvada and (fellow UDFA) long snapper Ben Mann have proven their worth this summer. The big question now is whether the Giants can hang on to Ben Sauls and sign him to their practice squad. It was notable that the Giants didn’t use Sauls at all in their win over the Jets — while Jason Sanders missed an extra point and a 54-yard field goal for the Jets. The Giants would obviously love to keep two NFL-caliber kickers around, but they may be able to parlay Sauls into a draft pick for 2027 if they think he’ll be claimed off of waivers. Meanwhile, Zvada has come a long way since he announced himself that he would sign with the Giants as an undrafted free agent. title: Giants-Jets winners and losers: Odell Beckham makes his case
summary: The New York Giants finished their preseason on Friday with a 23-6 victory over the New York Jets. Odell Beckham Jr. had a big night. Dominic Zvada learned he had won the placekicking job. Let’s review the action in our unique ‘Kudos and Wet Willies’ style. Kudos to … Odell Beckham Jr. — Is anyone […]
full_text: Odell Beckham had a lot to smile about Friday night. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants finished their preseason on Friday with a 23-6 victory over the New York Jets. Odell Beckham Jr. had a big night. Dominic Zvada learned he had won the placekicking job. Let’s review the action in our unique ‘Kudos and Wet Willies’ style. Kudos to … Odell Beckham Jr. — Is anyone still questioning whether or not Beckham is making the 53-man roster? Beckham nearly had a 73-yard touchdown reception, but Jameis Winston slightly overthrew him and the ball fell incomplete. Beckham still had an outstanding night. He caught three passes for 53 yards, an average of 17.7 yards per catch, with the longest being a 23-yard grab. He has enough juice to be a useful player for this Giants team. John Harbaugh said after the game that Beckham has done enough to make a roster, but stopped short of anointing him as part of the Giants’ 53-man roster. "Super grateful for the opportunity. At this point, it's in God's hands. I know that I have a good feeling about myself – there's ball to be played, plays to be made." – Odell Beckham Jr. pic.twitter.com/aLCY7LCHgA — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) August 29, 2026 Tyrone Tracy — The third-year running back needed a big night after mishaps in the first two preseason games. He got one with four carries for 37 yards, including a 16-yard run, and a 6-yard touchdown. He also survived an injury scare, passing a concussion test and seeming to be fine while on the sideline in the second half. Offensive line — There were holes to run through and pockets to pass from all night. The Giants traded offensive linemen Daniel Faalele and Josh Ezeudu over the past week, because they liked their depth. Friday night you could see why. Sisi Mauigoa was outstanding in his brief stint. Guys like rookie J.C Davis, Evan Neal, and Jake Kubas all played well. It was fun, and sort of mystifying, to watch Neal push guys backwards all night. Where has that been for the last four years? Zaire Barnes — Barnes capped off an excellent summer with a tremendous, athletic interception. The fact that he was also a game captain was a massive pre-game hint that he is making the 53-man roster. Trace Ford — I don’t know if there is a place for Ford on the 53-man roster, but he certainly made a case on Friday for the Giants to find one. Ford, an edge defender, had five tackles, three for loss, a sack, two quarterback hits, and two passes defensed. Question is, will he have a roster spot on Sunday night? Dominic Zvada — Zvada has won the placekicking competition with Ben Sauls. Zvada made field goals of 23, 46, and 53 yards, and added two extra points. It didn’t hurt that short-time Giant Jason Sanders missed an extra point and was short on a 54-yard field goal try. John Harbaugh made it official after the game that Zvada will be the placekicker. Jake Haener — After just joining the Giants a couple of weeks ago, Haener was impressive in his only game action of the preseason. He went 6 of 7 for 101 yards, a touchdown, and a perfect 158.3 passer rating. Haener’s touchdown was a beautifully directed and thrown ball to wide receiver Xavier Gipson. Did Haener do enough to take a practice squad spot away from Brandon Allen? Jordan Stout — Thanks to a penalty, Stout was forced to re-kick after a 63-yard punt. He responded with an amazing 81-yard punt that was nearly downed at the 1-yard line by Darius Muasau and Dalen Cambre. Najee Harris — The newly-signed running back got his first game action, and looked good. He carried 11 times for 39 yards, with a long run of 9 yards, as the Giants got him ready for Week 1. Wet Willies to … Run defense — Not sure that the Giants need to be scouring cuts for defensive line help? All you had to do was watch the Jets’ opening 10-play, 36-yard drive to know that the answer is absolutely. The Giants need rotational players to join D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris, and they are sorely lacking in capable run defenders on the interior defensive line. Darius Alexander, Bobby Jamison-Travis, Leki Fotu, and pretty much everyone the Giants put out there left a lot to be desired in run defense. Jamison-Travis and his sack celebration are fun. His job, though, is run defense. He needs to get better at it. Turnovers — The Giants committed two. One, a Jameis Winston interception after a pass bounced off Beckham’s hands, set up the Jets’ touchdown. The other, a red zone fumble by Braxton Berrios, denied the Giants a scoring opportunity.
author: Ed Valentine

title: Tyrone Tracy injury: NY Giants’ RB leaves game against Jets
summary: Tyrone Tracy’s nightmarish preseason took another seemingly unfortunate turn on Friday night when he left the New York Giants’ game against the New York Jets with an injury. Tracy, the Giants’ leading rusher the past two seasons, has had a rough preseason. He missed a block in the first preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings […]
full_text: Tyrone Tracy is attended to after being injured Friday night. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyrone Tracy’s nightmarish preseason took another seemingly unfortunate turn on Friday night when he left the New York Giants’ game against the New York Jets with an injury. Tracy, the Giants’ leading rusher the past two seasons, has had a rough preseason. He missed a block in the first preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings that led to quarterback Jaxson Dart taking a big hit. In Week 2 against the Miami Dolphins, Tracy fumbled in the red zone despite being untouched. Running backs Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary did not dress for Friday’s game. Tracy, looking to play a clean game after the miscues in the first games, and Najee Harris did. Tracy was having an excellent night before being injured. He had four carries for 37 yards, an average of 9.3 yards per carry. Tracy had a 6-yard touchdown run, and a long run of 16 yards. This is the hit that led to Tracy’s injury: Tyrone Tracy down after this hit pic.twitter.com/bUSDtQsTb4 — Giants Nation Show (@GiantsNationPod) August 29, 2026 Tracy reportedly cleared concussion protocol. He is reportedly “fine” , but is no longer in uniform and won’t return to the game.

title: Final Score: Giants backups crush Jets backups in preseason finale
summary: In the New York Jets’ third and final preseason game of 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Jets were defeated by the New York Giants, 23 – 6. The Jets opened on defense and on third down they intercepted Jameis Winston. That set them up with first and ten at the Giants 36. The […]
full_text: New York Jets safety Jarius Monroe (25) blocks the ball as New York Giants wide receiver Braxton Berrios (87) attempts to catch the ball during a game at MetLife Stadium, Aug 28, 2026, East Rutherford, NJ, USA. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co In the New York Jets’ third and final preseason game of 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Jets were defeated by the New York Giants, 23 – 6. The Jets opened on defense and on third down they intercepted Jameis Winston. That set them up with first and ten at the Giants 36. The Jets proceeded to run a 10 play drive that ended with a short Chip Trayanum touchdown run. No passes were thrown in the drive. Jason Sanders missed the extra point to make the score Jets 6, Giants 0. The Giants proceeded to put together a long drive that ended when the Jets forced a fumble by old friend Braxton Berrios into their own end zone for a touchback. The turnovers are flowing for the Jets this preseason. Late in the first quarter the Giants took advantage of a short field to go on a drive culminating in a Tyrone Tracy touchdown run and a 7 – 6 Giants lead. The first quarter ended a few seconds later with the score still 7 – 6. A few plays into the second quarter Cade Klubnick threw a terrible pass into tight coverage that was picked off by the Giants. The Giants then put together a long drive that bogged down inside the Jets five yard line. They converted on a chip shot field goal to take a 10 – 6 lead with less than three minutes left in the half. Neither team got much going on offense the last few minutes and the half ended with the score still Giants 10, Jets 6. The Jets opened the third quarter on offense. Bailey Zappe took over for Cade Klubnik at quarterback and promptly led the team on a scintillating three and out. The Giants offensive scrubs took over and put together a short drive ending in a 53 yard field goal and a 13 – 6 Giants lead midway through the third quarter. Zappe took over on offense and engineered a thrilling three and out as he made his case to be cut on Sunday. Legendary quarterback Jake Haener took over for the Giants and led them on a long drive. The third quarter ended with the score still Giants 13, Jets 6, but the Giants were lining up for a field goal attempt. On the first play of the fourth quarter the Giants hit on a 46 yard field goal as the Giants took a 16 -6 lead to open the fourth quarter. Bailey Zappe proceeded to lead the Jets on a stirring three and out as he continued to impress. Jake The Legend Haener then led the Giants on a swift drive resulting in a touchdown on a 37 yard pass to old friend Xavier Gipson as the Giants piled on with 23 unanswered points. The score was Giants 23, Jets 6 with 10:30 left in the game. Midway through the fourth quarter the Jets turned to Brady Cook at quarterback. Cook led the Jets on a short drive ending in a missed 54 yard field goal by Jason Sanders, who had a rough night and may have played himself off the team. Jake The Goat Haener and the Giants then closed out the game with a long drive to the Jets one yard line before taking a knee on the last three plays of the game. Final score: Giants 23, Jets 6. The loss brought the Jets’ preseason record to 1-2. The score doesn’t really matter. The record doesn’t really matter. The most important development in the game were injuries to Anez Cooper, Chip Trayanum, Dominic Richardson and Joseph Ossai. We’ll see if these end up being injuries that threaten to keep these players out for an extended period of time. Now the Jets move on to getting their roster down to 53 players by 6:00 P.M. EDT on Sunday. They then begin preparations for their opening day game against the Tennessee Titans on September 13.
author: MacGregor Wells

title: Jets vs Giants Game Thread
summary: The New York Jets are at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey tonight to take on the New York Giants in the third and final preseason game of 2026 for both teams. Kickoff is scheduled for shortly after 7:30 pm EDT. The Jets starters are not expected to play tonight. With backups and backups […]
full_text: Members of the grounds crew work to change over the end zones in the New Meadowlands Stadium from Jets green to Giants blue Friday afternoon in East Rutherford, November 26, 2010. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The New York Jets are at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey tonight to take on the New York Giants in the third and final preseason game of 2026 for both teams. Kickoff is scheduled for shortly after 7:30 pm EDT. The Jets starters are not expected to play tonight. With backups and backups of backups controlling the action, we are unlikely to see compelling football. Tonight is, however, a big night for the so-called bubble players, who will be stating their case for whatever roster spots may still be open. The biggest thing for the two teams will be coming out of this game without any serious injuries, if fortune allows. For the bubble players, it’s an audition, not just for their respective teams, but for every team in the NFL. With the shortened preseason schedule there are few opportunities to put good things on tape for the rest of the league to see. Tonight is the last such opportunity of the preseason. Players who don’t end up making it through final cuts have a chance here to showcase their skills for the entire league, which might earn them a shot with a different franchise down the road. One thing to keep an eye on is the order of when players enter the game. Those players still on the field in the fourth quarter are unlikely to make the team. Those players starting tonight are likely to be the primary backups for the team. It’s the Jets and the Giants in the 2026 preseason finale. Enjoy the game everybody.

title: I hate to say it, but Bill Belichick belongs in the Hall of Fame
summary: I’m probably the last person anybody would ever expect to write an article defending Bill Belichick. I have hated him for the last two and a half decades. When I say that, I don’t mean that I have held any actual malice towards the man or hoped for genuine harm. He simply has been my […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - DECEMBER 17: Head coach Bill Belichick of the New England Patriots looks on during the second half against the Kansas City Chiefs at Gillette Stadium on December 17, 2023 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’m probably the last person anybody would ever expect to write an article defending Bill Belichick. I have hated him for the last two and a half decades. When I say that, I don’t mean that I have held any actual malice towards the man or hoped for genuine harm. He simply has been my ultimate sports villain. His few and far between professional failures have been glorious for me. Belichick was supposed to become the Jets’ head coach in January 2000. The line of succession was set. Bill Parcells stepped down a day after the 1999 season ended. For years there was an understanding that Belichick would ascend to the head coaching job after that happened. Instead, Belichick resigned at what was supposed to be his introductory press conference. A few weeks later he was announced as the head coach of the New England Patriots, a bitter division rival. From there he built one of the most enduring dynasties in sports history, capturing a record six Super Bowl wins in a span of less than two decades. As the years have passed I have come to understand and even respect why Belichick passed on the Jets job at a point where the team’s ownership situation was unclear and ended with Woody Johnson buying the team. Still, Belichick could have handled the whole thing much more professionally. Scribbling out his resignation letter on a napkin? Come on. It also felt like Belichick saved unnecessary venom for the Jets. There was always a passive aggressive shot at a press conference or a deep ball late in the fourth quarter with New England leading the Jets by three or four touchdowns to rub a little extra salt into the wound. Given the Patriots’ position dominating the league and the Jets typically occupying the cellar, it felt a bit like the schoolyard bully picking on the weakest kid on the playground. A year ago at this time the eyes of the football world were fixed on Chapel Hill, North Carolina. There was a lot of intrigue about how Belichick would do moving to the college game and taking over as the head coach of the University of North Carolina’s football team. As the Tar Heels begin a new season tomorrow, I think it is fair to say the program and Belichick have plenty of eyes on them once again. This year, though, it is born out of a grisly curiosity. The Belichick Era at North Carolina veered badly off course from the start, an embarrassing 48-14 loss at home to TCU. The team stumbled to an ugly 4-8 season. The football was bad. The headlines were worse. From Jordon Hudson to Mike Lombardi the North Carolina football program has become as notable for its off field dysfunction as for its on field failures. At this point the biggest question around the program is precisely when UNC will pull the plug on this disaster, and how bad it will get before that happens. Note that I said, “when,” not, “if.” As if all of this wasn’t enough, Belichick suffered another embarrassment in January as the selection committee of the Pro Football Hall of Fame declined to enshrine him in his first year of eligibility. The only sign of Belichick during induction weekend in July was a joke his former kicker Adam Vinatieri made at his expense. 🚨🚨INSANE🚨🚨 ADAM VINATIERI TOOK SHOTS AT BILL BELICHICK DURING HIS EPIC HALL OF FAME SPEECH. “UNFORTUNATELY, BILL COULDN’T BE HERE RIGHT NOW… IT’S BECAUSE HE’S JUDGING HIS GIRLFRIEND’S CHEERLEADING COMPETITION” 💀💀💀 pic.twitter.com/QLNQOIWSWr — MLFootball (@MLFootball) August 8, 2026 This is where I have to draw the line. I am a Jets fan, yes. I am also passionate about the history of the game. When I was a kid my dad instilled in me that to appreciate the sport as a fan, you have to understand its history. The past explains how we got here. I cringe whenever I log onto social media these days because inevitably I will see some graphic ranking the “greatest of all-time” at a position. Inevitably the list would make you believe NFL history began in the year 2000. Occasionally one of the lists will at least trace back to players from the 1980s. Once in a blue moon, it will include the entire Super Bowl era. But there are so many greats that fans never learn about. For whatever reason, this problem is more pronounced in football than any other sport. We don’t treat the history of the game with reverence. The average baseball fan has heard of Ty Cobb, Babe Ruth, and Ted Williams. The average basketball fan has heard of Bill Russell and Wilt Chamberlain. How many football fans don’t know Sammy Baugh, Bronko Nagurski, Don Hutson, Raymond Berry, Chuck Bednarik, and so many other all-time greats who played before the Super Bowl era? We owe the game we enjoy to the contributions these players made to the sport. Yet they are lost to history. So I think about fans in the future. I ask myself whether there’s a reasonable way to justify the coach who has the most Super Bowl wins, is tied for the most overall NFL championships, and has the second most wins not being in the Hall of Fame. The answer is a clear no for me. Many fans don’t agree with that. They argue Belichick was a vastly overrated coach. I think there are five reasons people make this argument. Belichick was at the center of a massive cheating scandal that tarnished his image. When he left the Patriots, the franchise was a mess. Within two years of his departure, they were rebuilt into a Super Bowl team. Tom Brady departed New England and immediately won a championship with another team. As this happened, the Patriots under Belichick slowly sunk to the bottom of the league. This suggests that Belichick was along for the ride after lucking his way into having arguably the greatest quarterback of all-time. The end of Belichick’s career has been hideous. Not only did the Patriots sink to the bottom of the NFL after Brady left. We have the current fiasco at North Carolina. People just don’t like Belichick and revel in any chance to knock his legacy and call him a fraud. If you are in the fifth category, I understand where you are coming from. However, I will warn you right here that if you won’t listen to any arguments that Belichick was a great coach, this article won’t be for you. I harbor no hard feelings if you want to leave right now and check out something else on this site. For those of you who are willing to engage with a nuanced discussion on the greatest of a complex figure, please join me below. I fully intend to address each of the five arguments against Belichick’s greatness before we finish. First, however, I think it’s important to establish what actually made him great. Great coaches come in all shapes and sizes. It always makes me chuckle a bit when a team is conducting a coaching hire, and fans state that inherently an offensive coach is greater than a defensive coach or that running a particular scheme is important. At the end of the day, no two coaches are alike. All bring something different to the table. As for Bill Belichick, there are the five things I would argue that set him apart. Belichick was the greatest defensive mind of his era. As time passes our memories fade. We have a way of jumbling things in our mind to fit convenient narratives. When it comes to the Patriots dynasty, we tend to think about the end years when Tom Brady was an unstoppable force. It wasn’t always that way, though. New England was a balanced team through its first three Super Bowl wins. Tom Brady wasn’t yet TOM BRADY . Now don’t get me wrong. He was still an elite quarterback in this era, arguably still the best in the league. But rather than serving as a wrecking ball to defenses for 60 minutes, his game was more defined by playing efficient football and then delivering the clutch fourth quarter drive to win the game. Brady…

title: Scouting Jets cornerback Keenan Garber
summary: The Jets recently signed cornerback Keenan Garber, who has already played one game for the Jets in preseason. Today, we break Garber down in detail. The 26-year old Garber is listed at 6’0” and 188 pounds and was undrafted out of Kansas State last season. He has yet to make his NFL debut but started […]
full_text: Dec 26, 2024; Phoenix, AZ, USA; Kansas State Wildcats cornerback Keenan Garber (1) against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the Rate Bowl at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Jets recently signed cornerback Keenan Garber, who has already played one game for the Jets in preseason. Today, we break Garber down in detail. The 26-year old Garber is listed at 6’0” and 188 pounds and was undrafted out of Kansas State last season. He has yet to make his NFL debut but started 17 games in college, during which he recorded 52 tackles, nine pass breakups and two interceptions. Background Garber was a three-star high school recruit, who originally headed to Kansas State as a wide receiver in 2019. In his first three seasons, he played in 19 games, during which he registered 88 yards on nine touches. That included a 54-yard reception. In 2022, Garber remained as a wide receiver, but wasn’t getting any opportunities, so he opted to transfer to defensive back. An injury crisis during the Big 12 title game meant he was called into action, making one tackle. That was his only statistical contribution in 14 games that season. Garber opted to remain at cornerback for his redshirt season, then remained there for another year, as he had an extra season of eligibility due to the pandemic. During those two seasons, he started 17 of 26 games and recorded 52 tackles, nine pass breakups, 1.5 tackles for loss and two interceptions, including a pick-six. Despite a solid pro day workout, Garber was not considered as likely to be drafted and ultimately signed as an undrafted free agent with the Vikings, for whom he attended training camp and played in three preseason games. After final cuts, he had brief stints on the practice squad for the Colts and Lions, but didn’t get elevated for a regular season game. The Jets signed Garber just over a week ago, but he already led them in defensive snaps in his first appearance with them in preseason. He had three tackles in that game having registered no stats in three preseason appearances with Minnesota. Let’s move onto some more in-depth analysis of what Garber brings to the table, based on in-depth research and film study. Measurables/Athleticism Garber has average size, but lacks ideal length. However, he is a good athlete. At his pro day, he ran a 4.50 in the 40-yard dash and managed 18 bench press reps with good agility and explosiveness numbers. Usage Garber has played almost exclusively as an outside cornerback in college and preseason action. When he was a wide receiver, he also played exclusively outside. Coverage Garber’s coverage numbers in his first season as a full-time cornerback were solid as he only allowed a catch on 50 percent of his targets for an average of less than 12 yards per catch. However, his numbers were worse in his final season as he gave up a 67 percent catch rate and almost 15 yards per catch. He’s still relatively new to the position, although he did play defensive back in high school, but Garber moves around relatively smoothly. However, he can be late to react to route breaks. Tet McMillan was a good test for him in his first season as a full-time cornerback, but he gave up five catches for 80 yards as McMillan went 11-for-138 in total. At times, you’re left wondering if Garber completely trusts his own abilities because he often seems to play too far off his receiver. Over the two seasons, Garber gave up three touchdowns. The longest play he gave up was only 45 yards but he gave up four plays of over 35 yards in his final season. Generally, he hasn’t been someone who has let receivers get behind him on deep throws, though. Ball Skills With nine passes defensed and two interceptions, including a pick-six, Garber has flashed some abilities to make plays on the ball with good timing and the ability to knock the ball out before a receiver can secure the catch. Garber was only targeted 11 times in four seasons but didn’t have a dropped pass as a wide receiver. However, he doesn’t have a big catch radius to get his hands on the ball. Tackling Garber only had six missed tackles in each of his seasons as a full-time cornerback but he wasn’t a particularly productive tackler so his missed tackle rate was higher than you’d ideally like to see. Even on plays he makes, he displays rawness as a tackler, often diving in low or throwing a shoulder recklessly at the ball carrier. He did not force any fumbles in his college career. Run Defense Garber has been rated as below average in run defense on analysis sites such as Pro Football Focus. Since he played on the outside, he barely contributed in this role. In his two seasons as a full-time cornerback he had eight tackles and six missed tackles in the running game. Only two of those tackles were near the line of scrimmage. Blitzing It was extremely rare for Garber to blitz from the outside cornerback position and he didn’t register a sack in his college career, although he did have one pressure. Special Teams Garber was on the field goal defense and saw some time as a vice and as a punt gunner in college, but didn’t have a great deal of production as he had just one special teams tackle. He did have one highlight, though, returning this extra point 91 yards for a score. Physicality Garber only had seven penalties in his college career but was called for defensive pass interference twice and defensive holding once in 2024. He can also be outmuscled at the catch point from time to time. Instincts Playing on the other side of the ball may have helped Garber in terms of being able to read offensive formations or anticipate the receiver’s routes. He also displayed good play recognition on the best play from his Jets debut, as he reacted well for this stop in the flat. He was an academic all-Big 12 selection in 2024. Attitude/Demeanor Garber showed a good team-first attitude when he converted from wide receiver to cornerback. No doubt frustrated at not getting any opportunities on offense, it was Garber himself who approached coaches with the idea of converting. Injuries Injuries haven’t affected Garber during his collegiate career. He played in 59 games in total, including 58 over his last five years. Scheme Fit As noted, Garber is an outside cornerback, and that’s where he played – with the third unit – in his preseason debut. He may be considered more of a developmental piece though. He was a teammate of current Jets safety VJ Payne at Kansas State. Conclusions Garber acquitted himself well enough in his first preseason appearance but the Jets have a few cornerbacks not currently playing who are clearly going to be on the final roster so there is no realistic chance of him making the team. If he has another solid performance against the Giants, then perhaps Garber will have convinced the coaching staff that he’s got some potential and could continue to develop on the practice squad or if he is re-signed before camp next season. The latter option, giving him a chance to play in the UFL this spring, could be a viable path to getting back into camp with the Jets or another team a year from now.

title: Nate Lynn: More Than Your Typical Camp Standout?
summary: Anyone who has followed the Jets at any sort of detailed level over the years knows they have seen their fair share of preseason standouts. For the most part, these players don’t work out. For every Wayne Chrebet, there have been countless guys who Jets fans have gotten excited about, only for them to never […]
full_text: Aug 21, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; New York Jets defensive tend Nate Lynn celebrates with New York Jets defensive end Paschal Ekeji (54) after sacking Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Drew Allar during the fourth quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Anyone who has followed the Jets at any sort of detailed level over the years knows they have seen their fair share of preseason standouts. For the most part, these players don’t work out. For every Wayne Chrebet, there have been countless guys who Jets fans have gotten excited about, only for them to never make much of an impact at the NFL level. Zach Sudfeld, Rontez Miles, Chris Streveler, Ryan Spadola, Clyde Gates…well, you get the point. Preseason normally doesn’t tell us much, and unfortunately, beating up on a bunch of backups and fringe roster players doesn’t necessarily translate to making valuable contributions during the regular season. However, what if I told you there was a player on the 2026 Jets who might actually be able to make an impact going forward because of his intriguing profile and history? Listen, listen. I know how this sounds. I just gave you a complete warning about why you cannot delude yourself into buying into positive preseason performances. I’m always reminded of Tobias Fünke’s hilarious line from Arrested Development whenever I start talking myself into one of these guys: That pretty much sums it up. It never works. Or, at least, it hardly ever works in NFL terms. But as fans, we delude ourselves into thinking there’s a chance. This year, my guy is Nate Lynn. Lynn is a recent acquisition who stood out in the Jets’ preseason opener last week. And while it would be incredibly premature to suggest he’s going to become some sort of impact player (or even make the team), there are enough things about his background and profile to make me at least a little more interested than I normally would be in a preseason standout. Let’s take a look at Lynn’s history and why there might be something here. Background Lynn is a 24-year-old edge rusher entering his third season in the NFL. He originally came into the league as an undrafted free agent in 2024 after a strong collegiate career at William & Mary. Known for his versatility, Lynn played all over the defensive line in college, often moving inside despite weighing around 255 pounds. That versatility was a big part of what made him interesting. He had impressive speed for someone who spent so much time lined up around the B-gap, although his testing numbers were much more modest when viewed strictly through the lens of a stand-up edge rusher. Still, Lynn evidently did enough to impress then-Lions general manager Brad Holmes and defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn. After a solid offseason and training camp, Lynn’s rookie season was unfortunately cut short in his very first preseason game against the Giants. He suffered a torn ligament in his shoulder, which was particularly discouraging considering he had already flashed with a sack in the game. Lynn spent the entire 2024 season on injured reserve. Then came 2025. Once again, Lynn generated buzz throughout the offseason, with Brad Holmes publicly describing him as “impressive.” And his preseason performance backed that up. In four preseason games (the Lions played in the Hall of Fame Game) Lynn accumulated 10 total pressures and a sack. Those 10 pressures ranked among the top three of all edge rushers that preseason, while his PFF grade and pass-rush win rate were both in the 99th percentile among qualified pass rushers. Despite all of that, Lynn was cut. That came as somewhat of a surprise. A quick look at the Lions 53-man roster projections from beat writers that summer shows that Lynn was generally expected to make the team. The overall sentiment seemed to be that he had done enough to stick around. Instead, he ended up signing with the Titans’ practice squad. Then came another regime change, and Robert Saleh ultimately opted not to keep him around. That brings us to the Jets. So, What Do We Make of Him? Lynn has played just one preseason game with the Jets, but he immediately looked like one of the best players on the field, even if he was doing it against backups. He finished with two sacks against the Steelers and was the Jets’ second-highest graded defensive player in the game. One of those sacks came against Steelers starting tackle Broderick Jones. Obviously, none of this means Lynn is suddenly going to become a star. If anything, he might still be more likely not to make the Jets’ 53-man roster. That’s the reality of being an undersized, relatively unproven edge rusher who has bounced around the league. The intriguing part though, is Lynn has now produced in essentially every preseason setting in which he’s been given an opportunity. In 2025, he was one of the most productive pass rushers in the entire preseason and still couldn’t crack the Lions’ roster. Now, a year later, he has joined another team and immediately flashed again. Maybe this is just another case of a guy dominating against players who won’t be on NFL rosters in a few weeks. There are certainly plenty of reasons to believe that. But unlike some of the classic Jets preseason stars we’ve fallen in love with over the years, Lynn at least has a track record that makes me a little more interested. He has collegiate production, legitimate versatility, and he has already flashed on multiple occasions in preseasons. Now he has one more preseason game to make his case. He’s got a lot to play for tonight. And I’ll be rooting for him.

title: Philadelphia Eagles 53-man roster prediction: Final edition
summary: Now that the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason schedule is over, the team’s focus shifts to cutting their roster down to the regular season 53-player limit before the 6:00 PM Eastern deadline on Sunday, August 30. Here’s our best effort at projecting what the INITIAL roster is going to look like. The Birds will likely make some […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Uar Bernard #93 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts against the New England Patriots during an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason schedule is over, the team’s focus shifts to cutting their roster down to the regular season 53-player limit before the 6:00 PM Eastern deadline on Sunday, August 30. Here’s our best effort at projecting what the INITIAL roster is going to look like. The Birds will likely make some tweaks (injured reserve placements, trades, waiver claims, etc.) before they actually play the Washington Commanders in Week 1. Note that this activity is about predicting what the Eagles WILL do as opposed to what we necessarily think they should do. OFFENSE QUARTERBACK: Jalen Hurts, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton (3) [3] Hurts threw a lot of interceptions this summer, yes, but I challenge you to find a daily practice observer who feels like he had a bad camp. On the whole, the good outweighed the bad. It seems like he’s embracing the new offensive direction. The Eagles are hoping Hurts doesn’t get, well, hurt … because the depth behind him is very uninspiring. There was no clear winner from the Eagles’ training camp backup quarterback battle. McKee somehow looked worse than ever after previously showing encouraging signs in previous years. Dalton looks somewhat physically diminished, which tracks for a quarterback entering his age 39 season. Maybe he gets traded … but what price is he even fetching at this point? I wonder if the Eagles might trade both Dalton (for very meager draft pick compensation) AND McKee (included in a deal for another team’s quarterback, such as Anthony Richardson or J.J. McCarthy)? Payton has shown some promise but the Eagles didn’t really do a good job of getting him more action in the preseason. Utilizing him on special teams in the final preseason game points to them trying to find a role for him. This is a tough position to figure out. OUT: Andy Dalton RUNNING BACK: Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley (3) [6] Barkley looks poised for another big season and he might actually be involved as a pass-catcher more than ever this year, no, for real, I mean it this time?! Bigsby’s role is obviously limited with Barkley blocking his path to playing time but he’s simply too good to be a total afterthought in this offense. Shipley finished training camp strong and did enough to earn his RB3 role, which was evident by the team resting him in the third preseason game. Carson Steele was basically the entire Eagles’ passing offense in the preseason but I don’t think they need to keep him on the roster; he spent all of last year on the Kansas City Chiefs’ practice squad. Dameon Pierce looked good early in camp, got hurt and missed a lot of time, and then looked good upon returning … before maybe getting banged up again? Steele and/or Pierce will be on the practice squad. Jordan Mims was recently added to the roster to help fill practice reps/preseason snaps. OUT: Carson Steele, Dameon Pierce, Jordan Mims WIDE RECEIVER: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore (6) [12] As the Eagles’ undisputed top receiving option, Smitty is going to have his first career Pro Bowl season. There’s every reason to believe in him. In a more perfect world, Wicks might ideally be WR3 … but he’s clearly WR2 in this configuration. Hurts was not scared to throw to him over and over while Smitty and Lemon missed most of camp. Lemon doesn’t look ready to be a starting receiver in Week 1 after missing most of the Eagles’ offseason practices but it seems like they’re going to try to make it work anyway. Brown didn’t have a great summer and Hurts threw a number of interceptions when the ball went his way … but his guaranteed money signals the Eagles holding onto him, unless he exits in a trade. The Eagles do seem to value Brown’s deep threat ability. Cooper proved that he deserves playing time on offense but it remains to be seen if the Eagles will actually give it to him. Moore is firmly on the bubble and I could see the Eagles cutting him since he’s a vested veteran who could be brought back on the practice squad. But the coaching staff has spoken favorably of Moore and he’s had a good summer and Hurts has thrown to him a lot. Plus, with Lemon looking a bit shaky, the Eagles could afford to go heavier here. Britain Covey is a contender to be temporarily elevated from the practice squad to help out at punt returner. OUT: Britain Covey, Quez Watkins, Danny Gray, Samori Toure, Erik Ezukanma, Tahj Washington IR: Johnny Wilson TIGHT END: Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Grant Calcaterra, Cameron Latu (4) [16] Goedert is the Eagles’ top tight end, which is fine-to-good. The depth behind him is not great. Mundt has built a reputation as much more of a blocker than a pass-catcher. He’s consistently been TE2 in the Eagles’ 12 personnel packages. Calcaterra is currently dealing with a back injury and the severity is unclear. I wouldn’t keep him and I know Eagles fans won’t want to see him on the roster. But I think the team likes him more than you do. Latu is a special teams standout. E.J. Jenkins and/or Stone Smartt are practice squad considerations. I have Eli Stowers, who is currently dealing with a hamstring injury, beginning the season on injured reserve/designated to return. He’ll be required to miss four games before being eligible to return. Using this mechanism also avoids the likelihood of him being a healthy scratch, at least early in the season. Stowers showed nothing this offseason to suggest that he’s ready to significantly contribute in 2026. OUT: E.J. Jenkins, Stone Smartt IR (DESIGNATED FOR RETURN): Eli Stowers OFFENSIVE LINE: Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen, Lane Johnson, Markel Bell, Drew Kendall, Willie Lampkin, Micah Morris, Cameron Williams (10) [26] The starting offensive line is set. Dickerson appears to be less than 100% physically, which is something to monitor this season. By contrast, Jurgens looks healthier than he did in 2025. Steen looks like he’s better than he was last year. Johnson is entering his final NFL season, according to him (though there’s plenty of time for him to change his mind). Bell is currently banged up and the severity of his injury is unclear, so, maybe the Eagles need to keep Fred Johnson. But we have Big Fred off because he’s had a bad summer and he could be brought back on the practice squad; we’ve already seen that the league doesn’t really value him. Also, Bell has looked good and deserves to be the swing tackle. Kendall has emerged as this year’s Brett Toth, meaning that he’s poised to be the top interior backup. Lampkin earned his roster spot by having an impressive offseason; he could be active as the eight offensive lineman on game day. Morris showed developmental potential and the Eagles might not be ready to give up on the 22-year-old Williams. Jake Majors is a strong practice squad contender and John Ojukwu might return in that capacity as well. Myles Hinton played his way out of practice squad contention and Jeff Stoutland, who seemed to be high on him, is no longer around. The Eagles don’t need Michael Jordan now that the Sixers have LeBron James. OUT: Fred Johnson, Michael Jordan, Jake Majors, John Ojukwu, Myles Hinton, Zeke Correll DEFENSE EDGE RUSHER: Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, A.J. Epenesa, Arnold Ebiketie, Josh Weru (6) [32] There’s concern that Greenard won’t be ready for Week 1 but the Eagles might have hope he can at least return by Week 4, which would justify not having him begin the season on the reserve/PUP list. But I wouldn’t fault the team for keeping him on PUP in an effort not to rush him back and instead try their best to get him right. Hunt was the star of the summer for the Eagles; he looks ready to…

title: Eagles vs. Bengals preseason game: 7 winners, 6 losers, and 8 IDKs
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles lost to the Cincinnati Bengals in their preseason finale on Friday night. Final score, which doesn’t matter, but we’re logging it here anyway: 30 to 13. The Eagles’ final preseason record, which also doesn’t matter, but we’re logging it here anyway: 0-3. Time to hand out some winners, losers, and I don’t […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals linebacker Antwaun Powell-Ryland (56) reaches for Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee (16) in the first quarter of the NFL Preseason Week 3 game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field in Philladelphia on Friday, Aug. 28, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Philadelphia Eagles lost to the Cincinnati Bengals in their preseason finale on Friday night. Final score, which doesn’t matter, but we’re logging it here anyway: 30 to 13. The Eagles’ final preseason record, which also doesn’t matter, but we’re logging it here anyway: 0-3. Time to hand out some winners, losers, and I don’t knows ahead of the team making roster cuts from 90 players down to 53 before 6:00 PM Eastern on Sunday, August 30.‘ WINNERS DARIUS COOPER The Eagles rested him. He’s on the roster. The question is: how many snaps will he play on offense, if any at all? WILLIE LAMPKIN The Eagles also notably rested him, though he’s also been banged up a bit recently with a stinger. Regardless, he’s on the roster. CARSON STEELE Steele finished the preseason as the Eagles’ leading receiver and it wasn’t close: Eagles 2026 preseason receiving leaders RB Carson Steele: 14 recs, 136 yards, 2 TD WR Darius Cooper: 5 recs, 65 yards TE Stone Smartt: 7 recs, 47 yards WR Britain Covey: 5 recs, 44 yards, 1 TD — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) August 29, 2026 Meanwhile, his 21 rushing attempts produced just 59 rushing yards (2.8 average). The Eagles might not keep him on the roster since, at best, he would be RB4 behind Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley (who was among the rested players tonight). But Steele has made a case for himself and perhaps the Eagles envision using him in a fullback role. If he doesn’t stick in Philly, Steele shouldn’t struggle to find a landing spot in some capacity with a different NFL team. JAKE ELLIOTT After attempting zero field goals through the Eagles’ first two preseason games, Elliott made kicks from 45 and 56 yards out on Friday night. Good to see. Elliott’s had a good summer: Jake Elliott's kicks this summer: 28/31 in training camp 7/7 in preseason games 35/38 overall — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) August 29, 2026 Then again, he also did last year before struggling in the regular season. KEYSHAWN JAMES-NEWBY KJN missed most of the Eagles’ offseason practices due to injury. But their final pick from the 2026 NFL Draft followed up a good moment in practice earlier this week with a sack in this game by chasing down Josh Johnson from behind. He’s earned practice squad consideration. ZION WILSON Wilson popped in every preseason game this summer. He logged a TFL and a QB hit on Friday night. The Eagles may have found a diamond in the rough here with a player whom originally intended on playing college football in 2026 before being ruled ineligible . Good developmental option for the practice squad. JORDAN MIMS Totally forgot the Eagles signed him earlier this week . He has no chance to make the team but he did have a nice punch out for a forced fumble on kickoff coverage. LOSERS MAKAI LEMON Five targets, three receptions, three yards, one drop that went through his hands for an interception, and a muffed punt. Not exactly the most encouraging NFL debut by the Eagles’ 2026 first-round pick. Tough debut for Makai Lemon so far. 4 targets, 2 recs, 2 yards … and a dropped pass that caused an interception. pic.twitter.com/rImEbkC4Zj — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) August 29, 2026 I wrote more about Lemon and his outlook here . THE ARCHITECT(S) OF THE EAGLES’ BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE Training camp competitions are designed to bring out the best from players battling for a given job. “Iron sharpens iron!” Well, not in this case. I think the Eagles splitting QB2 reps between Tanner McKee and Andy Dalton did neither of them any favors. Maybe it wouldn’t have actually made a difference if one of the two took all the second-team reps. Maybe they’re just not very good players at this point and it is what it is. Still, I struggle to feel like the Eagles handled this situation well. I think their approach may have undermined McKee’s confidence. I just refuse to believe he was merely this bad all along. We’ve previously seen him look much better than he has this offseason! And specifically against the Bengals last summer! It’s just weird to me how much worse McKee looks now. Anyway, the Eagles better hope Jalen Hurts doesn’t get hurt, because neither McKee nor Dalton are inspiring much confidence. It makes me wonder if Eagles QB2 might be behind door No. 3 … Eagles QB2 preseason numbers Tanner McKee 34/54 (62.9%), 263 (4.9 y/a), 2 TD, 1 INT, 79.5 passer rating Andy Dalton 18/35 (51.4%), 168 yards (4.8 y/a), 1 TD, 0 INT, 74.5 passer rating — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) August 29, 2026 TANNER MCKEE He was inaccurate. He held the ball too long. He wasn’t helped by Lemon’s drop that turned into an interception. But he hardly did enough to help himself. McKee’s worst miss came when he overthrew an open Britain Covey for what should’ve been a touchdown. MAC MCWILLIAMS McWilliams has looked better in practice than he has in preseason games this summer. He got beat multiple times on Friday night. AMBRY THOMAS The veteran cornerback was roasted and committed multiple penalties. BASICALLY THE ENTIRE EAGLES’ DEFENSE ON THIS PLAY In the running for the worst tackling I’ve ever seen. Haynes to the house. #CINatPHI on CBS/Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/SpGkzLiQHs — Cincinnati Bengals (@Bengals) August 29, 2026 I DON’T KNOWS SEAN MANNION For the second week in a row, the Eagles’ offensive coordinator called plays from the booth … and not the sideline, like he did in the first preseason game. Unlike last week and much more like their first preseason game, however, the Eagles’ offense was pretty bad. They ultimately (s)logged 210 total yards at 3.6 yards per play. I’m not here to crush Mannion; we all know the vanilla play-calling and (almost) no starters caveats apply. We’ll soon get a better read on him when the real games start. ANDY DALTON Dalton had better numbers than McKee on Friday night, which isn’t really saying much. And he still looked far from great. Maybe the Eagles feel like he’s done enough to be QB2? I don’t know. COLE PAYTON Payton showed some promise in the Eagles’ first preseason game but he only logged three pass attempts in their final two preseason games. Does he make the team ? I lean towards putting him on. Seems like a good sign for his stock that the Eagles were experimenting with using him on special teams coverage units in this game. But I don’t know that he’s a lock by any means. DAMEON PIERCE Pierce looked good early in training camp. Then he suffered a hamstring injury that caused him to miss most of the summer. He’s looked good in practice since returning and he also had four carries for 44 yards on Friday night. He clearly has some juice. But he did also drop two passes, albeit one thrown low to him. And he also paid a visit to the medical tent. Early in camp, it looked like Pierce might challenge for the RB3 role. Early in this game, I felt like he was building a case for RB4 consideration, likely while occupying a practice squad spot. But between him getting hurt (?) again and Steele having another good night, I don’t know where Pierce stands. ANDRE’ SAM Sam had an active night (multiple tackles, two fumble recoveries, a dropped gift of an interception that counted as a pass breakup) before ultimately being carted off the field. That’s a shame. While the 27-year-old’s limitations probably would’ve prevented him from making the roster, he would have been a good practice squad option to keep around. Especially with the Eagles being relatively thin at safety. As of me typing this sentence, I don’t know the specifics about his injury … but it doesn’t seem good. KAPENA GUSHIKEN The Gush had some good moments on special teams but he struggled with missed tackles…

title: Makai Lemon’s NFL debut could have gone better
summary: Makai Lemon was the sole projected 2026 starter who suited up to play in the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals on Friday night. It was a sensible decision. Lemon missed half of the Eagles’ spring practices and the majority of training camp with the same hamstring injury. The team didn’t want his […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up before the game against Cincinnati Bengals in a preseason game at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Makai Lemon was the sole projected 2026 starter who suited up to play in the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals on Friday night. It was a sensible decision. Lemon missed half of the Eagles’ spring practices and the majority of training camp with the same hamstring injury. The team didn’t want his first NFL game action to come against the Washington Commanders in Week 1. With Lemon not exactly popping during the limited practices he has participated in, it would’ve been encouraging to see some positive signs from him in this game. Unfortunately, that wasn’t the case. Lemon finished his first professional football game with five targets that resulted in three catches for three yards. He had a pass go through his hands for an interception and he muffed a punt that he fielded off of multiple bounces before ultimately recovering possession. Tough debut for Makai Lemon so far. 4 targets, 2 recs, 2 yards … and a dropped pass that caused an interception. pic.twitter.com/rImEbkC4Zj — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) August 29, 2026 To his credit, Lemon took accountability for the turnover after the game: Makai Lemon on the interception that went off his hands: “It was a drop. It went through my hands. I gotta catch that.” #Eagles pic.twitter.com/Tjiam2ozSn — EJ Smith (@EJSmith94) August 29, 2026 Lemon wasn’t exactly done any favors by Tanner McKee, who largely struggled. McKee threw short of the rookie on the first target of the game. The backup quarterback also probably could’ve placed the pass in the following video better, though Lemon also didn’t exactly generate much separation here: Makai Lemon's second target of the night: pic.twitter.com/FOctqjIVmA — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) August 29, 2026 It goes without saying that it’s entirely too early to write the book on Lemon’s career. But I do think it’s fair to raise questions about his readiness to contribute early on as a rookie. There was a play in this game where Lemon ran into Elijah Moore. There was a rep in practice this week where Lemon didn’t know he was supposed to be on the field. Based on what I’ve seen this summer, Darius Cooper and Moore currently inspire more confidence as WR3 options than Lemon does. If beating Washington is the top priority, one of them should be starting alongside DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks in 15 days from now. But I don’t think that deployment is necessarily likely. Lemon has been working with the starters since returning from injury. And the Eagles have been making an effort to force feed him touches, albeit to not much success in practice. Perhaps patience with Lemon will pay off and any short-term struggles will subside as he improves over the course of his rookie season. I’m sure many will be quick to compare his path to Cooper DeJean, who also missed a lot of time in training camp before struggling in the Eagles’ preseason finale in 2024. A few things about that comparison: DeJean is pretty great player who is probably more of the exception than the norm. It wasn’t until Week 6 that the coaching staff trusted DeJean to see regular playing time that year. DeJean’s layoff may have been less detrimental than it is for a rookie receiver missing out on time to build chemistry with his quarterback. Maybe one day we’ll look back at this Lemon performance and laugh that there was any concern about his outlook. Until we see more from him, though, I think it’s fair to have some reservations. Especially since the Eagles kind of need him to be ready to have a meaningful role in this offense sooner than later.

title: 10 fascinating Eagles questions as training camp ends
summary: Fantasy football drafts have been set. The preseason games are almost over. Training camp is done. Yep, the 2026 NFL season is nearly here, and your Philadelphia Eagles are once again a contender. Are they the favorites to get back to the Super Bowl and/or win it? Nope. But that’s OK. It’s always better to […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - AUGUST 15: Jihaad Campbell #11 of the Philadelphia Eagles lines up before the snap during an NFL preseason football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fantasy football drafts have been set. The preseason games are almost over. Training camp is done. Yep, the 2026 NFL season is nearly here, and your Philadelphia Eagles are once again a contender. Are they the favorites to get back to the Super Bowl and/or win it? Nope. But that’s OK. It’s always better to fly under the radar. We do know that this Eagles roster is stacked with really good players, particularly on the defensive side of the ball, featuring a potential top-five unit. Offensively, there are questions, and there will be struggles. But it was time for this scheme to evolve, so it’s fun anticipating what it all may look like once the regular season begins. Still, there are a number of questions as yet unanswered as training camp winds down. Here are 10 of the more fascinating ones. 1) Who is the backup QB? Or perhaps an even more fascinating question… “Is the Eagles’ backup QB for 2026 currently on the roster?” The “battle” between incumbent No. 2 Tanner McKee and veteran ginger Andy Dalton has not been a scintillating one. Dalton appeared to be getting more run as Jalen Hurts’ backup this summer, but McKee appeared to outplay him during his more limited action. Neither QB bathed themselves in glory though, and given the fact Dalton appeared to be the front-runner for most of training camp, it’s fair to wonder how much faith the organization has lost in McKee following his lackluster performance in Week 18 last season. In an ideal scenario, one of these players will be traded after the team’s final preseason game. I would keep McKee over Dalton. There’s more upside there. But if Howie Roseman doesn’t feel good about either player, perhaps a long-rumored trade for Minnesota’s J.J. McCarthy or Indianapolis’ Anthony Richardson will come to fruition. 2) Can Saquon Barkley lead your fantasy team’s RBs? Last year, I picked Barkley No. 2 overall in my fantasy draft. I finished in 11th place in a 12-team league. The two were related. No one expected Barkley to repeat his 2,005 yard performance from 2024, but a drop from 125.3 yards per game to 71.3 wasn’t on anyone’s bingo card. The offensive line was banged up all year and the playcalling and scheme did no one any favors, either. So we’re all curious to see how Barkley will do in a Sean Mannion offense with a healthy offensive line. If you draft Barkley as your RB1, are you doomed to failure like I was a year ago? 3) Which receiver finishes with the 2nd-most yards? Barring a disaster (or a breakout performance, I suppose), DeVonta Smith is going to be this team’s leader in receiving yards. But who will be No. 2? The Ringer’s Philly Special spent the last couple of podcasts asking this question and it made me want to weigh in, too. Based on the preseason, it would appear Dontayvion Wicks is the most likely answer. He looked elusive and quick and is familiar with Mannion and what he’s likely to do. He’s also likely to get a lot of snaps, probably as the team’s slot receiver to start. Makai Lemon will enter the season as the No. 2, but he missed most of the summer with a hamstring injury. Will he be able to ramp it up and develop enough chemistry with Hurts in a short amount of time to emerge as the team’s second-leading receiver? Rookie receivers rarely have that kind of immediate immpact. And what about camp superstar Darius Cooper? Is he capable of making a “leap?” And don’t forget tight end Dallas Goedert, who made 15 starts for the first time in his NFL career a season ago, finishing with 591 yards and a career-high 11 TDs. How will Mannion’s offense affect his productivity? Health will be a major factor. My money is on Wicks. 4) How many starts does Markel Bell make? The rookie third-round pick has been one of the most impressive new players in camp this year and it sure does look like the team has found its eventual Lane Johnson replacement. For 2026, he’ll enter the season as the team’s swing tackle, and while I’m optimistic about the health of Lane Johnson and Jordan Mailata, I say that every year. And every year, one of the tackles misses time. I think we have to pencil Bell in for at least two starts at one of the tackle spots, and if Johnson or Mailata is out for longer, he’s going to be the guy to get those reps, not veteran Fred Johnson. I’m excited to see more of Bell, but hopefully it doesn’t come this year at the expense of either of the team’s Pro Bowl offensive tackles. 5) Is the Eagles’ No. 2 TE currently on the roster? Goedert will be the starter, but he’s also an injury-prone, 31-year-old tight end. The team drafted Eli Stowers in the second round of the draft hoping he’d be TE2, but his well-documented summer struggles have torpedoed those chances. Right now, run-blocking specialist Johnny Mundt is the No. 2, and if Goedert were to go down, there would be absolutely zero pass-catching options at the tight end position. In a recent Philly Voice post , Jimmy Kempski noted the Rams appear to have a few too many tight ends on the roster and that one of them could be had in a trade, with Davis Allen mentioned as the most obvious candidate. Earlier in the off-season, former Eagle-turned-Cardinal-turned-Commander Zach Ertz expressed a desire to return to Philadelphia. He has recovered from a devastating knee injury at the end of 2024 and believes he can still play. Other names in the ether, more likely to be dealt at the trade deadline, are Carolina’s Ja’Tavion Sanders, Denver’s Evan Engram and Atlanta’s Kyle Pitts. 6) When will Jonathan Greenard be back? The Eagles’ biggest off-season acquisition has missed the entire summer with a pec injury that landed him on the PUP list, and NFL insider Adam Schefter said this week he’s unlikely to play in Week 1. ESPN's @AdamSchefter Doesn't Think Jonathan Greenard Will Play Week 1 #FlyEaglesFly | @asalciunas975 🎙️ 📸 Mitchell Leff/Getty Images pic.twitter.com/Mi5pA7488R — 97.5 The Fanatic (@975TheFanatic) August 26, 2026 Thankfully, the Eagles are pretty deep on the defensive line, but edge rusher was an area of uncertainty as the off-season began and, without Greenard, they’re lacking one big pass rusher. Also, how long will it take Greenard to get into game shape and perform at his normal levels of production when he does return? Greenard should not return until he’s fully healthy, even if he misses the first month. No one wants him to come back too soon and play at a sub-optimal level, like we saw with Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson a year ago. 7) Who will lead the Eagles in sacks? Jalyx Hunt had perhaps the best training camp of anyone on the roster and, with Greenard hurting, he could be the guy. But he’s not the only candidate. Nolan Smith is finally healthy to start the season and is looking to have a big campaign in the final year of his rookie deal. And on the inside, Jalen Carter, with a big-money contract extension tucked under his very large arms, looks exceedingly good right now, too. It’s harder for tackles to pile up as many sacks as edge rushers, but Carter’s immense talent automatically makes him a possible exception to that rule. My money is on Hunt, with Greenard piling up some sacks late in the season once he returns. 8) Are we sleeping on Jihaad Campbell? The talk this summer has been centered on the emergence of Jeremiah Trotter, Jr. as a starting-caliber linebacker in the NFL. That’s a wonderful development and a fantastic legacy story, but are we sleeping on Campbell? Remember, Campbell was a first round pick and had all the hype in the world at this time last year. Opposing players were cursing that the Eagles had landed a player with the kind of potential impact Campbell has. He understandably moved to the bench last season when…
