title: Eagles News: Time to bring Zach Ertz back?
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Observations: Can Howie Roseman keep Uar Bernard and Josh Weru on the 53? – NBCSPWOULD HOWIE CONSIDER BRINGING BACK THIS FORMER EAGLE? We know Howie Roseman loves bringing former Eagles back to Philly. He does it all the time (Marcus Epps, C.J. Gardner-Johnson, Vinny […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 26: Zach Ertz #86 of the Washington Commanders leaps with the football during the fourth quarter in the NFC Championship Game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on January 26, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Observations: Can Howie Roseman keep Uar Bernard and Josh Weru on the 53? – NBCSP WOULD HOWIE CONSIDER BRINGING BACK THIS FORMER EAGLE? We know Howie Roseman loves bringing former Eagles back to Philly. He does it all the time (Marcus Epps, C.J. Gardner-Johnson, Vinny Curry, Nick Foles, Jordan Howard, DeSean Jackson, Jordan Matthews, many others). We also know that with Eli Stowers struggling this preseason Roseman could be in the market for a second receiving tight end who could be an upgrade over Grant Calcaterra or E.J. Jenkins. Here’s an idea: Zach Ertz. Ertz is reportedly healthy after tearing his right ACL in the Commanders’ loss to the Vikings in Minneapolis last December. Ertz is 35, but he can still play. We saw him catch 11 balls for 104 yards in the 2024 NFC Championship Game and last year before he got hurt he was in the top 10 among all tight ends in catches and yards and on pace for 65 catches and 659 yards. He played with Jalen Hurts in 2020 and the first half of 2021, before he was traded to Arizona, so he’s got some chemistry with the quarterback. Ertz has made over $80 million in his 13-year career, so he won’t be looking for a big payday. He’s a class act and still has strong ties with Philly through his Ertz Family Foundation. One side note to this: Ertz is fifth all-time among tight ends with 825 catches and only needs 11 receptions to break Harold Carmichael’s franchise record of 589 receptions, and when he was traded back in 2021 he said he’d love to come back one day and finish his career here. Probably unlikely but ya never know. Eagles 53-man roster prediction: How tough decisions at wide receiver, tight end and D-line will shake out – Inquirer Tight end has overtaken safety as the most likely area Roseman might address via trade or by some other means. The Eagles were probably expecting Stowers to need time, especially when it came to blocking. But he rarely practiced with Hurts, if at all, and recently suffered a setback with his hamstring. Redshirting the second-rounder would set off alarms, so it’s unlikely Roseman takes that route. But a swap — or signing a veteran like Zach Ertz off the street — would also speak volumes. Goedert is still a competent “Y” receiver, while Mundt will shoulder some of the “F” blocking responsibilities. But tight ends often need to be dual-purpose within Sean Mannion’s new Kyle Shanahan-style scheme and neither is as competent in the opposite discipline. If Stowers isn’t healthy by the opener, or is unable to contribute on special teams in the early going, Latu seems the likely fourth option. He can also fill the fullback role if Mannion adds that wrinkle to the offense. The first “per sources” in the history of the @LockedOnBirds squad show dropped today by @MarcFarzetta 👀 Zach Ertz would love to return to the #Eagles in 2026 and thought it was likely not happening when they drafted Eli Stowers Could it happen now that Stowers is struggling? https://t.co/hpGjrqUIGJ pic.twitter.com/RTdLdmrxBI — Louie DiBiase (@DiBiaseLOE) August 27, 2026 Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Some hints for the final preseason game? – BGN Wednesday marked the seventeenth and final Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! PHLY Adds Two-Time Super Bowl Champion Brandon Graham Back To Roster Ahead Of 2026 Season – Barrett Media What We Know: Brandon Graham will appear regularly on PHLY’s Eagles postgame coverage. The Super Bowl-winning defensive end retired after a 15-year Eagles career defined by his signature strip-sack in Super Bowl LII. His podcast, Unblocked, returns September 9. PHLY also added two new Eagles contributors: Brandon Lee Gowton, founder of Bleeding Green Nation, and Miles Johnson, known for Real Talk with MJ. Both join returning voices Bo Wulf, EJ Smith, and Fran Duffy across pre- and postgame programming. 10 players to watch in the Eagles’ final preseason game vs. the Bengals – PhillyVoice iDL Uar Bernard and EDGE Joshua Weru: In the Patriots game, Weru dusted a Pats OT with a highly athletic Eurostep move, and Bernard made a couple of nice run stops. I have both Eagles “exchange dudes” on the initial 53-man roster after they proved throughout camp and in the preseason games that they have enticing traits that are worth developing over time. They’ll get one last chance to play in an NFL game this season before they’re buried on the depth chart during the regular season. How every 2026 NFL draft pick has looked in the preseason – ESPN Round 2 (No. 54): Eli Stowers, TE. It has been a slow start for Stowers. He has worked primarily with the second and third teams and hasn’t had many eye-catching moments in camp. Stowers needs to develop as a blocker, and while he has the mentality to do so by all accounts, it’s going to take time. He suffered a hamstring injury in the second preseason game against the Patriots. Round 3 (No. 68): Markel Bell, OT. Bell has been the best Eagles rookie this summer, looking smooth in pass protection while creating lanes in the run game. He is in position to serve as the swing tackle and might be Lane Johnson’s eventual replacement at right tackle. Eagles-Bengals week: 6 burning questions, from grading Jalen Hurts to training camp MVP – The Athletic How would you grade Jalen Hurts’ training camp? Berman: By letter grade, I’ll give him a B/B-. He practiced three weeks without DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon, and any quarterback would look better with Smith. Hurts adjusted to the offense and embraced changes to footwork, cadence, operating under center, and throwing across the middle. Hurts calls it “sponge mode” this time of year. There’s something to be said about his willingness to embrace change at this point in his career. He made several high-level passes that Super Bowl MVPs and franchise quarterbacks make. But there were more inconsistencies than in previous summers, with inefficient practice. There were also far more interceptions. We’ll see what translates to games. I’ve also been impressed by his mobility and am curious how that factors into the offense this season. He’s had better camps in the past with A.J. Brown and Smith on the field. But Brown’s not here this season, so that point is moot. The key is keeping Smith (and Lemon) healthy. I’d be concerned about the passing game without him. As Eagles adopt more aggressive offense, Jalen Hurts ‘not afraid of making mistakes’ – Yahoo! Sports The Eagles believe their wide receiver room features versatility in the wake of trading A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots on June 1 for a 2028 first-round draft pick and 2027 fifth. Former Green Bay Packers receiver Dontayvion Wicks, 2026 first-round selection Makai Lemon and journeyman 2019 first-rounder Hollywood Brown join a room led by DeVonta Smith, who’s coming off his third 1,000-yard season in the last four years. “You have a No. 1 receiver in DeVonta Smith, who, we’ve always believed has been a No. 1 receiver,” Sirianni said. “You have a ‘Tay Wicks who I think has great qualities of a wide receiver: I always think that my ideal receiver in the NFL, before I look at speed and before I look at anything else, [has] play strength and body quickness [to get] in and out of the breaks. And this guy has elite of both.” Brown and Elijah Moore will be tabbed to add further speed while Darius Cooper will step up for “dirty work,” Sirianni said. summary: The Philadelphia Eagles will play their final preseason game of 2026 against the Bengals on Friday night at home in Lincoln Financial Field. full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 7: Darius Cooper #41 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs with the ball as he stiff arms Tycen Anderson #26 of the Cincinnati Bengals in the first half of the NFL Preseason 2025 game at Lincoln Financial Field on August 7, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles will play their final preseason game of 2026 against the Bengals on Friday night at home in Lincoln Financial Field. Several players are looking to put up performances impressive enough tonight to land one of the final roster spots. Teams have until 6pm ET on Sunday, August 30 to get their final roster down to 53 players and then start filling their practice squads. There’s a bit of an art to roster management, and while someone like Joshua Weru — who had never played football before, but has shown potential in the preseason — isn’t going to play right away, he’s also not someone the Eagles can risk losing on the waiver wire. This is where Howie Roseman has been exceptional, in terms of his plans to keep those at risk, waiting until other rosters are filled, and then making moves. It was a similar play last year for WR Darius Cooper, who was an attractive option for other teams, but showed the Eagles enough to hold on to him — and this year, he’s essentially a lock to be among the receiver rotation this season. Even for some of the depth players who are likely to make the roster, this final preseason game is another opportunity for reps and experience that they might not always get during the week at practice. title: Vote now for the 2026 Isaac Redman Award
summary: The time has finally come for Behind the Steel Curtain’s most prestigious tradition: The Isaac Redman Award. Now over a decade old (and with its own section on Wikipedia), the award, in the words of former BTSC editor Neal Coolong, is to be given to “the unheralded Steelers player who came from the furthest reaches […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - NOVEMBER 4: Running back Isaac Redman #33 of the Pittsburgh Steelers runs for a one yard touchdown against the New York Giants in the fourth quarter during an NFL game at MetLife Stadium on November 4, 2012 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Steelers defeated the Giants 24-20. (Photo by Rich Schultz /Getty Images) | Getty Images The time has finally come for Behind the Steel Curtain’s most prestigious tradition: The Isaac Redman Award. Now over a decade old (and with its own section on Wikipedia ), the award, in the words of former BTSC editor Neal Coolong, is to be given to “the unheralded Steelers player who came from the furthest reaches of obscurity to reach general heightened fame and appeal among Steelers fans.” As originally stated in that 2014 article, the basic rules are as follows: Eligibility Player must not be a draft pick higher than the sixth round Player can only have participated in two other training camps prior to this one Player demonstrated frequent references in comments regarding the likelihood of significant playing time in the coming year Weight of general fan sentiment leans towards the player being a “diamond in the rough” Player does not have to make the team in the year of his nomination to qualify (this isn’t meant to be included in 53-man roster discussion) Staff nominations Ryan Parish: This year, it was between two rookies for me: Gabe Rubio and Robert Spears-Jennings. Both impressed, but I’m going to give the nod to Rubio. In three games, the young nose tackle racked up six solo tackles and assisted on six others. He recorded five “Stops” which are plays PFF chart as tackles that produce a negative outcome for the offense. Rubio even managed two pressures the final preseason game against the Bills. There’s an argument that outside of Germie Bernard, he was the rookie with the most impressive preseason performance, which makes him the clear Redman winner on my ballot. Mike Nicastro: I’ll go off the grid a bit and give my nomination to Lew Nichols, who is a similar player to Isaac Redman in stature — he even won the award last year. Nichols just keeps on trucking. He led the team in rushing with 87 yards on 20 attempts – good for a 4.35 average. He also scored a touchdown and probably should have had another if he kept his balance on a great run in their first contest against the Packers. He isn’t going to necessarily be the belle of any ball, but he deserves some recognition, and possibly a roster spot, for his consistency and relentless approach. Jarrett Bailey : I’ll give mine to Robert Spears-Jennings. With the depth at safety (or lack thereof) being a big question, the seventh-round pick had a very strong summer in camp and in preseason play. He should get a spot on the 53-man roster. Joey Bray: It would be a shame if the Pittsburgh kid Eli Heidenreich didn’t get a nomination for the Redman Award. Steelers fans rejoiced when the Mt. Lebanon high school alumni was selected 240th overall back in April. Heidenreich’s middle name is versatility, playing wide receiver and running back in college. His awareness and ability in the open field makes him a serious big play threat and giving Mike McCarthy no shortage of ways to use him. The Steelers primarily used Heidenreich as a running back throughout the summer. After missing a few weeks in camp with a leg injury, his spot on the 53-man roster doesn’t seem to be a lock. Heidenreich played well in the Steelers preseason finale, scoring a touchdown and getting some run as a return man on special teams. “The Swiss Navy Knife” deserves a spot on the 53-man roster, and potentially a Redman Award victory. Ryland Bickley: While my vote will almost certainly go to one of Rubio or Spears-Jennings (please convince me which one), I’d be remiss if I didn’t get Will Howard onto this ballot as a former sixth-rounder who dominated preseason talking points even when his on-field performance didn’t always live up to the hype. Sure, Howard didn’t come from the depths of obscurity as a former National Championship-winning Ohio State quarterback, but he’s built up a fanbase worthy of Redman Award consideration, leading to discussion of the Steelers keeping a whopping four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster just to keep Howard from potentially being poached by another team. The point of this award is to recognize August storylines with a bit too much hype, and while Howard still has plenty of time to develop, I’m not sure if another player better encapsulates that sense of preseason overreaction than him. Other notable eligibles DB Devan Boykin DL Kevin Jobity Jr. TE Lake McRee WR Max Hurleman DB Doneiko Slaughter WR Brandon Smith OLB Julius Welschof LB Carson Bruener Vote! But enough of what the staff wants to say — this is your decision! Vote below in the poll, and if you want to write in an eligible candidate, recs on a comment stating a player’s candidacy will count as votes. The ballot will stay open through Saturday, with the winner announced before the cutdown deadline on Sunday. May the best Isaac Redman Award candidate win, joining a storied fraternity that includes the likes of Mike Hilton, Roosevelt Nix, and Tyler Matakevich. And make sure to fill the comment section with civil discourse election propaganda below.
author: Ryan Parish

title: The Morning After: Keeping four QBs is bad roster building
summary: The end of preseason has always been the unofficial beginning of fall in my eyes. As I stare out my window, I can see a hint of color becoming more prevalent in the trees, the sun is setting earlier with each passing day, and the pumpkin coffee I have sitting next to me tastes like […]
full_text: Aug 27, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Will Howard (18) looks to pass the ball against the Pittsburgh Steelers during the third quarter at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The end of preseason has always been the unofficial beginning of fall in my eyes. As I stare out my window, I can see a hint of color becoming more prevalent in the trees, the sun is setting earlier with each passing day, and the pumpkin coffee I have sitting next to me tastes like I’ll be turning on Halloween 6 later on in the day. The preseason is now complete for the Pittsburgh Steelers, and they will now have until Sunday night at 6:00 EST to trim their roster down to 53 players. And while the journey will end for many, it appears one player on the bubble has a spot secured. Plus, a pair of rookie receivers show exactly why they were drafted, and several defenders will make it very difficult to let them go. It’s the morning after game day. Let’s dive in. The Steelers should not keep four quarterbacks After the Steelers’ 28-27 loss to the Bills to close out the preseason, head coach Mike McCarthy was asked if all four quarterbacks did enough to secure a roster spot. “Very accurate evaluation on your part,” McCarthy said via Brooke Pryor. “We’ve got two vets to win with, and two guys we’re excited about their future.” Of course, nothing is official at the time of writing, but it certainly appears as if the Steelers will keep all four quarterbacks on their roster, which makes next to no sense. It would be one thing if Will Howard blew them away in exhibition play – he didn’t. He finished the preseason 26-of-40 with two touchdowns to three interceptions. For what it’s worth, both touchdowns he threw were a screen pass that Germie Bernard took 13 yards after making the first tackler miss, and practically a handoff to Lake McRee who dove over several players to get into the end zone. That’s not to see there weren’t good throws. The pass to Robert Tonyan on the goal line in Week 1 against the Packers was his best throw of the preseason, and he made a 16-yard completion to Ben Skowronek over the middle in Week 2. However, if he really popped, the Steelers wouldn’t feel the need to keep Mason Rudolph. Howard was comfortably the fourth-best quarterback for the Steelers throughout the summer. The logical decision would be to cut him and then sign him to the practice squad when no one claims him. Everyone in the Will Howard camp is so certain he would get claimed by another team, but that’s highly unlikely to happen. About 25-35 players total get claimed during roster cutdown. Last year, there were 29 players claimed. The year before that – 27, per Saad Yousuf of The Athletic . The high since 2015 is 44 players . The low is 17, which came back in 2020. Howard didn’t do anything in exhibition play to warrant a team putting in a claim for him. He would quickly have a home back on the Steelers’ practice squad should that be the route they would go. Instead, they will likely keep Howard, assuming he doesn’t go on IR with an injury he suffered against the Bills. Even if he does go on IR, though, eventually they’d have to take him off, which would lead to the team eventually carrying four quarterbacks. Who’s the player that will lose their helmet because of it? Robert Spears-Jennings? Doneiko Slaughter? Both of whom have had tremendous summers. If Howard gets a spot over someone who can contribute elsewhere, it’s roster building malpractice. Germie Bernard is WR3 I’ve seen enough from Bernard – he absolutely should be the starting slot receiver. The Alabama product has shown more this preseason than Roman Wilson has going on three seasons. It’s great that Wilson looked good in camp. It means nothing, though, when he does nothing come game time. Bernard showcased exactly why the Steelers traded up to get him, making Max Hairston miss on a screen pass and taking it the rest of the way to the end zone. He finished his preseason with five catches for 64 yards and a touchdown. And as impressive as his first (unofficial) touchdown was, it may not have been his best play of the preseason. In Week 1 against the Packers, he caught a ball on the right sideline made several defenders miss, and picked up 25 yards. The best thing the Steelers could do at receiver right now is give Bernard the No. 3 spot on the depth chart, see if they can get a late-round pick swap in exchange for Roman Wilson, and sign a veteran to be the No. 4 wide receiver Brandin Cooks would be the name I’d prefer. He’s still a quality deep threat, and he had a nice pair of seasons under McCarthy from 2023-24, catching 80 passes and 11 touchdowns in that two-year span. Kaden Wetjen puts exclamation point on preseason The rookie out of Iowa began the preseason with a 74-yard catch and a touchdown, and he ended it by showing exactly why the Steelers took him in the fourth round. The two-time Jet Award winner struggled to get anything going in the return game in the first half. In the third quarter, though, he sprung away from the Bills’ punt coverage and returned a kick 45 yards for a touchdown. Should he be able to house at least one kick during the regular season, many will forget about the Steelers reaching in the fourth for a return specialist. While he rode the highs and lows of his first NFL training camp, the highs are very high for one of the best return men in college football history. Several defenders make their case for roster spots There will be at least one defender worthy of a roster spot who doesn’t get one – which, again, makes the likelihood of Will Howard having a spot even more irrational. Devan Boykin had a strong preseason and led the team with nine tackles on Thursday. D’Shawn Jamison has been a practice squad mainstay for Pittsburgh over the last two years and appeared in three games in 2025. He’ll likely be placed on the practice squad again despite a nice preseason. Slaughter and Spears-Jennings are another pair of guys who are on that roster bubble, and one or both could be placed on the practice squad. Having a lot of quality players is a good problem to have, and Pittsburgh may have one of the deeper set of reserves in the NFL once Week 1 rolls around. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: Seahawks Droppings: Jason Myers meltdown cements Seattle’s winless preseason
summary: Well, the 2026 preseason is finally over with the Seattle Seahawks tying the Kansas City Chiefs 9-9 on a missed 52-yard field goal by Jason Myers. Actually, the reason the game was tied in the first place was because of a missed extra point by Myers earlier in the game. More on that later. I […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Place kicker Jason Myers #5 of the Seattle Seahawks misses a field goal as time expires in the fourth quarter of NFL preseason game action against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, the 2026 preseason is finally over with the Seattle Seahawks tying the Kansas City Chiefs 9-9 on a missed 52-yard field goal by Jason Myers . Actually, the reason the game was tied in the first place was because of a missed extra point by Myers earlier in the game. More on that later. I wouldn’t say that Seattle was impressive by any sense of the imagination against Kansas City, but they played well enough to win the game. Once again, there were no starters to be found on the field for the Seahawks while the Chiefs had a number of their first string get snaps including Travis Kelce, and Chris Jones. Maybe the best news of all was that there were no major injuries considering the shitshow that encompassed the trip to face the Tennessee Titans. Seahawks Droppings Jalen Milroe looked the best he has as a Seahawks QB throwing for over 200 yards and 1 TD . It would’ve looked even better if some of his teammates had made routine plays – a trend that’s been going on throughout this preseason. Milroe was credited with a fumble on a backwards pass to Jacardia Wright. Sure, the throw was a little low at waist high, but Wright needs to catch that. The next time Julian Hicks catches a pass will be the first time. I was impressed with Milroe’s decision making and accuracy overall tonight as he made some beautiful explosive passes of 40, 30, and 24 yards. Milroe also had an easy rushing TD on a read option that was (surprise, surprise) called back on a holding call. He followed that up with a TD pass to Nick Vannett. Milroe is still a work in progress, but definitely one that deserves to stick around on the roster. Yes, it is officially time to be concerned with Jason Myers. I touched on the subject last week, and Myers missed two more kicks tonight. The worst part was that neither was particularly close with a miss both wide left and wide right. All he needed for a hat trick was another one that came up short. Five missed kicks in three games is scary. Kickers are weird, man. It seems like they’re good until all of a sudden they aren’t and there’s no coming back from that. The rushing game was poor for Seattle on both sides of the ball . They were only able to manage 54 yards rushing on offense while giving up 155 rushing yards on defense. Seattle’s backup offensive lineman have played quite poorly all preseason blowing blocks and getting penalized. The game against the Chiefs was no different. Nehemiah Pritchett had a good game again tonight. He seems clearly set as the third CB behind Devon Witherspoon and Josh Jobe. Newcomer Trevon Diggs had an INT after only two practices with the team. Not too shabby. I’m not entirely convinced that Montorie Foster Jr has locked up a roster spot . Fans fret every year that the guys they cut will get scooped up by someone else, but every team has their own version of Foster. Cody White and Emmanuel Henderson Jr played well in this game and are just as deserving of a roster spot. At least the Seahawks had less than 100 penalty yards finishing with 90. This whole preseason it seems like Seattle has shot themselves in the foot on two thirds of their drives with a stupid penalty. It’s hard to dig out of a hole when you’re sitting at 1st and 20. I expect that to get cleaned up when the starters are on the field. Jamie Sheriff had two great special teams tackles while also getting some pressure off the edge . I don’t know if it was enough to get him a spot on the roster, but no one has really pulled away in that EDGE competition. I’m guessing it was just because of the lack of depth at safety, but seeing D’Anthony Bell playing into the 4th Quarter was surprising considering it seems like he’s a lock for the roster. Rodney Thomas II was back in action after an injury which was good to see. He’s still in the mix for a spot due to the Bud Clark injury. Honestly, I wouldn’t be surprised if Clark’s replacement is not yet on the roster. Maybe it’s time for a Jerrick Reed II reunion in a trade with TEN or a Nino signing after Week 1? Despite the Myers fiasco, I came away pretty encouraged with this game. The stream I was watching was the Chiefs broadcast so it was interesting to hear some of their analysis. Former Chiefs QB and current NFL Analyst Trent Green was on the broadcast and came away quite impressed with Milroe. Sometimes it’s good to get a different perspective from someone who doesn’t religiously follow the team. We can have such high expectations as fans that it colors our view of how some of the players are actually progressing. No, the Seahawks didn’t win any preseason games this year which we would’ve all liked to see. Their young players, however, did get vital reps to aid in their progression should they be called upon in the regular season. Real ball is up next, and I couldn’t be more excited!
author: Ted Zahn

title: Winners and Losers from Seahawks vs. Chiefs: Jalen Milroe has his best game
summary: The Seattle Seahawks’ preseason is over, although the Kansas City Chiefs game slogged on for so long that I thought they’d play beyond the roster cuts deadline. Unfortunately, Seattle could not notch a victory and only mustered up a 9-9 tie in large part because of some poor kicking from the normally reliable Jason Myers. […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Quarterback Jalen Milroe #6 of the Seattle Seahawks throws a pass during the second quarter of an NFL preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks’ preseason is over, although the Kansas City Chiefs game slogged on for so long that I thought they’d play beyond the roster cuts deadline. Unfortunately, Seattle could not notch a victory and only mustered up a 9-9 tie in large part because of some poor kicking from the normally reliable Jason Myers. Forget the scoreline and let’s focus on the overarching story. This was an important showcase night for Jalen Milroe as a full-game starter, as well as looking at the roster bubble players and whether they could make one last impression before Sunday’s cut-down day. Let’s get to the last Winners and Losers for the 2026 preseason! Seattle Seahawks Winners Jalen Milroe needed that in the worst way And by “that” I mean a series of quality plays with his arm that ward off any more calls that he should be waived. The first half was the best Milroe has looked in either preseason, making decisive, accurate, and on-time throws to Cody White, Montorie Foster, Nick Kallerup, and Elijah Arroyo. He even lost some yards and completions because Julian Hicks couldn’t handle the ball. It helped that (outside of one particular person) the offensive line was rarely troubled by KC’s pass rush, so Milroe had time to go through his progressions before making a decision to throw or run. His statline of 16/26 for 223 yards and a touchdown (to go with 20 yards rushing) actually is a bit unkind to his overall performance. This is the first time Milroe has looked demonstrably better than third and fourth-string opposition, which is what you want to see as a clear sign of improvement. The game seemed to slow down for him on Friday and the end result was a performance more in line with what his biggest supporters hoped he would look like. There’s very little to critique! If you were ready to send him to the waiver wire after the Tennessee Titans game then maybe tonight was a step back in the right direction. I imagine there are a few out there who don’t fully believe in Sam Darnold and are intrigued by the thought of not extending his contract and developing Milroe until he’s QB1. I’ll settle for staying the course and seeing if he can be QB2 in 2027. Trevon Diggs’ hands work just fine Did Garrett Nussmeier make a horrendous rookie mistake throwing off his back foot to Xavier Worthy? Yes. Did Trevon Diggs remind everyone he has tremendous ball skills and will gladly accept gifts sent his way? You better believe it. Welcome to Seattle, Trevon 🕺 📺: KING 5 pic.twitter.com/giOKelbrnh — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) August 29, 2026 He had one open-field missed tackle on Travis Kelce and a completed tackle on the game’s first play, and that’s about all there was to note. We’ll see if that suddenly makes him CB3 or if that in itself was enough to put him on the 53-man roster. Based on Mike Macdonald’s comments, I think he’ll be on the roster, and maybe above all else he looked healthy. Nehemiah Pritchett hangs tough in the red zone When the Seahawks were backed up at their own goal line, Pritchett was stuck like glue to his assignment on consecutive passes and helped hold the Chiefs to a field goal. I don’t see any roster danger for Pritchett, even if he’s not necessarily CB3 come September. Cody White has a bounce back game It was not Cody’s best day against the Tennessee Titans, having muffed a punt and dropped a deep pass last Sunday. He came back strongly with three catches for 69 yards. Whether or not he makes the initial 53-man roster, I bet White will be playing regular season football again for Seattle this year. Emmanuel Henderson Jr emerges late It’s been a quiet preseason for the rookie from Kansas, but he had his best night as a receiver with three catches for 58 yards, including the big grab that set up Seattle’s only touchdown. He also had an explosive catch that set up Jason Myers’ would-be game-winning field goal. Henderson has special teams versatility as a gunner and returner, which Ricky White III really does not from the returner perspective. There may be a slim chance Henderson makes the roster, but I think he has earned a practice squad spot. Michael Dickson even dominates the preseason When R Mason Thomas got through the line it looked like he was going to swat Dickson’s punt into the stands. Dickson pinned the Chiefs inside the 5 instead. There’s no one in the league doing it better than Dickson. He is as great a punter as there is in the NFL. Seattle Seahawks Losers Are you worried about Jason Myers yet? Combining field goals and PATs, Jason Myers went 3/8 in preseason. He missed more than half of his kicks! Luckily he’s built up equity up into the stratosphere when much lesser kickers would be out of a job by now, but this is not a nothing slump he’s in right now. Myers is knuckle-balling makeable kicks well wide for reasons I don’t understand. This is a contract year for Myers and it is starting inauspiciously for someone who’s been so reliable over the past few seasons. Myers was huge for Seattle throughout last season, particularly against the Indianapolis Colts and in the Super Bowl. Kickers at any level and of any ability can decline abruptly and precipitously. I want this to be an August funk and not something that bleeds into games that matter. Logan Brown was “don’t bring back to the practice squad” bad Brown’s brutal preseason continued with multiple pressures allowed and a strip sack given up to R. Mason Thomas. He offered up almost nothing as a run blocker, either. There’s no way he will make the 53 as a swing tackle. Uso Seumalo is a nice story, but… …He is not an NFL level defensive tackle. The Seahawks are not going to have any UDFA rookies on this roster, which is hardly the end of the world given the perceived weakness of the entire draft, let alone the undrafted. Seumalo had some intrigue as a big body who could take up space, control gaps, and be effective against the run. Pick any running play and he’s likely getting driven back several yards. I’m not even sure he’s going to be on the practice squad. Don’t even try to deeply assess the run game The third and fourth-string offensive line did not open up many holes for Jacardia Wright. Outside of Beau Stephens and maybe one of Christian Haynes or Bryce Cabeldue, most of the guys who played tonight are not on this roster by Sunday. At least there was some late traction toward the end of the game. Julian Hicks… whoo boy that was bad Two drops and a penalty on special teams. I hope he has a great backup plan for his career. Final Notes Why was Elijah Arroyo playing so much? I get that he was with Darnold and Lock and Milroe in training camp, but I wasn’t expecting him to get deep first half snaps in the final game, too. It was a little nervy seeing him come up grabbing his right wrist after falling awkwardly on a pass interference. Bryce Cabeldue got some late game snaps as a center, which continues what happened last year when he was primarily a G/C. Jalan Gaines made a great backside pursuit play to stop a 3rd and goal touchdown at the 1. I think he’ll be another practice squad stash after a solid camp and preseason. Aidan Hubbard had a “better late than never” best showing of August, showing an impressive motor and generating a couple of pressures. I thought Andre Fuller had some good reps as a tackler, and he could’ve had an interception if not for the ball bouncing off his hands. It will be fascinating to see if Seattle is able/wants to roster either Fuller or Michael Dansby. Shout out to the 12s for coming out in droves for a preseason road game! Did you hear the SEA-HAWKS chants come through? It’s roster cuts weekend. Seattle typically tends to wait until the deadline to…

title: NFL roster cuts: Where Seahawks sit in waiver wire, which players are eligible
summary: The preseason is in the books, and it is almost time for the regular season to begin, affording the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks an opportunity to defend their title as top dog in the NFL. Of course, even as the defending Super Bowl champion after having bested the Los Angeles Rams twice over the […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 25: Jalen Milroe #6 of the Seattle Seahawks and guard Bryce Cabeldue #77 warm up prior to an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 25, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The preseason is in the books, and it is almost time for the regular season to begin, affording the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks an opportunity to defend their title as top dog in the NFL. Of course, even as the defending Super Bowl champion after having bested the Los Angeles Rams twice over the final two months of the season, the Seahawks enter the season as underdogs in the NFC West according to FanDuel Sportsbook . FanDuel currently has Los Angeles ( +500 ) with better odds of winning the Super Bowl than Seattle ( +1100 ), as well as the over/under for wins by the Rams (11.5) higher than that of the Seahawks (10.5). Before the regular season opens against the New England Patriots on September 9, though, the Seahawks and the rest of the league will need to trim rosters down to 53, which will include several noteworthy players both in Seattle and around the league on waivers. As a refresher, in the NFL the waiver order through the offseason and into the third week of the regular season is set based on how teams finished the 2025 season. Thus, the Las Vegas Raiders have first dibs on any player placed on waivers, while the Seahawks will only be able to claim a player after all 31 other teams have passed. In addition, being awarded a player after a waiver claim does not change the waiver order, thus a team atop the waiver order can claim as many players as it wishes, with the only stipulation that every player claimed must then be placed on the 53 man roster of that team, which means moving on from another player that had initially been kept at roster cuts. The deadline for teams to trim their rosters down to 53 is 6pm New York time on Sunday, with waiver claims due before 1pm New York time on Monday. For those curious, the difference between a player who goes on waivers and a player who is outright released is based solely on the experience level of the player, specifically, how many accrued seasons the player has earned in their career. Any player who has four or more accrued seasons does not go on the waiver wire, and becomes a free agent immediately upon their release, while a player with three or fewer accrued seasons is subject to waivers. title: Seahawks Reacts Survey results: Fans split on Jalen Milroe’s future with Seattle
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seattle Seahawks fans and fans across the country. The preseason serves as an opportunity to make an impact and cement a roster spot but unfortunately, it’s a double edged sword — and Seattle Seahawks […]
full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seattle Seahawks fans and fans across the country. The preseason serves as an opportunity to make an impact and cement a roster spot but unfortunately, it’s a double edged sword — and Seattle Seahawks second-year quarterback Jalen Milroe learned that. After disappointing performances against the Dallas Cowboys and Tennessee Titans, opinions are mixed on whether his time with Seattle has reached its end. In an extremely tight poll, fans still believe Milroe has the support of the organization and see him making the 53-man roster with 54% of votes trending in that direction. However, 31% view the former third-round pick getting waived and 15% think the Seahawks will opt to trade him. Although he’s shown little promise since being drafted, Seattle doesn’t particularly stand to benefit from moving on after just one season. It’s worth remembering Milroe is in the second of his four-year, $6.2 million rookie contract so his release wouldn’t do much to ease the cap situation. From a performance standpoint, it seems risky to enter the season with just two quarterbacks (Sam Darnold and Drew Lock) on the roster. If the Seahawks opted to do so and cut Milroe, it would likely occur for one of two reasons; to add depth at a position of need or reward a training camp/preseason standout. Luckily for the young quarterback, wideout Montorie Foster Jr. is the lone candidate who’s unexpectedly performed at a level where the team would be foolish to cut him. You could make an argument for newly signed cornerback Trevon Diggs who’s appeared to be reliable in his time with the team so far, but it’d be much more realistic envisioning Seattle moving him to the practice squad — unless he hits the field looking like his 2021 self in the Seahawks’ final preseason game. Based on his previous performances, the hope should be Milroe makes the team once again and continues to take steps in his development, but doesn’t have to enter a game this season. That way, his fit within the organization becomes much clearer heading into the third year of his rookie contract and if he still isn’t showing signs of improvement, it’ll be far easier to cut ties. As for those who believe it’s in Seattle’s best interest to move on from the second-year quarterback, there’s certainly reason to back it up. Coming out of Alabama, he was viewed as a boom-or-bust candidate, largely in part to his eye-popping speed and rushing ability, but inability to be a consistent decision maker and accurate passer. Despite limited playing time, the former third-round pick hasn’t done much to ease those concerns. Through two preseason games, he’s netted a measly 88 passing yards to go alongside no touchdowns and two interceptions while also taking five sacks — one of which came on a costly fourth down against the Tennessee Titans last week. With teams required to release their 53-man rosters on August 30, time is running out for Milroe to prove his worth and his last chance will come in Friday’s preseason finale against the Chiefs. Head coach Mike Macdonald named him the starting quarterback and unlike their first two games , he’ll remain under center the entire night. The reality is, Milroe has factors working in his favor to make the 53-man roster, but his spot is far from safe. Friday’s game will certainly provide Macdonald and general manager John Schneider a clearer vision of how and more importantly, if he plays a role in the team’s future. title: Is Kyle Shanahan’s most infamous draft tradition finally about to bear fruit?
summary: It is one of the more frustrating patterns of the Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch era — the 49ers spend a relatively high pick on a running back, they struggle for playing time and they inevitably move on. However, entering the 2026 season, there is reason for optimism that this could be the year that […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Jordan James #29 of the San Francisco 49ers runs against Cian Slone #48 of the Las Vegas Raiders during the second quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is one of the more frustrating patterns of the Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch era — the 49ers spend a relatively high pick on a running back, they struggle for playing time and they inevitably move on. However, entering the 2026 season, there is reason for optimism that this could be the year that Shanahan’s commitment to investing draft capital in the running back position bears fruit. In the first four years of the Shanahan-Lynch regime, the 49ers only spent one draft pick on a back, doing so in their first year in 2017 when they took Joe Williams in the fourth round. Williams never played a snap. But since 2021, the 49ers have spent six draft picks on the position, the latest being a third-round selection used on Kaelon Black this year. Most of those picks have had limited success, though Elijah Mitchell led the 49ers in rushing as a rookie in 2021 before injuries derailed his progress with the team over subsequent seasons. Trey Sermon, a third-round pick that same year, lasted only one season, while 2023 third-rounder Tyrion Davis-Price’s career with the team was similarly short-lived. After encouraging signs in his rookie season, 2024 fourth-rounder Isaac Guerendo could soon see his time as a 49er come to an end, but the two most recent running back selections by the 49ers offer hope that Shanahan and San Francisco could be vindicated in continuing to throw draft resources at that area of the roster. Black and James provide reason for hope The 49ers need backs who can take some of the pressure off the now 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey, who has dealt with ‘tightness’ for much of training camp and preseason. And both Black and 2025 fifth-round pick James have provided evidence they are ready to do just that. Black rushed for 61 yards on 12 carries in preseason, an average of just over five yards a carry, but even more intriguing is the play he demonstrated in pass protection. If a younger back is going to eat into McCaffrey’s snaps, they must be able to hold up in pass protection, and the 49ers’ faith in Black’s ability to do so should be boosted following preseason. 49ers 3rd-round rookie Kaelon Black won the RB2 job with his performance in Preseason Week 2. He had two great pass protection reps versus blitzers. His vision stood out between the tackles. He flatten a few guys on contact. Shanny *cooking* spreadsheets with Strib & Black. pic.twitter.com/V06HP46BEp — Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) August 21, 2026 James did not earn any carries as a rookie until the 49ers’ blowout loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the divisional round of the playoffs. Having fractured his ribs on the second day of training camp, James’ only appearance of preseason came on Thursday as the Niners rounded off their exhibition schedule against the Las Vegas Raiders, and he gave San Francisco reason for encouragement. James displayed nice burst to the second level and contact balance on a 17-yard run that accounted for the bulk of his 35 yards on eight carriers, and he also demonstrated his abilities as a pass-catcher on a well-designed screen pass that went for 20 yards. “It was good to see him out there,” Shanahan said afterward. “He missed a ton of camp, too, with his injury, and had the same thing last year where he missed all of training camp. So he only got to play in that one game for us, got a couple carries versus Seattle at the end of the year last year. So I was really excited to watch him tonight, and from what I saw out there live, I thought he ran real hard and ran real well.” It may be a limited sample size in an exhibition game, but James coming back from injury and flashing as both a runner and a receiver theoretically improves his odds of getting on the field, even if Black likely has the edge as the second-string running back at this point. The 49ers aren’t likely to ask Black or James to try to replicate McCaffrey’s all-encompassing impact on the 49er offense. Very few backs in the NFL can have the influence McCaffrey has on both the run game and the passing attack. But as even more miles are put on the legs of a future Hall of Fame starter with a checkered injury history, the need for fresh backs who can take on more of the load increases. Leaning on Black and James to alleviate the strain on McCaffrey is a gamble given they have zero regular-season carriers between them. However, the flashes in preseason have been enough to suggest that, between them, they can help McCaffrey get the necessary rest and keep the 49er offense on the tracks when he is off the field. The Niners have waited a long time for Shanahan’s commitment to drafting backs to have a tangible positive impact on the team. There are no guarantees of preseason play translating into regular-season results, but there’s cause to be hopeful 2026 could be the season in which that wait ends.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Who was the biggest surprise of the preseason for the 49ers?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers’ preseason is officially over. The team will make roster decisions. The coaching staff should know by now who will make the team. Realistically, we’re talking about 3-5 spots up for grabs. Kyle Shanahan said he likes when players make it easy on him. Jacob Cowing did that with an 80+ yard […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Jordan Watkins #17 of the San Francisco 49ers signals first down after catching a pass against the Tennessee Titans in the first half at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers’ preseason is officially over. The team will make roster decisions. The coaching staff should know by now who will make the team. Realistically, we’re talking about 3-5 spots up for grabs. Kyle Shanahan said he likes when players make it easy on him. Jacob Cowing did that with an 80+ yard punt return in the second preseason game. De’Zhaun Stribling’s roster spot was never in doubt, but he made an impact in both games. Defensively, Jack Jones had the ball production the 49ers so desperately covet at cornerback. He gave Raheem Morris confidence during the preseason. Now that the preseason is over, who surprised you? Who was the biggest surprise of the preseason for the 49ers? It’s always fun to read what people-watching practice is saying and then see for yourself how the players perform. In a practice setting, it’s easy to get caught up in one flashy play and ignore what happens on a down-to-down basis. That brings me to my answer. I have two: one pleasant surprise, and one…not so much. Jordan Watkins is the kind of player who has preseason production in the box score, but once you go under the hood and focus on him, I’m not sure he’s an NFL player. Not for the 49ers, at least. Football is a violent game. Unfortunately for Watkins, there were too many exposures during the preseason of him either shying away from contact or failing to produce through contact. If we use the final preseason game as an example, Watkins turtled up on his first kickoff return when he was about to get tackled. He had an opportunity to block a safety, but he waited and was driven back instead of being the aggressor. Then you get into tracking the ball in the air, and you’re left wondering whether Watkins is worth investing in, or if you should listen to the signs he’s telling you and move on. Kurtis Rourke only played in one game. He’s closer to Mac Jones than Adrian Martinez. It’s too bad that Rourke was banged up, because it would have been fun to see him grow over three weeks with extended reps. The good news is that we saw him drop back 16 times, and that was more than enough to see a quality backup. Half of Rourke’s completions went for first downs. He was selectively aggressive—which is another reason multiple games would have been fun, to see if Rourke would’ve opened it up even more. Rourke completed all four of his passes beyond 10 yards. The 32-yarder to Stribling on third down was a thing of beauty, and the type of aggressive decision Kyle Shanahan wants at the position. Rourke handled pressure well, and even avoided a sack. I thought he looked the part and wouldn’t dare think about losing him to waivers. Who surprised you the most this season?

title: 4 Winners and 2 losers: Is the 49ers’ defensive line depth good enough?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers’ preseason finale didn’t have a touchdown scored. The special teams showed out, while the rookies continued to learn on the fly as the coaching staff evaluated the roster. Let’s get into the final winners and losers from August. Winners Eddy Pineiro Kyle Shanahan said he was “pissed” at Pineiro for deferring […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 17: Alfred Collins #95 of the San Francisco 49ers stands on the field with his teammates during the second quarter of an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers’ preseason finale didn’t have a touchdown scored. The special teams showed out, while the rookies continued to learn on the fly as the coaching staff evaluated the roster. Let’s get into the final winners and losers from August. Winners Eddy Pineiro Kyle Shanahan said he was “pissed” at Pineiro for deferring to the second half in the preseason. The 49ers kicker followed that up with a touchback on the opening kick. You’re here to evaluate players covering kicks, so it was an 0-2 start for Pineiro. That would be his last blunder. Dineiro Pineiro made all six of his field goal attempts, including three from 50+ and a 59-yarder. The ball barely moved. Pineiro was making his kicks with room to spare. Corliss Waitman Waitman could end up being one of the better additions for the Niners this offseason, if his preseason performance is any indication. He had four punts with a net average of 46.5 yards. All four of his punts landed inside of the 20. Two of them were fair caught. The other two didn’t gain any yards. And Waitman’s long was 53 yards. Any time you can make your opponent go 80+ yards, you’ve done your job. Jack Jones Jones only played six snaps. He gave up a curl route for 14 yards. But he jumped a Brock Bowers route for a near interception. Those are the types of plays 49ers cornerbacks haven’t been in a position to make in several years. Jones also made an open-field tackle and was a willing run defender in limited action. Jones is a different type of player than what the Niners have had at cornerback in some time. That might end up being a good thing. Khalil Dinkins This kid is worth investing in. On Dinkins’ second play, the team trusted him to stay in and pass protect. He ended up helping right tackle Brandon Parker on a defensive lineman. On the next play, Dinkins drove the safety about seven yards from where he started. On the play where Jordan James ran for 17 yards, Dinkins worked to the linebacker and secured him, paving the way for James. Who knows if Dinkins ever turns into a viable pass catcher, but he is the exact type of prospect the team has drafted in the sixth round under this regime. Dinkins is a keeper. The aggression he plays with is palpable. Dinkins blocks with the intent that George Kittle would admire. He should stick on the practice squad. Losers The defensive line We did not see Sam Okuayinonu, Osa Odighizuwa, Nick Bosa, or Romello Height. So, the players who project to log starter snaps. Alfred Collins, a second-round pick, played late into the third quarter. Shanahan cited that it was because of rust. The reality is that Collins has not been effective. It was the same as it’s been in each of the previous two games for Collins. He was moved easily against the run and did not win as a pass rusher. I’d argue the best run play from a defensive tackle was by Keion White on third down. Outside of that, Collins, CJ West, Sebastian Davis, James Thompson Jr., and Bryson Eason all left a lot to be desired against the Raiders’ first- and second-team offensive line. They made Spencer Burford look good. Nobody really won when it came to rushing the passer, either. Ogbo Okoronkwo had a couple of pressures, but no other defensive lineman can say the same. West won once as a pass rusher. So did Thompson Jr. and Valdez. But that does it as far as wins are concerned. It was an uninspiring performance from a group that had given us hope during the past couple of weeks. Maybe this is who they are, and it’s a sign the 49ers need to add bodies who are not on the roster in an effort to find somebody who can contribute while Mykel Williams is out. The defensive line depth, unsurprisingly, is concerning. Carver Willis Willis may win the left guard job because nobody else around him can stay healthy. But it won’t be because of the product he put out in the preseason after Week 1. Willis is inconsistent, as you’d expect from a rookie. He played the entire first half. In those 29 snaps, it’s problematic if Willis is going against a defensive tackle with length. He still looks unsure of who to block at times when on the move. But I think his ability to strain blocks, aka hold his ground when he’s head up against somebody 1-on-1, could be an issue. I think Willis will end up being a good player, but it’s obvious he needs some time. Can the 49ers afford to give him that time?
author: Kyle Posey

title: 3 stars from the 49ers preseason finale: The depth at running back looks better than ever
summary: The third preseason game is usually the dress rehearsal for the regular season, but with a trip across the world looming, Kyle Shanahan decided to see what roster spots 23-53 look like to close the preseason. While the Las Vegas Raiders went with their starters, Thursday turned into a kicking battle, with Eddy Pineiro outdueling […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 20: Kaelon Black #26 of the San Francisco 49ers rushes during the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. The 49ers defeated the Chargers 41-17. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The third preseason game is usually the dress rehearsal for the regular season, but with a trip across the world looming, Kyle Shanahan decided to see what roster spots 23-53 look like to close the preseason. While the Las Vegas Raiders went with their starters, Thursday turned into a kicking battle, with Eddy Pineiro outdueling Matt Gay and leading the 49ers to an 18-12 victory. Had this been a regular-season game, Pineiro would have been a runaway for the No. 1 star, but with him already a lock for the roster, let’s look at three players who used the preseason finale to earn a job and/or earn a spot on the initial 53-man roster. These are the three stars as the 49ers close the book on the preseason and look forward to Melbourne: 3rd Star – RB Kaelon Black/RB Jordan James The 49ers are set at running back. It might not matter with Christian McCaffrey taking the lion’s share of the carries in the regular season, but the depth is there. Both Black and James looked the part as neither blew up the box score, but both certainly passed the eye test. The duo combined for 63 yards on 12 attempts, with both recording impressive runs during their reps. Black got the first look on Thursday, looking to build off his impressive debut last week. While he didn’t get too many chances, just four carries, Black made the most of them, averaging seven yards per attempt, closing his day with 28 rushing yards. A bulk of those 28 yards came on one run. With the 49ers deep in Las Vegas territory following a Fernando Mendoza interception, the 49ers wanted to get Black involved early. He would take the opening carry around the right edge and show an impressive speed boost to get the corner and turn upfield for a gain of 14. Shanahan seemed impressed enough to make that Black’s final touch of the evening. James entered from there and got chances early. On his first drive, he was fed the ball on three straight plays, gaining nine on the first two plays before losing a yard on third down, forcing a San Francisco punt. But James would turn it on from there. It would start with a quick 20-yard reception that would move the 49ers into plus territory. A few plays later, James would get his big play, exploding through the line for a gain of 17, leading to another Pineiro field goal. Black and James were already locks to make the initial 53-man, but seeing what they look like sharing the backfield gives plenty of confidence to a backup running back spot that’s had plenty of turnover in recent years. 2nd Star – LG Carver Willis The 49ers have treated the left guard spot like a carousel over training camp and the preseason, with Connor Colby and Robert Jones getting first looks before Austen Pleasants got a look last week. It was Willis’s turn this week and he might not give up the spot. Willis played the entire first half without being noticed too much, which is probably a good thing for an offensive lineman trying to earn a spot on the starting line. While Willis was on the field, the 49ers didn’t allow a single sack. And while that’s an accomplishment for the entire line, Willis also didn’t allow a single pressure according to Pro Football Focus. It might have been a very backwards way to find a starting left guard, but Willis’s performance on Thursday might have done the trick to find an answer to the more infuriating question of 49ers training camp. 1st Star – LB Tatum Bethune/LB Jaden Dugger With the 49ers acquiring Deion Jones earlier this week, the 49ers have about eight linebackers with a case to make the roster. Last year, the 49ers kept five linebackers on the initial 53-man, but the year before they kept six, so eight players for either five or six spots. Obviously, somebody is going to miss out. Dugger seemed like a sure thing to make the roster, especially with his versatility to play the defensive line. He made a strong final impression against the Raiders, leading the 49ers with 10 tackles and hit the Raiders quarterback twice. Sure, there was a bad missed tackle to stop what would turn out to be a Las Vegas third-down, but overall it was a solid performance from the rookie who has proved he could be used in a vital role this season for a somewhat rebuilt San Francisco defense. If there was one player who stood out as much as Dugger on Thursday night, it would be Bethune. Bethune entered Thursday night more on the fringe than Dugger, which might make his game slightly more impressive. Only Dugger finished with more tackles than Bethune, who finished with nine tackles, but Bethune was more present in the passing game, recording a pass breakup and finding himself in the right spot at the right time to intercept Mendoza in the first quarter. Two impressive performances, one from a rookie who’s looking to earn a role in the NFL, and one on the roster bubble. We will see how the 53-man roster looks come Sunday, but it was an emphatic final performance from both Bethune and Dugger.
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: Buccaneers preseason finale was a disappointment for many
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers closed out the preseason Friday night with an offensive performance they will quickly want to put behind them, falling 19-0 to the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium. With Tampa Bay sitting its starters, rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels received an extended opportunity to make his case for a roster spot. But after […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Bryan Thomas Jr #57 of the Jacksonville Jaguars sacks Jalon Daniels #10 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during a preseason game at EverBank Field on August 28, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers closed out the preseason Friday night with an offensive performance they will quickly want to put behind them, falling 19-0 to the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium. With Tampa Bay sitting its starters, rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels received an extended opportunity to make his case for a roster spot. But after leading five scoring drives over the first two preseason games, Daniels and the offense never found a rhythm. He completed eight of 15 passes for 57 yards, was sacked three times and finished with nine rushing yards as Tampa Bay managed just 87 total yards. The struggles went well beyond the quarterback position. The Bucs had trouble protecting Daniels, failed to establish the running game and committed a costly botched snap that handed Jacksonville possession deep in Tampa Bay territory. Head coach Todd Bowles did not sugarcoat the performance afterward. “Not good enough,” Bowles said . “Anytime you get shut out, you know. I didn’t think we protected the quarterback enough. We couldn’t run the ball. We gave up a special teams touchdown. The defense fought; they made some mistakes but at least they fought. I thought two out of the three phases didn’t show up.” Tampa Bay’s defense provided several bright spots, including sacks from Anthony Nelson and Jack Pyburn, but the headlines belong to an offense that failed to score as the Bucs finished the preseason 2-1. Several players will look at Friday’s night game as one they wish they can have back. Offensive linemen played poorly and receivers dropped pass which made the rookie quarterback’s stats look worse than what they should have been. Daniels should still make the roster. Whether he is named QB2 remains to be seen.

title: Commanders News: Preseason ends; now come final roster decisions
summary: The Daily Slop – 29 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: The Daily Slop – 29 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links FINAL: @Ravens dominate on both sides of the ball and get the W! pic.twitter.com/mdUpmX3s4z — NFL (@NFL) August 29, 2026 Articles The Athletic (paywall) Commanders 53-man roster projection: Help needed on O-line, tough choice at WR Outside linebacker (4): Odafe Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson, Joshua Josephs, Javontae Jean-Baptiste *Dorance Armstrong is placed on the reserve/suspended list The NFL suspended Armstrong for the season opener for violating the personal conduct policy, which temporarily clears a roster spot. Jean-Baptiste missed much of last season due to a pectoral injury and didn’t show much in the early going of camp. If Washington’s outside linebackers finished camp healthy and available, Jean-Baptiste may have been hard-pressed to get a spot, but Armstrong’s suspension and injuries to Oweh (calf) and Chaisson (knee) — Quinn has not provided a timetable for their return — make it worth keeping him. Cornerback (5): Mike Sainristil, Amik Robertson, Trey Amos, Rasul Douglas, Fabian Moreau There are a number of outstanding questions about this group, none bigger than the availability of Amos. The 2025 second-round pick was Washington’s most consistent corner last year, but a fractured fibula cut his season short and cost him the entire offseason. He returned two weeks into camp but suffered an ankle sprain in his second practice. It’s unclear if he will be available for Week 1. Washington added Douglas and Moreau to give the team more veteran experience and depth, and both proved their worth. Whenever Amos returns, it’ll be interesting to see whether Robertson or Sainristil shifts inside to the slot. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room Washington Commanders Initial 53-man Roster Projection [There are] two factors in deciding to keep three quarterbacks for me. The first is the injury Marcus Mariota suffered in the preseason opener against Miami. It’s expected he’ll be back in time for the opening game of the season, but if there’s any sort of setback or delay in that return, then you need a third quarterback. Even if he is healthy enough to play, he hasn’t practiced in weeks so he might be lacking sharpness. So it feels wise to keep a third quarterback on the roster just in case. But the second and more prominent reason to keep a third quarterback is Kaliakmanis’ performances. He’s played so well so far in the preseason that I think he’s earned a spot on the 53. I know a lot of fans will speculate about another team claiming him if they cut him and try to stash him on the practice squad, but I don’t think that would be so much of a risk. If you’re looking for a quarterback during roster cut down day, it’s either because your starter or back up is injured. If you need a starter, you’re searching around the NFL for a more established player than Kaliakmanis and probably trying to trade for him. If you need a back up, you’re likely looking for someone with familiarity in your system that can come in and be ready to go right away. It’s pretty rare that you see teams claim a rookie quarterback that they could have drafted with any pick higher than 223rd overall pick a few months ago. So I do think if Washington really wants to save a roster spot and stash Kaliakmanis on the practice squad, where he can still be designated as the emergency third quarterback on game day, then I think they’d probably manage to do it without anyone claiming him. But based on his preseason performances so far (obviously he could have a terrible outing against Baltimore tonight and change the equation here), I think he’s earned his spot on the 53. If you subscribe to the theory of just keeping your best 53 players, I think Kaliakmanis has been one of their best 53. That would lead me to rewarding that performance level with a roster spot. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Projecting Commanders depth chart after preseason WR (6): Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown, Jaylin Lane, Treylon Burks Skinny: Luke McCaffrey was the lone one from the [‘likely to make it’] group who played on Friday night, with just one catch to show for it — a humbling showing in a potential final audition. Friday’s showing dropped the number of wide receivers from seven to six, though whether Washington does ultimately find a trade suitor as some have speculated could be worth tracking. TE (4): Chig Okonkwo, John Bates, Ben Sinnott, Colson Yankoff Skinny: the top of the room is clear with Okonkwo now anchoring the room while Bates returns as the in-line blocker and Sinnott as a secondary receiving threat. Yet with an offense that’s expected to feature two tight end sets, coupled with a strong offseason, Yankoff could be another piece in the room. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Commanders’ final 53-man roster prediction after intense preseason battles Defensive Line (5): Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw, Tim Settle Jr., Charles Omenihu, Ricky Barber The Washington Commanders were dealt another blow on their defensive front after Johnny Newton suffered a torn pectoral muscle that required surgery, ending any hopes of his breakout campaign. Daronte Jones will have to make the best of a bad situation, and it places even more pressure on the starting trio to stay healthy. Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw, and free-agent signing Tim Settle Jr. have the scope to be productive. Charles Omenihu offers versatility and proven production. Deatrich Wise Jr. would have been the call, but he hasn’t practiced all summer and could land on the physically unable to perform list to start the season, paving the way for Ricky Barber to make the team. Linebacker (4): Sonny Styles, Frankie Luvu, Leo Chenal, Jordan Magee Washington’s linebacking corps will be a real strength, or at least it should be. But that doesn’t make it any easier to figure out who’ll be on the team to start the campaign. Frankie Luvu is moving back to his off-ball role in a contract year. Free-agent signing Leo Chenal fits the athletic, explosive prototype Daronte Jones is looking for. No. 7 overall selection Sonny Styles has all the makings of a franchise cornerstone, even if he is coming in for some extremely harsh criticism on social media right now. Behind them is the intriguing part. Jordan Magee and Kain Medrano both offer special-teams value, but Ale Kaho has also made a strong push for roster consideration. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE A to Z Sports Preaseaon game 3: The consolation awards On defense, a few names stood out. Ale Kaho looked like a player who belongs. He showed up, put in effort, and tackled well. Car’lin Vigers hustled enough to save a touchdown on a chase-down play. Washington is always susceptible to falling in love with a player who runs down a fast ball carrier, and Vigers earned that moment. Byron Cowart also made a case for himself in a defensive line room full of heavy defensive tackles who somehow gave up 195 rushing yards. He was one of the few to actually get backfield penetration. The Commanders played the Ravens last night in the preseason finale and had 41 players inactive. If not claimed by another team, after noon on Wednesday they are eligible to be a part of Washington’s 17-man practice squad. Which Washington Commanders are subject to waivers? Johnson S Quindell Johnson WR Jacoby Jones DE Joshua Josephs LB Ale Kaho QB Athan Kaliakmanis S Qwuantrezz Knight WR Jaylin Lane LB Jordan Magee DE T.J. Maguranyanga S Quan Martin DT Jeffrey M’ba WR Luke McCaffrey TE Tre’ McKitty LB Kain Medrano TE Quentin Moore WR Nick Nash DT Jer’Zhan Newton S Tyler Owens OL Nicholas Petit-Frere CB Darius Rush CB Mike Sainristil TE Ben Sinnott K Drew Stevens LB Sonny Styles OL Tanoa Togiai CB Car’lin Vigers WR Antonio Williams TE Colson Yankoff How waivers work in the NFL When a player is ‘waived’, he is subject to the waiver wire, where any team can claim him and assume his current contract. Currently, the waiver wire order (listed below) is dependent on the NFL Draft order from this past April, but without any trades. Every team that is interested in acquiring a player will file its waiver claim in the same time window, but only the team with the highest claim will successfully ‘claim’ the player and his current contract. Which NFL players are subject to waivers? Whether or not a player is put on the waiver wire or becomes a free agent depends on a player’s NFL service time. Six games active in a season earns a player an accrued season. Players with at least four years of accrued NFL service time are released outright (not subject to waivers). In this case, upon release, the player’s contract ends and he immediately becomes an unrestricted free agent who is eligible to sign with any team. However, as described above, if a player has less than four years of service time, he is subject to waiver wire claims. Any player who is not claimed after being waived is eligible to sign wherever he’d like, including his former team’s practice squad. Mainly, the group of players who get waived comprises those who are currently not eligible for unrestricted free agency status entering the year — Exclusive Rights Free Agents (less than three years of service) or Restricted Free Agents (three years of service). What is the NFL waiver order right now? The NFL waiver order during the preseason and the first three weeks of the regular season mirrors the 2026 NFL Draft order (absent trades). Once we get through three games, the waiver order resets weekly to the current NFL standings. So, until Week 4, the Raiders have first crack at every player on waivers. The Washington Commanders had the No. 7 pick in this year’s draft, selecting Ohio State LB Sonny Styles. They are also 7th in the waiver wire list, meaning there are six teams ahead of them to claim any eligible players that get released over the next month.
